Host-side toolchain friction removed

epochs.name: Security Hardening
epochs.goal: Validate every saved security candidate, fix each confirmed root cause, add hostile regression proof, and close with an independent security review and a clean follow-up scan.

epochs.name: Cross Platform
epochs.goal: macOS, Windows, and every other non-Linux target. Jet development targets Linux first, so cross-platform support is sequenced deliberately after the Linux experience is right, and a red macOS or Windows row never blocks Linux work.

epochs.name: Developer Experience
epochs.goal: Jet programs on every target get the best developer experience of any ecosystem: one-command entry, one observation protocol with panels rendered in the browser, dev dashboard, terminal, editor, and native overlays, a live loop that keeps state on every tier, a first-party web suite, and equal-depth tooling for games, backend, live debugging, systems, mobile, data, and CLI work.

epochs.name: Foundations for every domain
epochs.goal: Every critical area (web, games, CLI and scripts, data analysis, backend services, AI/ML apps, GUI apps, embedded) can be built by a library author with Jet's primitives, ecosystem tools, core library, and shared data types. Probes find the primitive gaps; only primitives are proposed; buildable niches get executable examples; critical areas get batteries as needed. Replaces the withdrawn domain-matrix slate (owner, 2026-09-02).

epochs.name: Sprint: owner goals
epochs.goal: Owner sprint goals (2026-10): live high-level targets with measured completion; each goal is a milestone whose criteria are its checkpoints; finished goals are closed out and archived.

epochs.name: Best scripting language
epochs.goal: Jet becomes the best scripting language of all time: it beats Lua, JavaScript, TypeScript, Bash and Python on startup and run time for real scripts, and on how easy a script is to write, read and reason about, measured by tokens per task and by review of the same programs written in each language. Jet already runs the repository's own tooling, so its scripting surface is infrastructure.

verification.evidence: Composed targeted sweep on the integrated tree: cargo check --workspace --all-targets 0 errors 0 warnings; cargo test --test debug 39 passed 0 failed; cargo test --test machine_output 10 passed 0 failed; tower node --test 292 passed 0 failed. milestones.title: M20 · Enum language, types, and reflection
milestones.goal: Close the ordinary E3 language contract for enums, tagged values, callables, reflection, checked ingress, and their execution-tier behavior without creating a second enum model.

criteria.text: Enum declarations, payload patterns, generic substitution, methods, derived behavior, empty/singleton/default cases, and related sums agree across parser, semantic facts, runtime, and diagnostics.
Checked numeric ingress distinguishes representability from declared membership, preserves the existing fallible-conversion law, and leaves C ABI work to the foreign-boundary owner.
Callable constructors, labels, captures, dispatch, ownership, layout, and storage choices have explicit observable contracts; source-level compactness is not treated as a cost proof.
Reflection, builtin catalogs, case descriptors, completion, navigation, and rename use the same semantic identity and preserve payload typing and source identity.
Tier parity, discriminant evaluation, and build invalidation name their compiler/build prerequisite; wire representation remains an encoding choice under the existing data model.

milestones.title: M21 · Iterator and standard-library contracts
milestones.goal: Make one E3 iterator and standard-library contract explicit for sources, ownership, stop and failure, adapters, collection consumers, streams, channels, and bounded concurrency.

criteria.text: One authoritative iterator operation/capability record names eager or lazy work, source ownership, callback order, buffering, failure, cancellation, and cleanup.
Collection, view, stream, channel, environment, command, filesystem, I/O, and network sources preserve their distinct item, remainder, encoding, EOF, and error rules.
Borrowed, mutable, copied, boxed, erased, replayed, and destination-producing paths state lifetime and capability behavior without hidden materialization or payload-copy promises.
Selection, grouping, joins, partitioning, combinations, set operations, top-k, formatting, and copy boundaries reuse the one model; ratified top-k law D-COLLECTION-TOPK1 remains the source choice.
Parallel and asynchronous consumers name bounds, ordering, short-circuit, end, race, and task-cancellation behavior; optional dependency leverage remains an E5 choice.

milestones.title: M22 · Encoding, validation, and data boundaries
milestones.goal: Close canonical E3 encoding, validation, text, numeric, schema, and data-boundary behavior without a parallel codec or validation model.

criteria.text: Canonical readers and writers preserve typed identity, paths, causes, framing, unknown/duplicate policy, and explicit validation boundaries.
JSON, binary, text, URL, MIME, locale, markup, configuration, patch, and schema projections have separate contracts where their wire jobs differ.
Streaming, selective, fixed-buffer, partial, canonical, and lossless operations state allocation, early-exit, malformed-input, and round-trip behavior.
Peer interoperability and optional codecs are compared against the existing Core/data owner; dependency or provider placement is separately routed to E5.
Data/UI validation and ordinary network values reuse one typed result/failure model rather than inventing a second validator.

milestones.title: M23 · Core CLI and text foundations
milestones.goal: Make E3 command, configuration, text, formatting, locale, and entry foundations coherent for ordinary Jet programs.

criteria.text: ArgsSpec, command metadata, validation, entry sugar, configuration inclusion, and text parsing expose one checked source of truth.
CLI completion, help/reference projections, text comparison, formatting, locale, and message catalogs preserve source identity and explicit output policy.
Interactive or documentation-specific surfaces are routed to E14/E10 only when they are advanced tooling or release/reference work, not merely because they emit text.
Encoding, text, and command errors retain structured causes and actionable source locations.

milestones.title: M24 · Checked source facts and identity
milestones.goal: Keep basic IDE and compiler-facing source identity facts stable across semantic queries, diagnostics, locations, catalogs, and source-backed repairs.

criteria.text: A semantic identity and checked source snapshot anchor definitions, references, edits, diagnostics, generated origins, and source spans.
Unknown, stale, incomplete, and unavailable facts are explicit; no empty fallback is presented as a proved fact.
Basic navigation, rename, source-linked diagnostics, callable contracts, and local obligation facts preserve the existing semantic-index contract.
Advanced observation panels, live-loop cancellation, replay, and human/agent change-loop measurements remain E14/E7 work and consume these facts rather than redefining them.

milestones.title: M25 · HTTP and service runtime
milestones.goal: Close the E3 HTTP, application, request, transport, and service-lifecycle contracts used by ordinary programs and backend foundations.

criteria.text: Typed HTTP routes, forms, schemas, clients, bodies, dispatch, policy order, deadlines, cancellation, and generated projections agree on one checked operation model.
Request authority, transaction, resource readiness/drain, completion, retry/ack, cache absence, and local scheduling state their distinct semantics.
Browser, TCP, GraphQL, gRPC, messaging, socket, and endpoint adapters preserve the canonical error, cancellation, and source identity contracts.
Security-sensitive controls retain E12 review where the card is about identity, disclosure, capability, or containment; package/adapter placement remains E5.
Backend batteries and matched domain workload measurements remain E15 only when they are explicit domain examples or comparisons.

milestones.title: M26 · Runtime lifetimes and concurrency
milestones.goal: Close E3 ownership, cleanup, task, channel, process, stream, and concurrency behavior without hidden lifetime extension or a second runtime.

criteria.text: Scopes, deferred cleanup, finalizers, callbacks, task groups, channels, joins, cancellation, and fail-fast outcomes are observable and tier-consistent.
Process argv/pipes/child cleanup and ordinary resource lifetimes preserve bounds, partial failure, exit identity, and close behavior.
Runtime and standard-library work does not claim security closure; hostile containment routes to E12 and agent policy routes to E7.
Measurements distinguish correctness/ownership from performance admission and keep matched workloads attached to the owning E3 contract.

milestones.title: M27 · Numeric and CPU foundations
milestones.goal: Close ordinary E3 numeric, simulation-randomness, and CPU-value behavior used by programs and domain batteries without moving shared primitives into a domain epoch.

criteria.text: Fixed, big, decimal, rational, complex, checked, wrapping, saturating, statistics, and repeatable-randomness operations state their value, overflow, precision, and seed behavior.
Native, interpreter, and web/portable paths preserve the same typed numeric identity and failure behavior where the target supports the operation.
Shared numeric and physical-value correctness is proved once for E3 consumers; GUI, games, AI, and device examples consume it rather than redefining it.
Measurements distinguish correctness and representation from a performance admission claim.

milestones.title: M09 · Compiler facade and build facts
milestones.goal: Expose stable read-only compiler/build facts and invalidation boundaries on the ratified E4 metaprogramming and programmable-build foundation.

criteria.text: Public compiler/build operations agree in checking, evaluation, source-origin, diagnostic, semantic-fact, and JSON/Rust projections.
Generated modules, generic/enum facts, cache identity, reload invalidation, and build provenance preserve exact source snapshots and do not silently claim current success.
Build-time I/O, dependency, toolchain, and generated-source policy remains under E4 law; E3 source facts are consumed rather than duplicated.
Public API choices remain read-only/compiler-facade choices; package/provider placement belongs to E5 and self-hosting/port work remains E11.

milestones.title: M08 · Plugin and embedding lifecycle

Release, finalizer, callback, re-entry, and retained-guest-root witnesses show ownership and cleanup without hidden lifetime extension.
Native and sandbox/wasm hosts preserve typed values, source locations, and structured guest failures under the existing foreign-boundary contract.
Source, cache, and compiled-artifact admission has deterministic identity/provenance; named exports and embedding examples use the accepted surface.
Each applicable tier records supported, unavailable, and error outcomes; no second plugin API or unratified dependency is introduced.

cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-GAME-ASSET1=A in Jet. Core/game owns scene-scoped asset identity, the typed image and sound handles, kind and path validation, and the atomic hot-reload transaction. The host keeps only file-read and decode leaves.

## Current state
- Core/game/game.jet:19-48 has only plain `Scene{name, max_frames, tick}`, `Replay{path}` and `Backend{name, running}`. The exports are `Backend`, `Replay`, `Scene` and `run` (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1944).
- Every asset semantic is Rust: GameState asset roots and handles (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Game.rs:10-20), `jet_game_assets_image` and `jet_game_assets_sound` (:402-441), and the reload transaction (:444-493).
- Codegen routes game handles to host symbols (Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet:1095-1099). Sema is Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Game.jet.
- Examples/features/game/core_game_headless.jet:17-18 uses `scene.assets.image` and `scene.assets.sound`, and has a golden.
- Ratified shape (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:3695-3706): `player: scene.assets.image("assets/player.png")?`, with handles tied to scene identity.

## Changes
1. Core/game/game.jet: a `SceneAssets` registry keyed by scene identity, with typed `GameImage` and `GameSound` handles {scene, path, kind, revision}; `image(path)` and `sound(path)`; and `reload`, which validates the import fact (kind, declared path, owning scene) and then publishes one deterministic handle and receipt. A missing file, wrong kind, stale scene, corrupt import fact or failed reload returns a typed error and leaves the last valid handle and its provenance unchanged.
2. Game.rs keeps only the provider leaves (read bytes, decode header into an import fact, the dev-session watch relay). Delete `jet_game_assets_image`, `jet_game_assets_sound` and the reload policy. Route `scene.assets.*` to the Jet source in HandleMethods.jet and Sema Calls/Game.jet.
3. Add the new types to CoreCallRows.jet:1944 and run `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --write`.
4. New Examples/features/game/game_assets.jet with Examples/features/expected/game/game_assets.out. It covers success; each failure cell, printing the retained handle and receipt; and a handle used on a second scene. It must fail if `scene.assets` bypasses the Jet registry.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden game/game_assets` passes.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden game/core_game_headless` still passes.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden game/game_assets` passes on O0, O1 and O2.

## Batch
batch-core-ui: Core/game plus Jet codegen and sema routing, proven by game goldens.

## Dependencies
None open. #3690 is the umbrella direction, not a prerequisite.

Game window: Core copies raylib's unpaired begin_drawing(window)/end_drawing() and window_should_close loop condition (raylib.jet:44,56-62). Proposal from APICompCraft: a scoped raylib.frame(window, (draw) -> {...}) that always pumps events, including while minimized, and carries minimized/resized/frame_time facts. Unreal game-thread talk (KxREK-DYu70): 22 trivial ticks cost 44 us, aggregating 18 same-type actors cut 2.8 ms to 0.95 ms, and one deferred end-of-frame write replaces up to three moves per frame; both match D-SYSSCHED1=A. Proposed acceptance: N entities give one system invocation per frame; handles follow D-POOLID-API1 generations and a despawned handle reads as absent (now ballot D-GAME-ENTITY1); structural changes are stage-end commands, so D-GAME-REPLAY1 transcripts match under .Serial, parallel and one worker; attachment-chain propagation is one ordered stage. cards.plan:
## Outcome
Prove the native terminal-baseline config in a real QEMU guest. This is an integration proof card, not a plumbing-tier substitute and not a NixOS comparison.

## Ordered work
1. Wait for the active native prerequisites in the blocker list: profiles, mutable `/etc`, activation, accounts, PAM, composition, systemd, kernel packaging, boot rollback, and the no-installed-Nix gate. Resolve #909's D-JOS-BOOTKERNEL2 owner gate before claiming a boot result.
2. Trace `jet os vm run` through `vm_commands.rs`, `installer_media.rs`, and `vm_proof.rs`. Bind the source config, closure, toolchain, kernel, initrd, generation, package set, service, identity, and login facts into one receipt.
3. Build the terminal baseline only through the native pipeline. Launch real QEMU with the required firmware and serial channel. Strip PATH so neither `nix` nor `nix-store` is reachable in the build or guest lane.
4. Capture serial assertions for getty login, `/etc/os-release`, prompt, store paths, generation, service, network, rollback, and absence of NixOS or Nix. Attach the serial log and a screenshot or equivalent real-guest artifact.
5. Exercise at least one failed boot or rollback path without replacing the real guest with a mock or cached plumbing marker.

## Exit proof
The four existing criteria stay open until a fresh real-QEMU run produces the required guest facts and artifact. QEMU/OVMF and serial capture are hard proof prerequisites; installation, QEMU, and product proof are not run during preparation.

cards.plan:
**Goal**
Add a non-skipping native Windows C ABI runtime matrix for x64 and x86 (it absorbed #997). Production-generated Jet Rust links against real MSVC C, and the matrix proves per architecture:
- exact imported and exported symbols;
- struct and enum layout checked against C;
- capture-free callbacks under reentrant and concurrent foreign threads;
- poison-byte safety of status and out-pointers;
- borrowed UTF-8 string returns;
- default C/system and every supported Windows calling convention, including the x86 stdcall and fastcall spellings.

**Deferral**
The owner moved this to e13. Linux cannot prove it.

**Current state**
- The harness is `tests/cffi_native_matrix.rs` (Linux rows only) plus `tests/cffi.rs`.
- Self-hosted FFI lowering is `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/ForeignFunctions.jet` and `CffiFacts.jet`, with jet-ffi-descriptor-v1 per-language ABI leaves.
- The Rust parser and sema mirrors are in `crates/jet-foundation/src/AST/ffi.rs` and `crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Items/external_tests_ffi.rs`.
- #436 exhaustiveness and hostile gates are done.

**Changes**
1. Add Windows x64 and x86 rows to the shared fixture in `tests/cffi_native_matrix.rs`, with pinned `cl.exe` and rustc identities. A missing tool, architecture row, or case fails the job.
2. Add CI jobs for `windows-latest` (x64 and x86 MSVC) in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
3. Fix convention and layout defects in ForeignFunctions.jet and the Rust mirror. Update `Docs/spec/diagnostics.md` if a diagnostic changes.

**Proof**
- On Windows x64 and x86 runners, `cargo test --test cffi_native_matrix` passes with both Windows rows executed.
- `cargo test --test cffi` passes.
- Independent review confirms the #436 gates are unregressed.

**Batch**
`batch-deferred`: e13 cross-platform.

**Dependencies**
Native Windows MSVC runners (external).

cards.title: Cross compilation: target toolchain and sysroot resolution
cards.body: [R-POSTE3-1:#758:0] Split from the former #758 umbrella. This card owns only “Cross compilation: target toolchain and sysroot resolution.” It keeps the ratified decisions, invariants, and production seams linked from #758. The other 3 delivery slices have separate cards.
cards.plan:
## Goal
This is the toolchain and sysroot slice of the #758 cross-compilation umbrella (siblings #1058, #1059, #1060). For a selected target, the host must resolve the real toolchain, standard library, sysroot and linker, and pass them to the Jet driver as HostFacts. Jet owns the list of supported target names. A missing prerequisite fails honestly, with Jet wording that never tells the user to run a rustc or rustup command. No artifact built for the host is ever labeled with a target name.

## Current state
- The Jet side is ported:
  - `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Target/TargetMachine.jet:47` (hosted), `:71` (bare metal), `:464` (`jet_target_machine_for_facts`), `:487`/`:508` (wasm browser/wasi) and `:529` (dossier).
  - `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet:732-761` selects the machine from `HostFacts.target_triple` (E0003 when it is missing or empty). `:760` always passes `no_os: false`.
- On the host side, `Source/CmdCompile.rs:10786-10805` (`validate_target`) calls `Doctor::probe_target_component` (`Source/Doctor.rs:535`) and emits E3302. rustc and rustup text leaks to the user:
  - `Source/Doctor.rs:524` says "run `rustup target add {triple}`".
  - `Doctor.rs:156` and `CmdCompile.rs:14251,14401` say "install Rust from https://rustup.rs".
  - `Source/main.rs:2897` says "or a rustc target triple".
- The target-name list is the Rust const `crates/jet-driver/src/Driver/mod.rs:995` (`TARGET_MACHINE_NAMES`). There is no Jet-owned list.
- `tests/cross.rs` covers freestanding E3301 and OS gating only. There is no toolchain or sysroot check. The old plan's `crates/jet-foundation/src/TargetProfile.rs` does not exist.

## Changes
1. **JetFoundation.** Add `jet_target_supported_names()` in `TargetMachine.jet` as the single list of machine names and triples. Point the host at it and delete the Rust `TARGET_MACHINE_NAMES` duplicate.
2. **JetDriver.** `Pipeline.jet` passes the HostFacts toolchain facts (sysroot, linker, standard-library path) into the target machine and dossier, so provenance records the resolved toolchain.
3. **Host CLI (retained).**
   - `Doctor.rs` and `CmdCompile.rs::validate_target` resolve the sysroot, linker and standard library for the selected triple.
   - Rewrite the E3302 fix text and the E2105 texts in Jet terms. The fix names the Jet-owned remedy (`jet toolchain`, which exists at `main.rs:3691`) or the supported-target list.
   - Register the text in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet` and its Prelude twin.
   - Owner gate: if a new `jet toolchain` verb is needed to install a target library, stop and put it on a ballot; do not ship it unapproved.
4. Update `Docs/spec/architecture.md` where it describes target resolution.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test cross cross_toolchain_resolution`: the new test covers success, a missing standard library, and a bypass that must fail.
- `cargo test --test cross`: existing tests stay green.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/target_std_missing.jet cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots`, if the diagnostic is renderable as a fixture.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-host-cli`: most of the work is in `Source/` CLI and Doctor toolchain resolution. The Jet side is a small registry and driver edit.

## Dependencies
None blocking. #1059 and #1060 build on this slice.

Replaces the Rust-compiler proof: "`cargo test --test cross cross_toolchain_resolution` passes: (a) `jet build --target=<installed foreign triple>` produces an artifact whose file header matches the target (ELF machine / Mach-O / PE / wasm) and whose provenance names the selected target machine; (b) with the target standard library absent (test points the probe at an empty sysroot) the build stops with registered E3302 whose rendered text contains no `rustc`/`rustup` and lists the Jet-supported target names; (c) the check fails if `Compiler/JetDriver` target selection or the `Source/CmdCompile.rs::validate_target` probe is bypassed."
[#1058] C headers, libraries, linker inputs and runtime objects bind to the selected target. Host leakage, ABI mismatch and link failure fail honestly, with no mislabeled host artifact.

[#1059] A typed target profile controls ABI, Core runtime, linker inputs, sysroot, artifacts, debug data and provenance. Unknown or duplicate profiles and missing tools are rejected before codegen. The check fails when JetDriver target validation is bypassed.

[#1060] Every declared native-to-foreign row in tests/cross.rs (Jet-side successor) builds and smoke-runs or validates, and matches native results where applicable. The check fails when JetDriver target selection is bypassed.

From a Linux x86-64 host, `jet build --target=<t> hello.jet` for aarch64-linux, x86_64-macos, aarch64-macos and x86_64-windows produces binaries that run on matching CI runners; each is smaller and builds faster than `deno compile --target <t>` of the JS hello (Jet/Deno < 1.00 for size and for time).

Plain `jet build` in a package whose targets: selects a non-host profile (Examples/embedded/heap_free_core, web.no_os) builds for that target or refuses with a registered diagnostic; it never silently produces a host x86-64 ELF (BallotDesign repro q/bd/probe/fx/target_today: od -N4 .jet/build/run prints 7f 45 4c 46)

## Outcome

**Goal**

cards.plan:
## Goal
Add the MCP client role on the single revisioned Jet protocol core (D-MCP-SURFACE1=A): typed client builders, the request lifecycle, client-side negotiation, bounded failures and redacted audit facts.

## Current state
- The protocol core is ported: Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Mcp/McpProtocol.jet (502 lines) and McpMessages.jet (501, working-tree edits under #3609), listed at sources.list:98-99.
- It provides McpRevision (:29), McpCodec (:75), McpVersionPolicy (:88), McpLimits (:120), McpPolicy (:147), the lifecycle profile and state (:221, :229), McpPeerRole.Client (:263), McpAuditFacts (:367), and McpPeer with `client(policy)` (:392-399). The core carries no transport or authorization code (:5-6).
- Claims are in Jetpack/PackageModel/Tests/McpProtocol.jet (tests.list:17).
- Rust has only a role constructor, crates/jet-pkg-model/src/MCP.rs:861-864,1106-1113, and serves as reference only. #768 (protocol core) is done.

## Changes
1. Add Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Mcp/McpClient.jet:
   - A McpClient builder over McpPeer.client and McpPolicy: stable default, explicit preview opt-in.
   - The initialize, initialized, request/response, shutdown and exit sequence on McpLifecycleState.
   - Typed calls for tools/list and tools/call, resources/list and resources/read, prompts/list and prompts/get, pagination cursors, progress and cancellation (notifications/cancelled).
   - It reuses McpCodec encode and decode and McpLimits, and adds no transport.
2. Failures are version conflict, hostile schema, oversize, timeout, disconnect and cancel. They map to the existing McpNegotiationError, McpLifecycleError and McpCodecError, or to a new McpClientError variant. Every failure is bounded and secret-free, and McpAuditFacts records the role, revision, codec and outcome.
3. Add Jetpack/PackageModel/Tests/McpClient.jet. Drive a client against an in-process McpPeer.server over message values, and cover each failure. Bypassing McpClient must fail the claims.
4. List both files, document the surface in Docs/spec/reference, and register the diagnostics.

## Proof
1. `JETPACK_WORKER=b19mcp Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --area PackageModel --deps-from-head` -> `JETPACK CHECK OK`.
2. The same command with `--tests` -> `JETPACK CHECK OK (check, default run, AOT test)`, with every McpClient claim passing. This is criterion 9's command, spelled with the canonical `Tools/agent/jet-env`.

## Batch
batch-jetpack-mcp.

## Dependencies
#3609 (finishing the MCP core port). #768 is done.

cards.title: jet cc: hermetic C/C++ toolchain front end
cards.body: Zig's adoption wedge: teams adopt the toolchain before the language. Ship jet cc / jet c++ as drop-in C/C++ compiler entry points that behave identically on every machine and cross-compile to every supported target, so CC="jet cc" works in unmodified Makefiles/CMake. Toolchain sourcing strategy (bundle vs store-provisioned vs host wrapper) is owner-gated: D-ADOPT-CC1. Gap G2 in the field audit. Proof: build unmodified upstream C projects (curl/sqlite class) natively and cross-target.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove `jet cc` / `jet c++` as hermetic, flag-compatible C/C++ front ends over the ratified Hangar-provisioned toolchain (D-ADOPT-CC1=B, D-ADOPT-CCSPELL1=A). Unmodified Make/CMake projects must build natively and cross-target, reproducibly, including offline and air-gapped. They must never use a host compiler, a PATH fallback or a test key.

## Current state
- Criterion 1 is verified. The shipped Rust driver is `crates/jetpack/src/CLI/cc.rs` (integrated e9fd8f756), and `tests/cc_cli.rs:4` checks registration.
- The Jet port exists at `Jetpack/CLI/Source/CcDriver/{DriverArguments,DriverInvocation}.jet`, with acquisition in `Jetpack/Provider/Source/Toolchain/{CcToolchainAcquisition,CcToolchainDescriptor,CcToolchainHangar}.jet`. `DriverInvocation.jet:265` uses `NixIndexClient`, which is not yet defined in Jetpack; it is owned by the #3622 NixIndex port.
- The contract is `Docs/spec/reference/cc-driver.md`. The old plan named `Source/CmdCompile.rs`, but the driver lives in the Jetpack CLI, not the compile command.

## Changes
1. Build fixtures under `tests/fixtures/cc/`: an unmodified sqlite amalgamation with its Makefile, and a small CMake C++ project with a dependency file and a response file. No source edits.
2. Add `tests/cc_cli.rs` cases:
   - `cc_builds_unmodified_make_and_cmake_projects_natively_and_cross`: `CC='jet cc' CXX='jet c++'`, native plus one declared cross target, validating artifacts with the target oracle (run natively, `file`/qemu-user for the cross target).
   - `cc_negative_cases_publish_nothing`: a PATH compiler shim, an unsupported target, a corrupt closure member, an ABI/sysroot mismatch, a path escape and a link failure. Each gives an actionable diagnostic and no output file.
   - `cc_offline_and_airgap_bundle_reuse_identical_identities`.
3. Fix defects found by these runs in the Jet CcDriver/Provider first, and mirror them into `cc.rs` only so the shipped binary proves them.
4. Reproducibility: build on two clean machines and compare artifact and descriptor digests and tool identities. Time first use, cached use, offline preload and air-gapped bundle, and document the results in `cc-driver.md`.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test cc_cli` passes all cases above.
- Two-machine digest comparison is recorded (equal).
- Production acquisition goes through the owner-controlled signed index/cache and pinned key (criterion 6). A fixture key cannot satisfy it, and that step runs only once the owner provides the chain.

## Batch
`batch-jetpack-cli`: the driver's canonical home is the Jetpack CLI CcDriver and Provider toolchain.

## Dependencies
Owner-provided signed index/cache chain and a second clean machine, both for criteria 3 and 6 (environment prerequisites). #3622 is needed for the Jet driver to compile, but it does not block the shipped-binary proof.

## Goal

cards.plan:
**Goal**
Close the epoch-12 security gate. The 134-candidate reconciliation is already done. Remaining: a fresh full-repository scan at the integration revision with zero unresolved reportable findings, and the final report plus canonical evidence committed.

**Current state**
- Blockers #1377-#1385 are done; #1386 was folded into #1385. Criteria 1, 2 and 5 are met.
- `Docs/audits/security-closure-2026-09-02.md` records 134 unique dispositions (133 `already-fixed`, 1 duplicate; receipt :237-270). Its fresh-scan gate is `pending-external-gate` (:210-235).
- **The scan procedure is missing.** The gate command (:217-225) calls `scripts/agent/security-scan.mjs` and publishes to `docs/audits/…`. That script was deleted in 2efc938b3 and exists in neither `Tools/agent/` nor anywhere else in the tree.

Tower has no card title for any of the four. Separately, #3697 (P0, ready: "manifest-less scripts can spawn processes: the ambient floor grants the whole Exec root") is an open authority defect that a fresh scan would report.

**Changes**
1. Main maps each of the four 2026-09-01 defects to a done card with file:line evidence, or files one card each.
2. Restore the scan driver from `2efc938b3^:scripts/agent/security-scan.mjs` to `Tools/agent/security-scan.mjs`. Fix its paths (`Tools/agent/jet-env`, `Docs/audits/…`) and commit the procedure next to the report (the 2026-08-19 gate note).
3. Once the defect cards and #3697 are done, run prepare, scan and finalize on a clean checkout at the integration HEAD. Publish to `Docs/audits/security-final-<date>/` and update the report's gate section and receipt.

**Proof**
`Tools/agent/jet-env full node Tools/agent/security-scan.mjs finalize --repo . --request <REQ>/request.json --scan-dir <SCAN> --plugin-dir "$CODEX_SECURITY_PLUGIN_DIR" --publish-dir Docs/audits/security-final-<date>` exits 0. The official validator passes with 0 reportable findings, 0 deferred items and 0 open questions, and the publish directory plus report are committed.

**Batch**
`batch-measure`: an evidence run. The script restore is tooling with no compiler build.

**Dependencies**
#3697, plus the four 2026-09-01 authority defects, each needing a card, and a clean checkout.

cards.title: jetos takeover: reversible in-place adoption from a running Linux host
cards.plan:
## Why

Bedrock Linux's main adoption path installs onto the user's running system (its hijack script). No spare machine, no repartition. Its documented flaw: the conversion is one way — the installer makes the user type "Not reversible!". jetos already owns generations, activation proof, and rollback, so it can offer the same on-ramp reversibly: capture the current install as generation 0, switch only after proof passes, and let `jet os rollback` restore the original system exactly.

Evidence: video mine 2026-08-04 (youtu.be/ENejkGhMTww, Bedrock segment) + bedrocklinux.org FAQ/installation docs. Claim ledger at /tmp/ENejkGhMTww.claims.json (topic: hijack-in-place-install).

## Scope (blocked on D-JOS-TAKEOVER1)

- In: takeover surface per the ratified option; generation-0 capture contract; refusal diagnostics for unsupported layouts; proof gate reuse; rollback-to-host proof.
- Out: fleet rollout; non-Linux hosts; the NixOS config importer (#415 owns migration semantics).

Do not start before the ballot is ratified and the native terminal baseline boots (epoch spine).

## Owned paths and ordered work

- `docs/proposals/jetos/native-jetos.md`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/generations_activation.rs`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/activation_provenance.rs`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/kernel_bootstrap.rs`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/initrd_overlay.rs`
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/vm_proof.rs`
- `tests/jetpack_jetos.rs`

1. After #410's native terminal baseline is available (D-JOS-TAKEOVER1=A is already ratified), trace the existing switch, activation-proof, generation, and rollback paths; do not create a second proof gate.
2. Define the supported disk/layout contract from the ratified option. Capture the managed root, boot entry, closure identity, generation-0 provenance, and mutable-data policy; refuse layouts that cannot retain two bootable roots before any mutation.
3. Implement `jet os takeover` through the existing generation and activation models. Switch only after the same activation proof as `jet os switch` succeeds; preserve byte identity for managed and declared immutable paths.
4. Add VM proofs for supported capture/switch/rollback and unsupported-layout refusal with a registered diagnostic and pre-mutation snapshot. Keep fleet, non-Linux, and NixOS importer scope out.
5. Move the `/tmp/ENejkGhMTww.claims.json` evidence pointer to a committed `docs/research/` path before completion; retain the source URLs and claim boundaries.

## Proof

Use the existing activation-proof and VM proof mechanisms. The supported VM must capture generation 0, switch, and restore it byte-identically under the declared mutable-data policy; the unsupported VM must refuse before mutation. A targeted check must fail if the shared activation-proof path is bypassed.

cards.title: jetos provenance query: file, command, and process to package, universe, and generation
cards.plan:
## Authority and dependency gate

D-JOS-PROVENANCE1=A is ratified: extend `jet info` rather than create a new public command. The old “blocked on D-JOS-PROVENANCE1” wording is stale. Implementation remains gated by #969, which owns the configuration-side provenance contender. Keep trust/signature provenance with #950/#958 and do not absorb those cards.

## Owned paths

- `docs/proposals/jetos/native-jetos.md`, `docs/proposals/jetos/jetos-studio.md`
- `Source/main.rs` and `Source/CmdInspect.rs` (existing `info`/inspection dispatch)
- `crates/jetpack/src/CLI/update_search_info.rs` (package-info seam)
- `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/activation_provenance.rs` and `crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/studio_projection.rs`
- `tests/jetpack_jetos.rs` (native/imported/PID/unowned proof)
- `docs/research/file-process-provenance-query.claims.json` (committed claim ledger)

## Ordered implementation

1. Wait for #969 and consume its typed option/provenance boundary; apply ratified D-JOS-PROVENANCE1=A without reopening a ballot or adding a second resolver.
2. Trace one resolver from artifact to package to universe (native hangar or imported Nix closure) to generation to declaring option. Accept file, command, and `--pid` targets, preserve exact identity, and return an honest unowned result for user/runtime-created artifacts.
3. Route the existing `jet info` dispatch and the existing inspection/package seams through that resolver. Studio must consume the same result via `studio_projection.rs`; keep JetOS source canonical and make human and structured output derive from one fact model.
4. Cut over all direct callers found by the trace, remove obsolete parallel provenance lookup, and preserve the out-of-scope #950/#958 trust/signature ownership.
5. Add focused tests for native and imported-closure package paths, command/file/PID targets, unowned artifacts, and the Studio projection. Move the research claims from the temporary ledger to the committed claims file before close.

## Acceptance and proof

After #969 and implementation, use the real `jet info`/inspection and Studio production paths. Receipts must show one identical resolver answer for native, imported, PID, and unowned cases, with package/universe/generation/declaring-option identity and the ratified public surface. Targeted tests must fail if either command or Studio bypasses the resolver; no `/tmp`-only claim ledger or canned projection counts. This preparation does not claim runtime proof.

## Dependencies and non-goals

#969 is the board dependency. #950/#958 remain separate trust/signature provenance owners. Do not invent a new command, duplicate config provenance, or infer ownership when the resolver cannot establish it.

### Canonical ownership handoff — #3398

Use #323/#470 for option facts and #1424 for provenance. Keep activation, live-switch, CAS, UI and foreign-evaluation authority separate; preserve #410’s full no-nix native pipeline.

cards.title: JetOS install trust: safety without App Store gatekeeping
cards.body:

cards.title: tests/jetpack_jetos writes 24G into /tmp and trips the memory guard
cards.body: The tests/jetpack_jetos suite writes about 24G of scratch into /tmp. On this machine /tmp is RAM-backed tmpfs, so the suite fills swap and trips the critical-memory block in scripts/agent/tmp-guard.sh. This is the exact OOM failure mode AGENTS.md warns agents about, caused by the test suite itself, and it blocks full-suite runs.
cards.plan:
## Authority and current state
Planning is complete for card #1638. The historical ~24 GiB `/tmp` report is the trigger, not current proof: `tests/jetpack_jetos.rs:99-109` now verifies a disk-backed `Scratch`, and the heavy cases remain explicitly ignored at `:111-112`. Preserve criterion 1's verified status and exact evidence. Leave criteria 2-4 open. This card owns only jetpack_jetos scratch safety, fixture size, and bounded measurement; #956 remains the single epoch-wide full-suite evidence owner.

## Current scratch and cleanup paths
`tests/common/mod.rs::test_scratch_root` uses `JET_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR` when set, otherwise the gitignored repository path `.tmp/jet-test-scratch`; it rejects paths on the system temp filesystem. `Scratch::new` creates `scratch/jet-it-<tag>-<pid>-<stamp>-<thread>` below that root. `Scratch::Drop` makes realized trees writable and removes only its case directory. `tests/support/jetpack_fixtures.rs::neutral_command` uses `jetpack-command-tmp` and sets child `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, and `TEMP` to its disk root. `scripts/agent/jet-env` rejects `/tmp` for target and scratch variables. `scripts/agent/tmp-guard.sh` keeps the 70% cleanup, 85% critical, under-3-GiB/swap critical, and exit-2 thresholds unchanged. The 10 GiB default `JET_TEST_ALLOC_CAP_GB` in `tests/common/mod.rs` guards live allocations; it is not cumulative scratch bytes and must not be raised.

## Future implementation and bounded measurement
Begin only when the owner opens the jetos epoch and the integrated tree is ready.
1. Inventory every `tests/jetpack_jetos.rs` case and its fixture helpers, including os-import and image paths, for direct `temp_dir`, `/tmp`, or whole-store materialization. If an escape remains, route it through the existing `Scratch`/`test_scratch_root` mechanism. If the inventory is clean, do not rewrite the verified path.
2. For any materialized whole-store fixture, measure each case separately and reduce it to the smallest semantic fixture that preserves the existing assertions. Keep the ignore gate until the bounded run proves the reduced fixture; do not hide a large allocation or change the product contract.
3. Allocate one dedicated disk root per run, such as `$HOME/.cache/jet-test-scratch/card-1638/<run-id>`, and set `JET_TEST_SCRATCH_DIR`, `TMPDIR`, `TMP`, and `TEMP` to it. Predeclare and record a disk-scratch ceiling no greater than the current 10 GiB allocation-guard default, or use a stricter owner-approved value; never raise `JET_TEST_ALLOC_CAP_GB` or any `tmp-guard` threshold. A sidecar records timestamped `du -sb` samples for the run root and aborts before the ceiling. If a ceiling is not owner-approved, leave criterion 2 open rather than inventing one.
4. With the guard active, run the complete ignored jetos test binary once using `scripts/agent/jet-env full cargo test --test jetpack_jetos -- --ignored --test-threads=1`. Record the exact command, tree identity, peak and final scratch bytes, ceiling, exit status, and sidecar output. A cap breach is a safe failure, not a passing receipt.
5. Prove criterion 3 from the same clean run with the unchanged `scripts/agent/tmp-guard.sh`; retain its exit/output and show that no `/tmp` pressure trip occurred.
6. Prove criterion 4 separately from a clean root with the exact `cargo test --test jetpack_jetos` command. Close criteria 2-4 only from fresh receipts; do not mark them from the current default ignore-gate observation.
7. Copy receipts to the owned `$HOME/.cache/jet-luna` evidence area before removing only the run-specific disk root. Keep per-case `Scratch::Drop` cleanup and never clean broad `/tmp` paths from this card.

## Cutover and handoff
No new scratch API, allocator exception, or memory-guard waiver is in scope. Preserve the owner deferment, the default ignore gate, the verified disk-path criterion, and #956's composed epoch-proof ownership. Preparation claims no implementation, full-suite run, or criterion closure.

cards.title: wasm32-wasip2 as a full supported server target (D-WASISRV1=A)
cards.body:
The WASM-on-backend argument treats server-side wasm as the deployment unit; its comments dispute that containers already won. E3302 refuses the triple today and the CryptoEntropy prelude carries wasi shims. 

STATE CORRECTION 2026-08-19: D-WASISRV1 is RATIFIED =A. This is an implementation card for the ratified outcome; no ballot wait remains.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Finish D-WASISRV1=A: `jet build Examples/features/net/http_server_wasip2.jet --target=wasm32-wasip2` produces a component that wasmtime runs, and the server binds, listens and answers a request.

## Current state
- Met: target support (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Target/TargetMachine.jet:467,508-512`), the stdlib surface and teaching diagnostics (`tests/ui/wasip2_unsupported_*_e3304/e3305.jet`), the CI lane and E3302 retirement. Criterion 9 is also met: D-WASISRV1=A is recorded at `Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7296-7300`.
- Gap (card log 2026-09-15): the generated Rust passes `JetOutcome<T, JetAbsent>` values for the optional TLS/deadline parameters of `jet_http_server_bind(addr, mux, tls: Option<..>, deadline: Option<..>)` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/HTTPServer.rs:1916-1929`). MIR `Option` emits as `JetOutcome<_, JetAbsent>` (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Types.jet:69`), while `jet_rust_emit_core_operation` (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Operations.jet:1508-1560`) forwards arguments unprojected. The route row allows arity 2..4 (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:1799`), so omitted trailing optionals also need an explicit `None`.
- The example exists at `Examples/features/net/http_server_wasip2.jet:1-12`. No test builds it or serves it under wasmtime.

## Changes
1. `Emit/Operations.jet` (`jet_rust_emit_call_arguments` path for Core routes): project every `Option`-typed argument into the host `Option` carrier (`.ok()`), and emit `None` for omitted trailing optional parameters up to `max_arity`. Apply this to every Core route with optional parameters, not only this one.
2. Keep HTTPServer.rs and the wasi-sockets adapter as the host leaf. No signature change.
3. Add `tests/wasip2_http_server.rs::wasip2_http_server_serves_under_wasmtime`. It builds the example for wasm32-wasip2, runs `wasmtime run -S inherit-network`, requests `/` and asserts `hello from wasip2` plus the `true` address line. When wasmtime is absent the test fails loudly (a named missing tool), never passes silently.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test wasip2_http_server -- wasip2_http_server_serves_under_wasmtime` passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=net/http_server Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes natively, so the native bind with omitted optionals is unchanged.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: the fix is in the self-hosted Rust emitter (JetCodegen Emit).

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Publish the Jet trust root at a stable address so signatures have an anchor
cards.body:
Owner acquired `jet-lang.dev` 2026-08-25. This card makes signing possible later without doing the key ceremony now.

WHY THIS IS THE FIRST DOMAIN CARD: card #2157 deferred official signed publication partly because there was nowhere to publish. A signature is only worth something if a verifier can independently obtain the public key from a place the project controls. Owning a domain supplies that place.

MEASURED TODAY: the only working catalog is signed by a hardcoded test key `jet-test-index-v1` whose seed is 32 bytes of the value 7 (`target-nixfeed/sign-test.mjs`). Anyone can forge it. Card #2157 requires deleting it rather than promoting it.

WHAT TO BUILD: a documented, stable location under the owned domain that serves the Jet public signing key or keys, in a form the client already understands (`trust/nix-index-v1.ed25519.pub` is the current shape read by `IndexClient::from_roots_with_mode` in `crates/jetpack/src/NixIndex.rs`). Include key id, algorithm and validity, and a documented rotation story even if rotation is manual at first.

EXPLICITLY NOT THIS CARD: generating production key material, choosing custody, or signing a real catalog. Those stay owner-gated on #2157. This card only establishes the address and the format so the later ceremony has somewhere to land.

TRAP: fetching a key over HTTPS is not the same as trusting it. The client must pin or verify the key it already has rather than accepting whatever the host returns. A trust root served over a network is only an anchor if the client refuses substitutions.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Establish the stable public trust-root address and client format, and prove that the client pins its local key and refuses substitutes. This card creates no production key material and performs no ceremony.

## Current state
- Criterion 1 is verified: `Docs/site/dist/keys/README.md:9-22` fixes `https://keys.jet-lang.dev/nix-index-v1.ed25519.pub`, the one-line `key-id:base64-public-key` format, validity via `issued_unix`/`expires_unix`, and the pin path `<JETPACK_ROOT>/trust/nix-index-v1.ed25519.pub`. `trust-manifest.json` is `awaiting-key-ceremony`.
- Rotation is written up in `README.md:45-48` and `Docs/spec/packaging/trust-root.md` (criterion 4).
- Client refusals already exist in `crates/jetpack/src/NixIndex.rs`: test-key rejection `:32,3563-3598` and `nix_index_refuses_a_server_signature_from_a_substituted_key` `:3832`.
- Publication tests exist in `tests/jetpack_trust_root.rs`: `trust_publication_contract_is_owned_pending_and_has_no_fake_root` :21 and `trust_publication_exporter_rejects_the_test_index_key` :50. The exporter file names are at `TrustRoot.rs:1527-1529`.
- Missing: a test that stages a key with `Tools/jetpack-infra/stage-trust-root.sh` and has the existing client read that exact file and verify a signed index (criterion 2).
- The Jet `NixIndexClient` referenced at `Jetpack/CLI/Source/CcDriver/DriverInvocation.jet:265` is undefined; its port is #3622 and is not required here. #2157 is done.

## Changes
1. `tests/jetpack_trust_root.rs`: add `staged_index_key_file_is_read_by_the_pinned_client`. Generate an ephemeral Ed25519 key under `~/.cache/jet-test-scratch`, stage it with `stage-trust-root.sh --index-key`, copy the staged `nix-index-v1.ed25519.pub` to the pin path, then have `IndexClient::from_roots_with_mode` verify a fixture-signed manifest. A host-served different key must be refused.
2. Keep the test key rejected, and do not promote `jet-test-index-v1`.
3. After the DNS, TLS and hosting gates, publish the static files (criterion 6, owner-gated).

cards.title: Named results for task.all (Await-Dictionary / Promise.allKeyed analog)
cards.body: Video mine 2026-08-28. ES2027 track: Await Dictionary (Promise.allKeyed, Stage 3) exists because positional Promise.all results get mis-ordered as call sites grow; the video audience explicitly welcomed the keyed form. Jet live state: task.all {double(1), double(2), double(3)} works positionally (prints 2 4 6); the named spelling task.all {first: f(), second: g(), third: h()} is a parse error E0003 'expected , between task branches, found :'. Whether Jet gets named concurrent results — and how they are spelled — is a syntax choice, so it is owner-gated. Ballot attached.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-CONC-ALLNAMED1=A at runtime. `task.all {first: f(), second: g()}` returns an anonymous record whose fields hold each branch's result. Positional `task.all {…}` keeps its ordering and failure behavior on every tier.

## Current state
- Criteria 1-4 and 6 are met. That covers Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions, grammars, snapshots, and the mixed-form diagnostic at `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/DiagnosticRows.jet:14988-14992`.
- The checker is done: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/TaskGroups.jet:600-613` types a named tuple of Tasks as `Type.Tuple` of their success types.
- Codegen routes it: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet:4590-4619`. `jet_codegen_task_group_result_tasks` accepts `.Tuple`, and `jet_codegen_lower_task_group_value` emits `jet_std::jet_task_all_result` with one operand. `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Evaluator.jet:7952-8013` validates the same route but only assembles positional lists.
- Runtime is wrong. `Examples/features/concurrency/task_all.jet:11-12` printed 0/0/0 on 2026-09-15; the golden `Examples/features/expected/concurrency/task_all.out` is `10`/`20`/`30`.
- The Rust fix commit 39b9ffd41 ("Support named task.all results across tiers") is not an ancestor of HEAD. It touches `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs`, `MIRRust.rs`, `MIRWeb.rs` and `Prelude/Scheduler.rs` (+152/-24).

## Changes
1. **Jet compiler first.** In `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet` (`jet_codegen_lower_task_group_value`), when `tasks.ty` is a named tuple, carry the field names and order to the join. The joined value is then built as the record type (`expression.ty`), not a list.
2. **Both Jet emitters.** In `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/*.jet` (Rust text) and `Emit/Web`, assemble the record from the scheduler's joined ids.
3. **Jet evaluator.** In `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Evaluator.jet` (`jet_eval_task_group_exchange`), build the named record for a tuple operand.
4. **Retained host and shipped-binary mirror.** Cherry-pick 39b9ffd41. Its `Prelude/Scheduler.rs` join is the retained host piece, and the MIREval/MIRRust/MIRWeb edits are the mirror the shipped binary needs to prove the fix. Resolve any conflicts against current HEAD.
5. Leave positional behavior untouched.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden concurrency/task_all`: pass.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden concurrency/task_all`: O0, O1 and O2 match the golden.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden concurrency/task_group`: positional goldens unchanged.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.
- Web: `Tools/agent/jet-env jet build --target=web Examples/features/concurrency/task_all.jet`, run the emitted module under the existing web harness (node), and confirm stdout matches the golden.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-back`: the change lives in lowering, the emitters and the evaluator.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Automatic build optimization: one graph, hidden units, one store
cards.body:
Epic for docs/proposals/automatic-build-optimization.md (2026-09-01).

ACTUAL: jet build runs the whole front end every time, emits one Rust crate per program with dependencies flattened in, runs one rustc, and pays thin LTO over the runtime at every link. Eleven reuse mechanisms coexist with separate keys, stores, and failure rules. Measured 2026-09-01 (debug compiler; rustc/link phases unaffected): nbody edit 2.95s vs cargo release edit 0.55s; 3349-line program spends 29s in link on a no-change build; cold builds pay 17-21s compiling the runtime rlib; receipts never replay.

EXPECTED: one content-addressed action graph in one machine-wide store; hidden compile units inside each package; per-unit bitcode with a persistent ThinLTO cache; persisted memoized module checks; Cranelift fast lens wired; sealed dependency unit sets; prebuilt runtime objects; live board + explain-build --html; matched Cargo benchmark with a strict win gate against out-of-box and tuned Cargo.

A failure cancels only its dependents, and keep-going continues the rest.

cards.title: jet dev live-reload latency loses to Vite, Bun, and nodemon
cards.body: Fresh gauntlet live_reload axis (2026-09-02, `gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --axis live_reload`, 6/6 samples per runner) measured median edit-to-result latency: jet dev cold/warm 288.96/297.22 ms; Vite 21.69/0.92 ms; Bun 42.75/43.43 ms; nodemon 82.81/64.78 ms; entr+cc 470.25/472.13 ms. Jet wins only against entr+cc. Under the competitive performance gate every non-Rust peer requires Jet/peer < 1.00, so this axis is a loss on three cells and blocks #2272 criterion 3 and the #2268 campaign.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Make `jet dev` edit-to-result latency strictly beat Vite, Bun and nodemon (Jet/peer < 1.00) on the gauntlet `live_reload` axis, cold and warm. Reload semantics must not change (I9): output after a reload is byte-identical to a fresh `jet run` of the edited source on every engine.

## Current state
- Measurements:
  - 2026-09-02: jet dev cold/warm 288.96/297.22 ms, Vite 21.69/0.92, Bun 42.75/43.43, nodemon 82.81/64.78, entr+cc 470.25/472.13.
  - 2026-09-03: Jet 215 ms both.
  - Jet wins only against entr+cc, so this axis blocks #2272 criterion 3 and the #2268 campaign.
- Criterion 2 (semantics unchanged) is met. The watch-loop fix 532775b7e ("fix(dev): wait for web file changes") is in HEAD.
- The retained host pieces exist: `Source/CmdDevTools.rs` (`run_dev_inner`), `crates/jet-jit/src/Watcher.rs`, and `crates/jet-jit/src/lib.rs:361-364` (`RESIDENT_MODULE`, `RESIDENT_RUNTIME`, reuse counter).
- Warm front-end reuse exists only in the archived `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/HotSwap.rs` and the `crates/jet-driver` incremental check. `Compiler/JetDriver` and `Compiler/JetSema` have no resident-bundle or incremental reuse. The only D-HOTSWAP1 mention in Compiler/ is `DiagnosticRows.jet:13021`.
- Harness: `Tools/gauntlet/harness/live-reload.mjs`, `run.mjs` and `status.mjs` (stale `gauntlet/` and `scripts/agent` paths are fixed here).

## Changes
1. **Attribute first.** Run `jet dev` on the axis program with `JET_TRACE_TIERS_PATH` and the dev trace. Split the latency into watch debounce, front end (lex/parse/sema), lowering, JIT re-lower, swap/restart, and first output. Record the split on this card.
2. **Host (retained, shipped path).**
   - `Watcher.rs`: no fixed wait beyond the coalescing window (target < 5 ms), using a content digest shared with #2504 slice 1.
   - `lib.rs`: re-lower only the changed functions into `RESIDENT_MODULE`.
   - The restart path must not rebuild the heap from scratch.
3. **Front-end reuse, Jet compiler first.** `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Pipeline.jet` keeps the resident checked bundle and re-checks only the changed module. `Compiler/JetSema` computes the D-HOTSWAP1 type-surface comparison that chooses swap or restart.
   - Mirror it in the shipped Rust driver, the existing `HotSwap.rs` and incremental path, until #218 makes the Jet driver the shipped front end. Delete those Rust files then, not before, because the measurement uses the shipped binary.
4. Non-goals: no change to the swap-versus-restart law (#2504 owns it), no harness change, and no edits to the live_reload axis programs.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev --test dev_latency --test dev_default_parity --test dev_tier_parity --test dev_interp_parity`: green.
- Measurement: `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --axis live_reload` then `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/status.mjs --merge Tools/gauntlet/results`. All three live_reload cells (Vite, Bun, nodemon) show Jet warm and cold medians with Jet/peer < 1.00 and verdict `win`.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-host-cli`: the latency is won or lost in the `jet dev` host (watcher, resident JIT, dev command), and the proof is a CLI measurement run.

## Dependencies
None blocking. #2504 is related (the shared content digest and the hot-swap default).

Evidence: Source/CmdCompile.rs:10903-11010 — jet dev's web loop waits through the WatchSession polling boundary, so this is a dev-tool/watch path rather than a Compiler/ language pass. ; crates/jet-devserver/src/WatchService.rs:1527-1530,2131-2135 — the watcher uses a 5 ms poll interval and an explicit coalescing window, which are the latency-sensitive implementation seams. ; Source/CmdDevTools.rs:1334-1336 — the dev tooling also waits on WatchSession changes rather than performing compiler policy itself.

cards.body:
Owner clarification, 2026-09-14: hide all expert columns from the main Gauntlet chart for now. The visible languages are Rust, C, Zig, Go, Python, and JS. Keep recorded expert evidence unchanged; this is not a claim that expert benchmarks passed.

Owner direction, 2026-09-14: compare Jet ahead-of-time (AOT) results with Rust, C, Zig, and Go. Compare both `jet run` and `jet dev` with Python and JavaScript (JS). The owner selected "Apply the split throughout" for first-result and edit-to-result latency.

The main chart has one JavaScript language column and no separate Node language column. Node is a runtime, not another language. Keep the runtime and tool versions as measurement metadata. Migrate current Node language rows into the canonical JS comparison without losing workload coverage or counting JavaScript twice.

Keep Node, Bun, and Vite as separate web-development workflow comparisons against `jet dev`. Use the existing live_reload axis. Its Node workflow currently uses nodemon; disclose that watcher and its version. Vite is a development tool, not a language or a separate JavaScript engine. These web-development comparisons remain required, not advisory.

The peer groups define required performance comparisons, not just display filters. Apply them to runtime, startup, first-result, edit-to-result, and other applicable execution measurements. Keep cold start, warm start, and steady-state measurements distinct. Comparisons outside these groups remain visible as non-blocking evidence. Competitive O0 performance against O2 remains a long-term goal, not a current closure condition or a claim of physical impossibility.

cards.title: Text pipelines: per-use literal String allocation, owned split results and redundant clones
cards.body:
Generated Rust for line-oriented corpus entries (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json), 'jet emit --rust') shows general codegen costs on every line of input:

- string literal arguments allocate on each use ('" ".to_string()' three times per line in logreport; '"".to_string()' for an equality test)
- 'jet_unicode_split_once' returns owned (before, after) Strings, then the emitter '.clone()'s the fields again (14 clones in logreport's loop)
- every user function call pays 'jet_stack_enter(...)' plus a JetOutcome wrapper even when infallible (bump() per line)
- map lookups clone the key twice ('get(&key.clone()).cloned()')
- datasummary: group_by/sort_by_compare clone each record (8 clones), float ordering through a comparator host

Measured AOT losses: logreport 4.0x Rust, 4.2x Python, 7.1x Zig, 6.3x Node, 2.8x Go (109 ms vs 27 ms); text-script 1.23x Rust; datasummary 11.7x Rust; taskfile-cli 1.13x Rust (2026-09-01 partial run, before its AOT ICE). These are the text.report-cli, text.script, numerics.script, numerics.notebook, cli.app and formats.json-app cells.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Remove the general per-line costs from AOT text pipelines: literal `String` allocation on each use, owned split results that get cloned again, doubled map-key clones, cloned records in group_by/sort, and stack frames on infallible calls. Output bytes, diagnostics and tier behavior stay the same. This is one emitter and ownership path, not a fast path per corpus entry, and it adds no public API.

## Current state
- Measured AOT losses (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl): logreport 4.0x Rust (109 ms vs 27 ms), 4.2x Python, 7.1x Zig, 6.3x Node, 2.8x Go; text-script 1.23x Rust; datasummary 11.7x Rust; taskfile-cli 1.13x Rust. These are the text.report-cli, text.script, numerics.script, numerics.notebook, cli.app and formats.json-app cells.
- The Jet Rust printer turns every MIR String constant into an owned String: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Types.jet:1344` (`.String(value) -> "{quote}.to_string()"`) and the const-key path at `:1389`.
- Split routes through `jet_unicode_split_once` with owned arguments: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet:522`. The Prelude already borrows its inputs: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/UnicodeString.rs:131` takes `(&str, &str)` and returns owned `(String, String)`.
- The shipped Rust printer already skips the stack frame for infallible functions in release. `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:12064-12099` wraps `jet_stack_enter` in `#[cfg(not(jet_release))]` unless the function is fallible, unsafe or policy-scoped. The Jet printer (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Functions.jet:429`) emits only sentry and deadline scopes.
- The split-literal borrow fix from 2026-09-21 (ebe828003) exists only in the archived MIRRust.rs.

## Changes
1. Jet lowering (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/{Expressions,BuiltinMethods,Statements,Functions}.jet`): when the checked ownership and escape facts prove a value does not escape, pass literal arguments, split results, map keys and group_by/sort records as borrowed MIR operands (`MirAccess.Read` place or const). Values that escape stay owned.
2. Jet printer (`Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/{Types,Operations,Values}.jet`):
   - Print a borrowed String constant as a `&str` literal where the Prelude parameter is `&str`.
   - Stop re-cloning split-result fields.
   - Print map `get` with one borrowed key.
   - Port the ebe828003 split-literal rule.
3. Jet printer (`Emit/Functions.jet`): match the MIRRust.rs:12065 rule. The default profile gets no frame for `MirFailureCarrier.Infallible` functions without unsafe or policy scopes. Debug and hardened profiles keep the frame.
4. Rust mirror, so the shipped binary proves the change: apply the same borrow rules in `MIRRust.rs`. Change Prelude signatures in `Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Text.rs` and `Prelude/Core/Collections.rs` only where the checked ABI already allows a borrow. Add no second text representation.
5. Add a witness `line_parsing_witness_borrows_literals_and_split_results` in `tests/tir_collections_and_methods.rs`. It covers literal args, split_once, map lookup, group_by and sort. It asserts on the emitted Rust and calls `assert_tiers_agree`.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test tir_collections_and_methods -- line_parsing_witness`: passes. The loop body has no `" ".to_string()`, no `.clone()` of split fields, and no `get(&key.clone())`. O0, O1 and O2 output are identical.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden text/` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=strings/ ...`: no golden changes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: no new errors in the touched JetCodegen files compared with the pre-change receipt.
- Measurement (batch-measure pass): run `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry X` for logreport, text-script, datasummary and taskfile-cli. Jet/peer must be < 1.00 for every peer, Rust included, on every metric, and Jet/ceiling <= 1.00 against the asm-parity reference. Record each loss separately.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: this is Jet lowering and printer work, with the MIRRust.rs mirror landing in the same build.

## Dependencies
None blocking. The ownership facts are already checked by sema.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT); the Rust-free toolchain (Jet suites and tests/cases rows replace cargo tests and .rs sources); the AGENTS.md Performance gate (Jet/peer < 1.00 with no Rust band, then the asm-parity ceiling).

AsmPar-1 measured logreport on dev bb770de593 + AsmPar-38..42: 3,720M → 2,976M instructions; w10 370.6M → 252.9M.
- The remaining allocator cost is structural: 6 rt_text_slice copies per line (split_once ×3, 2 parts each). Each copy is a 24-byte header plus a separate data buffer, so 12 allocs and 12 frees per line, about 800 of the ~9.9k instructions per line.
- Removing it needs a text representation change: either inline small text, with header and data in one block (15+ runtime files read text +16 and its cap directly), or borrowed text views as on this card.
- Deferred past the 2026-11-01 deadline.

AsmPar-1, 2026-11-01: split_once views were parked. A view header with cap 0 reads as an immortal literal, so jet_rt_string_clone returns the same pointer and a clone of a view would alias a dead frame. logreport hands the halves straight to user calls that clone them (bump does counts[key] =), and at IR build time nothing proves a callee never clones, so a conservative rule declines every use. A sound design needs either an interprocedural 'param never owned' fact or a runtime borrowed-header class that clone copies. In the post-fix logreport profile, split_once costs 15.7% (2 rt_text_copy plus 2 alloc/free per call, 3 calls per line).

Distill 2026-10-05 (youtube 7_o-YRxf_cc): a string literal lives in the binary and a borrowed view of it costs no allocation. This card's per-use literal String allocation is the cost the explainer says should be zero; keep 'literal reads allocate nothing' as an acceptance row.

Phase 0 triage 2026-09-28 (perfconc1a, Opus 5.5): C_RETARGET. The text-pipeline AOT losses are still open. The plan points at archived crates/jet-codegen TIR lower/*.rs. The self-hosted Rust printer still renders every String literal as "..".to_string(); split/map-key/record clones need Jet-side ownership facts. Evidence: Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Types.jet:1344,1389 (MIR String constants print as .to_string()); log 2026-09-21 ebe828003 (split literal borrow fixed only in archived MIRRust.rs); crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:11964-11983 (archived stack-frame emission)

Triage 2026-09-28 (Luna 5.6 high legwork, Pip reviewed): RETARGET_JET. The reported allocation and stack-frame mechanisms are still visible in the Rust AOT emitter/Prelude, but owner direction makes compiler policy work belong in Compiler/. The Jet emitter surface exists, while exact generated-shape and peer proof are unverified. Evidence: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIRRust.rs:11964-11983 — the Rust emitter still emits jet_stack_enter frames around generated calls, including the infallible path concern named by the card. ; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:1905-1923 — the split iterator owns a source String and separator state. ; crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:1985-2012 — split creates owned source/separator state and each synchronous piece is converted with to_string, so the card's allocation mechanism remains represented in the archived Rust path. Jet target: Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Emit/Functions.jet, Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Expressions.jet, Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet, Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Statements.jet.

Integrated ebe828003: builtin String.split/rsplit now pass pure literal receiver/separator values as &str through the existing literal helper; variable values retain borrowed references, and owned JetIter/String output semantics remain unchanged. Only MIRRust.rs and Prelude/Core/Collections.rs changed. Worker and integrated jet-codegen lane checks returned CHECK OK; text corpus/per-peer performance proof remains deferred, so criteria stay open.

Static source trace found String.split/rsplit built-in emission bypasses the existing literal-string fast path: MIRRust prelude_values_with_receiver materializes literal receiver/separator Strings, while Prelude split takes &String and clones the source into a boxed iterator. A bounded worker will remove only the literal-call allocation by using the existing literal helper and an &str-compatible split seam; owned split results and iterator allocation remain open.

Campaign triage: integrated borrowed map-key/literal/split/frame repairs have no focused tier and matched gauntlet receipt yet. All four strict criteria remain open; no speculative emitter cycle or unmeasured performance claim made.

Integrated source lane now reuses borrowed string-key map update and retains prior literal/split/frame hot-path repairs. Focused tier and matched gauntlet proof remain pending; no performance win claimed.

Preparation complete: source-grounded plan, references and observable criteria. No dependency or owner gate is open. The existing plan has a real performance and ownership design, but its TIR/emit paths are stale; current code is under Codegen/TIR/lower and Prelude/Core. DOCS ONLY; no implementation or product proof.
Prep: plan refreshed as five general emitter slices with an emit-shape witness test first.

criteria.text: The canonical paired O2 cells for logreport, text-script, datasummary, and taskfile-cli record Jet versus the plain implementation and every required peer; Jet/peer is below 1.00 for every required peer and metric, Rust included, and Jet/ceiling is at most 1.00 against the asm-parity reference, with losses kept open.
Emitted code for a line-parsing witness has no per-line String allocation for literals, no double clone of split results, and no stack-frame call on infallible functions in the default profile.
Every changed shape keeps byte-identical output on O0, O1 and O2; existing goldens unchanged
Debug and hardened profiles retain their existing stack sentry, failure carrier, panic text, and diagnostics, while the default profile removes a frame only when checked infallibility proves it safe.
[#2866] csvtransform O2 Jet/{Rust,Go,Zig,Python,Node} < 1.00. The Decimal parse/add/format micro witness is at least 5x faster with byte-identical output and Decimal goldens unchanged.
[#2871] embedded-data and binparse O2 Jet/{Rust,C,Zig,Python,Node} < 1.00. The fixed-width take_pattern loop and byte checksum loop are each faster than Rust (Jet/Rust < 1.00).
[#2872] embedded-sensor-ring O2 Jet/{Rust,C,Zig} < 1.00. The integer mod/div micro witness is faster than Rust (Jet/Rust < 1.00). Bigint promotion and checked-arithmetic tests are unchanged.

[#2890] The elementwise `c[i] = a[i] + b[i]` loop over N=20M on AOT release has a median < 0.1 s, RSS < 500 MiB and no list clone in the loop. N=20k runs in < 2 s and N=200k in < 20 s on O0. L2510 no longer fires on that shape, or its Fix names a user edit. Bare, shared, write, copy, nested, out-of-range and non-place cases keep ownership, alias, order, bounds, cleanup and error-location semantics.

[#3560] A dead `String.from_bytes(token)` binding followed by a map increment uses the borrowed-byte map-update helper (optimizer transform), keeping UTF-8 validation, ordering and fallback. cards.title: HTTP substrate after #2255: http-service p50 3.2x Go, concurrency-service loses to Node, http-client 1.25x Rust, run-tier probes time out
cards.body:
Fresh matched cells on gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl (full matrix, release compiler, gauntlet/results/2026-09-03.json) for the shared HTTP serving and client substrate:

- http-service (netserv.service) AOT p50: Jet/Go 3.19x, Jet/Node 1.90x, Jet/Rust 1.58x, Jet/Python 1.09x; p99: Jet/Go 92.9x, Jet/Node 1.38x, Jet/Rust 1.24x. Run and dev tiers failed probe 2 (PUT /kv) with an HTTP probe timeout while the AOT tier passed every probe.
- concurrency-service (concurrency.service) AOT p50: 8.5 ms vs Node 8.05 ms (1.06x); wins Go 0.93x, Rust 0.94x, Python 0.90x. Startup on run/dev: 1.03-1.10x Go and Node.
- http-client (netserv.client) AOT wall: 1.25x Rust; wins Go 0.63x, Python 0.04x, Node 0.02x.

#2255 closed on its implementation evidence; these are the cells that remain red.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Turn the remaining red HTTP-substrate cells green after #2255, and first fix the run/dev-tier probe hang (I9).

**Measured baseline** (gauntlet run 20260902-1649436-mtkr9fvl, release compiler)
- http-service (netserv.service) AOT:
  - p50: Jet/Go 3.19x, Jet/Node 1.90x, Jet/Rust 1.58x, Jet/Python 1.09x.
  - p99: Jet/Go 92.9x, Jet/Node 1.38x, Jet/Rust 1.24x.
  - The run and dev tiers fail probe 2 (PUT /kv) with an HTTP probe timeout. AOT passes every probe.
- concurrency-service AOT:
  - p50 8.5 ms vs Node 8.05 ms (1.06x). It wins against Go 0.93x, Rust 0.94x and Python 0.90x.
  - Startup on run/dev is 1.03-1.10x Go and Node.
- http-client AOT wall: 1.25x Rust. It wins against Go 0.63x, Python 0.04x and Node 0.02x.
- Targets: Jet/{Rust,Go,Node,Python} < 1.00 on every listed cell and tier, and Jet/ceiling <= 1.00 against the asm-parity reference.

**Current state**
- Server: `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/{HTTPServer.rs,HTTPMessage.rs,HTTPRoute.rs}`. Client: `HTTPClient.rs`, `NetHTTP.rs`. `Core/http/server.jet` delegates to the native provider.
- JIT marshalling: `crates/jet-jit/src/{net_http_rt.rs,net_http_hosts.rs,Net.rs}`.
- Tests: `tests/http_i9.rs`, `tests/http_server_lifecycle.rs`, `tests/http.rs`, `tests/services_runtime.rs`.
- Gauntlet: `Tools/gauntlet/entries/{http-service,concurrency-service,http-client}` (`jet/run.jet`, `entry.json` probes). The harness is `Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry <name>`.

**Changes (in order)**
1. I9 first:
   - Reproduce with `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Tools/gauntlet/entries/http-service/jet/run.jet` plus the entry.json probes. The second probe never answers.
   - Trace where the JIT-tier server blocks: a blocking accept-loop read, or a task that never yields while a Shared write is pending.
   - Fix it in marshalling only, so the JIT host hands requests to the same scheduler path AOT uses.
   - Add `kv_get_put_get_matches_across_tiers` to `tests/http_i9.rs`.
2. Attribute on the current tree with `perf record` on the AOT binary under harness load: health vs kv, Shared state on/off, prebuilt vs formatted response, accept wakeups, per-request allocations. Record the split on the card.
3. Server substrate (HTTPServer/HTTPMessage/HTTPRoute): headers prebuilt once per route, no per-request `String` for static parts, one `writev` per response, keep-alive without a wakeup per request, a bounded accept batch.
4. Client (HTTPClient/NetHTTP): connection reuse and one allocation per response body.
- Writable paths: the Prelude files above, the jet-jit net files (marshalling only), and `tests/http_i9.rs`.
- Do not touch: `Tools/gauntlet/entries/` sources, `crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs`, `crates/jet-jit/src/ambient_interp.rs`, or `crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_call.rs`.
- Non-goals: HTTP API, authority model, TLS, and scheduler policy in a host.

**Proof**
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases http_i9/ --test http_server_lifecycle --test http --test services_runtime` → green.
- `node Tools/gauntlet/harness/run.mjs --entry http-service`, then `--entry concurrency-service`, then `--entry http-client` → every probe passes on AOT, run and dev with identical responses, and the ratios meet criteria 1-3. Any losing cell stays on the card.

**Batch**
batch-host-runtime: Prelude HTTP runtime, JIT host marshalling, and tier parity.

**Dependencies**
None.
