cards.title: Expose bounded checked local obligations through the existing semantic index
cards.body:
Expose bounded checked local obligations through the existing semantic index.

Public local definitions already carry type/mutability, references have targets, and callable/returned-view contracts exist. Private FlowFacts additionally holds moved places, open views, invalidation and reachability. The captured index builder publishes checked-definition derivations, not a complete per-source-point local-flow witness. A friendly callable view must not pretend these are the same coverage.

Under D-READ-STATE1, add a bounded source-point local-obligation projection to the existing checked semantic index and reasoning records, or retain current public facts if the owner chooses B. First prove the field-availability matrix on selected source points; reuse existing producers and avoid duplicating facts already exposed.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f10. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

## Owner scope extension — 2026-09-21

## Outcome

Deliver this existing canonical owner without a parallel mechanism. Preserve every existing acceptance criterion and ratified decision. Integrate its complete checked facts, source-version identity and observable errors into the reflection/compiler-session consumers in #3509.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/mod.rs:1067-1286
- crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/FlowFacts.rs:624-827
- crates/jet-semindex/src/Types.rs:1-148,303-389,521-573
- crates/jet-semindex/src/Build.rs:116-265

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

1. Keep existing public type/mutability, reference targets, callable access/failure and returned-view provenance; do not call those absent.
2. For one selected expression, identify its source/version, binding definition and precise before/after point. Cover mutable binding versus writable access, moved/partly moved ownership, active views and their owner/invalidation, scope cleanup obligations, and reachable versus unknown state only where the current checker establishes them.
3. The finite availability matrix must account for every captured plane: binding/type/narrowing, initialization, frozen state, sendability, origin/ownership/moves, views/invalidation, reachable state, typestate, compile-time string/path constraints and cleanup. Distinguish public facts already available, checker-established candidates, unsupported projection and nonapplicability. Do not export raw runtime values or treat module/name liveness as statement-point local liveness.
4. Use one compiler-owned fact source. Retain bounded facts from the existing check; do not re-check source in the renderer, create a second ownership analysis or expose mutable compiler internals.
5. Use the existing semantic-index/check result and jet.reasoning route. Version the exported fact shape under D-SEMINDEX1; coordinate the typed/JSON facade with BIG-F17 and version authority with READ-F16. No new runtime core.compiler use.
6. Discriminate current empty facts from unavailable, unsupported, invalid, stale and truncated coverage. An absent local-flow record is not proof that no obligation exists.
7. Preserve the existing clean-check publication gate. Invalid editor input yields unavailable current facts or an explicitly stale last-good snapshot; do not publish recovered partial checker state as fresh valid local facts.
8. Prove shadowing, branch joins, a moved place, a last-use read view, a Fixed backing that remains borrowed until close, invalid editor input and an edit that makes retained facts stale. Preserve static-versus-observed labels.
9. READ-F01 may present currently available callable facts without this addition. The new local-obligation API is an independent owner choice, not hidden scope inside that display.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Under D-READ-STATE1=A, publish a bounded source-point local-obligation projection (mutable binding vs writable access, moved and partly moved places, active views with owner and invalidation, cleanup obligations, reachability) from the Jet checker's own ownership state into the existing checked semantic index, with no second analysis.

## Current state
- The previous attempt stalled because Rust FlowFacts are private (crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/FlowFacts.rs:626), and that path is archived.
- Jet homes:
  - `SemaOwnershipState` (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership/Checks.jet:98) already holds declarations, moved places (`SemaOwnershipMovedPlace`:64 with origin and consumer), loans (:69) and view facts (:36).
  - LastUse.jet and Crossings.jet hold last-use and sendability facts.
  - The index is Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/SemanticIndex.jet:1570 `sema_compiler_semantic_index_from_checked`, which publishes definitions, references, calls, effects, view provenance (:195-233) and checked locals (:1543-1567).
  - Source/LSP/Features.rs:454 is the callable-summary consumer.
- The owned Rust paths (crates/jet-sema Sema/mod.rs, FlowFacts.rs, crates/jet-semindex) are archived. Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-read-f10.

## Changes
1. Produce the finite availability matrix first and log it on the card. Its planes are binding/type/narrowing, initialization, frozen, sendability, origin/ownership/moves, views/invalidation, reachability, typestate, compile-time string/path constraints and cleanup. Mark each plane public, checker-established, unsupported or not applicable.
2. Ownership/Checks.jet: at each statement boundary where the checker already runs, snapshot a bounded `SemaLocalObligationFact` (point span, binding key, moved and partly moved places, open loans and views with owner, pending cleanups, reachable flag) into the check result. The snapshot comes from the same state, with no re-walk.
3. CheckProgram.jet: carry the facts in the checked result, publishing them only when the check is clean. Invalid input yields `unavailable`, or an explicitly stale last-good snapshot with a revision.
4. SemanticIndex.jet: add a versioned `CompilerLocalObligation` record (D-SEMINDEX1 version bump, coordinated with BIG-F17 and READ-F16). It separates empty, unavailable, unsupported, stale and truncated states. Runtime values are never exported.
5. Add no Rust mirror. crates/jet-semindex and FlowFacts are archived, and the shipped LSP consumes the record only after the self-hosted index serves it.

## Proof
- The fixture Examples/features/tooling/local_obligations.jet covers shadowing, a branch join, a moved place, a last-use read view, a Fixed backing still borrowed until close, and an invalid-input twin. Run it through the self-hosted `jet inspect semindex <file> --json` and check every plane, including static vs observed labels, and the stale/unavailable states.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: the facts come from JetSema ownership state and the semantic index.

## Dependencies
No card blocker. The behavioral proof can only run once #218's execution route serves the Jet index; until then the card can land its code with check.sh proof and stays open. #3509 consumers integrate the record later (criterion 10).

cards.title: Share checked callable and source facts across developer tools
cards.body:
Show the checked callable contract at ambient and foreign boundaries.

A reader needs the callable's actual arity, parameter/result identity, failure and rights facts. A declaration stub may omit behavior handled by a special semantic path.

First compare print hover/signature help, qualified calls and the checked callable record. If they disagree, make existing presentation consume the authoritative checked contract. Keep unknown external behavior distinct from checked Jet guarantees; do not infer effect facts from return-type dispatch tables.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-big-f04. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Ownership reconciliation: Exact #2986 owns named Core module drift and generated declaration/dispatch conformance; its current plan does not own ambient print hover/signature agreement. This new bounded presentation proof coordinates with that producer rather than adding hidden work to its criterion.

Exact final evidence boundary: Declaration and special semantic arm differ in expressed arity. No hover mismatch or terminal-effect propagation failure is observed.

Owner choice: None for agreement with the existing checked contract. No new effect syntax or analysis safety exemption is proposed.

## Goal
One checked fact owner for developer tools (D-ONE-TOOLS1=A). Calls, hover, signature help, diagnostics and reasoning views show the same checked callable contract (arity, parameter/result identity, failure and rights facts) at ambient and foreign boundaries, with no parallel analyzer.

## Current state
- The Jet fact owner exists. `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/CompilerQueries.jet:10-13` defines `JetDriverCompilerCheckResult{checked: JetCompilerServicesCheckedFacts?, diagnostics, failed_stage}`, and `Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerServices.jet:39-42,399` builds `JetCompilerServicesCheckedFacts{value, semantic_index_complete}`.
- The host tools still run their own projections. The LSP has a private `CheckedBundle` (`Source/LSP/Server.rs:51-54`: diags, `ProgramBundle`, `SemIndexEffectFacts`). `jet inspect` has `CheckProjection` (`Source/CmdInspect.rs:35-38`: bundle, facts, `jet_semindex::SemIndex`). Both are built from the archived Rust sema/semindex.
- Recorded evidence boundary: the `print` declaration stub and its special semantic arm disagree on arity. No hover mismatch has been observed yet.
- Coverage today: `tests/lsp.rs` has `lsp_hover_returns_signature` (:3055) and `lsp_signature_help_returns_active_parameter` (:2480).

## Changes
1. Step 1, now, host only: add the print hover/signature/call comparison test. Where the declaration and the semantic arm disagree, make the presentation read the checked callable record. Do not infer effects from return-type tables. Keep unknown foreign behaviour marked unknown.
2. Step 2, after #218 routes execute: define one typed projection of `JetCompilerServicesCheckedFacts` that carries source, overlay, target, settings and package identity across the host boundary (`Compiler/Bootstrap/Host`). Replace `CheckedBundle` and `CheckProjection` with consumers of that projection in `Source/LSP/{Server,Check,Features}.rs` and `Source/CmdInspect.rs`, and delete the Rust-side analyzers in the same cutover.
3. Derive compiler CLI flag ownership from the command declarations. App `ArgsSpec` (#3242) keeps its own schema.
4. Preserve registered codes, fixes, byte/UTF-16 spans, URI escaping, privacy and every LSP, report and replay contract. A backend failure stays an internal error (I2).

## Proof

- `jet test Compiler --profile cases lsp/` and `jet test Compiler --profile cases live_inspect/` stay green after the cutover.
- A pure-looking helper that adds an outward operation shows the updated rights/failure explanation in hover and in `jet inspect --json` output (criterion 3).

`batch-host-cli`: the LSP and inspect consumers are host CLI/tooling.

## Dependencies
Step 2 needs #218 (the Jet check query must execute through the host). #3325 owns operation facts, which this card consumes. #2986 owns Core module drift.

cards.title: Choose structured source origin for public compiler diagnostics
cards.body:
Choose structured source origin for public compiler diagnostics.

A build/comptime tool receiving only a diagnostic byte span cannot safely identify an imported source snapshot. The current CLI location repair does not by itself change this public Core record.

Recommend a versioned optional origin on CompilerDiagnostic with a source path when known and a source digest. Keep byte spans relative to that origin. Retain the existing read-only core.compiler module and mirror, not a new library or dependency. Submit the complete short ballot before changing the public record/schema.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-big-f20. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

Exact final evidence boundary: Current public shape inspected; no runtime Core-API misattribution claimed. The related CLI import-origin failure is separately observed.

Owner choice: A: add versioned source-origin data to existing stock core.compiler diagnostics. B: keep the current thin facade and require other tools for per-file attribution. A recommended; no new module/dependency.

## Owner scope extension — 2026-09-21

## Outcome

Deliver this existing canonical owner without a parallel mechanism. Preserve every existing acceptance criterion and ratified decision. Integrate its complete checked facts, source-version identity and observable errors into the reflection/compiler-session consumers in #3509.

## Owned paths and integration

- crates/jet-semindex/src
- crates/jet-driver/src

One implementer owns this coherent patch. Main owns integration and closure. Serialize shared AST, Reflect.rs, Driver and pipeline edits with their other owners; do not duplicate those models.

## Scope limits

This is planned implementation, not completed behavior. Standard mode retains level 5; privileged operations require the owner's explicit opt-in contract. No new external dependency, unsafe exception, alternate parser, compatibility alias, or tier deferral is approved. Preserve ratified history and use the latest owner direction for current behavior.

## Proof

1. Owner ratifies D-BIG-DIAGORIGIN1 or retains the current thin facade explicitly.
2. If A, every source-bound diagnostic identifies its actual checked snapshot; pathless input still has a digest, while genuinely source-free diagnostics use no origin.
3. No diagnostic inherits the entry path merely because its own origin is absent; imported/local contrasts identify the right document.
4. Typed, Rust and CLI compiler values undergo one consistent versioned cutover; package-model schemas are not silently changed.
5. Reuse originating source identity and compute/reuse a digest per snapshot, not once per diagnostic or from changed disk text.
6. No new runtime compiler service, AST mutation, third-party dependency or optional Core library is introduced.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-BIG-DIAGORIGIN1=A (ratified; criterion 1 met). Every source-bound compiler diagnostic identifies the checked source snapshot it came from with a versioned optional `origin {path: String?, source_digest: String}`, and byte spans are relative to that origin. Source-free diagnostics carry no origin, and no diagnostic inherits the entry file's path. The public `core.compiler` CompilerDiagnostic, the host DiagnosticCodec and the CLI/LSP report cut over together. There is no new module, service or dependency. Source: BIG-F20. Integrates with #3509's compiler-session consumers.

## Current state
- The model exists but nothing sets it:
  - `Compiler/JetLexer/Source/Lexer/Tokens.jet:25-30` (`DiagnosticOrigin{display, path, source, revision}`) and `:149` (`Diagnostic.origin`).
  - `:194-197` (`diagnostic_with_origin`) has zero callers in Compiler/.
- Source segments already carry the file: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Diagnostics.jet:14-72` (`sema_source_location_at`, `sema_diagnostic_with_source_location`) and `Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Loader.jet:915-916`.
- A per-source digest is already computed for the semantic index: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/SemanticIndex.jet:1666` (`mir_sha256_hex(source)`).
- The public value has no origin: `Compiler/JetEval/Source/CompilerServices.jet:69-79` (`code`, `severity`, `message`, `why`, `fix`, `span`), with sema typing in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/CompilerServices.jet`. The shipped Rust field table (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib/core_types.rs:951-954`) also lacks it.
- The host round-trips origin already: `Compiler/Bootstrap/Host/DiagnosticCodec.rs:351-354`. The CLI report is `crates/jet-foundation/src/Report.rs` (`jet.report/v3`).

## Changes
1. **JetDriver.** Compute the digest once per loaded source snapshot, store it on the source unit (`Identity.jet` `JetDriverSourceUnit`), and reuse the semantic index's digest rather than hashing twice.
2. **JetSema.** In `sema_diagnostic_with_source_location` (`Diagnostics.jet:72`), attach `DiagnosticOrigin` from the segment's own file and digest. Compiler-generated segments carry their generated path. A diagnostic with no segment stays `origin: None`.
3. **JetEval and JetSema public value.** Add `origin: CompilerDiagnosticOrigin?` (`path: String?`, `source_digest: String`) to CompilerDiagnostic in `CompilerServices.jet`, and declare the type once in `Core/compiler`. Bump its schema version.
4. **Shipped-binary mirror.** Make the same field in `core_types.rs`, the Rust diagnostic origin attach, and `Report.rs` JSON (`file` from the origin, plus `source_digest`). Update the LSP (`Source/LSP/Server.rs`) to publish per-origin URIs. Package-model schemas stay unchanged.
5. Remove `crates/jet-semindex` from this card's owned paths; it is not the home.

## Proof
- `cargo test --test compiler_api diagnostic_origin_identifies_imported_snapshot`: pass.
- `cargo test --test report diagnostic_origin_in_report_json`: pass.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases lsp/`: existing projections green.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh`: exit 0.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: origins are attached in JetSema/JetDriver diagnostics. This card batches with #3205, whose causes reuse these origins.

## Dependencies
None. The ratified decision is in hand. #3205 consumes this card's origins.

cards.title: Share typed codec values, field errors and override precedence
cards.body:
Close custom codec and reflection interoperability.

Compare generated and hand-written Encode/Decode against selected Serde, Glaze and Jackson custom mappings without importing their separate reflection systems.

Compare generated and hand-written Encode/Decode against selected Serde, Glaze and Jackson custom mappings without importing their separate reflection systems.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f007. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Close custom-codec and reflection interoperability under D-ONE-CODECS1=A, with D-VALIDATE-DECODE1=B stated as current law. Field traversal, constraint application, override precedence and field-error paths get one canonical owner. Each wire format keeps its own leaves (duplicate keys, binary/text, extension tags, mixed XML, lossless numerics). The comparison targets are selected Serde, Glaze and Jackson custom mappings, without importing their reflection systems. No new marker, public error family, data-algebra category or storage mechanism is added.

## Current state
- The original finding is `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f007`. The old `docs/` path is stale.
- Sema: `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Serde.jet` checks codec admissibility, generic bounds and wire reachability (`sema_serde_field_reaches_wire` at :94, `sema_serde_type_is_admissible` at :148). Registration lives at `Registration/Checked.jet:140-141`.
- Codegen: `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Functions.jet:277-286` lowers type-level `MirSerdeAttribute` (RenameAll, Tag, Untagged, DenyUnknownFields). `AutoDerives.jet` and `EncodingCodecs.jet` generate Encode/Decode.
- The format adapters are `Core/encoding/*.jet` and the host kernel `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/JetStd/JSONCodec.rs`.
- Existing witnesses in `Examples/features/serde/`: `hand_codec`, `field_metadata_edges`, `serde_derive`, `serde_generic`, `codable_default`, `decode_migration`, `json_typed`, `csv_typed`, `cbor_profile`, plus the `encoding_*_stream` examples.

## Changes
1. Capability inventory (criteria 1 and 3). Build a table covering alias, rename, skip, read-only, constraints, variants, enums, chrono, custom context and generic targets. For each row give the Jet spelling (derived and hand-written), the owning code (Serde.jet / AutoDerives.jet / EncodingCodecs.jet / Core adapter) and the status: supported, missing-by-law or missing-defect. Classify every missing capability before proposing anything. A new marker or API needs its own ballot. The table goes in the card log.
2. One owner (criterion 4). Move field traversal, constraint application and error-path construction into one helper set in `AutoDerives.jet`, which `EncodingCodecs.jet` and every format adapter call. The precedence rule is: an explicit custom codec wins, then field attributes, then type-level `MirSerdeAttribute`, then derived defaults. Format syntax errors stay distinct from field errors.
3. Formats (criterion 5): full, selective and streaming decoding must agree in meaning for each profile. Streaming does not fake buffering or allocation parity.
4. Add examples for any gaps the inventory finds: `Examples/features/serde/codec_override_precedence.jet` and `codec_field_errors.jet`, each with a golden.

## Proof
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden serde/`: passes on O0, O1 and O2, including the two new examples.
- `jet test Compiler --profile cases auto_derive_policy/`: passes.
- The capability table (criteria 1 and 3) is attached to the card log.

## Batch
batch-jetc-back: the consolidation lives in derive generation (AutoDerives and EncodingCodecs). The Core adapters ride in the same build.

## Dependencies
None. D-ONE-CODECS1 is ratified.

cards.title: Prove task outcomes and structured cancellation
cards.body:
Prove task outcomes and structured cancellation.

Exercise task groups, all/race/any, timer/select behavior and cancellation with explicit task versus domain-failure identity.

Exercise task groups, all/race/any, timer/select behavior and cancellation with explicit task versus domain-failure identity.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f012. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Prove task outcomes and structured cancellation (groups, all/race/any, timers/select, sibling drain, cooperative wait cancellation) with explicit task-failure versus domain-failure identity. Reconcile the two `TaskFailure` meanings into one owner, and stop ordinary `Err` from being flattened into a panic.

## Current state
- There are two meanings. Core has `pub struct TaskFailure { message: String, raised: Bool }` (`Core/tasks/tasks.jet:35-38`). The host and sema use an enum: `JetTaskFailure::{Cancelled, DeadlineBlown, Panicked(String)}` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/TaskGroup.rs:40-83`) and `Type.Result(ok, Type.Named("TaskFailure"))` (`Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/TaskGroups.jet:339-341`). `TaskFailure` is a registered error leaf in `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/FailureLaw.jet:22`.
- Err flattening: `jet_task_flatten_result` maps an ordinary body `Err(e)` to `jet_task_failure_from_code("TASK_BODY_FAILED", …)`, which falls through to `Panicked(reason)` (TaskGroup.rs:44, :52-62). A domain error is therefore reported as a panic, which violates criterion 3 and the research warning.
- Witnesses with goldens: `Examples/features/concurrency/{task_group,task_all,all_failfast(.err),select_channel,completion_order,release_join_failure,race_cancel,cancel_cleanup,task_panic(.err)}.jet`. The race_cancel and cancel_cleanup goldens now exist.
- The finding is at `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f012`.

## Changes
1. One owner: make `Core/tasks/tasks.jet` declare `TaskFailure` as the enum `Cancelled | DeadlineBlown | Panicked(message: String)` that sema and host already use, and delete the `{message, raised}` struct and `exception()`. Migrate callers.
2. Domain errors: a task body typed `T E!` joins to `(E | TaskFailure)!`, so the domain `E` stays itself and is not rewrapped. Change `jet_task_flatten_result(s)` and the JIT and interpreter equivalents to propagate `E`. Add sema typing for the joined union in `TaskGroups.jet`.
3. Add `Examples/features/concurrency/task_domain_error.jet` with a golden. A group child returns `Err(ParseError…)`; the parent matches it as `ParseError`, not `Panicked`; siblings are drained, which is observed through a cleanup print.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=concurrency/ Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `for f in task_group task_all select_channel completion_order release_join_failure race_cancel cancel_cleanup task_domain_error; do Tools/agent/jet-env jet run Examples/features/concurrency/$f.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/concurrency/$f.out; done` gives empty diffs, and the same holds with `--interpret`.

cards.title: Generate four CLI reference formats from one checked model
cards.body: One active implementation home for the ratified Markdown, man, ReST and YAML command-document outputs. Former cards #3291,#3292,#3293 become historical redirects. Every original criterion and immutable decision remains traceable; no output implementation is claimed complete.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Deliver the four ratified ArgsSpec reference projections from one checked command model: `to_markdown` (D-CORE-CLI-MARKDOWN1=A), `to_man` (D-CORE-CLI-MAN1=A), `to_rest` (D-CORE-CLI-REST1=A), and `to_yaml` (D-CORE-CLI-YAML1=A, exact version1 fields). #3291, #3292, and #3293 are historical redirects, and their criteria map to 9-30 here.

**Current state**
- `crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Args.rs:85` `JetArgsSpec::help` is the only renderer.
- No `to_markdown`, `to_man`, `to_rest`, or `to_yaml` exists in Compiler/, crates/, or Core/.
- ArgsSpec methods are routed through:
  - `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/ProcessHandles.jet:55-145` (op, arity, return type, and parameter tables);
  - `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/HandleMethods.jet:1175-1185`;
  - the Rust mirror in `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/mod.rs:13101`, `routes.rs:2927`, `TIR/subset/handles.rs:354`, and `crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/ArgsLite.rs`.

**Changes**
1. Jet compiler first. In `ProcessHandles.jet`, add ops `ArgsSpecToMarkdown`, `ToMan`, `ToRest`, and `ToYaml`:
   - arity 0, except `to_man(date: String)` (explicit date, never ambient);
   - return `String`;
   - receiver access `Read`.
   Add the `HandleMethods.jet` routes to `jet_args_to_*`.
2. Rust mirror (needed so the shipped binary proves it): the same four ops in TIR `mod.rs`, `routes.rs`, `subset/handles.rs`, and ArgsLite.
3. `Args.rs`: add one `jet_args_command_doc(&JetArgsSpec) -> CommandDoc` projection (command path, inherited options, defaults, visibility, examples, with hidden/secret entries omitted) and four small leaves:
   - Markdown fences and anchors;
   - roff escaping with an explicit `.TH` date;
   - ReST sections and links;
   - YAML through the existing Core YAML writer's escaping rules.
   Output is capped with a structured error on overflow. There is no parsing of help text.
4. Malformed metadata returns the fallible error path, never a panic or exit.

**Proof**
- New golden `Examples/features/cli/args_reference.jet`, one shared fixture with nested, inherited, hidden, and secret options, multiline punctuation, and fences: `jet test Compiler --profile golden cli/args_reference` matches `args_reference.out` on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Close Unicode, regex and text-encoding contracts
cards.body:
Close Unicode, regex and text-encoding contracts.

Compare the selected text/regex/format/codec families with Jet on scalar boundaries, malformed text, views, conversions and repairable errors.

Compare the selected text/regex/format/codec families with Jet on scalar boundaries, malformed text, views, conversions and repairable errors.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f038. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Close the core.text/core.regex/codec contract on scalar boundaries, case and normalization, regex complexity and invalid encoding, with exercised witnesses. Fix the one real gap: case folding beyond Latin-1.

**Current state**
- Core/text/text.jet:14-19: UTF-8 decode, Hangul NFD/NFC, UAX #29 graphemes and words, and width are Jet. Case mapping is Latin-1 only, and full case-fold tables map to identity. :73-78 `lower`/`upper`/`casefold` → `map_case` (:467). `casefold` is just `lower`, so `casefold("Straße")` stays `straße`.
- :82-88 `nfc`/`nfd`/`nfkc`/`nfkd`/`graphemes`/`words` exist.
- Core/regex/regex.jet:15-18 is a bounded backtracking NFA over UTF-8 bytes with ASCII-only `ignore_case`. :488-498 `budget_limit` is (nodes+1)×(min(bytes,4096)+1)×32, clamped to [4096, 1,000,000]. :458-461 caps quantifiers at 4096.
- Examples/features/text/unicode_text.jet, unicode_17.jet and regex.jet have goldens. Related open cards: #1471 (regex gaps, building), #3370 (producers), #3107 (index boundaries).

**Changes**
1. Core/text/text.jet: generate full Unicode simple and full case mapping plus C+F folding tables into Jet data, the same way the existing normalization tables are generated. Route `map_case` and `casefold` through them. Casefold is locale-neutral; Turkish dotted I is not special-cased. Update the header comment at :14-19.
2. Regex: keep the byte NFA and budget. Document in regex.jet that budget exhaustion is a typed failure, and add a witness that proves it. `ignore_case` stays ASCII, stated explicitly; Unicode case-insensitive regex belongs to #1471.
3. Invalid encoding: `String.from_bytes` → None and codec `EncodingError` are the policy. Add a witness for lossy vs strict where core.text exposes it.
4. Add Examples/features/text/unicode_contracts.jet plus its golden. Record unsupported cells as printed lines.
5. Owned vs view costs: measure only the rows exercised above, through the existing text perf cell. Make no claim without a receipt.

**Proof**
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden text/unicode_contracts`: passes.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden text/unicode_text` and `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=text/regex …`: still pass. Existing goldens change only where casefold output was wrong.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden text/unicode_contracts` passes on O0, O1 and O2.

**Batch**
batch-core-text: Core/text and Core/regex Jet only, proved by text goldens.

**Dependencies**
None. New parser or control APIs (for example, a Unicode regex mode) need their own ballot (criterion 3).

cards.body:
Prove selective and lazy decoding without hidden validation loss.

Compare projected/partial/lazy/fixed-buffer operations with the canonical reader and generated decoder, preserving the exact validation boundary.

Compare projected/partial/lazy/fixed-buffer operations with the canonical reader and generated decoder, preserving the exact validation boundary.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f058. cards.plan:
## Goal
Record what full versus selective JSON decoding actually does: validation scope, failure timing, and repeated scans and allocations. Ordinary decode must never silently weaken validation, and any lazy expert API goes to a ballot.

## Current state
- Core/encoding/json.jet:93-95: `reader(text)` is a pull parser whose first call validates and materializes the whole value, after which it walks events. There is no demanded-prefix extraction.
- The shipped bounded event reader is the host `jet_enc_json_reader(input: FileReader, limits)` (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/EncodingStream.rs:534; dispatcher crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet:749), with a golden at Examples/features/serde/encoding_json_stream.jet.
- Typed `json.decode<T>` is compiler lowering through `jet_std_json_decode_lenient` (Core.jet:731).
- Examples/features/serde/shape_projection.jet depends on argv, the environment and a DB (:6, :30-31, :35), so it cannot be a golden. It is a Shape-projection witness, not a selective-decoding one.

## Changes
1. New Examples/features/serde/json_selective.jet with its .out. It runs one document through three paths: (a) `json.parse` in full, (b) `json.decode<Small>` projecting 1 of 20 fields, and (c) `json.reader(^file)` events, stopping after the first key. The inputs are: valid; malformed inside a skipped subtree; trailing garbage after the root; a duplicate key in a skipped subtree; and an invalid UTF-8 escape in a skipped string. It prints, for each path, whether and where it fails.
2. Expected law: (a) and (b) validate the whole document and fail identically. (c) fails when it reaches the bad bytes, or at `finish`, and the failure timing is printed. If (b) accepts malformed skipped data or trailing garbage, fix the lenient typed decoder at its owner so that typed decode stays strict (D-ENC-DYN1).
3. Measurement: `Tools/agent/jet-env jet perf run` on a scratch program over a 1 MB document records wall time and allocations for (a), (b) and (c), plus repeated `parse` calls, and the numbers go on the card.
4. Record the cell `demanded-prefix or lazy extraction: unsupported`. Any expert lazy or borrowed API is a ballot (criterion 4), not a change to ordinary decode.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/json_selective cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env jet run --interpret Examples/features/serde/json_selective.jet | diff - Examples/features/expected/serde/json_selective.out` prints nothing.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=serde/encoding_json_stream cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes.

## Batch
batch-core-encoding: a JSON witness plus at most one decoder fix.

## Dependencies
None.

cards.title: Investigate ordinary color-value conversion
cards.body:
Investigate ordinary color-value conversion.

Map captured color-space conversion to existing typed color/numeric/UI values without selecting another renderer.

Map captured color-space conversion to existing typed color/numeric/UI values without selecting another renderer.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f068. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.
cards.plan:
**Goal**
Give Core one color value with stated spaces, ranges, alpha and rounding, and have tui, game and ui adapt to it instead of each keeping its own color struct.

**Current state**
- Core/tui/tui.jet:30-35 `TuiColorProfile`, :37-41 `TuiColor` (Ansi16/Ansi256/Rgb(red, green, blue) as Int), :85-88 `color_rgb`.
- Core/game/raylib.jet:19-22 `RaylibColor{r,g,b,a: Int}`, :34-35 `color()` clamps with `clamp8`.
- Core/ui/ui.jet:157 `node_color(label, width, height, color: String)` takes an untyped string.
- No Core color model and no hex/HSL/linear conversion exist.
- Evidence: Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-core-f068.

**Owner question (open; plan written for recommendation A)**
Should Core define one `core.color.Color` (sRGB8 plus alpha, with linear/HSL/hex conversions) that tui, game and ui adapt to, replacing the per-provider structs? A) one Core Color, providers adapt; B) keep provider structs and add conversions only; C) no change. Recommendation: A (one mechanism).

**Changes** (A)
1. New Core/color/color.jet (`core.color`): `Color{r, g, b, a: U8}`; `Color.from_hex(String) -> Color ColorError!` (#rgb, #rrggbb, #rrggbbaa); `to_hex()`; `from_hsl`/`to_hsl` (Float degrees/unit ranges); `to_linear`/`from_linear` (IEC 61966-2-1 sRGB transfer, round half to even into U8). Alpha is straight, not premultiplied.
2. Providers: `TuiColor.Rgb` takes a `Color`, and ANSI downgrade by profile stays in tui. Raylib draw calls take `Color`, and `RaylibColor` is deleted. `ui.node_color` takes `Color`. Migrate every example caller.
3. Register in crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core.jet, regenerate with `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs`, add a core-library.md section.

**Proof**
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden ui/color_conversions` -> hex/HSL/linear round trips, clamping and rounding match on every tier.
- Existing tui/game/ui goldens pass after the migration: `jet test Compiler --profile golden ui`.
- `node Tools/agent/check-core-surface-ledger.mjs` -> OK.

**Batch**
batch-core-ui.

**Dependencies**
The owner ballot on the question above. No card blockers.

2. compare useful asset/UI values.
3. preserve one color model.
4. any missing public operation gets a narrow gate.

cards.title: Iterator capability facts must survive adaptation and type erasure
cards.body:
Iterator capability facts must survive adaptation and type erasure.

The inspected JetIter boxes a forward iterator; ViewIter and user-defined Iterator hooks also exist. The bounded public inventory does not establish general exact-size, reverse, permanent-exhaustion, or borrowed-remainder operations across these paths. A helper name alone does not establish those capabilities.

Carry verified capabilities through the existing iterable protocol and storage representations. Add precise proofs for reverse traversal, exact remaining size, exhaustion, and clone/replay only where the source and adapter support them. Do not label an upper bound as an exact size.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f005. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Carry verified iterator capability facts through the existing Iterable/Iterator protocol, adapters and storage representations, without a public iterator hierarchy or mandatory dynamic allocation. Build the three ratified slices now:
- **D-ITER-SIZE1=A:** one runtime `size_hint()` pair; equal bounds convey exactness. There is no ExactRemaining hierarchy, no `remaining_len()` sibling and no runtime `@remaining`.
- **D-ITER-FUSED1=A:** a checked `fused` capability fact plus `fuse()`, which latches the first true end.
- **D-ITER-BORROW1=A:** `by_ref()` borrowed driving that reuses View/ViewMut provenance and sema overlap checks.

The open ballots D-ITER-BACK1 (reverse and mixed-end reads) and D-ITER-REPLAY1 each gate only their own slice.

## Current state
- The public `Iter` has no `size_hint`, `fuse` or `by_ref`: there are no rows in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`.
- The host uses `size_hint` only internally (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:453`).
- `JetIter` boxes a forward iterator. `ViewIter` and the user `Iterator` hooks (`Examples/features/collections/iter_hook.jet`) exist.
- Merged from #3336: a fused iterator never yields after its first end. Type erasure, `map` and driver loops never tag a source as fused. Async not-ready and channel `Empty` stay distinct from end (coordinate #3343), and nothing fuses silently.
- Canonical handoff (#3398): use #3325's checked operation facts, and keep the exact-size, double-ended, fused and remainder guarantees separate.

## Changes
1. Jet compiler:
   - `Collections.jet`: add `size_hint() -> (lower: Int, upper: Int?)` (non-advancing), `fuse() -> Iter<T>` and `by_ref()`. Adapters propagate conservative bounds (`map` keeps them; `filter` sets lower to 0; `take(n)` clamps; overflow sets upper to `None`) and the `fused` fact.
   - `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Ownership`: `by_ref` creates a loan on the source owner. Overlapping mutation is rejected with the existing overlap code, and the remainder stays usable after the loan ends.
   - Add ops in `TIR.jet`, with routes in `BuiltinMethods.jet`.
2. Host mirror:
   - `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` and the TIR lowering.
   - Prelude `JetIter` exposes `size_hint`, a `JetFuse` wrapper (one wrapper for non-fused sources) and `by_ref` over `&mut`.
   - The JIT rows and the MIREval arms.
3. Docs: `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md` and a disposition row per stable Rust inventory entry (criterion 1). BACK1 and REPLAY1 rows are marked "owner-gated".

## Proof
- New `Examples/features/collections/iter_capabilities.jet` covers exact, bounded and unknown hints; a non-advancing query; a dishonest user hint that stays safe; overflow; a `fuse()` over a source that resumes after an empty poll; and `by_ref().take(2)` followed by reading the remainder.
  - `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/iter_capabilities.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
  - `JET_1216_STEM=collections/iter_capabilities Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test dev_tier_parity collections_memory_and_streams_match_interpreter_jit_and_aot` passes.
- `JET_UI_FILTER=tests/ui/iter_by_ref_overlap.jet Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots` shows the mutation-while-borrowed rejection.

## Batch
`batch-host-runtime` (iter cluster, with sema loan checks).

## Dependencies
None for the three ratified slices. The reverse/mixed-end slice waits on D-ITER-BACK1 (recommended A) and replay on D-ITER-REPLAY1. No speed claim.
cards.checkSteps:
1. Each stable Rust inventory row has a semantic Jet disposition, including positive and negative capability bounds.
2. Mixed front/back consumption never duplicates an item and preserves the remaining range.
3. Exact-size operations are unavailable or explicitly fallible when only bounds are known; overflow cannot produce a false exact length.
4. A permanently exhausted wrapper remains exhausted, while a source that can resume after an empty poll is not mislabeled fused.
5. The representation and lowering preserve these facts without a separate public iterator hierarchy or mandatory dynamic allocation.

[#3315]  • User and built-in sources support repeated pulls, exhaustion, scoped adapters and continuation from the exact remaining item. • An early-returning consumer releases its borrow without losing or replaying items. • Moved sources, overlapping mutable drives and escaping borrowed items are rejected before any backend runs. [#3331]  • A callback failure stops at the triggering item; the next pull starts at the exact next item. • Accumulator and partial-output ownership is explicit. The source is neither replayed nor destroyed. • Infallible, propagating and error-as-data callbacks stay type-distinct through shared IR. • JP: `collections/fail_remainder`.

[#3333]  • A repeated peek does not pull again, and the first peek's side effects are documented. • A rejected conditional consume keeps the pending item, or the replacement returned by the rejection branch. • An accepted consume advances once with no item copy. • Peeked mutation targets the buffered item. Loans cannot outlive or overlap a cursor mutation. • JP: `collections/peekable`; `peek_loan_across_next`.

[#3334]  • Non-consuming bounds and exact remaining length are distinguishable. • filter drops exactness; map keeps it; chain checks representability. • Hints never authorize unchecked access. Unknown, infinite and over-range sizes stay honest. • JP: `collections/size_hint`.

[#3335]  • Mixed front/back pulls never duplicate or skip an item and meet exactly at exhaustion. • Reverse search reports the original index. • Adapters forward exact bounds. Forward-only streams are never collected to fake the capability. • Golden `collections/iter_back`; UI `next_back_one_way_source` (Stream, and after filter).

[#3341]  • A custom BagIter `map` runs without a second map implementation. • User sources, built-in Iter, Stream and ViewIter compose the same adapters, with no hidden collection, replay or lifetime extension. • JP: `collections/iter_interop`.

[#3355]  • A short final group keeps every value read (typed partial result, or returned to the cursor). • Too few is distinguished from too many, with no overconsumption. • Width zero, move-only values and remainder lifetime have explicit contracts. • Golden `collections/read_exact`.

[#3362]  • Too-many detection reads only the documented extra item and keeps the remainder. • Equality keeps the representative policy and short-circuits. • Existing compositions are shown before any new alias is proposed (aliases need a ballot). • Golden `collections/cardinality_search`.

[#3375]  • The remainder reflects mixed front/back advancement without copying. • A mutable projection is exclusive. `into_remainder` keeps the source lifetime. • UTF-8 byte units are preserved. Opaque and filter sources do not expose a contiguous remainder. • JP: `collections/iter_remaining`; `iter_remaining_filter`, `iter_remaining_mut_overlap`.

[#3394]  • A copied borrowed slice iterator starts at the same position, advances independently and keeps its loan. • One-shot and exclusive cursors are not copyable. Shared external state stays shared. • Assigning from an explicit copy gives `clone_from` semantics with no alias. • JP: `collections/iter_copy`; `iter_copy_one_shot`.

[#3350]  • Fast/slow branch traces measure retained items and cleanup. • A finite capacity backpressures or fails explicitly. • Cloned replayable sources are compared with buffered one-shot sources. • Any caching API goes to a separate owner ballot. • Golden `collections/fork_replay`.

[#3368]  • Warns only on proven endless normal production. `take(n)` removes the warning; effectful infinite loops are not flagged. • The message explains demand, buffering and cancellation without inserting a bound. • JP: `tests/ui_lint/endless_full_drain`.

cards.title: One checked operation contract for collections and execution engines
cards.body:
Publish one authoritative operation contract for collection readers.

Names do not reveal eager versus lazy work, source ownership, callback order, error handling or buffering. Rust and Jet use some identical names for different contracts.

Document each existing public operation from its authoritative contract; feed existing generated API/docs and explain surfaces from the same semantic facts. Include corrected all/any teaching and link READ-F02/READ-F12, not another mutation-repair mechanism.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f013. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ONE-OPERATIONS1=A (ratified 2026-09-13) in the self-hosted compiler. Author one checked operation-contract row per collection/Iter operation and derive every repeated view from it: arity and access, callback types, result types, TBuiltinOp/TClosureOp selection, docs, completion and explain. Remove the replaced tables in one cutover. Keep D-CORE-EAGER1/2=A and the LAST ties from #2298.

## Current state
- The operation facts are split across four parallel `if method == …` tables in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`:
  - arity and access in `sema_collection_method_contract` (`:136-282`);
  - callback and argument types in `sema_collection_method_argument_type` (`:301-420`);
  - result types in `sema_collection_method_result_type` (`:423-667`);
  - operation selection in `sema_collection_method_operation` (`:669-924`).
- Each new Iter method (#3315, #3333, #3334, #3371 and others) must currently touch all four.
- Core call facts also live in `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/CoreCalls.jet` (565 lines) and `CoreCallRows.jet` (2011 lines). Their consumers are `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Collections.jet`, `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet` and `ClosureMethods.jet`, and `Compiler/JetEval/Source/Routes`.
- The host kernels (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs`, `Prelude/Core.jet`) are retained runtime. The rows reference them without re-describing them.
- The archived `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` and `Syntax/core_calls.rs` are reference only, and this card does not edit them.
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f013 (READ-F02/READ-F12).

## Changes
1. `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet`:
   - Define one `CollectionOperationRow`: receiver kinds, access, arity, callback shape, result projection, TIR op, eager/lazy timing, callback count/order, stop-item consumption, failure channel, empty result, buffering, and a status of current, proposed or source-only.
   - Author every existing operation as a row.
   - Rewrite the four functions as lookups over the rows, then delete the `if` chains.
2. Cut every consumer over in the same pass: JetSema `Calls/Collections.jet`, JetCodegen `BuiltinMethods.jet`/`ClosureMethods.jet` (route rows keyed from the operation row), JetEval `Routes`, and the Web/JIT route inventories in Compiler/. Remove the replaced Path, owned-adapter and inclusion inventories.
3. Generate the Core reference operation table and the explain/completion text from the rows, through the existing `Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs` pipeline.
   - Correct the all/any teaching: empty `all` is true and empty `any` is false.
   - Rewrite `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md:289-320` from the generated table.
4. Add `Examples/features/collections/operation_contract.jet` with the criteria cells. The remainder-continuation cell uses the #3315 `next`.
5. Criteria 1-6 and 7-12 duplicate each other (the pre-retarget and retargeted wording). Closing 7-12 closes 1-6.

## Proof
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.
- `node Tools/agent/gen-core-tables.mjs --check` passes.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden collections/operation_contract` passes on O0, O1 and O2.
- `jet test Compiler --profile golden collections/` passes, as a regression check that every existing collections golden is unchanged.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: JetFoundation tables consumed by JetSema first, then codegen and eval.

## Dependencies
#3315 is needed only for the remainder-continuation cell and can land in the same batch. Land this row refactor first within the batch: the new-method cards (#3315, #3333, #3334, #3371, #3329, #3354) then add rows, not four table edits.

cards.title: Make selection-by-absence distinct from dropping a failure
cards.body:
Make selection-by-absence distinct from dropping a failure.

Rust filter_map consumes Option outputs. The inspected Jet helper consumes Result and drops errors; current filter_map examples deliberately keep successful parses.

Pin selection semantics and add any missing absence-returning callback support without silently changing deliberate error filtering or introducing a second failure type.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f015. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-SELECTION1=A (ratified): lift the existing `filter_map` so that the callback carrier decides the selection rule.
- `-> U?` skips `None`.
- An explicitly returned `Result` keeps the ratified success-only selector.
- A callback failure effect propagates and is never silently dropped.

Add `map_while` (`None` stops) and `find_map` (`None` continues) under their own exact contracts; the triggering item is consumed. There is no new absence or error type and no second selector engine.

## Current state
- Jet typing already unwraps an `Option` success (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:607-614`) and routes to `TClosureOp.FilterMap` (`:864`, `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/ClosureMethods.jet:65-67`).
- The runtime requires `Result`: `jet_iter_filter_map` needs `F: FnMut(&T) -> Result<U, E>` and calls `.ok()` (`crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Core/Collections.rs:2261-2268`, list form `:2551-2558`). As a result an `Option` callback cannot lower, and a propagating error is dropped.
- JIT: `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs:11884` (`checked_iter_filter_map_typed`).
- `map_while` and `find_map` exist nowhere in `Collections.jet`.
- The only example is `Examples/features/collections/filter_map.jet` (Result form, successful parses).
- Merged from #3357: an error item survives an ordinary data-preserving map unless a selector explicitly drops it. Nested optional/outcome items, all-error sources and empty sources keep their types. Remainder behaviour follows #3331.

## Changes
1. Jet compiler:
   - `Collections.jet` records the callback carrier (Option vs Result vs failure effect) in the operation, and adds `map_while` and `find_map` rows (arity, argument type, result `Iter<U>` and `U?`).
   - Add `TClosureOp.MapWhile` and `.FindMap` in `TIR.jet`.
   - Add route rows in `ClosureMethods.jet`.
2. Host mirror for the shipped proof:
   - `crates/jet-foundation/src/Collections.rs` tables.
   - `crates/jet-codegen/src/TIR/lower/builtins.rs` and `TIR/routes.rs`.
   - Prelude `Collections.rs`: an `Option` variant of `jet_iter_filter_map`, the Result variant kept, the failure route propagated, plus `jet_iter_map_while` and `jet_iter_find_map`.
   - `crates/jet-jit/src/Collections.rs`.
   - Interpreter `crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/MIREval.rs`.
3. Docs: the iterator family list in `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md:308-312`.

## Proof
- New `Examples/features/collections/filter_map_absence.jet` prints `[1,3]` for `odd` (`-> Int?`) and keeps successful parses via Result. It also shows a propagated callback failure, error-as-data (#3357), `map_while` stopping at the first `None` with the remainder observable, and `find_map` skipping `None`.
  - `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/filter_map Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` covers both examples.

cards.title: Construct generic collection destinations through one explicit protocol
cards.body:
Construct generic collection destinations through one explicit protocol.

Rust FromIterator supports more than Vec. Jet collect/to_list and explicit Map/Set construction exist, but no complete general destination protocol is proven in this corpus.

Ratify one explicit destination-construction protocol over the existing Iterable/Iterator model. Preserve eager yielding-loop List semantics and keep the collection choice visible.

Evidence and the complete original finding: docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f017. The retained report keeps source versions, exact locators, witness inputs, observed outputs and uncertainty. Source inspection is not execution. Frozen binary receipts do not prove the changing source tree. This card does not ratify a new API, default, dependency or distribution choice.

The exact final per-row contract is retained in target-mine-playlist-20260911/analyses/iterators/stable-capability-map.json. This card owns its named delta only. Current-source runtime is NOT RUN; frozen e841 receipts remain historical.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Implement D-ITER-COLLECT1=A. `FromIterator` becomes the one user-extensible destination-construction protocol: one `Item` type, and `from(source)` consumes the source through the canonical Iterable conversion. The existing `Set.from` adopts it. List, Map, text, tuple and custom destinations own their ordering, duplicate and failure-cleanup policies. `collect()` and `to_list()` stay List terminals, and an expected type never changes eager or yielding behaviour. Extending existing state stays with D-ITER-EXTEND1 (#3330).

## Current state
- `collect` and `to_list` always return `List` (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:266-268,647,893-894`).
- `to_set` is List-only (`:265,654,905`).
- `Set.from([…])` exists but takes a List (`Examples/features/collections/set.jet:12`).
- The only generic static is `Map.fromkeys`/`from_keys` (`Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuiltinStatics.jet:160-161`).
- There is no FromIterator trait. Compiler-owned traits are listed in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/Types.jet:77`.
- The finding is at Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-09-12.md#finding-iter-f017. Operation facts come from #3325 (per #3398).

## Changes
1. Jet compiler:
   - Declare a compiler-owned `FromIterator` trait (`type Item`, `from: fn(source: &&Iter<Item>) -> Self`) beside Iterable/Iterator: add it to `Types.jet:77` and the associated-name table in `Functions.jet:2175`.
   - `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuiltinStatics.jet`: add `List.from`, `Set.from`, `Map.from` (items `(key, value)`) and `String.from` (items String or Char) as FromIterator statics that accept any Iterable.
   - `Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Static.jet`: `T.from(src)` on a user type resolves through its `impl T.FromIterator`.
   - A fallible source (an `Iter` whose items carry `E!`) makes `from` return `T E!`: construction stops at the first error and drops the partial destination.
   - Add routes in `Compiler/JetCodegen/Source/Codegen/BuiltinMethods.jet`, plus JetEval.
2. Host: `jet_set_from_iter`, `jet_map_from_iter` and `jet_string_from_iter` over `JetIter` in `Prelude/Core/Collections.rs`/`Core.rs` and the JIT, plus the Rust mirror.
3. Migrate `Set.from([..])` callers to the protocol form (the spelling is unchanged). Update `Docs/spec/reference/core-library.md` to document the protocol and the explicit destination rule.
4. Add the example and the UI fixture named in the criteria. The example includes tuple destinations through `unzip`, which is unchanged.

## Proof
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/from_iter Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` passes.
- `JET_GOLDEN_FILTER=collections/set Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test golden examples_compile_and_run` still passes.
- `jet run` and `jet run --interpret` of `from_iter` produce empty diffs.
- The UI snapshot passes.
- `Tools/agent/jet-env bash Compiler/Bootstrap/check.sh` exits 0.

## Batch
`batch-jetc-sema`: trait resolution and static-call typing.

## Dependencies
None. #3354 builds on this card.

cards.title: Translate Nixpkgs into native Jet packages managed only by Hangar
cards.body:
Owner requirement: ingest Nixpkgs through an adapter that translates definitions into the canonical native Jet package/build model. Jetpack owns resolution, builds, installation, updates and removal; Hangar is the only store. No separately installed or bundled Nix package manager, Nix daemon, Nix profile, or Nix store is permitted, including hidden or mounted compatibility stores. Native Jet packages bypass the adapter. Existing Nixpkgs packages use the adapter until converted to full native Jet packages. Out-of-the-box support ships with normal Jet/Jetpack installation. This fixes product ownership, not the adapter implementation; no code implementation is authorized in this stream.

Owner licensing choice: Jet/Jetpack code is MIT. Compatible permissive dependencies may retain their licenses and notices. Managed package payloads may use other licenses and retain their original terms. This is not permission to relicense third-party code. Independently, the Nixpkgs adapter must not depend on Nix implementation executables, libraries, daemons, services or storage.

D-NIX-UPSTREAM1 is superseded unratified. Its old A required an upstream Nix provider; its old B retained a bounded subset. Neither matches the owner’s settled native Nixpkgs-to-Jet-package translation requirement. Do not count this as ratification of either old option. Owner direction and licensing answers are recorded in this card; no replacement choice is needed for that settled boundary.

## Goal
Ship a Jet-owned Nixpkgs-to-native translator inside Jetpack. Translated and authored packages share one checked package and build model, Hangar is the only store, and there is no Nix executable, library, daemon, profile or store. Owner contract (c1, met): Jet and Jetpack code is MIT; managed packages keep their own licenses.

## Current state
- No translator exists.
- The installed-Nix escape path is still live in Rust (crates/jetpack/src/NixFallbackPolicy.rs:14,158,242) and was carried into the Jet port: Jetpack/Nix/Source/Fallback/FallbackPolicy.jet:7-8 (JETPACK_NIX_FALLBACK_POLICY and _BIN), :139 (`nix build --json`), :176-179 (PATH discovery). This contradicts the card.
- The bounded evaluator is Jetpack/NixEval (#3600).
- The mixed fixture tests/fixtures/jetpack-project/env.jet currently expects native `hello` to realize and `postgres@nixpkgs` to stay an E1272 hole. That is gap evidence, not completion.

## Changes
1. Cutover: delete the installed-Nix fallback from the Jet port and the Rust reference together: Fallback/FallbackPolicy.jet, FallbackImport.jet, FallbackIdentity.jet, the Nix/Tests/Fallback*.jet claims, the env vars, the flags and the callers. Keep no disabled fallback.
2. Translation:
   - Evaluate Nixpkgs sources with Jetpack/NixEval/Source.
   - Translate dependencies, builders, source identities, platform constraints, path and string contexts, and evaluation-triggered builds into native facts in Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Recipe and Provider plus Jetpack/Provider/Source.
   - Keep upstream provenance so that updates re-translate.
3. Realize and admit only through Jetpack/Store/Source/Hangar:
   - Native builds from translated recipes are the baseline.
   - Build with the #3620 native derivation builder in the sandbox.
   - No /nix/store, mounted store or profile.
   - Any binary reuse separately proves references, integrity, target and license.
4. Preserve:
   - trust, locks, offline mode, precedence and limits;
   - #410's native build-and-boot independence;
   - native packages bypassing the adapter;
   - an ordinary standalone install that needs no Nix;
   - MIT and permissive dependency notices, with no Nix implementation code imported.
5. Unsupported valid packages stay open defects, never silent fallback. Rust crates/jetpack remains reference only.

## Proof
Criterion 11:
1. `JETPACK_WORKER=b19np Tools/agent/jet-env bash Jetpack/Bootstrap/check.sh --tests` -> `JETPACK CHECK OK (check, default run, AOT test)`.
2. The Jet-built jetpack runs a mixed native plus Nixpkgs environment through resolve, build, install, run, update and remove on AOT and default `jet run`, with PATH free of nix. `postgres@nixpkgs` realizes natively instead of raising E1272.

## Dependencies

cards.body:
## Outcome

Deliver the complete applicable LSP 3.18 protocol contract through the real Jet server, with truthful capabilities and an executable applicability inventory.

## Shared stream contract

cards.title: Unify inferred effects, trusted defaults, and restrictive policy
cards.body:
## Current owner direction

This is the existing owner of the effect-policy change, not a new duplicate stream. The owner asked for high-priority delivery during the prep/build interview.

The latest direction changes the default assumed by D-TRUST-LAUNCH1. Preserve that ratified decision as history. Do not implement its old metadata-free prompting rule as the new default.

## Trust prompt rule (owner ruling, 2026-10-01)

The owner rejected the trusted-folder framing and gave this rule in chat (logged on this card 2026-10-01):

- When a program needs trust, Jet asks one question with three answers: Always trust, Once, Cancel.
- Once: run this time only. The next run asks again.
- Always trust: record trust for that target. Later runs never ask again.
- Cancel: do not run.
- A CLI flag that skips the prompt (for example --trusted, or a run-unsafe style flag) answers the prompt as Once. It never records Always.

There is no separate owned-root or trusted-folder concept. Trust comes only from an Always trust answer or from a prompt-skipping flag for that one run. #3705 owns the prompt itself (it absorbed #3419); this card owns the effect model the prompt feeds.

## Requirements stated by the owner

- Always infer and retain effects, including when source omits an effect row. Make the effect facts available for reflection, explanation, and enforcement.
- Do not ask again for a target the user chose Always trust for.
- Provide a deny-by-default restricted mode selected through invocation policy and package/module policy. Enterprise policy can make this the default.
- Positive source effect rows are ceilings. Listing an effect permits it within the source contract but does not prove that the body uses it.
- Authors can explicitly reject effects at package, module, entrypoint, or function scope. Keep positive ceilings and explicit empty ceilings as expert controls.
- In restricted mode, explicit package or function budgets must cover the required effects. Resolve inherited coverage without requiring repeated declarations on every helper.
- Keep implementation source reusable across trust policies. Choosing a policy must not require rewriting function bodies or automatically editing source.
- Dependencies do not inherit trust from the program that uses them.
- Apply one effect model to ordinary execution, shared program preparation, and the AOT build procedure. Keep their effect provenance separate by phase and entrypoint.
- Prep prepares the program for every execution path. For AOT, its results are prepared into the artifact, not rerun as application startup. Build is the AOT procedure for executables, libraries, and linkable objects.

## Model

Keep three facts separate: inferred potential effects, written source ceilings and prohibitions, and approved execution authority (an Always trust record, a Once answer, a prompt-skipping flag, package.jet authority, --allow/--deny, or enterprise policy). A declaration in third-party source never grants itself authority. An outer approved budget can cover unannotated helpers. Inner source can narrow a boundary, not defeat an enclosing mandatory restriction. Enterprise policy is highest.

Always-on compiler tracking is not the same as recording every runtime operation. Static analysis stays conservative for dynamic calls and opaque foreign code: unknown effects are never reported as pure. The owner selected always-available effect provenance and the existing required authorization receipts, with detailed runtime auditing controlled by policy. Enterprise may require that audit; ordinary development does not record every effect occurrence.

No new public spelling is approved by this card. Restricted mode uses the existing --trust/-T axis plus package.jet authority policy; any new syntax needs its own ratification and registry cutover. Ordinary effect trust must not erase independent checks: Secret, FFI, Unsafe, provider consent, environment/package/toolchain trust, and sandbox boundaries stay separate.

## Existing mechanisms

Source inspection, not runtime proof: the Jet homes are Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Authority/Resolver.jet, Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Policy/EffectBudget.jet, Jetpack/Foundation/Source/Authority.jet and Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Effects/Checks.jet. The shipped host resolver is crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs plus the Source/CmdCompile.rs launch paths. Reuse these; do not add a second effect system.

Relevant law: D-EFFECT-OMIT1, D-EFFECT-ROW2, D-EFFBUDGET1, D-TEAMPOLICY1, D-TRUST-LAUNCH1 (history), D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1 (#3705), and D-META-GATE1. Existing source spellings include -[Net]>, -[!Net]>, and -[]>.

## Effect-preserving caching: owner clarification

A cache hit must not suppress an observable effect from a logically invoked operation. A user-written status print remains program behavior. Cache pure computations where valid, but preserve effects and their order at each logical invocation. Do not replace fresh effects with a replay of old console output. Trust selects authority; it does not license an optimizer to remove effects.

Launching an already-prepared AOT artifact does not invoke prep. Shared preparation and compiler-hook details are owned by #3509.
cards.plan:
## Goal
Build one effect-policy model:
- Effects are always inferred and explainable.
- Trust comes from the owner's prompt rule: one prompt (Always trust / Once / Cancel); Once re-prompts next run; Always never prompts again for that target; a prompt-skipping CLI flag counts as Once.
- A deny-by-default restricted mode is selected by invocation or package/enterprise policy.
- Positive rows are ceilings and negative rows are enforced prohibitions.
- The same law applies to run, dev, test, prep and AOT build, with separate provenance for each phase.

## Current state
- Owner ruling 2026-10-01 settles trust establishment (logged on this card). The owned-root ballot in the old plan is withdrawn; no owner gate remains.
- #3705 implements the prompt UI (with #3419's rows). Its own rows still describe the older default-yes confirm; reconcile them with the three-answer rule when that card is worked.
- Jet homes: Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Authority/Resolver.jet, Jetpack/PackageModel/Source/Policy/EffectBudget.jet, Jetpack/Foundation/Source/Authority.jet, Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Effects/Checks.jet. Host mirror: crates/jet-foundation/src/Authority.rs plus Source/CmdCompile.rs launch paths. #3607 ports the PackageModel authority.

## Changes
1. JetSema Effects/Checks.jet: always infer and keep effects, including transitive, generated, callback and opaque calls. Positive rows are checked ceilings; negative or empty rows are prohibitions enforced through reachable calls.
2. PackageModel Resolver.jet / EffectBudget.jet: one resolver. Authority sources, in order: enterprise policy, package.jet authority and --allow/--deny, the Always trust record, a Once answer or prompt-skipping flag (this run only). Enclosing budgets cover inferred helpers. Dependencies never inherit the caller's trust. Package, environment and toolchain authenticity stay separate.
3. Trust store: Always trust writes one record per target; Once and prompt-skipping flags write nothing. Cancel runs nothing and writes nothing.
4. Apply the resolved policy before effects on every run/dev/test/prep/build path. Mirror into Authority.rs and the Source/ launch paths in the same batch (Rust/Jet parity). Prep results persist into AOT artifacts; cache reuse and child execution keep receipts.
5. Migrate the CLI, diagnostics (E1803 family), reflection, examples and tests in one cutover. Coordinate the prompt surface with #3705 and prep capabilities with #3509.

## Proof
Tools/agent/jet-env cargo test --test authority and --test effects pass, including new cases once_answer_reprompts_next_run, always_trust_never_prompts_again, skip_prompt_flag_counts_as_once, restricted_mode_refuses_uncovered_inferred_effect, negative_ceiling_blocks_transitive_callback and dependency_does_not_inherit_caller_trust; tests/ui E1803 snapshots re-blessed through jet test Compiler --profile ui.

## Batch
batch-jetc-sema: effect inference and ceilings live in JetSema. The resolver and host mirror land in the same build.

## Dependencies
None open. #3705 (prompt UI) and #3509 (prep capabilities) are coordinated, not blocking.
cards.checkSteps:
After rebuilding, use isolated harmless fixtures with counted effects and unchanged source hashes. Run the same program under trusted and restricted policy. Exercise inherited package budgets, function positive ceilings, explicit denials, pure functions, dynamic callbacks, foreign-call uncertainty, and a third-party package that tries to declare its own authority.

Cover source and externally selected policy, TTY/no-TTY/CI/JSON, dev edits, child forwarding, required receipt failure, and cache hits after policy changes. Exercise JIT, interpreter, AOT execution, shared prep, and AOT-only build separately. Prove refused effects never occur. Use fake local trust fixtures; do not grant real external trust.

Check that prep runs during AOT preparation and is not rerun by launching the artifact. Check that JIT/interpreter preparation does not execute the AOT build entry. Verify inferred versus declared effects and source-linked refusal from user-facing output. Verify every required audit record and report actual runtime tracing only if exercised.

Existing focused starting points named by this stream are tests/authority_receipts.rs and tests/jet_env_boundary.rs. They are starting points, not proof of the new contract. Add only missing behavioral regressions and run exact focused cases; broad suites are not card proof.

The owned-root ballot is withdrawn, no owner gate remains, needs-owner and needs-info tags removed, phase ready: agent work. #3705 owns the prompt UI.

Owner ruling 2026-10-01 (asked in chat; owner rejected the trusted-folder framing): "there should be a one time request. Always trust, once, or cancel. if once trust, then run once and reprompt in future. If always trust, then no prompt needed in future. for running the cli if a command has a flag to run without the prompt, like run unsafe, trusted, etc. then it should automatically answer the prompt as if it were run once". So: one prompt with three answers (Always trust / Once / Cancel); Once runs and re-prompts next time; Always records trust and never prompts again for that target; a CLI flag that skips the prompt (e.g. --trusted) counts as Once, never as Always.
