cards.title: Constant ranges that can never run: one advisory lint and one written stride law (S19/S22)
cards.body:
Split from the NC-DIAG draft by the fresh review (2026-10-05) and extended with the v3-P2 delta.

NEW small card completing existing law. S22 (inclusive `a..b`) and D-RANGE-EXCL1=C (half-open empty when a >= b) are ratified; S19 states a dynamic nonpositive stride raises E0123. The law never states what a constant inclusive range with start above end, or a constant stride whose sign contradicts the bounds, does; observed behavior is zero iterations. This card documents that behavior (no semantic change) and adds an advisory lint under D-LINTPOLICY1=A, visible per D-LINT-VISIBILITY2=A. Joins the lint family owned by #2141/#3919. No existing card (searched 'reversed range|empty range|descending').

## Actual (dev candidate jet dev-05ea86f65, 2026-10-05; probe p17)

```jet
loop n in 10..1 -> print(n)        // prints nothing; jet check: no problems
loop n in 10..1, -1 -> print(n)    // 10 down to 1
loop n in 1..10, -1 -> print(n)    // prints nothing; jet check: no problems
```

A beginner Python course shows the presenter repeatedly writing a countdown whose start and stride disagree and wondering why nothing happens (youtube 4M87qBgpafk 03:37-03:39). Rust's Clippy treats this as a correctness lint (`reversed_empty_ranges`: "this range is empty so it will yield no values"); R's `1:length(x)`, which counts down to 0 when x is empty, is the commonly cited counterexample against automatic reversal (unfetched corroboration lead; not load-bearing).

## Expected

When both bounds and the stride of a source-loop range or slice bound are compile-time constants and the range is empty because direction and stride disagree, jet check and the editor report a registered advisory with the fix that counts the intended way (`10..1, -1`). Dynamic bounds stay silent: an empty range at run time is legitimate work. The spec states once that a constant inclusive range with start above end and positive stride is empty.

## Stride law gap (PYB-61)

S19 (syntax-decisions.md:537,542-544) specifies only a positive source stride ("Stride N visits source indexes 0, N, 2N") and makes a dynamic nonpositive stride E0123. A constant negative stride is accepted and counts down over the inclusive bounds (`10..1, -1` prints 10..1, prior probe p17) but that meaning is written nowhere. With an empty list the countdown header `xs.len() - 1..0, -1` runs zero times with no error (probe p6). The spec sentence this card adds must cover both: reversed bounds with a positive or omitted stride run zero times; a constant negative stride walks from the first bound down to the second inclusive.

Re-confirmed on release dev-05ea86f65 (sha256 bc088ced...f9b): probe p4 `loop i in 10..1` and `loop j in 0..1, -1` print nothing, `jet check` clean; probe p6 empty-list countdown prints only 'done'. Course witnesses: 4M87 3:37-3:39 (PYB-3) and 5:15-5:17 descending index loop (PYB-61).

log.text: Folded into #6006 as a criterion (CardTrim 2026-10-28).

criteria.text: `10..1` and `1..10, -1` with constant bounds in a source loop produce one registered advisory lint each with a structured fix; `0..<0`, ranges with any non-constant bound, and intentionally empty fixture ranges do not.
The lint never changes exit codes and follows D-LINT-VISIBILITY2; a UI snapshot pins the report.
Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md S22 states the empty-range rule for inclusive ranges in one sentence; range_step.jet shows the countdown form.

S19 states the meaning of a constant negative stride (countdown over inclusive bounds) and of reversed bounds without one, with an example in Examples/features/basics/range_step.jet whose expected output is golden-tested.

cards.title: jet learn: a zero-experience beginner arc from first value to first small project
cards.body:
NEW content card attaching to ratified D-LEARN1 (#1918: 'one offline path from install to competence'; exercise suite runs in CI) and D-LEARN-FEEDBACK1=A (#2947: predict, then reveal), consuming the learning census (#2926) and the first-hour script (#2900). Uses the existing jet learn runner, schema jet-learning-curriculum-v1 and Examples/learn layout; no new runner, tutor, AI mode or language levels (D-LEARN1 scope; learnability report 5.1 notes one-mechanism excludes language levels). Builds on D-EXAMPLES-SHORTPATH1=A (short path first). Not a duplicate: today's curriculum has 3 repair katas (Examples/learn/first_arc) and 4 predict tasks (loop, borrow/state, effects, foreign bindings); no task covers values, functions/return, branches, collections, maps/sets, failures or tests for a learner with no prior programming.

## Why

Jet's goal includes people who have never programmed. D-LEARN1 ratified a toolchain track 'from install to competence'. The packaged curriculum today starts at loop ranges and jumps to borrow views, effect rows and foreign bindings; the first-hour guide teaches the tool flow (new, run, check, test, explain), not programming. A complete 7-hour beginner course (Boot.dev Python for Beginners, youtube 4M87qBgpafk, ~100 exercises, 12 chapters, reviewed end to end in this batch) gives a measured-in-practice ordering and, more valuable, a corpus of misconceptions the instructor herself demonstrated on camera.

## Deliverable

One additional arc in the existing curriculum, about 12-16 tasks, each a jet-learning-curriculum-v1 task with prediction, reveal, counterexample, controlled edit and transfer. Order (course chapter in parentheses):

1. Output and values; `print` vs program result (ch1-2).
2. Bindings `::`/`:=`, interpolation and `{x=}` (ch2).
3. Functions with a result type; return vs print (ch3; the course's most repeated error).
4. Block scope and if-as-value (ch4; Python's function scope is the transfer trap).
5. Tests beside code and `debug(value)` instead of temporary prints (ch5; the course repeatedly tells learners to delete debug prints before submitting; Jet's debug() writes to stderr and release builds reject leftovers, E3405).
6. Exact division, `/%` floor division and signs (ch6; the instructor's own negative floor-division slip).
7. Bool-only conditions and ordered arm tables (ch7; truthiness and overlapping independent ifs).
8. Inclusive ranges, stride and the countdown (ch8; off-by-one and empty countdown).
9. Lists: value iteration first, indexes on demand, empty-list contracts (ch9).
10. Maps: missing-key outcome, counting, sorted iteration (ch10).
11. Sets: membership vs multiplicity; what dedupe preserves (ch11). Open evidence gap: no verified order-preserving distinct-values spelling (`.unique()` is E0311; `lazy().dedup()` collapses only consecutive runs) — resolve the canonical spelling before authoring this task.
12. Failures as typed values: `??`, propagation, matching by case not by message text, unreachable arms (ch12).
13. Capstone: a small text-processing project combining 9-12 (course ch9 capstone shape).

## Misconception seeds (wrong_model fields) taken from the source body

Floor division is truncation (01:59-02:03); the last index is the length (03:50-04:00); a set prints in a different order every time (06:22-06:23); distinct values have distinct hashes (06:25-06:27); removing an absent key is invisible (06:02-06:04; in Jet `&m.pop(k)` returns `.None`, which the learner must handle); None and 0 mean the same 'no arrows' (06:56-06:58); a broad handler before a specific one is fine (06:59-07:00); an error is identified by its message text (07:04-07:06); printing a value returns it (01:13-01:16).

## Hidden boundary case per task

The course's run-versus-submit split catches empty input, ties and absent keys that the visible examples omit. Each task's oracle adds at least one boundary input (empty, absent, zero, tie) that the learner does not see before the reveal.

Extra witness: '31 nooby C++ habits' (youtube i_wDa2AS_8w) shows that most beginner traps are structurally absent in Jet; the arc should show the absence (the compile error or the missing construct) rather than only the happy path.

Additions from the v3-P1 depth-gate re-mine of the course's first half ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/mine/v3/P1-python-a, supersedes the first-pass PY claims for 0:00-3:35): the course's single-domain ordering (print, variables, functions, scope, tests, arithmetic, comparisons, loops) is the arc's spine (PYA-001); hidden Submit cases map to D-TEST1 property generation for each task's boundary inputs (PYA-059); visible branch coverage (#1904) answers 'which branches did my tests reach' (PYA-099); the equal-bounds transfer trap is new: Python range(5, 5) is empty but Jet 5..5 has one item and only 5..<5 is empty (PYA-110); the course's 'make it global' NameError fix is an anti-lesson the arc must teach against, because Jet does have mutable module globals (spec.md:230-237; PYA-055); never copy the plaintext-password login demo (Argon2id policy; PYA-086); the 'a decimal point means float' and container-of-value definitions are misconception seeds (PYA-021, PYA-012).

Distilled 2026-10-05 by DistillLang from the six mining batches; Tower snapshot rev 74843 (jet-state digest INCONSISTENT during collection: rerun before posting).

Learn arc additions from the claims pass: hidden boundary cases from property tests (v3-P1:PYA-059, v3-P2:PYB-59), learner-visible branch coverage (PYA-099), zero-install browser lane balloted separately.

cards.title: Prove jet perf on a game-frame workflow: wait attribution, inclusive time, recursion, scoped spans
cards.body: #2997 (profiler source hotspots) and #2487 (frame profiler) are done, but four questions from game-thread profiling are unproven for Jet. Unreal Insights talk (KxREK-DYu70 10:00-12:00): WaitForTasks gaps are attributed to the awaited task by manually aligning timelines; the fix was to start that work earlier, so a frame critical path matters; timer tables show count, inclusive and exclusive time; capture channels and profile build configuration change results; a frame strip coloured against the budget finds hitches first. Jai iprof (DaJWWePhRsM; Win32 re-mine DAJ-12, DAJL-01): time does not bubble correctly to parents of recursive zones, and manually balanced begin/end zones crash or slow down when an early return skips the end; misused manual instrumentation records nothing silently (DAJ-60). Jet knows join edges, spans and budgets at the language level, so each should be answerable without manual alignment.
cards.plan: Write one game-shaped program (a frame that joins a task group, a recursive function, early returns inside core.log spans, a declared D-GAME-BUDGET1 frame budget) and capture it with jet perf on the shipping toolchain. Check each criterion; fix gaps in the existing profiler and trace product, reusing #2528's critical-path computation, with no second recorder.

log.text: #6563 c1 precut audit re-added 1 criteria from archived #2487: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

Per source location, inclusive and exclusive time are both reported; a recursive fib reports inclusive time without double counting.
A core.log LogSpan left by an early return or failure is closed at scope exit and visible in .jettrace; an unclosed manual span is reported, never silently dropped.
Frames are coloured against the declared D-GAME-BUDGET1 budget, and a frame critical path reuses the #2528 computation.
The receipt names the build profile and capture settings used.

(was #2487 c1) Frame profiling and draw-event tracing work through typed game events, bounded canonical relay, strict identity/truncation checks, and perf run/attach consumption, proven by runtime tests on every applicable tier.

cards.title: Stdout buffering: terminal lines, file/pipe batches, meaningful flush and ordered stops
cards.body:
mCoding (i_wDa2AS_8w 00:43-00:54) lists std::endl in a loop as a beginner habit because it flushes every line. Jet does this for every program with no opt-out: jet_term_write_stdout_bytes (Prelude Term.rs:152-161) flushes when `flush || !bytes.is_empty() || is_terminal`, and every print frame is non-empty, so every print, stdout.write and stdout.write_line flushes even into a file or pipe. The flush argument is dead (Term.rs:158; FSIoEnvOsTesting.rs:279-301 pass false and still flush) and the explicit stdout.flush() that D-COREIO1's story relies on does nothing. The stated reason (Term.rs:156-157) is stdout/stderr ordering on one sink, which can be kept without per-write flushing: buffer stdout only when it is not a terminal and flush before any stderr write, stdin read, child process start, runtime stop report, exit and explicit flush. Source reading only; cost unmeasured. Under D-EXEC1 the policy belongs to the one runtime (#4013).

Current application amendment (2026-10-07, #27 clarified by #29/#31; Sol writes / Opus reviews #28):
D-STDOUT-BUFFER1=A
Measurement-before-change receipts include syscall counts and matched timings for 1M/2M lines/file/pipe/terminal; one shared Jet stdout buffering policy selected from TTY fact; stderr never delayed; flush occurs before every named boundary including first report/stderr; prompt visible before input; explicit flush works; native image print issues one buffered write; existing interleaving and stop-prefix goldens retained.

Timing: JET RUNTIME PORT NOW, RtL7 owns buffering; minimal both-half port/seed seam allowed #29 and dies at cutover. Actual Jet flush/buffer layer REQUIRED #31; frozen Rust flush is only a tracked temporary seed/verification path. cards.title: http.serve must route through the Jet-owned server runtime
cards.body:
http.serve must not bypass the Jet server runtime: requests go through the Core/http Jet port (#3665) for routing and response handling. The Rust-side routes and server paths named in the old body are removed with Rust removal #4717. Criteria: serve() uses the same route table on every tier; a golden request covers routing and a bad-request path.

Earlier text, kept for reference (Rust-era homes such as Rust crates, TIR/MIR/LIR, the JIT and generated Rust are retired):

Source reading on dev 3f64b4fb6 (v3 H2-http-b re-mine of FknTw9bJsXM 181:29-192:02; not executed). Jet has two server runtimes. The mux path bounds admission, wraps handlers and middleware in catch_unwind, keeps connections alive and drains on shutdown with an atomic flag. But http.serve(addr, lambda) and router serve lower to jet_http_serve (routes.rs:8046 to HTTPServer.rs:6898-6941), which spawns one OS thread per connection without bound, has no panic isolation, always sends Connection: close, has no shutdown path and calls process::exit(1) on a bind failure. Accept errors are mishandled on both paths: the mux loop stops serving and force-cancels every active stream on any non-WouldBlock accept error such as EMFILE (HTTPServer.rs:2280-2288), while the lambda loop prints E2801 and retries in a tight loop (6914-6919). The serializer has four divergent reason-phrase tables and falls back to "OK", so a 503, 429 or 422 goes out as "503 OK" (HTTPServer.rs:5761-5783, 1504-1524, 5025; http.jet:312-381). #3666 (server framing) is done on the board but this policy is still present, and the earlier mining claim that Jet bounds admission holds only for the mux path. Unverified: the default jet run tier's route to jet_http_serve was not traced (the JIT host path is being retired); the AOT route was.

Fresh review 2026-10-05: protocol parsing and framing criteria for the same course stay on #3665 (attached there); graceful drain must reuse the App lifecycle of #3078 rather than a second shutdown path.
cards.plan: 1. Reproduce per tier: a lambda-served program under a connection flood (thread count), a panicking handler, SIGTERM during a slow request, a port already in use, and fd exhaustion. 2. Route every serve spelling (lambda, router, mux) through one server runtime with bounded admission, panic page, keep-alive, graceful drain and a typed bind error returned to the caller. 3. One accept policy: classify transient errors (EMFILE, ENFILE, ECONNABORTED), back off with a cap and keep serving; fatal listener errors end the server with a report. 4. One reason table in Core: an unknown code gets an empty reason (valid per RFC 9112 s4), never another code's text. 5. Under the Rust freeze, land the policy in the Core/http Jet port (#3665) with Rust keeping only provider leaves, and delete the duplicate runtime in the same cutover.

cards.title: Build the ratified strong pause: pause(mode: .CheckLoops) and one shared back-edge check on every engine
cards.body:
D-TASK-PAUSE-TIER1=E (ratified 2026-07-31) gives experts a strong pause: `handle.pause(mode: .CheckLoops)` stops a task at its next loop back-edge on every engine, while default pause stays at wait points. It is unbuilt. Exercised on release jet dev-05ea86f65: `t.pause(mode: .CheckLoops)` is rejected with E0764 ('pause has no parameter labelled mode'). Source reading at master 3e5349196: Prelude Scheduler.rs:1343-1359 defines `jet_scheduler_loop_pause_check` and nothing calls it. Today a busy task also ignores cancellation, #Context deadlines and fair turns until it waits: task.race drains a busy loser by blocking on it (TaskGroup.rs:485-498, Scheduler.rs:3956-3959), while plugins already stop runaway guests with Wasmtime epoch interruption (Plugin.rs:240-243, 1372-1406). Sources: Riot talk IxQ586TS8Gw 45:46-48:32 ('a while-true actor bricks the scheduler'); BEAM talk RntfkL8lUY4 ('a greedy green thread can never block the scheduler'). This card builds the one shared back-edge mechanism. Ballot D-TASK-SLICE1 decides whether cancellation, deadlines and fair turns also use it by default.

Fresh review 2026-10-05: this card builds only ratified D-TASK-PAUSE-TIER1=E, which needs no vote. Whether cancellation, deadlines and fair turns also use these sites is ballot D-TASK-SLICE1 on its own card (key N-TASKSLICE), so this work is never blocked by that vote.
cards.plan: 1. Register `pause(mode:)` and `PauseMode` once; the self-hosted compiler accepts the same form. 2. One per-worker attention word; back-edge and recursive-entry checks emitted from one shared lowering rule on every engine and optimisation level; strip-mine counted loops; elide checks in loops that already reach a wait point. 3. Strong pause delivers through the existing Prelude hook. 4. Leave the attention word ready for D-TASK-SLICE1 delivery without turning any default on. 5. Measure under the strict performance gate on the #2254 hot-loop kernels before any default turns on.

log.text: N-TASKLOOP: a detached task spinning without a wait point keeps the process alive after run returns; other tasks still progress (APICompLangB r4_spin_starvation: rc 124 after 40 s). jet check on `loop { n += 1 }` in a spawned fn reports no problems (p09). Add the exit contract for detached tasks at run return.

criteria.text: A golden spawns a task running `loop { n += 1 }`, calls `handle.pause(mode: .CheckLoops)`, observes `paused=true` within a bounded wait, then resumes and cancels it; identical on every execution level.
The same program with default `pause()` documents that the loop keeps running (wait-point law), with identical output on every level.
The back-edge check comes from one shared lowering rule; a test fails if any engine omits it.
Default-mode cost on the #2254 hot-loop kernels is within noise under the strict performance gate, recorded in the canonical manifest.
Spec, core-library and examples updated; no second cancellation or scheduling mechanism is added.

cards.title: Busy tasks honour cancellation, deadlines and fair turns at loop turns (ballot D-TASK-SLICE1)
cards.body:
Host card for owner ballot D-TASK-SLICE1, split by the fresh review (2026-10-05) from the strong-pause build (key N-TASKLOOP) so ratified work is not held by this vote.

Today a task that never waits ignores cancellation, #Context deadlines and fair turns: task.race drains a busy loser by blocking on it (TaskGroup.rs:485-498, Scheduler.rs:3956-3959), a request deadline cannot stop a runaway handler, and busy tasks can starve others. D-FOUND-LIFECYCLE1=A states this as its tradeoff. Plugins already stop runaway guests by epoch interruption (Plugin.rs:240-243, D-CORE-PLUGINLIMITS1=A). Sources: Riot talk IxQ586TS8Gw 45:46-48:32 (a while-true actor bricks a cooperative scheduler), BEAM reduction budgets (RntfkL8lUY4), Go 1.14 asynchronous preemption.

Implement only the ratified outcome, through the back-edge sites built by N-TASKLOOP and the D-CANCELMODEL1 unwind path.

criteria.text: D-TASK-SLICE1 is ratified and this card implements only its outcome.

criteria.text: D-TASK-SLICE1 is ratified and its outcome is implemented: for A, task.race/any/all return within one slice of their decision when a loser is busy, a #Context deadline and SIGTERM drain stop a busy handler with Drop cleanup, and busy tasks cannot starve a runnable task beyond a bounded number of slices.
Any new default turns on only after the #2254 hot-loop kernels show no measurable slowdown under the strict performance gate; until then the wait-point rule stays.
Spec (D-FOUND-LIFECYCLE1 tradeoff, D-CANCELMODEL1), core-library and examples state the ratified rule once; no second cancellation or scheduling mechanism is added.

cards.body: Proven: print(2 ** 3) gives E0208 "Taking a raw pointer requires #Unsafe" (t25). print(7 // 2) gives only E0083 unclosed ( (t26). cards.title: REPL runtime failures keep committed prefix; fatal stops restart and list lost bindings
cards.body:
D-REPL-FAIL1=A is ratified. Keep already-executed mutations/output and earlier published bindings on recoverable runtime failure; discard failed-turn unpublished slots. Fatal panic/trap/resource exhaustion restarts child, lists lost bindings, never replays. No transactional clone/rollback feature is required. Static check rollback remains exact. Native session host admission is #4720.

Current application amendment (2026-10-07, #27 clarified by #29/#31; Sol writes / Opus reviews #28):
D-REPL-FAIL1=A
Recoverable runtime failure retains earlier published slots and already-executed mutation/output prefix, frees failed turn unpublished names through native slot ABI without clone/glue; ordinary static failures roll back exactly; panic/trap/host fault and stack E3012/MaxDepth/OOM restart child, state which names lost and never replay; registered run report identical; notebook failed cell publishes no names, descendants stale, earlier cells unchanged; demonstrate canonical push4/bad-index case once host admitted.
Paths: Compiler/JetBackend/Source/Image/SessionHost.jet; OS/{SessionTransport,SessionOutput,Linux}.jet; Lower/{Callable,ComptimeBoundary}.jet; Compiler/{JetEval/Source,JetSema/Source/Sema,JetCodegen/Source/Codegen}/ReplSteps.jet in ExecHostEntry1 worktree; runtime published/unpublished session slot ABI; notebook descendant invalidation
Registry/spec/UI/goldens: No Syntax.rs language change; session/report/native ABI decision provenance D-REPL-FAIL1=A/D-RTFAIL1/D-EXEC3; E3012/report reset/lost-name rows consumed unchanged where already registered; Docs/spec/reference/cli.md REPL failure-prefix/session reset; syntax-decisions D-REPL-FAIL1 with D-RESOURCE-LIMIT1/D-DX-CELLS1; #4719 body removes clone/rollback requirement; #4720 drops Learn current scope; Recoverable failure registered same report as run, no automatic session reset; failed-turn name unknown; fatal resource stop report E3012/#MaxDepth/OOM + lost names; notebook stale-descendant snapshot; static failure exact rollback preserved; items=[1,2,3], push4 then bad index retains [1,2,3,4]; earlier bindings survive, unpublished new slots released without glue; cancellation/deadline prefix retained; panic/trap/host loss/resource stop child restart never replay; prior output preserved; notebook earlier cells unchanged/descendants stale
Timing: JET NOW in owned native retained-session work, waits #4720 producer/slot admission, not Rust exit. Do not implement Rust cloning/transaction snapshot or resurrect evaluator/Learn path. CURRENT #29/#31: a MINIMAL seam necessary to port an existing Core row/runtime layer/test harness may also change the Rust half, registered as dies at cutover; all actual layer policy/carriers must still be ported to Jet. This exception does not permit duplicating new features. #28 Sol authors, Opus reviews. Features outside required port work resume after port/Rust exit; contract/docs/tests planning may be prepared now.
Open prerequisite/conflict: ExecHostEntry2 initially reports BudgetDepth preserves slots; clarified bounded COMPTIME budget != REPL MaxDepth/resource stop and committed turn/resource BudgetDepth fatal adjustment. Track distinction, not blanket-reset all budgets. #4719 old transaction/clone brief wrong; #4720 Learn removed by owner. Session producer still unfinished/unadmitted, ratification not admission.

cards.title: Move dev canvas, debug and retained REPL off the evaluator; Learn excluded
cards.body:
Implementation task under ratified decisions; no owner decision is needed. D-EXEC1 = A: one runtime; O0 serves run, dev and compile-time code. D-EXEC2 = A: until the native backend covers every program, run and dev use the build path and execute the result; dev rebuilds and restarts on a saved change instead of replacing functions in a running process. D-DX-DEBUGBACK1 = A: reverse execution extends jet debug. Work: (1) jet dev --canvas: restart on save per D-EXEC2; live values stream from the built program over the devtools channel. (2) jet debug: the native LLDB/DAP backend becomes the only backend; record/replay and reverse execution stay in jet debug per D-DX-DEBUGBACK1 through a native recorder. (3) jet repl: each input runs through the build-and-execute path (reuse :run). (4) Learn (REMOVED; e10 frozen, no current delivery): run the exercise as a child jet run and compare output. Owner: JitRemoval2. Context: $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/JitRemoval1/HANDOFF.md.

Current scope: NO Learn evaluator retirement/reimplementation or browser lane; owner #4752 removes it, #4630 frozen e10. D-REPL-FAIL1=A supplies prefix-preserving recoverable failure and fatal resource-stop restart/lost-name behavior; retained producer still requires admission. #29 permits minimal port seams only, with dies-at-cutover ledger; #31 forbids skipping actual Jet runtime ports.

log.text: Folded #5051 "Jetpack reaches the compiler through one `jet check --listen=-` session; delete `jet __jetpack`" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #4720 (Move dev canvas, debug and retained REPL off); 3 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: ## Outcome D-JETPACK-SERVICE1=A with D-SESSION-ENTRY1=C. Each Jetpack command starts one `jet check --listen=-` child, or attaches to a running `jet dev --serve` / `jet self lsp --serve` endpoint. cards.title: Public-by-default visibility and local imports with declaration re-exports
cards.body:
Owner directive, 2026-10-07, clarified in chat (Odin/GingerBill model adapted to Jet; a Jet module plays the role of an Odin package). Supersedes D-MOD3, D-VISDEFAULT2, D-PUBPKG1 and the #PubFile / priv-subtree rules.

Rules:
(1) Everything is public by default. Declarations (fn, struct, enum, trait, const, type alias, and so on) never carry a visibility marker.
(2) The only keyword is `priv`; `pub` is removed from the language.
(3) A module may be marked private: `priv module name { ... }` (and the equivalent marker for a file module). Plain `priv` means its contents are usable only by its enclosing module and that module's other children. `priv(package)` means usable by any module of the same package and invisible to other packages.
(4) Field exception: a struct or record field may be `priv`; it is readable and writable only by code in the type's own module (and its children). This keeps invariants for types like Secret, native handles and validated values.
(5) Removed: `pub`, `pub(package)`, `#PubFile`, and `priv` on non-module declarations. They are no longer Jet syntax and get no teaching diagnostic (owner order: no teaching errors for old syntax).
(6) Packages: no package-level privacy in this cutover (later, through the manifest).
(7) D-VIS-REEXPORT1=A: imports stay local; bare paths to declarations re-export through name: path (D-DECL-COLON1=A); pub use retires. Aliases are written Rows: [[String]] (D-DECL-COLON1=A) and generic aliases Grid<T>: [[T]] (D-ALIAS-GENERIC1=A); the alias keyword of D-ALIAS-BIND2=B is superseded.

Cutover: parser and sema in both compiler halves, Syntax.rs registration and decision IDs, diagnostics with UI snapshots, the spec (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md S18 and the reference), and every in-repo Jet file (Compiler/, Core/, Jetpack/, Examples/, tests/) migrated in one commit by a re-runnable rewrite script, so in-flight branches can apply it too. Helpers that were private declarations move into `priv module`s or stay public; invariant-carrying fields become `priv` fields.

Acceptance: no `pub` and no declaration-level `priv` anywhere in the repo; `priv module` and `priv(package) module` access rules and the `priv` field rule each have UI snapshots for the allowed and rejected cases; goldens and the compiler fixed point unchanged in behavior.

cards.title: jet perf memory method: per-line cache, TLB and page-fault counts, and a memory-level view in the code map
cards.body:
Owner note: 'Cache hits are critical: how can we give control over L1, L2, L3 cache, and visualize when we are no longer in cache and go to RAM or SSD?' (OwnerNotes1 digest section 1). Jet has layout control (D-PLACE1, D-LAYOUT-ALIGN1, D-LAYOUT-SHOW1), Columns<T> (D-SOA-SITE1), cache blocking (D-ACCEL1), a cost view (D-COSTLAW1) and source-line profiles (D-PROFILE-DETAIL1, D-PROFILE-METHOD1), but nothing measures or shows cache behavior. This card adds measurement only; user-facing cache hints are ballot D-CACHE-CONTROL1.

Scope: a third profile method beside sample and count, reading hardware counters (Linux perf_event_open first: L1D misses, last-level misses, dTLB misses, minor and major page faults), attributed to the same source rows D-PROFILE-DETAIL1 keeps. Rows state the counter set, the CPU and completeness, as D-PROFILE-METHOD1 requires. The code map (D-CODEMAP-VIEW1) gains a mode that shades lines by where their data came from (L1, L2, L3, RAM, disk), derived from the counters. Unsupported hosts report 'unavailable' with the reason, never zeros.

The exact flag spelling (for example --profile-method=memory) extends an approved command; if review judges it a new public command surface, raise a short ballot first.
cards.plan: 1. Counter reader in the Jet runtime behind core.mem.native (D-RT-NATIVE-CAP1). 2. Attribution to source rows. 3. Report rows and JSON. 4. Code-map mode. 5. Golden: a strided-vs-sequential array walk shows the expected miss ratio ordering.

cards.title: Quaternion in core.math (reserved j/k literals), usable F16, and Decimal-with-Complex literals
cards.body:
Owner note: 'include primitive types that Odin does: quaternions, endian types, complex numbers' (OwnerNotes1 digest section 6). Complex is built (D-NUMTYPE1, 3i literals). D-LITCARRIER1=D reserves i, j, k and shows `q: 1 + 2i + 3j + 4k -> Quaternion`, but no Quaternion type exists anywhere in Core, Compiler or crates. Probes on dev-595e0dca3: `F16{1.5}` is E0108 ('needs F16, value is Decimal') and `print` of an F16 is E0112, although D-LOWFLOAT1 ratified F16; and `2.0 + 3.0i` is E0109 ('Decimal and Complex') because a bare 2.0 is Decimal.

Scope: (1) Quaternion beside Complex in core.math as an ordinary Core struct of four Floats, built from the reserved j/k component literals, with `*` as the Hamilton product, `+`, `-`, scalar `*`, conj, norm, normalize, inverse, from_axis_angle, rotate(Vec3) and slerp, all through the existing operator hooks (D-OPMIX1). (2) F16/BF16 literals and printing per D-LOWFLOAT1. (3) A decimal literal next to a Complex or Quaternion adopts Float the way an expected Float parameter does (D-LITCARRIER1 inference), so `2.0 + 3.0i` works. Item (1) follows the ratified reservation; if review finds any method name needs owner choice, raise a short ballot for it. Endian types are ballot D-ENDIAN-TYPES1.

cards.title: Portable first-party GPU kernel library in core.compute, written as #Kernel Jet, checked against the CPU result
cards.body:
Owner notes: 'Mojo supports split compilation on CPU/GPU ... has a portable GPU kernel library; can Jet do similar?' and 'need a cohesive experience to push code to the GPU' (OwnerNotes1 digest section 20). The design is ratified: core.compute owns operations and devices (D-COMPUTE1, D-COMPUTE-TYPE1), placement is automatic with receipts (D-COMPUTE-PLACE1), safe kernels are `#Kernel(.parallel)` Jet functions launched with `compute.launch` (D-COMPUTE-KERNEL-SURFACE1, D-GPU-COMPUTE-LAUNCH1), one portable contract with a CPU oracle covers CPU SIMD, CUDA, Metal, Vulkan and WebGPU (D-COMPUTE-BACKEND1). In the tree there is no GPU code generator (no SPIR-V/PTX/MSL emitter in Compiler/, no GPU crate) [INFERENCE: compute runs on CPU today]. Cards #3026 (user-authored kernels) and #3028 (GPU provider matrix and real dispatch) are prerequisites.

Scope after #3026 and #3028: a kernel library in core.compute written as ordinary #Kernel Jet code: elementwise map, reductions, prefix scan, radix sort, matrix multiply with tiles (D-GPU-TILE-SCOPE1), convolution, softmax and attention. Each kernel has a CPU reference test under each precision profile and a gauntlet cell against the vendor library on the same device (AGENTS.md performance gate). Beginners keep using tensor operations and compute.launch; no new syntax.

cards.title: Portable math: sin, cos, exp, log and pow written in Jet with stated accuracy and identical bits on every tier and target
cards.body:
Owner note: 'Sine is defined in Mojo so that it is portable; I want custom declarations where we can to make Jet code more portable and accurate' (OwnerNotes1 digest section 21). Today `math.sin` forwards to the compiler built-in `core.math.sin` (Core/math/math.jet:122) [INFERENCE: ends in the host libm through the Rust runtime], so results may differ in the last bit between systems, and they cannot serve as the CPU oracle GPU results are checked against (D-COMPUTE-BACKEND1). Directive 19 (no Rust) also requires these leaves to move into Jet.

Scope: implement the elementary functions in core.math as Jet code with a stated error bound per function (correctly rounded where the cost is acceptable, after the CORE-MATH project's results), using D-CORE-BOUNDARY1 instruction entries for chip speed-ups whose plain Jet body defines the meaning. Faster, looser versions are available only through a named compute precision profile, never silently. Test identical bits across jet run, jet build, release and every supported target.

cards.title: Execution architecture: shared meaning, portability boundaries and reported quick-run waits
cards.body:
Owner direction (2026-10-07): one meaning structurally (AOT tiers only optimize, never change behavior); no running every test on every tier; a hardware-agnostic optimizer then hardware-specific AOT; a native-speed immediate tier instead of a slow interpreter; portability strong enough to replace Wasm/JS, plus a sandbox.

Research: $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/ExecArch1/RESEARCH.md (revision 2; adversarial audit AUDIT-adversary.md and fact-check AUDIT-Verifier.md beside it, both 'sound after repairs'; all 63 findings answered in §12). Owner questions and where each is settled: §9 and §9.12.

Ballots: D-EXEC3 (overall: shared optimizations, test policy, quick-run code generator chosen by measured contest; amends I5, I9 and D-EXEC1's code-generator clause), D-RESOURCE-LIMIT1 (stack/memory limits across levels), D-PERF-RUNCELL1 (is `jet run` time-to-answer a gated benchmark), D-PORTABLE2 (machine-code checker for the sandbox; reconciles D-PORTABLE1's interpreter start with D-EXEC2).

Already settled, no ballot: CPU floating point (D-SIMD3, D-CPU-DISPATCH1, D-COMPUTE-BACKEND1), precise traps (D-RTFAIL1, D-FAIL-BREACH1), capabilities vs authority and browser stance and portable boundary (D-PORTABLE1, D-WASISRV1), tier-up/OSR (D-ADAPTIVE-TIER1).

Current application amendment (2026-10-07, #27 clarified by #29/#31; Sol writes / Opus reviews #28):
D-PERF-RUNCELL1=B
Canonical gauntlet records same end-to-end run metric/peers/commands and precisely defined after-edit/repeat/install cache states as reported-only columns; gate/card/release selectors ignore these cells even when losing; required execution-time/build-time/native optimization cells remain fully gated.
Paths: Tools/gauntlet/{measurement-manifest.json,status.mjs} run end-to-end metrics/cache states; performance reports; Tools/agent release/card gate selectors exclude reported-only cells
Registry/spec/UI/goldens: No Syntax.rs/keyword/marker change. Canonical metric manifest cites D-PERF-RUNCELL1=B, report-only classification distinct from required gate; Docs/spec performance measurement rules/AGENTS scope note; architecture D-PERF-RUNCELL1=B; CLOSURE7.14 report state; do not weaken other required runtime/build cells; Performance report columns show end-to-end wait/time-to-first-output and cache state with report-only label; no diagnostic or UI language snapshot required; After edit: product caches cold, prebuilt standard libs kept; repeat warm; first after install also reported, not gated; hello + small CLI/script peer commands reproducible; performance summary/gate fixture proves losing run-wait never holds release
Timing: TOOLS/REPORTING NOW; no new feature/compiler seam or Rust-half work. #29 prioritizes ports; reported quick-run waits NEVER hold port/Rust-exit/release. Required runtime/build cells remain gates. #28 Sol author/Opus review.
Open prerequisite/conflict: Ballot CHECK acceptance text covers A only; chosen B expressly ignores metric for gates/cards. Do not hold Rust exit/release/NativeO2 progress on these cells or interpret B as dropping required runtime speed gates.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT); D-EXEC2=A (native code generator only; Cranelift and MIREval are retired).

Owner direction 2026-10-23: every improvement that takes the compiler to 30M lines/s must also be applied to codegen, so all code Jet generates is as fast as physically possible without taking control from experts. Rule for the throughput work: each slice is tagged GENERAL (a runtime, codegen or Core mechanism any Jet program gets automatically) or COMPILER-ONLY (a data-structure choice inside the compiler). Prefer GENERAL: implement it once in codegen/runtime/Core and let the compiler benefit as an ordinary Jet program (I8 one mechanism). Examples: non-atomic RC unless shared (#5475), frozen immortal constants (mapfreeze), no reclamation at process end (#5478), escape-proven bump/arena placement (Goose lesson), small-Int fast paths, tag compare (#5473), Shared/queue primitives without futex waits on hot paths, the work-stealing task scheduler, hashed Map instead of binary search (#5474), COW uniqueness at every place (#5480). COMPILER-ONLY wins (interned ids, SoA AST/IR) are each followed by a ticket asking how codegen or Core can give user programs the same (for example Columns<T>/SoA layout, an interned Symbol type, or arenas via escape analysis). Experts keep control via the existing explicit surfaces (layout attributes, #Region, #Unsafe, explicit allocators); defaults stay safe.

Owner direction 2026-10-23 ~08:45 (performance target): generated machine code must land roughly at the physical floor, i.e. what hand-written asm/binary achieves on the same machine. Jet aims to be the fastest language in existence, barring hand-written asm where that is physically faster; every case where hand-written code beats Jet is a codegen lesson to learn. A beginner who wants the best out-of-the-box performance must get near-floor code (aside from glaring design issues in their program), and it must beat C and Rust. Experts keep complete control and configurability. Consider advanced techniques. Implication: the perf manifest should gain hand-written asm floor references beside C/Rust/node/luajit for the core cells, and each gap to the floor is a carded codegen lesson.

Owner ruling 2026-10-23 ~07:30: profile reuse approved. Profiles gathered by jet run's O0 counters may feed O2 (tier-up) and jet build --release, and may be cached between runs in the project's .jet/ folder (beside the other jet data such as post-comptime expanded code). Condition: the cache must be robust and never go stale. Design requirements given to O0Load: per-function entries keyed by a content hash of the function's checked IR plus compiler identity, target and opt level, so an edit invalidates exactly the changed functions; mismatched or unreadable entries are discarded, never trusted; profiles are advisory only (they change optimization choices, never meaning; the O0-vs-O2 differential gate still applies); atomic write (temp file + rename) and safe under concurrent jet processes; one format version, mismatch = discard; size cap with eviction; removed by the existing clean path; --verbose reports profile hits and misses. Open owner question still to ballot: should jet build --release use a cached profile by default (build output then depends on local .jet state) or only when asked?

Owner 2026-10-23 ~07:00: tier-up stays required (start at O0, rise quickly to O1, approach O2 in long jet run; effectively a JIT). Separate and first: absolute performance is far off (O1 vs gcc -O2: fib 20.0 vs 3.9 ms, sieve 112 vs 9.1, push+sum 31 vs 9.0; jet run hello 186 ms vs lua 2 ms). O1/O2 must be real optimizing tiers (O2 essentially perfectly optimized, O1 the middle ground; more compile time allowed). Lanes: O0Image -> O1/O2 optimizer after the image slice; O0Speed -> startup + O0 codegen; tier-up lane after O0 completes (O0Load is the natural owner; the compiler stays resident beside the program).

O0Speed tier-up evidence (2026-10-23 ~06:50, HEAD+codecword, 7 runs median): fib(32) O0 21.6 / O1 21.1 / O2 21.1 ms; sieve 5M+2M structs 216/195/196 ms; with intdiv loop 68.0 vs 68.1, arith 221 vs 213. Max tier-up gain about 10% today; jet run wall is compile+startup (loop 324 ms total, program 68 ms). Conflict: in-process exec unmaps all but the image, so tier-up needs (a) fork mode with a shared memfd code area/table, or (b) not unmapping the compiler. OSR adds hours. Proposal: spend the day on startup and O0 codegen; owner asked to rule whether tier-up+OSR stays required.

OWNER ANSWERS (chat, 2026-10-23 ~05:50), binding as owner instructions: (a) relaunch: launching the running program's own script path (os.executable() under jet run) runs it through the same jet at the same level; (b) tier-up includes on-stack replacement at loop heads today; (c) a crash under in-memory jet run exits with the real signal, same as the built binary (no conversion to exit 1). Decision records D-EXEC-NOEXEC1 (A), D-EXEC-TIERUP1 (A), D-EXEC-RELAUNCH1 (A) posted as drafts with the owner's chat answers as outcomes; D-PERF-RUNCELL2 (reopen run-cell gate vs lua/luajit/python3/node) is a real ballot awaiting the owner. Tower requires a fresh-reader review before any verdict, so none was recorded.

Seed a0_011 (dev 23872f7ab) is current: chain FIXED POINT 9914d964688d2aab, packs identical, #5206 fixed, goldens 614 vs 537 (a0_010). One regression from dev source (comptime on the IR machine): collections/int_map_wide_keys E0956 'Compile-time evaluation does not implement materializing an IR value of type [Int:String]' (int_map_wide_keys.jet:7). Owned by lane O0Comptime: native comptime replaces the evaluator and this example is in its acceptance set. origin/master fast-forwarded to 23872f7ab (proven commit). O0 lanes O0Load/O0Image/O0Comptime/O0Speed started 05:45 on plan $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/exec/o0-plan.md.

OWNER INSTRUCTIONS 2026-10-23 ~05:35 (chat): (1) In-memory native O0 for jet run, jet dev and compile-time code, as designed in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/exec/o0-design.md, must be completely done by 20:00 today; at most 5 Opus subagents in total from 06:00. (2) Target: Jet at least Lua-level for scripts (measured here: lua/luajit hello 2.2 ms = process floor; jet run hello 241-311 ms). (3) If the OS forbids executable memory, jet run falls back to writing the same O0 code to a file and running it. (4) jet run recompiles hot functions at O1 in the background by DEFAULT (extends D-ADAPTIVE-TIER1=B). (5) Under in-memory jet run, os.executable() returns the script path (#4346; launches directly with a shebang per D-SCRIPT-ENTRY1). Still a ballot: reopening D-PERF-RUNCELL1 (gate time-to-answer against lua, luajit, python3, node).

Measured 2026-10-23 05:15, dev bb9414afd1 install-latest, machine loaded (load ~50), hello.jet (one print): direct 'jet run' 355-357 ms end to end (the jet-env wrapper adds about 240 ms more); 'jet --version' alone 122 ms, so about a third of the run wait is process startup before any work. The --trace of the run shows 0.2 s inside the compiler: sources 0.10 s, register 0.02, sema 0.02, ir.build 0.01, native.foreign 0.01, native.link 0.07; the rest is building and launching the executable. Biggest levers, in order: (1) startup cost of the jet binary itself, (2) link + exec, which in-memory O0 would remove, (3) loading the Prelude/Core sources on every run.

cards.title: Stored sibling links: inferred ties, Within disambiguation, frozen-source lifetime
cards.body:
D-LINK-SIBLING1=A
Eligibility, decided on the declaration. A link field of type @T or [@T] has as candidates the sibling fields of type T or [T]. For @String, a String field also qualifies, since @String reaches a string or part of one (memory-model proposal 5.5). A field whose type is a type parameter counts as a candidate, so a generic record's tie never changes with its instantiation. One candidate: the tie is inferred. Two or more: #Within(field) is required. None: no tie.

When a record is tied. A record is tied when a construction in its own module stores links taken from the candidate. From then on every construction and every later assignment to the link field, anywhere, must take links from that field; an empty list is fine. A construction that stores outside links, or might on some path, is an error naming the constructor. If no construction in the module takes links from the candidate, the record is untied and its links follow today's stored-link rules.

Adding a second candidate field later turns an inferred tie into the two-candidate error until #Within names one; writing #Within up front locks the tie against that. The tie is published like inferred link sources (D-MEMPROVENANCE2=A), so any change shows as an API change.

Freeze and lifetime. The source is frozen in shape and value while any link into it lives, not only while the record lives. Links inside the record are plain pointers. A link that leaves the record, such as a returned key, is a kept link holding a count on the source (memory-model proposal 5.4). So the source outlives it and stays frozen until it is gone.

Taking a record apart by move hands back both fields. The text stays frozen while the keys or any link from them lives, and is an ordinary string afterwards.

Copies. Copying a tied record shares its frozen source with one count and copies the other fields by their usual rules (D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A). Nothing can write the source, so the first-write copy never happens and both copies' links stay correct. Allowing item writes in a tied list would need copies to detach and retarget every link; that was rejected as costlier and harder to explain.

Decoders. A derived decoder (#Decode, #Codable) builds each field from saved data on its own, so it cannot know that keys point into text; it is rejected with an error naming the tie. #Encode still saves the fields. The durable form is the text: a loader decodes the text and reruns the parser, so keys are rebuilt, not loaded.

Implementation areas: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/{Registration/Items,Ownership/Checks,Ownership/WindowFacts}.jet tie inference/constructor analysis/freeze; Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/{AST,TIR,MIR}/ tie facts; Compiler/JetBackend/Source/Lower/ ownership/drop and kept links; Compiler/JetOptimizer/Source/Verification/Lint.jet; runtime link/source lifetime; derived codecs; hover/inspect types
Spec/registry: Docs/proposals/memory-model-2026-10-05.md 5.4/5.5 and C30; Docs/spec/{safety,mir-lint}.md; syntax-decisions D-LINK-ITEM1 exception and D-LINK-SIBLING1 inference, NOT from field grammar; Legacy Syntax/markers.rs + Policy::APPLIED_RULES reference; Jet Prelude Markers.jet + AppliedRules metadata add #Within(field) citing D-LINK-SIBLING1=A; no new from clause; registry ceiling approval traced

cards.title: Pinned shared Jet globals and isolated Core state providers
cards.body:
D-CORE-GLOBAL-STATE1=A
Proposed compiler law: sema admits a shared initializer for #Persist, checks T under existing Shared crossing rules, and records stable binding identity and type/layout facts. The new branch requires a `name: value` declaration (not `:=`) so the module handle cannot be reassigned, moved out, or transiently absent.

The initializer must be a closed, non-suspending, infallible state-construction expression: literal data and checked pure construction, no task/world capture, external effects, or access to other lazy globals. Cyclic global initialization is rejected, not allowed to hang. The example creates only an empty typed map inside Storage. Allocation remains subject to existing allocation behavior; no new retry policy is introduced.

All execution modes implement identical once-only publication. State is inaccessible until initialization finishes. Ordinary statements use the existing Shared lock/cleanup law, not scalar persist take/set. Transactions and guards remain unchanged; this ballot adds no new atomicity mechanism. A failed or cancelled ordinary update releases locks under existing Shared rules; this ballot does not promise rollback outside #Transact.

Reload never runs the initializer again for a retained cell. Layout/migration checks complete at the existing reload boundary before new code uses old storage. The process default and each test-world provider are implemented in Jet. Vetted #Unsafe FFI/syscalls may supply host synchronization, but no Rust implementation is retained.

Implementation areas: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Registration/Items.jet E0622 admission, stable Global binding facts; Compiler/JetBackend/Source/Lower/Statics.jet once/Shared global path; Jet runtime once+lock/reload/world provider; Core/math/random.jet, Core/sys/sys.jet env overlay, Core/testing/testing.jet fault switches, Core/auth/auth.jet and Core/web/storage*.jet; no scalar take/set gap
Spec/registry: Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md Persist writable/global/reload amendments, D-CONC-SHARE1 ordinary shared expr and migration precedence; core-library RNG/env/fault/auth/storage scope; CLOSURE 3.11 and existing leaf removal rows; Legacy Syntax.rs #Persist/KW_SHARED reference; Jet Persist registration/init constraints cite D-CORE-GLOBAL-STATE1=A; shared keyword remains D-CONC-SHARE1; NO new marker; DiagnosticRows E0622 and new cycle/initializer/handle refusal registered
Diagnostics/UI: Equivalent unmarked mutable table rejected; immutable handle assignment/move; cyclic/effectful/suspending/world-capture initializer refusal; initializer-only retained-cell reload report; fresh identity and layout restart/migration reports
Examples/goldens: Contended first access exactly once/no partial publication; indexed Shared map update #4751 mandatory; counter atomic statement; two-key Transact invariant + cancellation/panic guard release; compatible body/init reload retains; rename fresh/process restart empty; parallel worlds/children local-session separation; browser scope unchanged
Timing: JET PORT NOW; minimal Persist/Shared/global admission seam essential for existing Core state rows may be mirrored under #29 with dies-at-cutover ledger. Broader unrelated feature work remains frozen. Runtime policy, once/lock/world/reload implementations are Jet-owned; scalar Alloc root does not prove shared-cell semantics. CURRENT #29/#31: a MINIMAL seam necessary to port an existing Core row/runtime layer/test harness may also change the Rust half, registered as dies at cutover; all actual layer policy/carriers must still be ported to Jet. This exception does not permit duplicating new features. #28 Sol authors, Opus reviews. Features outside required port work resume after port/Rust exit; contract/docs/tests planning may be prepared now.

cards.title: BALLOT D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1: how Jetpack reaches compiler-only Core seams (held-directory process, held link)
cards.body: Owner decision needed (public API / visibility). Jetpack (the Jet package manager) needs two capabilities that exist only as raw Core kernels: run a child process with a held Directory as its cwd (#4895: kernel core.process.__with_directory_raw, CoreSystem2 d13edcfff) and the held link (compiler_link_held). Today they're reached through reserved __ names that the parser now rejects (E0067), so the Jet CLI's assembled source doesn't parse. Renaming them to legal names (files.compiler_process_directory, compiler_link_held) makes them ORDINARY PUBLIC Core functions: CoreReview5-2-2 traced Sema core_call 2607-2653: there is NO caller-privacy fence; the only gate (compiler_api_allowed, CompilerServices.jet:98-111) is a compile-time-only gate for core.compiler, not privacy; #Unsafe and names don't restrict callers. Visibility law today (D-VIS-MODULE1): public by default, priv only on modules and fields. Options (same program: Jetpack's TreeHash runs git with a held directory): A) Make them public, documented Core functions (e.g. process.spawn_in(spec, dir: Directory)). Beginner: one more safe capability (held handle, no path races). Expert: same. Cost: permanent public API to maintain. B) Add ONE toolchain-private visibility: a module-level marker so a Core module is importable only by the compiler and Jetpack (checked by sema, registered in Syntax.rs with a decision ID). Beginner: never sees it. Expert: can't call it. Cost: a new visibility mechanism (I8 allows it with this ratification). C) Jetpack calls the raw runtime route directly (#Import / ABI binding of the existing route symbol) with no Core wrapper. Beginner: unaffected. Cost: Jetpack carries unsafe ABI glue; violates the one-mechanism preference for Core access. Main recommends B if more toolchain-only seams are expected (they are: link, process dir, build receipts), else A for process.spawn_in only. Blocks: CLIParity1 / CLIParity2 composition (goal 4).

log.text: Main 2026-11-01: D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A is ratified; this card now tracks building it. Criteria 1-4 come from CardClose-1's plan (CardClose-63), and criterion 5 keeps seam 5 (build-receipt producer) here because no other card holds it. Seam 3 (pass a held lock to a child) stays on #5089 criterion 6. CardClose-1 is building criteria 1-2.
Board burndown 2026-10-22: the open decision in this card is drafted as owner ballot D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1 (draft for Main to file). The card text is background, not the decision.

Fourth case (NativeLead24-2 ruling on CLIParity2's retained-root lock): the Jet RuntimeLock must own an AdvisoryLock taken through the existing Core Directory.lock (same root inode, EX|NB flock on the held '.'); acquire / probe / marker / journal all from the same held root authority; nested identity from FileID, not path. A child process lease must INHERIT that same locked open file description (no reopen / re-flock / raw Int cast), but Core/process has no typed AdvisoryLock attachment / inheritance today. That's a Core/process seam needed by Jetpack only: public option (A) = a documented ProcessSpec capability to inherit a held AdvisoryLock; toolchain-private option (B) = the same seam behind the toolchain-private visibility. Same decision as the other three cases.

Third case (CopyPareto1, #4884 native List.sort_by): the compiler's sort_by intrinsic should lower to ONE private Core kernel (Core/collections, ordinary generic Jet function) so every tier shares the meaning (I9). Same-module private generic calls are fine today, but an EXTERNAL compiler intrinsic -> PRIVATE Core kernel call is not authorized by the current permission model (Sema Calls/Core.jet:160 / resolver 172 use public export / privacy); it must keep the registered declaration SymbolID / module owner / generics -> MIRCallee.User and still deny direct user calls to the private kernel. Options as in the ballot: A) make the kernel a public documented Core function; B) the toolchain-private visibility would also let compiler-lowered intrinsics target private Core kernels; C) n/a here (no raw route). Main's recommendation (B) now covers three cases: Jetpack seams, the compiler's build-receipt producer, and compiler intrinsics -> private Core kernels.

Additional case (CLIParity3, producer 0af618774): the compiler's own build-receipt producer needs Core/build internals that are module-private today: Core/build/keys.jet:280 (priv factory), session 127 / 147 (priv state / session, finished plan storage and target output readers). The pre-existing Driver BuildQueries already reaches the priv Core build session as a whole gateway, but that predates any ruling and isn't an authorized seam. So the ballot's question covers compiler -> Core-private access as well as Jetpack -> Core-private access; option B (one toolchain-private visibility) would cover both uniformly.

CoreReview5-2-2 confirmed there's no existing fence to reuse: compiler_api_allowed is granted only to the selected build entry (Rust BodyCheck 4232-45 / state 9902225: bundle.entry only), ordinary TreeHash / Git helpers don't qualify, and user comptime bypasses the gate anyway (6336 2680 / 2722); semantically core.build is a read-only graph / receipt query surface (6336 2712-49, D-BUILDQUERY1), not a mutable FS / Exec ProcessSpec carrier. So the ballot's options stand as written.

criteria.text: Mechanism (D-CORE-PRIVATE-SEAM1=A, ratified 2026-11-01). `priv(toolchain) module` parses only in a toolchain package, meaning one whose source root lies inside the Jet distribution root that supplied Core (Core, Compiler/*, Jetpack/*); package names play no part. In any other package it is E0414, whose registry text becomes "only `priv(package)` exists outside the toolchain". A `use` or qualified path into a toolchain-private module from a non-toolchain package is E0605 ("`core.files.toolchain` is private to the Jet toolchain"). LSP completion and the generated reference never list such a module. Proof: new UI snapshots tests/ui/priv_toolchain_in_user_package.{jet,stderr} (E0414) and tests/ui/core_files_toolchain_user_use.{jet,stderr} (E0605). The ballot probe (a user `run()` calling the held-folder seam, today `jet check` clean) becomes E0605. A JetLSP completion test shows `core.files.` does not offer `toolchain`.

Seams 1 and 2 have their home. Core/Files gains `priv(toolchain) module toolchain` with `run_in(spec: ProcessSpec, folder: Directory) -[FS, Exec, Env]> ProcessSpec IOError!` and `link_into(source: FileReader, folder: Directory, name: String) -[FS.Write]> Bool IOError!`. Both are typed and have no `#Unsafe` marker. `files.compiler_with_process_directory` and `files.compiler_link_held` are deleted, along with their registry rows (Prelude/Core.jet, CoreSourceOwned, CoreCallRows, StructureRegistry, RawHostKeys test). Jetpack/Foundation/Source/TreeHash.jet calls `held.run_in` / `held.link_into` with no `#Unsafe` block. Proof: the Core/Files held-directory tests pass on run_in; the Jetpack Foundation TreeHash tests pass; `grep -r 'compiler_with_process_directory\|compiler_link_held'` over Core/Compiler/Jetpack/tests returns 0 rows.

Compiler-generated calls pass. A call the compiler lowers into a toolchain-private module is admitted, while the same name written in user source is E0605. Proof via seam 4: user `list.sort_by(f)` lowers to the Core collections sort kernel, now moved into a `priv(toolchain) module`. Examples golden collections sort rows pass on o0/o1/o2, and tests/ui/sort_kernel_user_call.{jet,stderr} shows E0605.

Registry/spec/chain. Syntax-decisions S18 gains the `priv(toolchain)` line (Spellings ledger regenerated, `lexical-ledger.mjs --check` clean). spec.md visibility section and the E0414/E0605/E0609 rows name `priv(toolchain)`, and the diagnostic pages for those codes are regenerated. Chain FIXED_POINT; suites lose no row.

Seam 5 has its home under the same mechanism: the compiler's build-receipt producer reads Core/build's session and key state (Core/build/keys.jet factory, session plan and target storage) through a `priv(toolchain)` reader instead of module-private access, with a case proving the receipt is unchanged and a user `use` of the reader is E0605.

cards.title: BALLOT D-PRIVATE-NATIVE-CARRIER1: how a Core Source type holds a private native kernel value (blocks the HTTP Body cutover)
cards.body: Owner decision needed (new mechanism / public API). The ratified HTTP law (D-HTTPDEPTH1=A; Core + runtime joint ruling) wants ONE public source-owned Body capability facade over a PRIVATE opaque lazy native transport (the existing Arc<Mutex<JetHTTPBody>> kernel). NativeLead24-2 confirmed no mechanism for that exists today: opaque_methods only registers Source impl signatures on PUBLIC known native carriers; the old browser facade (BrowserServer { private native: BrowserTestServer? }) used an already-public carrier and the current line removed it; JetForeignHandle is public and needs a real C library / typedef / close metadata. Missing: a PRIVATE checked native identity with scope, default-constructor rejection, ownership / lifecycle and physical mapping on every tier (I9). Stand-ins (empty record, private RawInt, host RuntimeValue, public alias) are rejected. Blocks GoldenPareto1's Body cutover (6 HTTP goldens). Options (same program: req.body.text() on an incoming request): A) Make the transport a PUBLIC documented native carrier type (e.g. core.http.BodyTransport), not user-constructible, used as Body's field. Beginner: one more type name visible in docs / errors, never needed. Expert: can name the type; no new mechanism. B) Add ONE general private native-carrier mechanism: a Core module can declare a native kernel type private to that module (sema rejects naming / constructing it outside; ownership / drop / clone rules from its native metadata; mapped identically on all tiers). Beginner: never sees it. Expert: clean facades. Cost: a new mechanism (I8, needs this ratification), reusable for other facades. C) Drop the facade: Body IS the native carrier directly (public, as today's incoming body), with the outgoing Empty / Text / Bytes constructors as functions returning it. Beginner: one type. Cost: re-opens the Core + runtime ruling. Main recommends B if more Core facades over native kernels are expected (likely: streams, sockets), else A. Related but distinct: #4896 (which modules may IMPORT toolchain-private Core seams).

log.text: PROGRESS ONLY, sema part only: E0605 for omitted priv fields in literals and priv-module type paths, with 3 new ui tests; the Http Body cutover stays parked (IrTypes-45) Landed in wave 28 as dev bb770de593 (IrTypes-45).
Board burndown 2026-10-22: the open decision in this card is drafted as owner ballot D-PRIVATE-NATIVE-CARRIER1 (draft for Main to file). The card text is background, not the decision.

Joint Core + Native conclusion (CoreReview5-2-2): a Source facade privately holding a PUBLIC opaque seed handle DOES exist (encoding/stream JSONPush 870-877: private output: FileWriter; JSONWriter 201 output: JSONPush; constructor factory 1327; FileWriter known in core_types 303 with opaque constructability). That pattern supports option A directly (public, non-constructible native carrier held privately by the facade). cards.title: Report ALL errors by default: promote keep-going diagnostics from compiler-internal JET_KEEP_GOING to the default user behavior
cards.body: Owner 2026-10-09: the compiler must not stop at the first error; by default it reports ALL errors so a user or agent can fix them in one pass. Today (dev 2026-10-09): within a phase the Jet compiler already collects many diagnostics, but between phases it stops once errors exist (e.g. JetDriver Pipeline.jet:2220 'if jet_driver_has_errors(diagnostics) && !keep_going -> return None', BodyComptime.jet:221). A full all-phases mode exists only as the compiler-internal JET_KEEP_GOING=1 env var (Compiler/Bootstrap/Host/Entry.jet:10-128; JetDriverKeepGoing in JetDriver Identity.jet:524; sema keep-going traps CheckProgram.jet:2243+; comptime drops failed items; the optimizer traps rejected functions and reruns; the emitter keeps every failure), documented as never shipped. Work (Jet side only): make all-phases collection the default for check/build/run/test, with failed items replaced by typed traps so later phases still run without cascade noise (dedupe and suppress errors caused by an already-reported failure); no artifact is produced when any error exists; one canonical option to stop at the first error, available both as a CLI flag and as a build-config setting (owner rule #51: CLI and declarative config never diverge); registered diagnostics/snapshots for the summary line; docs. Keep the internal skip list (JET_KEEP_GOING_SKIP) as a compiler-developer tool only if still needed.

cards.title: Build take/replace out of a borrowed field (D-TAKE-REPLACE1=A)
cards.body: Found 2026-10-09 while fixing Core: Core CSV (streaming rows, ~791 self.fields) and crypto (~99 hash.pending.bytes) want to move a value out of a field below a read/write borrow and immediately reinitialize it. The current rules make that E0201 by design (spec.md:1077-1082, 1e1825f4e); there is no general take/replace/swap API (only Cell.replace, spec 1313-1316). Interim: crypto restructured to consume at finish; CSV uses a restructure or an explicit .copy() then reset (an extra allocation per row). Owner decision: add a canonical take/replace (e.g. mem.replace(place, new) -> old) or keep the rule and accept the copies. Needs a ballot with same-program alternatives.

cards.title: One build plan produces several configurations of the same program
cards.body:
## Outcome

`fn build` can register one program in several configurations in a single plan: debug, release, web, or a cross target. Each configuration has its own profile and target, and all are built by one `jet build` with separate outputs.

## Evidence

- In Jai, every `compiler_create_workspace` call carries its own `Build_Options` (The Way to Jai @19cb4b7 `examples/30/30.1_workspaces.jai`, `30.13_dynamic_libraries.jai`).
- Blow's "build all" builds a debug workspace and a release workspace in parallel (`OHZwYYW9koI` 00:03:01, 2015-10-15). Tsoding's game build produces release, debug and WebAssembly outputs on every build (`kjF_YuLsPqo` 00:05:13, 2022).
- In Jet, `BuildTarget` has a toolchain handle but no profile (`crates/jet-comptime/src/Comptime/Build/targets.rs:129-143`). The profile is chosen once per invocation (`--profile`/`--release`, D-BUILD-DEFAULT1). Two configurations of one program need two invocations.

## Owner gate

The public `BuildContext` API shape: a profile and target argument on each registered target, or a named configuration set applied to a target. Builds on #4913's one option table and D-BUILDCTX-FLAGS1 defaults.

log.text: Board burndown 2026-10-22: ratified D-TARGET-ONE1, D-JAI-BUILDOPT1 and D-JAI-CONFIG1 already decide several configurations per build plan; open check for the owner: no ratified decision names the per-configuration cache key or receipt.

D-JAI-CONFIG1 redesigned on owner feedback ('i dont like that we cant update build settings during a build like jai'): A now lets compile-time hooks change an output's settings until the stage that first reads each one, recorded and cached per stage; B Jai's pull loop; C fixed before compiling. One review: Round3Review.

D-JAI-CONFIG1 rewritten on owner instruction 2026-10-19 to align with card #5069's slate: now a short ballot (one review, CohesionReview) deciding only when build code may change an output (A: until fn build returns; B: Jai-style message loop, expert-gated). Old option C and the exact-options rule removed; per-output options moved to D-TARGET-ONE1, precedence to D-SETTING-ORDER1, BuildOptions to D-ENTRY-NAMES1, plan sealing to D-ENTRY-SHAPE1. Present fifth in the slate order.

criteria.text: One fn build registers the same program in at least two configurations with different profiles and targets, and one jet build invocation writes both artifacts to distinct output paths.
Each configuration's cache key and receipt name its profile and target; changing one configuration's settings rebuilds only that configuration.
An executable example with golden output proves the plan on every applicable tier.

cards.title: Host facts for prep and build-time code
cards.body:
## Outcome

Prep code and build-time code can tell the machine they run on (the host) from the machine the program is built for (the target). When an evaluated Core call has per-OS behaviour, the rule for which OS it uses is written down and tested.

## Evidence

- Jai hit this problem. A `#run` inside a module with per-OS implementations must use the host version, not the target version (Blow `jjCfAg_gtDw` 00:43:50, April 2023). By September 2024 Jai had added an extra hidden "host imports" workspace for compile-time code (`LPdMNsL5MgI` 00:03:21).
- Jet exposes only target facts: `$build.os` (`crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/OSTarget.rs:13-15`). No host fact root exists (searched `$host`, `host.os` and `HOST_OS` over `crates/jet-foundation/src`, `Compiler/JetFoundation/Source`, `syntax-decisions.md` and `metaprogramming.md`: no hits). Toolchain handles record host and target triples (D-BUILDTOOLCHAIN1), but prep code cannot read them.

## Owner gate

Adding a fact root or a `BuildContext` member is new registered surface (I7). The owner also decides what a prep-time call with per-OS behaviour does when cross-compiling (I9 keeps one meaning).

A cross-compiling example shows the host and target facts differing, and the rule for per-OS Core calls during preparation is stated and tested.
Host facts read during preparation are part of the cache key.

Registered host facts sit beside $build for prep and build-time code, and a per-OS Core call made during prep follows the host; proved by a golden example that cross-compiles and prints both host and target facts.

A project or package policy can reject host facts: any read of them then fails the build with a registered diagnostic (what/why/fix and a UI snapshot) naming the reading line, so a hermetic build can be enforced; every host-fact read is recorded in the build record for audit.

cards.title: Compiler event parity: import, program-wide generation, placeholders, link and artifact stages, per-invocation hooks
cards.body:
## Outcome

A package can replace the link step of one executable target with a declared, cached build action. That action receives the compiler's object files and libraries and produces the artifact. A package can also run checked steps on the written artifact, such as signing or embedding an icon or manifest, with failures reported as Jet diagnostics.

## Evidence

- Jai: setting `use_custom_link_command` makes the compiler stop at the `READY_FOR_CUSTOM_LINK_COMMAND` phase. `Message_Phase.compiler_generated_object_files` lists the objects, and the metaprogram links them itself, then calls `compiler_custom_link_command_is_complete(w)` (focus-editor `first.jai` @c6b3ead lines 75, 153-155, 357-391).
- `PRE_WRITE_EXECUTABLE` lets a metaprogram replace the executable (Blow `AdoShhhnsQA` 00:03:53, 2018). `POST_WRITE_EXECUTABLE` reports the linker exit code (The Way to Jai @19cb4b7 `examples/30/30.5_compiler_intercept.jai:46-53`). Focus sets the icon and manifest after a successful link.
- Jet links internally (`Compiler/JetBackend/Source/Image/ELF.jet:30`) or through rustc. D-HOOK-STAGES1 makes `compiler.emitted(Artifact)` read-only, with findings only. `b.action` (D-BUILDACTION1) can add steps over declared outputs, but it cannot take over an executable target's link.

## Owner gate

Amending D-HOOK-STAGES1 or D-BUILDACTION1 to allow a typed link step is public API. Linker-argument options belong to #5005.

log.text: D-COMPILER-EVENT1=A ratified 2026-10-17: one compiler.Event enum in core.compiler (Core/compiler/compiler.jet) lists every public moment (proposal section 2.3). Hooks, Session.stages(), `--json` and the jet.session.v1 wire all use its names and fields. The wire/--json schema is generated from its registry rows, and each new variant is a versioned public change. D-BUILD-UI1's event names become variants (none exist in Jet code today).
Scope widened 2026-10-16: decision D-JAI-EVENTS1 covers the custom link and post-link moments plus every other Jai message-loop capability (Docs/audits/jai-parity-2026-10-16.md, section D).

criteria.text: A package declares a custom link step for one executable target whose inputs are the compiler's object files and libraries; jet build runs it, caches it under the action rules, and reports its failure as a registered Jet diagnostic with a UI snapshot.
A post-link step (for example signing or embedding a resource) runs on the written artifact through the same typed action mechanism, with an executable example.

D-COMPILER-EVENT1=A: one `compiler.Event` enum in core.compiler carries every public moment with its ratified payload; `#On` hooks, `compiler.advanced.Session.stages()`, `jet build --json` and the session wire use its names; the JSON schema is generated from its registry rows and a check fails on a hand-written event name in JetCli/JetDriver.
`stages()` yields the same compiler.Event sequence with --threads 1 and --threads 16 on one program (test).

cards.title: Code-site facts: caller location, current location, function, constness, resolved call (Jai #caller_location family); resolve the stale #Caller()
cards.body:
## Problem

`Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:2056` (D-SHAPE2=A) lists "the compile-time value `#Caller()`" among the non-rule `#` constructs. It has no `Syntax.rs` row (I7), and nothing implements it: `Caller(` matches nothing in `crates/`, `Compiler/`, `Core/` or `Docs/spec/reference/`. The spec names a surface the language does not have.

## Why it matters

Jai's equivalent is `#caller_location`. Used as a default argument (`loc := #caller_location`), it gives loggers and asserts the caller's file and line without walking the stack (The Way to Jai @19cb4b7 `book/30A_Integrated_build_system.md:95`; Blow `yJukJS81o-k` 00:21:38). Jai's own `log` and `assert` use it (The Way to Jai `book/25A_Context.md` section 25.5). Jet's `#Track` / `$origin` records where a value came from, not who called. Runtime panic reports already show Jet locations (DiagnosticRows.jet:7453), but user helpers cannot capture their caller's location.

## Owner gate

Either register and implement a typed caller-location default value (new syntax, so a full ballot), or remove the stale mention in one cutover under the greenfield rule. In both cases the spec and the registry agree afterwards.

criteria.text: Spec and registry agree: either the syntax registry (Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax) registers the caller-location value with its decision ID, an example logger prints its caller's file and line, and the diagnostic snapshots exist, or every mention of #Caller() is removed in one cutover.
Syntax registry entry updated (Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax)
syntax-decisions.md log entry
jet devtools grammars regenerated

cards.title: Jai parity: Jet does everything Jai does, safe by default with expert opt-outs
cards.body:
## Outcome

Owner direction (2026-10-16): Jet must be as or more powerful and flexible than Jai. Every Jai feature or idea gets an explicit Jet counterpart. Safety and auditability stay the default, and experts can turn the guardrails off. The Jai author's regrets are designed out. Every owner choice is balloted.

## Evidence

The 1:1 audit is `Docs/audits/jai-parity-2026-10-16.md`. Each Jai feature row names its Jet counterpart, its state (shipped, groundwork, ratified, open ballot, gap or refused) and the decision or card that closes it. Sources and the Jai reconstruction are in `Docs/research/mine-for-jet-2026-10-15-jai.md`.

## Children

One child card per ballot, plus the existing build cards #5005, #5006, #5009 and #5010. This card closes when every audit row is shipped with an executable witness, or carries a ratified refusal the owner chose. The durable form of the audit is the executable coverage manifest that #3520 criterion 10 requires; this card adds the Jai rows to it.

cards.title: Expert opt-out model: how experts turn off Jet's guardrails to reach Jai-level power
cards.body:
## Outcome

Decision D-JAI-EXPERT1 picks the one opt-out mechanism every Jai-parity power uses. Jai has no guardrails; Jet keeps them as defaults. Today each power has its own switch (`metaprogramming: unrestricted`, `#Impure` plus `--gate impure=allow`, `#StepLimit`), and some powers have none (full host access while compiling, build-wide check relaxation, string code, duck-typed generics). Audit rows: A05-A07, A20, E12-E17, B03, B06, B16.

The ballot carries the full design; this card holds the vote and, once ratified, the delivery plan.

cards.title: Per-call generic control (Jai #modify, #bake_constants, #bake_arguments, $$ auto-bake, duck typing)
cards.body:
## Outcome

Decision D-JAI-GENERIC1. Jai lets compile-time code run at every generic call to reject, default or compute type arguments, bakes specialized procedures, and checks generic bodies per instantiation. Jet checks bounds at the definition (D-GENERIC-TYPEFN1) and has const generics (D-CONSTGEN2). Audit rows: B15-B20, B24-B26.

The ballot carries the full design; this card holds the vote and, once ratified, the delivery plan.

cards.title: Context parity with Jai: readable context, typed keys, scratch storage, assertion handler
cards.body:
## Outcome

Decision D-JAI-CONTEXT1. Jai passes an implicit context (allocator, logger, temporary storage, assertion handler, stack trace, print style, thread index; #add_context, push_context). Jet has the D-CTX1 `#Context(...) { }` block for allocator, logger and deadline. The earlier context-extension card #3502 is frozen by the owner pending what context adds; the owner's 2026-10-16 direction (every Jai feature) supersedes that freeze for this decision. Audit rows: F01-F13, E24, E34.

The ballot carries the full design; this card holds the vote and, once ratified, the delivery plan.

Any exact spelling D-JAI-CONTEXT1 leaves open goes to an owner ballot before step 2. Proof per step: executable example with goldens on O0/O1/O2, UI snapshots for new diagnostics, one shared runtime meaning (I9).

Decision D-JAI-DEFER1. Jai's `defer` schedules any statement or block at scope exit, and macros use it heavily. Jet allows only `defer close(x)` (D-SHAPE-RESOURCE2); `defer action()` and `defer { }` are E0003. The owner asked for defer when ratifying D-SHAPE-RESOURCE1. Audit row: G33.

The ballot carries the full design; this card holds the vote and, once ratified, the delivery plan.
