cards.title: C source import: translate C into editable safe Jet, keep the rest behind the checked binder (c2v lesson)
cards.body: Source: mine-for-jet V report (Docs/research, 2026-10-16). V's c2v translates whole C and C++ projects to V through Clang's JSON AST (vlang/c2v README:1-86; DOOM and Doom 3 demos) and is V's main on-ramp for C codebases. Jet has no C source importer: Docs/spec/reference/migration-tier-map.md:28 keeps C binder-only by D-ADOPT-TIER1=A. The owner wants C compatibility as an on-ramp for new users (2026-10-16). V's model has two defects Jet must not copy: translated files relax the language rules (@[translated]: globals, pointer writes without unsafe, C scalar conversions; doc/docs.md:10990-11014), and vlang/doom still links the C platform layer and has broken sound (doom README:5-9). Jet already ratified one Clang declaration extractor for C and C++ (D-CBIND-UPSTREAM1=A, D-CIMPORT1=A, #4174), so a body importer can extend the same extraction instead of adding a parser. Owner choice D-CSRC-IMPORT1 decides whether the C row of the tier map changes.
cards.plan: 1. Owner ratifies D-CSRC-IMPORT1. 2. If A: extend the shared Clang extractor from declarations to function bodies; translate each function into safe Jet when every construct maps (pointers to views/indices, arrays to fixed lists, unions to enums when tagged); leave the function in C behind the generated binder otherwise, with JT0101 naming the construct, span and reason. 3. Differential oracle per translated function against the original C (D-MIGRATE-SRC1). 4. Corpus: zlib, sqlite3 subset, Chocolate Doom src/doom; report translated/left-in-C counts per file.

cards.title: Core platform layer for games in Jet: present a pixel buffer, play PCM audio, read raw input, without SDL or raylib
cards.body: Source: mine-for-jet V report (2026-10-16) and owner direction 2026-10-16: the Jet Doom port must be as much Jet as possible, not leaning on C FFI. Today Core/game/game.jet is a 19-line shell and the only game backend is Core/game/raylib.jet (a C bridge with known gaps, #4663). Jet has no audio output module (only the done investigation #3287; jetos audio #334 is frozen) and no pure-Jet way to show a CPU-rendered framebuffer. V reaches these through sokol/gg C code and its DOOM links SDL through Chocolate Doom's C objects. A Doom-class program needs four things from Core: open a window and present an RGBA/indexed pixel buffer at a fixed rate with vsync or a timer; mix and play 16-bit PCM at 11025-48000 Hz with low latency; read keyboard and mouse as raw events; a monotonic tick clock (core.time exists, see #4662). The OS edge (Wayland/X11, Win32, Cocoa; ALSA/PipeWire, WASAPI, CoreAudio) stays inside vetted #Unsafe Core, exactly as files and sockets do, so user programs contain no FFI. New public API: an owner ballot is required on the module names and shapes before implementation.
cards.plan: 1. Survey the native UI host (#4951, #2999) and the existing Jet linker paths for what already presents pixels. 2. Draft and raise the API ballot (module home, Surface.present(pixels), Audio.queue(samples), input event stream). 3. Implement Linux first (Wayland + X11 fallback, PipeWire/ALSA), then Windows and macOS, all inside Core #Unsafe with audit reasons. 4. Example with golden output (headless surface checksum + recorded PCM checksum) on every tier (I5, I9).

Doom's source is GPL-2.0 (id Software release; Chocolate Doom, doomgeneric, gore are GPL-2.0), so the port lives in its own repository under GPL-2.0; nothing GPL enters the Jet repository. cards.title: Compiler session protocol: jet.session.v1 NDJSON, `--listen=-` on check/build/test/run/dev, `--serve` owners and attach
cards.body:
## Outcome
One session protocol for every external client, per the ballots ratified 2026-10-17. D-SESSION-WIRE1=A: newline-delimited JSON `jet.session.v1`, UTF-8, one message per line. Reports are the D-REPORT-MACHINE1 object unchanged, build events come from the `compiler.Event` registry (D-COMPILER-EVENT1=A), the first line is `hello` with the toolchain identity, a mismatch refuses the attach (the CLI runs fresh and explains under --verbose; Jetpack reports E1227), lines are capped at 1 MiB, and artifacts never cross the wire. D-SESSION-ENTRY1=C: `--listen=-` on `jet check|build|test|run|dev` serves the protocol on stdio, with no hidden verb. D-SESSION-OWNER1=A: `jet dev --serve` and `jet self lsp --serve` may own the workspace endpoint. The first owner holds the lock in `.jet/session` and the other attaches as a client. This amends D-BUILD-SESSION1 (`dev --serve` only), and D-JPK-NODAEMON1 holds because both are foreground processes.

This card also carries the real work of #2529 (D-BUILD-SESSION1). That card is `done` without code: there is no `--serve`, `--session`, socket or tests/cli_dev_session.rs at 161cf85cc (finding F1).

## Plan
1. T2 codec: CompilerService.jet's tagged-value/CtValue codecs become the session JSON codec; `foundation_parse_protocol_json` stays the reader; the narrow diagnostic codec is deleted and the D-REPORT-MACHINE1 writer used.
2. `--listen=-` flag row in CLICommands.jet next to --threads/--trace; Front.jet parsing for the five verbs; session loop over the S1 session; per-verb `update` per the ratified D-SESSION-UPDATE1 table.
3. `--serve` on `jet dev` and `jet self lsp`: endpoint security as ratified (0700 per-user dir, symlinks rejected, peer credentials, nonce from .jet/session, one owner per workspace by lock); `--session=auto|off|required` attach on build/run/test; `invoke` envelope; Ctrl-C cancels the client's request.
4. Docs/spec/reference/cli.md section for --listen and --serve; help snapshots regenerated in the same commit.

Identity set: Compiler/ only, so this lands after a0_004.

criteria.text: An attached `jet build` equals a fresh build for every corpus program across success, warning, error and ICE: binary SHA-256 identical, stdout/stderr and `--json` lines identical modulo observation fields (timestamps, durations, RSS).

`jet check|build|test|run|dev --listen=-` each answer hello, update, cancel and exit on stdio with the ratified per-verb `update` meaning; a malformed line gets an E2104 report line and the session continues; `--listen=<addr>` other than `-` is refused with a UI snapshot.
A toolchain-identity mismatch on `hello` refuses the attach; the CLI runs fresh and says why only under --verbose; a 1 MiB + 1 byte line is refused with a report.

With `jet self lsp --serve` running, `jet build` attaches (no second compiler process) and a later `jet dev --serve` attaches as a client; closing the owner leaves no endpoint and the next `jet build --verbose` prints the fresh-process note.
A foreign client (other user, wrong nonce, symlinked endpoint) is refused; an edit made while no session ran is picked up by the next attached build.
The adoption receipt (fresh-process vs attached overhead on the #2859 corpus) is recorded.

cards.title: jet build Compiler/ --trace just works: native multi-package builds, build-entry resolution, self-contained install
cards.body:
## Owner intent (2026-10-18 14:20)
From the repo root, `jet build Compiler/` (optionally with `--trace`) builds the compiler using the `jet` on PATH. It needs no .mjs assembler, no --runtime-dir, no env vars and no prlimit. The NixOS `jet` points at the latest approved or released compiler.

## Owner rulings (this session; recorded as ratified)
- **`--trace`** prints the live phase trace to stdout/stderr. Each phase prints as it ends (wall, CPU s, cores busy, memory), with a summary at the end.
- **`--trace=<file>`** writes the trace to `<file>` as Chrome trace events, readable in Perfetto.
- **`Compiler/` becomes a package root.** Add `Compiler/package.jet` as a workspace whose members are the compiler packages.
- **`jet build <dir>` runs the package's BUILD entry,** `fn build(...) -> ... { ... }` (the build script), not `run.jet`, which is the executable entry point.
  - The Compiler workspace's build entry builds the `jet` CLI executable from Compiler/JetCli.
  - Research the existing build-entry convention first and follow it: Project.jet already recognizes `@build.jet`, and `build.jet` is a project marker in ReceiptIdentity.jet.
  - Anything not yet ratified goes on a ballot.

## Gaps measured 2026-10-18 with the round-D compiler (dev bc5e44948)
1. **Multi-package builds with path deps.** `jet build Compiler/JetCli/run.jet` reads every dependency package (after 4 stray hard links were broken), then fails module resolution:
   - E0610 "No module named `jet_sema`/`jet_driver`/`jet_foundation` in scope";
   - E0603 "the imported dependency module is not present in its authorized package root";
   - 3,474 stderr lines in total.

   Port package-graph module resolution (transitive path deps) to the Jet driver. Then retire the Tools/agent/native-compiler.mjs assembly for the self-build (greenfield cutover: one mechanism).
2. **`jet build <directory>`.** The Jet CLI refuses it ("not part of the Jet-hosted CLI yet", Front.jet:583 jet_cli_not_ported). Port the resolution from directory to package.jet or workspace to build entry.
3. **Stack.** The compiler needs a 1 GiB stack (prlimit or ulimit). Run the compiler's main on a large stack inside the runtime or CLI.
4. **Toolchain root and identity** come from env vars (JET_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT, JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY). Default both from the install layout (the binary's directory); inside a Jet checkout, use that checkout. The interim launcher does this today.
5. **C toolchain** for the native link and foreign C. Today it comes from Tools/agent/jet-env (nix develop; ~3-4 s per command). The NixOS package should provide cc/ld directly.
6. **`--trace` and `--trace=<file>`** as above. Today only the JET_TRACE_FILE env var exists.
7. **The `jet` on PATH was the Rust implementation.** ~/nixos/modules/apps/dev/jetlang.nix execs the newest cargo target, and the cargo targets were removed in the 2026-10-18 cleanup.

## Interim (in place 2026-10-18 14:15)
- `~/.local/share/jet-seeds/current` points to `round-d/`, which holds `jet`, `jet-runtime/`, `toolchain/` (an export of bc5e44948), `IDENTITY` and `SOURCE`.
- The launcher `~/.local/share/jet-seeds/bin/jet` supplies the stack, the toolchain and identity defaults, and jet-env.
- It is linked as `$JET_STATE_ROOT/targets/approved/release/jet`, which the existing NixOS wrapper scans, so `jet` on PATH runs the approved compiler without a rebuild.
- Approving a new compiler means repointing `current`.
- Follow-up: change jetlang.nix to exec the launcher directly (one nixos-rebuild) and drop the cargo scan.

## Acceptance
- In a clean checkout, `jet build Compiler/` builds a jet CLI identical to chain s2 for the same SHA.
- `jet build Compiler/ --trace` shows the live phases.
- It works with only the approved `jet` on PATH.
- Collect-all diagnostics.
- Examples and UI snapshots cover the new CLI behaviour (I4/I5).
cards.plan:
## Track B plan (owner order A → B → C → E → D)

### B1. Entry-point cutover (D-ENTRY-CTX1, D-ENTRY-RUN1). One commit.
- **Types:** BuildContext → Build, TestSuite → Test, a new Dev context. BenchSuite and the bench command are removed (benchmarks are measurement tests).
- **Build:** `fn build(b: Build)` returns nothing. The driver takes the plan from the Build session after the call (BuildQueries.jet currently demands a returned BuildPlan, E3502). `b.plan()` stays only as an introspection query for graph/receipt_diff.
- **Run:** `fn run()` returns nothing; `-> App` programs call `.serve()`. The runtime host owns serve, and dev hot swap hooks it.
- **Sites:** sema Calls/BuildContext.jet, CheckProgram entry selection, eval BuildServices/CompilerServices, driver BuildAdapter/BuildQueries, codegen BuildMethods, Liveness, CoreRecordRows, the E3502 row text, the Host.jet @build.jet scaffold, Core/build, Jetpack (36/44 refs), Examples (9) and tests (~96).
- **Proof:** census, then a chain.

### B2. `jet build Compiler/`
- Compiler/package.jet becomes a workspace of the compiler packages, with one `fn build(b: Build)` that builds the jet CLI from Compiler/JetCli.
- It replaces sources.list, Compiler/Bootstrap/assemble.mjs (which still writes edition 2028), native-compiler.mjs --assemble-only, the shell chain, prlimit and env.
- `--trace` / `--trace=<file>` as already ruled.
- Gaps measured 2026-10-18 (module resolution across path deps) are fixed in the driver.
- **Proof:** `jet build Compiler/` reproduces the assembled compiler; then the release proof (stage 1/2/3 fixed point) moves into `jet build Compiler/ --release` or a `fn test`.

### B3. Generators become comptime (`prep` over source data)
- **Order:** prelude markers/derives/units, Core rows (CoreCallRows, CoreRecordRows, CoreEnumRows, CoreSourceOwned, CoreSources), runtime message tables, unicode chunks, C-ABI routes last (it needs the runtime emit).
- Each step deletes the generator and its committed output.

### B4. Checks become tests
- The ~60 `--check` scripts become `fn test(t: Test)` / #Test.
- The fixture gate becomes `jet test tests/ui`, with blessing through `jet test --bless`.

### B5. Remaining tooling ported by area (#5072); Tower last.

cards.title: Verb entries: run, build, dev and test with one settings table and magic defaults
cards.body:
## Outcome

Jet's project entry functions get one clear job each and one consistent shape:

- `fn run` is the program, identical under every command.
- `fn build(b: Build)` is the compile-time metaprogram: everything that ends up in the shipped bytes.
- `fn dev(d: Dev)` is runtime code that sets up the world around `run` while you work (dev server, port, reload, local services, dev jobs).
- `fn test(t: Test)` checks the program; benchmarking is part of test (`--measure`, D-CLAIM-BENCH1), so there is no separate bench entry.

Every setting is one row of the #4913 option table, written as a flag for one run (`jet dev --port=8080`) or as a line of entry code kept in the project (`d.port(8080)`). Beginners get a magic default from `jet dev` with no entry function; experts climb by adding one line at a time.

## Ballot slate (owner direction 2026-10-19: lighter ballots, one review pass)

1. One target registry (Output values vs `b.add_*`), where Jai's workspaces live; prerequisite for any Dev row that names a target and for D-JAI-CONFIG1 (#5006).
2. Entry shape: configure by default, orchestrate by opt-in (`d.run()` / `t.run()`).
3. One precedence order for settings across commands, with `pin`.
4. Names cutover: `Build`, `Dev`, `Test`; settings value type `BuildOptions`; `BuildContext`, `BuildPlan` return, `TestSuite`, `BenchSuite` retire.
5. Dev state across restarts (`#Persist` after D-EXEC2 retired hot swap).
6. Services stay data in env.dev, enabled by name from code or flag.

## Evidence

Design review 2026-10-19: fact cross-exam, beginner (RLI5) and adversarial passes on the proposal draft. Key law: D-EXEC2=A (dev restarts, hot swap retired), D-CMD-OVERRIDE1=C, D-CLAIM-BENCH1=A, D-RUN-WATCH1=A, D-BUILDTARGET1=A, D-SHAPE-OUTPUT-CALLABLE1=A, D-JAI-BUILDOPT1=A, D-JPK-DEVCOMPOSE1=D, D-JOB-SUBCMD1=C, D-CONF-KEY1=A; open D-JAI-CONFIG1.

cards.title: Jet for all repo scripting: replace .mjs/.js/.sh/.py tooling with Jet; every missing capability is a gap card
cards.body:
Owner directive 2026-10-20: everything done in the repo should be doable in Jet (Jet is a scripting language); non-Jet scripts are a gap.

Inventory at dev 2026-10-20 (git ls-files, excluding the Rust implementation, which goes with the Rust removal): .mjs 339 Tools + 166 Compiler + 92 tests; .sh 71 Tools + 30 tests; .py 57 Tools + 32 tests; .js 14 Tools + 13 tests + 12 Compiler; .ts 12 tests. C sources (190 Compiler, 43 Tools, 29 tests, 15 Examples) are FFI/runtime fixtures, not scripting; review separately.

Plan:
1. Classify every script: (a) dies with the Rust removal (Rust->Jet generators, parity checkers, cargo wrappers); (b) gates and harnesses the chain and receipts use (native-compiler.mjs assembly, fixture runners, preflight, phase-diff, census); (c) generators of Jet tables; (d) one-off migrations and codemods (delete); (e) perf/agent tooling.
2. Delete (a) and (d) during the Rust removal and greenfield cleanup.
3. Port (b) and (c) to Jet, gated by #5068 (multi-package jet build/test); assembly disappears once jet build Compiler/ works.
4. Every capability a port needs that Jet lacks (process spawn/stream, JSON, regex, fs walk, hashing, parallel jobs) becomes a gap card and gets fixed in Jet, not worked around.
Main scratch tooling ($JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/Main/*.mjs, *.sh: chain, census, preflight, fmt-verify) is included in the same port.

log.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (asked by Main with the 2026-11-07 conflict note as context): keep the 2026-11-06 pairing model as written. A non-Jet original may live and run in the repository until its Jet twin wins every c14 bar, then stays only as the gauntlet entry's reference. This narrows philosophy priority 6 (Jet fills every role, no fallback tool) for repository tooling during a port, and it replaces the 2026-11-07 note that said c12-c15 would not be built as written. c12-c15 stand and are buildable. #6035 is done; its deletions stay, and the ruling applies to new tooling from now on.

Main 2026-11-08 04:00: c12 is still blocked by the 2026-11-07 conflict, and G1Lead stopped it before committing. As written, a gauntlet entry.json names the original repo script, which conflicts with philosophy priority 6. A plain refuse-every-added-script gate (exempting browser JS) is a different rule whose scope the owner has not worded; it would also refuse new .mjs files under Tools/tower, the node-based Tower tooling. Owner: reword c12 to pick a rule and its exemptions.

Main 2026-11-08 01:30, c17 finding from PortsLead-2 (details in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/PortsLead/c17-gaps.md). Nine Core API gaps make Jet use more source tokens than Python across the nine named gauntlet entries: (1) tally/Counter; (2) bounded split into a tuple; (3) typed regex captures; (4) zero-pad format spec; (5) multi-aggregate group_by and .to_map(); (6) whole-unit Duration accessors; (7) find-and-update; (8) whole-tensor sum and negative indices; (9) infallible forms where the type proves success. Each is public API, so it needs an owner ballot before code; cards wait for owner direction. Two rewrites need no new API (wordfreq via top_n, regex-find-all via text.count); PortsLead-2 does them now. c12-c15 stay blocked by the 2026-11-07 conflict note.

c7 evidence, not a close (PortsLead-2, ScriptBench full2 on bddfd21c0b's runner, g4/full2/cells.tsv: 810 cells, 321 win, 467 LOSS, 22 other; most cells NOISY because landings overlapped the run). w05 jet-bin loses to every peer (python 1.53, node 2.76, bun 5.35, deno 2.46, perl 3.14, ruby 1.20, lua 1.98, luajit 1.99; php 0.98 wall). w07 jet-bin wins 0.53-0.99 except php 1.12 and perl CPU 1.03. w10 jet-bin wins 0.21-0.72 except bun 1.20 and php 1.49; jet-run loses 1.1-7.9. w11 jet-bin wins 0.09-0.95 except bun 1.21/4.51; jet-run: python 0.94, node 1.04, bun 1.86, deno 1.46, ruby 1.15. A quiet-machine rerun is needed before any cell is judged.

c7 progress (PortsLead-2): 4c36e83022 cuts the perf budget checker over to Tools/perf/budget/Check.jet (byte-identical to check.mjs on a real build trace across 4 flag sets; 6/0 unit tests). live-reload.mjs and the uncalled olevels/sweep.mjs, native-cells-baseline.mjs and test-source-compiler-gate.sh are deleted; git history keeps them. Next: ci-perf-check.sh and source-compiler-gate.sh, the gates. Parked: core-activation.mjs, which measures generated Rust and allocations through LD_PRELOAD, so its Jet form is a method question on #4275 c105; and jetc-trace/summarize.mjs, which waits on a Core local-zone API.

Conflict found 2026-11-07 (Main): c12-c15 keep a non-Jet original in the repository as each gauntlet entry's reference until its Jet twin wins the c14 bars. The owner's later ruling (Docs/spec/philosophy.md priority 6, dev acec3d1a06: Jet fills every role; a Core gap is fixed in Core, never with a fallback tool) and the #6035 c3 cutover delete those originals outright. Under the authority order the newer ruling wins, so c12-c15 are not built as written. A reference original may live only outside the repository (a pinned path in the entry manifest), and the bars in c14 stay as the comparison. Only this card's owner wording changes that.

Owner 2026-11-06 (later the same day): scripting performance and the full removal of non-Jet languages are G4 work, not G1/G2. #5072 returns to G4/e17 with criteria c12-c17 (pairing guard, AGENTS line, port bars, helper and runner pairs, Core API gaps from token losses) as its plan. Until then G1/G2 agents only prefer Jet for new tooling where practical; there is no guard and no pairing obligation.

Owner 2026-11-06 refinement: writing a script first in another language is allowed when its Jet twin follows; the pair is a gauntlet benchmark (capability, speed, ease of reasoning, terseness through library APIs that cover the common cases). Reference = the original language only. A port blocks until Jet wins every bar. Ease of reasoning = reviewer checklist plus measured proxies. c12-c15 reworded accordingly.

Owner 2026-11-06: #5072 moves into G2 now (epoch e11, beside #4717). No new .mjs/.js/.cjs/.ts/.sh/.bash/.py may be added to the repository or to agent scratch, enforced by a LaneCheck guard. The only exceptions are browser-executed JS and Nix/flake files. The seed bootstrap gets no shell exception. Existing scripts get only small fixes until ported; a missing capability is a gap card here. Port order: agent tooling (commit, verify, land, chain), then test runners.

Moved from goal 1 (hand-off) to goal 4 (Best scripting language) on the owner's direction (2026-11-04): porting every repo tool to Jet is not a hand-off need, and G22 already says every repo script is Jet.

Owner 2026-11-04: jet-env may stay a bash bootstrap only temporarily, for machines without jet. With a jet binary present every tool runs through jet directly, and the environment setup moves into jet as Jet replaces Nix (#6564 c6).
Owner 2026-11-04: executed together with #6564 (fresh-clone hand-off). The lander, chain, suite, ballot validator and preflight move from out-of-repo .sh/.mjs straight into Tools/ as Jet programs.

OWNER 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'Javascript that runs in the browser is fine so long as we definitely plan to and will generate jets web backend from jet. Tools is in scope right now for perf gauntlet and tower. Rebuilding tower in jet rather than TS/JS will be the goal as a stress test for jet as a web domain language. the agent tooling should be converted to jet while ensuring that jet supports the needed functionality and builds it properly, cohesively and idiomatically where needed.' Browser JS generation is #5201's new criterion; the Tower rebuild has its own card; C7-C9 added here.

OWNER 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'why is there a Compiler/Bootstrap folder? It only has mjs files in it, but I want everything in cohesive idiomatic jet not javascript in random places'. Census at dev 216cac590b: 571 tracked .mjs/.js/.cjs/.ts files and 319 .py/.sh files. Under Compiler/ there are 72 JetRuntime/Tests, 33 Prelude/Web (browser runtime), 12+2 JetCanvas (browser assets), 11 JetBackend/Tests, 5 JetSema/Tests, 3 JetIR/Tests, 1 each in JetParser/JetDriver/JetCli Tests, and the 2 Compiler/Bootstrap generators. Jetpack/Bootstrap has 5.

Body: Core gap found by the #5072 script census (2026-10-23). A new Core API needs an owner ballot before implementation. - Missing: `Core/Web/Browser.jet` is WebDriver BiDi only; no raw CDP client or websocket-CDP session. - Needed by: `Tools/web-test/sourcemap.mjs`, `Tools/canvas-test/driver-lifecycle.mjs`, `Tools/canvas-test/scenario.mjs`. - Acceptance: launch Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port`, open a CDP websocket, send/receive JSON-RPC commands with id correlation and event subscription.

Folded #5832 "Core gap for #5072 script ports: Parallel workers" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5072 (Jet for all repo scripting: replace .mjs/.js/.sh/.py tooling); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Core gap found by the #5072 script census (2026-10-23). A new Core API needs an owner ballot before implementation. - Missing: `Core/Tasks` provides timers and receivers only; no worker pool, fork-join, or process-pool API. - Needed by: `Tools/agent/port/claim.mjs`, `Tools/agent-eval/domain-foundations/prim-distributed/pkg/bench_parallel.py`, and the `jobs` fan-out in `Tools/agent/goldens-census.mjs`. - Acceptance: bounded worker pool (N jobs, per-job timeout, collected exit status) with deterministic result order; cancellation on parent exit.

Folded #5831 "Core gap for #5072 script ports: rlimit / rusage (process resource limits and usage)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5072 (Jet for all repo scripting: replace .mjs/.js/.sh/.py tooling); 1 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Core gap found by the #5072 script census (2026-10-23). A new Core API needs an owner ballot before implementation. - Missing: no `getrlimit`/`setrlimit`/`getrusage` in `Core/Sys` (only `umask`, `setpgid`, `kill`). `Core/Process` exposes shell `ulimit` only. - Needed by: `Tools/gauntlet/harness/memory-safety-fuzz.mjs`, `Tools/perf/enum_codec_bench.py`, `Tools/perf/stream_bench.py`, `Tools/gauntlet/harness/timer.py`. - Acceptance: `Core/Sys` exposes get/set RLIMIT_{AS,CPU,NOFILE,CORE} and getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF/CHILDREN) with max-RSS, user and system time; tests cover the set/get round trip.

Destination: No .mjs/.sh/.py tooling remains.
Notes: Batch SCRIPTPORT of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (opus), one build, one proof run: each ported script runs under jet run with the same output. Order: #5831 #5832 #5833 #5834.
Decisions so far: none linked to member cards.
Fog: no criteria yet on #5072 #5831 #5832 #5833 #5834 (proposals in consolidate-plan.json no_criteria).
Out of scope: cards outside this list; other batches of the consolidation plan.

Inventory 2026-10-20, infrastructure only (benchmarks, peers, gauntlet and FFI excluded): 465 .mjs (Tools/agent 168, tests 117, Tower 59, JetBackend 52, JetRuntime generators), 83 .sh and 30 .py. Also the release chain kept in scratch (cycle.sh, selfhost-chain3.sh, census.sh, fixture-gate.sh, native-preflight.mjs). The ~82 .js files are mostly the browser runtime (product code, kept).

Proposed order (owner to confirm):
1. #5068 `fn build` in Compiler/package.jet replaces sources.list, assemble.mjs, Jetpack/Bootstrap and the shell chains. `jet build Compiler/ --release` runs the stage-1/2/3 fixed-point proof in Jet.
2. Generators become comptime: about 37 generated files become `prep` computations over their source data. Both the scripts and the committed outputs go, and with them the stale-generated-file failure class.
3. The ~60 `--check` scripts become `fn test`/#Test; the fixture gate becomes `jet test tests/ui` (`--bless` to accept).
4. `fn dev` for watch/rebuild/census loops.
5. Long tail by area; Tower is its own project.

criteria.text: Tools/perf is Jet: every perf runner, manifest reader and gate in Tools/perf is a Jet program run with jet, switched over once its Jet twin wins the c14 port bars (the original stays only as the gauntlet entry's reference, c13), and the perf gate result on the canonical manifest is unchanged.

Tools/gauntlet is Jet: every gauntlet driver and checker is a Jet program, switched over once its Jet twin wins the c14 port bars (the original stays only as the entry's reference, c13), and a gauntlet run on the same inputs gives the same verdicts.

Tools/agent is Jet: native-compiler, preflight and every gate the chain and receipts use, beyond the test and landing gates #6035 c68-c71 port, are Jet programs; each Core capability they need is built properly in Core (cohesive, idiomatic, with examples and goldens), not worked around; each switches over once its Jet twin wins the c14 port bars. jet-env stays only as the #6628 bootstrap for a machine with no jet.

Gap (found 2026-10-30 porting Compiler/Bootstrap): comptime embed_file in the JetFoundation and JetCli packages can read Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet, Effects.jet and Core/** without E0957 package escape, through a declared, checked read of the toolchain's own Core sources, so the compiler can read Core declarations directly instead of committing generated rows.

The runtime pack builds with jet alone: prebuild-runtime.mjs is a Jet program that needs no node, cc, ar, nm or Nix-built musl/libgcc. It reuses the seed's foreign archives or builds them through Jet's own toolchain, and a fresh clone with only a seed jet rebuilds the pack when its recipe changes (found by SelfMem's #6564 census, 2026-11-04: G3).

Pairing guard: Tools/agent/LaneCheck.jet refuses a commit that adds a .mjs, .js, .cjs, .ts, .sh, .bash or .py file (or an extensionless file with a non-Jet shebang) unless a gauntlet entry under Tools/gauntlet/entries/ names that script as its original and holds its Jet twin, the shared fixtures, the expected output and a parity check, all in the same commit. Exempt: browser-executed JS and Nix/flake files (owner 2026-11-06), and test or example subjects that a Jet case or example consumes (tests/cases, tests/fixtures, tests/run, tests/*/inputs, Examples) (owner 2026-11-08, Q26 A). A ScriptBench workload folder holding run.jet and expected.out counts as a pairing like a gauntlet entry. The exemptions live in one place in the guard. A planted unpaired script is refused with a message naming the file; a planted paired script, a planted browser asset and a planted test subject pass.

AGENTS.md states the rule in plain prose: new tooling may be written first in another language and proven working, then its Jet twin is written and proven to give the same output; the pair is a gauntlet entry; the repository keeps running the original until the Jet twin wins every bar in the next criterion, and then switches to Jet and keeps the original only as the entry's reference.

Port bars, each judged per entry against the script's original language only (owner 2026-11-06): (1) identical output on the entry's fixtures; (2) Jet faster, with Jet/original below 1.00 in wall time and in peak memory; (3) Jet no longer, with Jet source tokens at or below the original's; (4) Jet easier to reason about: a fresh reviewer scores both on the fixed checklist (types visible at use, every failure path visible at the call, no hidden global or mutable state, data flows top to bottom, one obvious way per operation, effects such as files, network and processes visible), and Jet scores at least the original while its measured proxies (branch count, nesting depth, hand-written helpers that a library call would replace) are no worse. A port lands only when all four bars hold; until then the original keeps running and each lost bar is an open card (a speed loss on a performance card, a missing convenience as a Core API gap card on this card).

The orchestrator's helpers (lane commit, batch verify with its run-to-run diff, prepush, and the Tower spec apply) are each a gauntlet pair under the port bars, and they move into Tools/agent/ as Jet once the Jet twin wins every bar.

The witness runners (Compiler/JetRuntime/Tests/run-alloc-cache-witness.mjs, run-tdigest-witness.mjs, run-alloc-observer-witness.mjs and the remaining #6594 c5 runners) are each paired with a Jet test row under the port bars and switch to Jet once it wins every bar.

cards.title: Compiler architecture: Source -> AST -> IR -> Machine Code (non-SSA slot IR, structured control, data-oriented); ballot + plan before engaging
cards.body:
## Proposal: Source → AST → IR → Machine Code
Owner-directed redesign, 2026-10-20. Sequencing: the work starts AFTER the greenfield cleanup (#5071), and it needs a ratified ballot first.

**Today:** AST → TIR (typed desugared tree) → MIR (SSA + ownership) → LIR (SSA over words/layouts) → X64 instruction list → object. That is five representations, four full copies, and a validation pass per IR.

**Proposed:**
- **AST:** flat and lossless (integer node IDs; tokens and trivia kept). Sema writes its results as arrays keyed by node ID (types, names, ownership/copy, effects, failure contracts). There is no second typed tree.
- **IR:** one per function. Linear, slot-based, NOT SSA:
  - variables are mutable typed slots;
  - control flow is STRUCTURED (block / loop / if / break / continue), with no arbitrary jumps;
  - ownership is explicit instructions (move / copy / drop / close);
  - the IR is flat arrays, content-hashable, and serializable.
- **Machine Code:** per-target selection + slot-based register allocation (linear scan over slot live ranges) + encoding.

**Rejected:** a separate direct AST→machine-code O0 path. It would be a second code generator and violate I9.

## How each consumer maps
- **Comptime:** the evaluator executes the IR directly. Comptime and runtime share one representation, so I9 holds by construction. Effects, authority and determinism are enforced at IR host-call instructions.
- **Web (Wasm/JS):** Wasm requires structured control flow and locals. Structured control + slots map 1:1 (slots → locals; block/loop/br), with no relooper. JS emit is the same.
- **O1/O2:**
  - local passes, inlining, simplification and loop vectorization (it needs loop structure, which is kept) run on the IR;
  - a pass that needs SSA builds a per-function SSA view on demand and discards it, so debug builds never pay for SSA.
- **Ownership:** drop flags, last uses, partial moves and Close order are dataflow over slots; this is what MIR analysis computes today.
- **Debugging:** DWARF/DAP variables are slots, which is simpler than SSA location lists. Spans and node IDs flow AST → IR → machine.
- **Dev/hot swap** (NativeSwap/WebModuleSwap), **REPL/notebooks**, **in-memory O0 `jet run`**: IR is per function with stable identities, so code units swap per function, and in-memory machine code is a direct product.
- **Incremental, LSP and caching:** AST and facts are keyed by stable node IDs; the IR is content-addressed per function.
- **FFI** (C ABI, runtime routes, C++/Rust bridges), **data plans/columnar**, **SIMD lanes**, **tasks/async/realtime**, **#Kernel/compute/autodiff**, **acceleration decisions:** each is mapped explicitly in the ballot. Each one is an inventory row with its proof.
- **More targets** (ARM64, embedded) live behind the Machine Code layer. The IR is target-independent; layouts are resolved at a late IR stage per target.
- **Package management (Nix replacement) and JetOS:** these rely on the programmable build (`fn build`), comptime, hermetic and deterministic outputs, and content-addressed caching.
  - A deterministic, content-hashable per-function IR strengthens this: store keys for compiled units, distributed caching, reproducible builds.
  - Nothing in the design narrows it.
- **Rust emit:** removed with Rust.

## Speed and waste analysis (measured 2026-10-20 quiet run, 105 s)
**Phases:** front end ~45 s (parse, register, sema, comptime, finalize, names, merge), MIR lower 8, optimize 7, native.lower 14, native.object 23, foreign + link 6.

- **IR work alone** removes the MIR/LIR split, the copies, the lints and the SSA/block-parameter overhead in roughly 50 s of the back end. Estimate: 105 s → ~60-70 s. That alone does NOT reach 30 s.
- **30 s ALSO needs the data-oriented front end** (flat AST, facts tables, interned names, no per-node allocation). That is part of this architecture (its first steps).
- **To avoid wasted work, speed work before the switch goes only where it carries over:**
  - runtime (allocator, Shared/scheduler, threads);
  - lexer/parser;
  - sema/finalize/comptime contention;
  - parallelism;
  - the data-oriented AST/facts themselves.
- **NO further optimization of MIR→LIR→x64 lowering or the SSA passes:** they are replaced.

## Migration with no regressions
1. **Inventory:** every feature/consumer of AST/TIR/MIR/LIR, each with a proof (examples, UI tests, fixtures, comptime programs, web examples).
2. **Spike:** IR + O0 machine code for Core + examples. Measure speed and output against today's pipeline. This decides go/no-go.
3. **Flat AST + facts** (replaces TIR). The proof is an identical compiled object.
4. **IR replaces MIR + LIR:** O0 first, then O1/O2.
   - During the transition only, the chain builds old and new side by side and requires identical program behavior: the differential harness from #5064, plus the comptime evaluator agreeing on every comptime program.
   - The old path is deleted at each cutover (greenfield: no permanent dual paths).
5. **Web emit and comptime** on the IR.
6. **Lossless AST → new fmt** (the #5071 fmt root cause).

## Decisions for the ballot
- the names;
- non-SSA slot IR with structured control;
- on-demand SSA views only where a pass proves the need;
- no direct O0 path;
- order: cleanup → inventory → spike → front end → IR;
- go/no-go gates and their metrics.

Emission boundary: the IR path produces exactly X64CompiledFunction + X64FunctionDebug into the existing encoder, object writer, DWARF writer and static linker, same runtime symbols and ABI. D-ARCH-IR1 (one slot IR) shrinks the lower/optimize/native share (~1.3 s); the data-oriented front end shrinks sema; neither removes the per-build Core re-check, which needs checked Core interfaces + Core objects cached per compiler identity (spec: compiler-speed.md build-speed constraints). Owner 2026-10-20: build this SOON (after the cleanup), with a detailed plan ready. Scope widened: DATA-ORIENTED DESIGN THROUGHOUT JET, not only the compiler back end. Flat arrays, integer IDs, interning, struct-of-arrays, no per-node or per-item heap allocation, cache-friendly parallel passes: in the lexer/parser/AST, sema facts, the IR, machine code, the runtime (allocator, collections, strings), Core collections, comptime, LSP/incremental caches and the package store. cards.title: Scripting ergonomics ballots B1-B10 (list +, slot +=, char-index find, write, top-level statements, fail, Match.named, is_executable, Path.script_dir, Regex lint)
cards.body:
# Script ergonomics ballots (final; for Main to file on Tower)

One entry per proposed new API or syntax. Each names the exact spelling, the semantics, a
before/after taken from the four idiomatic tool rewrites
(`$JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/ScriptErgonomics/idiomatic/{TestShards,WebBundleCheck,LexerKeywordRows,Lifecycle}.jet`),
and the saving counted with `count.sh` (program lines / whitespace tokens: no blanks, comments,
`#Test` blocks or `package {}`). A saving marked [INFERENCE] is read off the before/after text,
not measured on a rewritten file.
Not ballots (bug fixes, no new surface). Landed: `pad_start`/`pad_end` link, `remove_prefix`/`remove_suffix`
methods (efbc29643), web baseline (17537755c). Patch ready, not landed (see lane report): the prelude
rows below and the collecting-loop propagation fix.
- readable prelude names `eprint`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `file_exists`, `keep`, `Clock`,
  `Instant`, `Date`, `Duration` resolve without `use` (Spec.md:305-317, D-CORE-PRELUDE1/2);
  `Date.today()` reaches `LocalDate` statics; `files.read`/`read_file` take `String | Path`
  like `write`; `.or_err(...)`/`keep(...)` no longer ICE (core.prelude loads);
- integer selectors of every width (`{i64:Hex(8)}`) and `Pad`/`PadLeft` of any displayable value
  (`{n:PadLeft(2, "0")}`), as codegen already lowered them;
- `"x".pad_start(n, f)` / `pad_end` link (they share the `rjust`/`ljust` runtime routes);
- `s.remove_prefix(p)` / `s.remove_suffix(p)` are methods (String.jet already had the bodies);
- `Int.parse` (any fallible call) inside a collecting loop propagates like the statement form
  (former draft B9).

---

## B1 — List concatenation with `+`
- Spelling: `a + b` where `a: [T]`, `b: [T]` → new `[T]`; operands unchanged (read, not moved).
- Semantics: eager copy of `a` then `b`. `View<T>` operands are E0108 (write `.copy()`); maps and
  sets keep their own operators (none). No new token: `+` widens its operand set, which is
  language surface, so it needs ratification.
- Beginner path: `all: header + rows`. Expert path: `xs.extend(ys)` (in place, no copy).
- Alternatives: (a) `xs.concat(ys)` method only; (b) status quo
  `out := xs.copy(); loop y in ys -> out.push(y)`.
- Before (Lifecycle.jet:62): `text: "{HEADER.join("\n")}\n{(loop row in rows -> "{row}\n").join("")}"`
  After: `text: "{(HEADER + rows).join("\n")}\n"`.
- Before (LexerKeywordRows, 2 sites): `values := m.get(k) ?? [String]{}` / `values.push(v)` /
  `m[k] = values` — After: `m[k] = (m.get(k) ?? [String]{}) + [v]`.
- Saving: −4 lines in LexerKeywordRows, −0 lines/−9 tokens in Lifecycle [INFERENCE].
- Trade-off: `+` hides an O(n) copy; the L0501 copy-in-loop lint covers the hot case.

## B2 — Compound update of a list slot (`xs[i] += n`)
- Spelling: `xs[i] op= v` for `xs: [T]` (mutable binding), `i: Int`, every compound operator that
  exists for `T`.
- Semantics: one bounds check, then read-modify-write of the slot; an out-of-range index stops
  before any write, so no partial update exists. Maps keep E0164 (a missing key has no value
  to update); maps get no sugar in this ballot.
- Today: E0164 "Compound assignment can't target an indexed slot".
- Before (TestShards.jet:44): `loads[lightest] = loads[lightest] + row.weight`
  After: `loads[lightest] += row.weight`.
- Saving: 0 lines, −2 tokens per site.
- Alternative: keep E0164 (explicit total update).

## B3 — `String.find` / `rfind` return a character index as `Int?`
- Spelling (changed signature, same names): `s.find(needle) -> Int?`, `s.rfind(needle) -> Int?`.
- Semantics: the character (Unicode scalar) index of the first/last match, `None` when absent, so
  it composes with `slice`, `len` and `regex.Match.start/end`, which already count characters.
  Byte search stays available as `s.bytes().index_of_seq(n.bytes())`.
- Today: `find` returns a UTF-8 byte offset (Core/Text/String.jet:83) and `-1` when absent;
  `"héllo // c".slice(0, "héllo // c".find("//"))` prints `héllo /` (probe r1.jet).
- Before (LexerKeywordRows literal port): `at: line.find("//")` +
  `code: if at < 0 -> line else -> byte_slice(line, 0, at)` plus a `byte_slice` helper.
  After: `code: line.slice(0, line.find("//") ?? line.len())`.
- Saving: the byte-helper family in every text port (PortReview counted 103 lines across ports;
  −1 line per site [INFERENCE]).
- Changes a ratified API: one cutover migrating every caller.
- Alternatives: (a) keep bytes, add `slice_bytes(a, b)`; (b) only document `split_once`.

## B4 — Ambient `write(text)` (stdout without a newline)
- Spelling: `write(text: String)` in the readable prelude, beside `print`/`eprint`.
- Semantics: writes `text` to stdout unchanged (no newline), same `IO` effect and flush rules
  as `print`; `#NoPrelude` hides it like `print`.
- Today: `print` always appends `\n`; raw text needs `out := term.stdout()` +
  `out.write(text).drop("...")`; `term.stdout().write(t)` is E0111 (a plain call cannot change a temporary).
- Before (Lifecycle.jet:64-66): `else if args[0] == "--print" {` / `out := term.stdout()` /
  `out.write(text).drop("lifecycle text")` / `}` — After: `else if args[0] == "--print" -> write(text)`.
- Saving: −3 lines in Lifecycle, and its `use core.term` line once B4 lands (−1).
- Alternatives: `print(text, end: "")` (labelled argument on an existing builtin); allow `&` on a
  temporary handle for one call.

## B5 — Script entry without `fn run()` (top-level statements)
- Spelling: a loose file (or `#!` script) with no `fn run` may contain statements at top level.
- Semantics: those statements, in order, are the body of an implicit fallible `fn run()`;
  `fn`, `struct`, constants and `use` stay items; a file that has `fn run` and top-level
  statements is an error. Authority and package rules are unchanged.
- Today: "Ordinary files execute only their explicit `fn run` body" (Examples/features/script_mode).
- Before: `fn run() {` … `}` (2 lines + one indent level). After: the body alone.
- Saving: −2 lines per script (TestShards, WebBundleCheck, Lifecycle, LexerKeywordRows: −8).
- Trade-off: two entry shapes (I8), mitigated because the implicit form desugars to exactly
  `fn run()`. Coordinate with lane ScriptMode (`#!`, `-A`).

## B6 — `fail(message, code)` for expected failures
- Spelling: `fail(message: String, code: Int{1}) -> Never` in the readable prelude.
- Semantics: writes `message` and a newline to stderr, runs scope guards, exits with `code`.
  Unlike `panic` (program bugs, E3001 frame) it prints no frame.
- Before (all four rewrites): `fn fail(message: String) -> Never {` / `term.eprint(message)` /
  `process.exit(1)` / `}` (TestShards names it `usage` with code 64).
- After: `fail("...")` / `fail("...", 64)` at the call sites; no helper.
- Saving: −4 lines per script (−16 over the four), and `use core.process` where only `exit`
  used it.
- Alternative: `#Error struct` + `return Err(...)` from `run()` (exists; prints a framed report).

## B7 — Named regex groups on `Match`
- Spelling: `m.named(name: String) -> String?` on `core.regex.Match`.
- Semantics: the text of the named group `(?<name>…)` in this match; `None` when the group did
  not participate or the name is not in the pattern (the pattern is known: a `Regex{…}` literal
  makes an unknown name a compile error).
- Today: groups are positional (`m.groups[2]`); named groups parse but have no accessor on the
  source engine path.
- Before (Lifecycle.jet:45-49): `kind: m.groups[0]`, `name: m.groups[2]`,
  `m.groups[3].trim()`. After: `m.named("kind") ?? ""`, `m.named("name") ?? ""`, …
- Saving: 0 lines; removes index bookkeeping (readability only).

## B8 — `files.is_executable(path)`
- Spelling: `files.is_executable(path: String | Path) -[FS]> Bool` in `core.files`.
- Semantics: true when `path` names a regular file the current process may execute; `false` for
  a failed probe, like `is_file`.
- Before (WebBundleCheck.jet:39): `if (process.cmd(["test", "-x", "{root}/{JET_ENV}"]).run() ?? fail(...)).code != 0 -> fail(...)`
  After: `if !files.is_executable("{root}/{JET_ENV}") -> fail(...)`.
- Saving: 0 lines, −8 tokens, and no `Exec` authority for the probe.

## B9 — `Path.script_dir()`
- Spelling: `Path.script_dir() -> Path` (static on the prelude `Path`).
- Semantics: the directory of the entry source file of the running program (the file `jet run`
  was given), canonicalized; for a built binary, the directory recorded at build time.
- Today every ported tool assumes cwd = repository root; the originals computed it from
  `import.meta.url` / `BASH_SOURCE`.
- Before: `root: files.cwd()` (wrong when run from elsewhere).
  After: `root: Path.script_dir().join("../..")`.
- Saving: 0 lines; fixes a behavior difference from the originals.
- Trade-off: one more ambient read of the entry path; must be defined for `jet build` output.

## B10 — Lint: constant `re.compile("…")` should be a `Regex{…}` literal
- Spelling: new lint code (next free L-code) "this pattern is a constant; write `Regex{…}`",
  with an auto-fix that rewrites the call and un-escapes backslashes.
- Semantics: fires on `re.compile(<string literal>)` / `compile_with(<literal>, flags)` with no
  interpolation; the literal is compile-checked and needs no `?? panic`.
- Evidence: the four ports re-implemented 873 lines of scanners (PortReview) and no port used a
  `Regex{}` literal; rewrites with literals were 0.7–1.1× the originals.
- Saving: per site, −1 `?? panic(...)` and doubled backslashes.


Evidence: idiomatic rewrites and measurements in $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/ScriptErgonomics/ (count.sh, idiomatic/, gaps.md). Additional owner-gated items from the port review not yet drafted here: merging a child process stderr into stdout or redirecting it to a file (ProcessSpec), and process.exit requiring the Exec effect.

cards.title: Jet-native raylib: a 1:1 raylib API written in idiomatic Jet that works out of the box
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-10-21: replace the dlopen-of-libraylib path with Jet-native raylib, API 1:1 with raylib, written in idiomatic Jet, working with no installed C library. Everything above the OS graphics boundary is Jet: windowing, input, rlgl, shapes, textures, text, models, audio mixing. Constraint to decide (owner): the GPU driver (libGL/libvulkan, libX11/Wayland) must be loaded from the user system at run time; the Jet runtime is fully static musl with no dynamic loader. Options: (a) graphical programs build as dynamically linked executables, (b) the runtime gains a minimal loader for driver libraries. Today the native tier implements raylib only on the no-library path (headless), from RouteRuntimeA2. Related: text shaping (HarfBuzz) is the same question - a Jet-native shaper (OpenType GSUB/GPOS) vs the fallback 1:1 glyph shaper.

A raylib example game runs headless (rendering to memory with the same calls) with a golden on O0, O1 and O2, and opens a window on a desktop with nothing installed.

cards.title: Ballot: native linking model - static by default vs dynamic platform libc (GPU drivers, musl exit, macOS/Windows)
cards.body:
## Situation
Jet native programs are fully static Linux executables today: the runtime pack carries a private musl libc (used only for pthread, getaddrinfo DNS, and libm math) and no dynamic loader. The code already marks musl as interim (Compiler/JetRuntime/imports.list:10 "musl until glibc dynamic linking"; Thread.jet: "interim pthread imports die when musl leaves the pack"; raw clone/futex already written). D-JPK-VARIANT1=D ratified `runtime/libc` and `linkage` as native variant axes with context-derived defaults, but no decision says which default applies when.

The owner wants Jet-native raylib (#5086) that works out of the box. The GPU is only reachable through the vendor driver the user's OS ships (Linux: libGL/libEGL/libvulkan + libX11/libwayland-client, built against glibc; macOS: Metal/libSystem; Windows: d3d/opengl32/kernel32). Those must be loaded from the user's system at run time by the platform's own loader. A static musl process cannot load a glibc-built driver (the driver expects glibc's loader, TLS and allocator).

Other languages: C, C++, Rust, Jai link the platform libc dynamically by default (Jai: `#system_library "d3d11"`, OS loader, no custom loader). Go and Zig build fully static binaries with no libc for pure programs and switch to dynamic platform-libc linking when a program needs system libraries (cgo / linkSystemLibrary). macOS and Windows effectively require dynamic system libraries for every program.

## Same program under each option
```jet
// tool.jet (CLI)        // game.jet
fn run() {               fn run() {
    print("hi")              window := game.open(800, 600, "demo")
}                            ...
                         }
```

### A. Static by default, dynamic when the program needs OS libraries (recommended)
- tool.jet -> one static file, no libc (musl removed: Jet's own threads/DNS/math), runs on any Linux of the same architecture.
- game.jet -> dynamically linked against the platform libc (glibc on Linux), GPU/window drivers loaded by the OS loader. The compiler decides from what the program reaches (graphics/windowing Core APIs, `#Import(c)` of a system library); no annotation needed.
- Expert path: `jet build --linkage=static|dynamic` (the D-JPK-VARIANT1 axis) to force either; forcing static on a program that needs drivers is a diagnostic.
- macOS/Windows: always dynamic against system libraries (the platforms require it); static only on Linux.
- Trade-offs: two link modes to maintain and test (I9 parity runs both). Dynamic Linux builds inherit glibc version skew: build against an old-enough glibc baseline (as Go/Rust release builds do) so binaries run on older distros.
- Edge cases: a static program that later adds graphics silently becomes dynamic (shown in `jet build` output and `jet inspect`); plugin hosts (#5087) stay static (the WASM interpreter needs no OS library).

### B. Always dynamic (C/Rust/Jai model)
- Both programs link the platform libc dynamically. One mode, simplest mental model, drivers always reachable.
- Trade-offs: no "copy one file to any Linux box" for CLI tools and servers (glibc skew; containers need a libc); slightly slower start; musl still leaves.

### C. Always static, with a Jet-written loader for driver libraries
- Listed for completeness, not recommended: vendor GPU drivers (Mesa, NVIDIA) are glibc-built and depend on glibc loader internals and TLS; a custom loader in a non-glibc process would have to reimplement glibc's ABI. Impractical and fragile.

### D. Keep today's model (static musl, no graphics without dlopen)
- Raylib stays headless-only natively; contradicts the owner direction in #5086.

## Related owner directions (2026-10-21)
- HarfBuzz is removed: core.font shapes with Jet's own shaper only (correct for Latin/Cyrillic/Greek; complex scripts wrong until a Jet-native OpenType GSUB/GPOS shaper exists - Rust's rustybuzz and Go's go-text are pure-language precedents).
- musl leaves the runtime in every option (Jet-owned threads, DNS resolver, math).

log.text: Board burndown 2026-10-22: the open decision in this card is drafted as owner ballot D-LINK-MODEL1 (draft for Main to file). The card text is background, not the decision.

Owner amendment (2026-10-21): linkage is decided PER LINKED ITEM, not only per program, and is controllable in the package's fn build settings. Each linked item (Jet runtime and libc, a system library such as libGL or libX11, a bundled C library, a foreign closure) carries its own linkage (static or dynamic); option A's rule supplies each item's default (pure Jet and bundled C sources static; OS driver and system libraries dynamic, which makes the executable dynamically linked against the platform libc). The build function can override linkage per item (and the CLI flag --linkage stays the whole-program expert override). A request that cannot work (static linkage for a system driver library, static libc on macOS/Windows) is a diagnostic. To ballot before implementation: the exact build-settings spelling, the per-item defaults table, and how jet inspect reports the resulting linkage per item.

Owner selected option A (2026-10-21): static by default, dynamic when needed. CLI tools, servers and scripts build as one static file with no libc (musl leaves the runtime: Jet-owned threads via raw clone/futex, DNS resolver, math). Programs that reach graphics/windowing Core APIs or import a system C library build dynamically linked against the platform libc (glibc on Linux, with an old-enough baseline for portability) so OS drivers load through the platform loader; macOS/Windows always link system libraries dynamically. Expert override: jet build --linkage=static|dynamic (the D-JPK-VARIANT1 linkage axis); forcing static on a program that needs drivers is a diagnostic. Also owner directions: HarfBuzz removed (core.font shapes with Jet's own shaper; a Jet-native OpenType shaper is the later path), Jet-native raylib (#5086), WASM-interpreter plugins after D-ARCH-IR1 (#5087).

criteria.text: D-LINK-MODEL1=A is built: each linked part has its own linkage (pure Jet and bundled C static; OS drivers and system libraries dynamic), the build function changes any part, and `jet inspect` lists each part with its linkage and source; a case proves the defaults and one override.

cards.title: Implement the ratified Core APIs the Jetpack port needs (process fds/exec, byte I/O, seek, net inheritance, pinned HTTP, json limits, streaming archives)
cards.body:
Found by lane CliFoundation porting the Rust Jetpack fetch/add/remove/update/init/split/fold closure (Store, Provider, Nix, Publication, Environment). Each item is used by the Rust reference and has no Jet Core equivalent; each is new public Core API (owner ratification).
1. ProcessSpec: pass an open FileReader/Directory/RuntimeLock fd to the child at a fixed descriptor slot (Rust clears CLOEXEC; CacheLease, NixProjection); exec-replace the current process (Rust CommandExt::exec; ShellEnv).
2. Process byte I/O: ProcessStdin.write_all([U8]); byte reads on ProcessStdoutStream (today only write(String) and lines()). CacheEndpoints, LeaseSnapshot. (Also needed by script ports: invalid UTF-8 child output.)
3. FileReader.seek.
4. core.net: socket-activation listeners and unix peer credentials (Store Broker).
5. HTTP fetch pinned to a pre-resolved, public-checked address set (Rust jet_net::get_stream_pinned + resolve_public_addresses; Publication already calls a nonexistent core.http.client.jet_http_build_resolve) and streaming Body reads.
6. json.parse with caller limits (Nix index needs 256 MiB / depth 16; Core caps at 16 MiB).
7. core.archive streaming tar and zstd readers (RegistryFetch, NixClosureAdmission).

Body: Found 2026-10-24 by O0Image-3 during the U7 port (#4589); detail in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/O0Image/u7/CORE-GAPS.md. Jetpack calls six Core APIs that never existed in Core: (1) HTTPDestinations/Client.destinations, the SSRF pin for registry fetches (SECURITY: currently unenforced); (2) ProcessSpec.keep_open(handle, at:) plus RuntimeLock.keep_open_for, to pass fds to a child (8 sites); (3) ProcessSpec.replace_process (exec); (4) net.inherited_listeners and unix_peer, for broker socket activation and peer-uid authz; (5) files.delete_at_reboot (Windows); (6) streaming gzip.reader, archive.tar_reader and TarKind. Interim handling (Main ruling): (2)/(4) fail closed with a typed 'not supported yet' error; (3) is emulated as spawn+wait+exit status; (5) is dropped; (6) uses in-memory bounded gzip plus a strict local ustar parser with a malicious-tar case; (1) is removed and listed as a security gap. Each of these is new public Core API, so each needs an owner ballot with exact syntax before it's built. Acceptance: ballots ratified, the Core APIs implemented with goldens, and Jetpack's interim code replaced. Log 2026-10-25 agent: Gap 12 (U7 CLI): there is no runtime-path wasm component load with a digest pin and Limits (fuel/memory/tables/timeout). The Jetpack compiler-extension and build-plugin hosts fail closed; this is owned by #5487 (own wasm engine). Log 2026-10-24 agent: More gaps from U7 Services, approved as Jetpack-local interim measures (Main 2026-10-24); each needs a Core ballot item. (9a) Process start identity: read /proc/<pid>/stat locally, parsing from the last ')' (field 22), and emit the same 'linux-proc-start:<starttime>' token as Rust; other hosts fail closed. (9b) process.find(identity) plus kill/terminate: alive means the identity matches and the state is not Z; the signal goes through the existing group kill path, with the identity rechecked first. (9c) Child stdout/stderr to log files: Core ProcessStreamMode has no File mode, so the unix path wraps argv in an sh exec redirect that keeps the pid and process-group leader. (9d) The Windows guardian Job Object needs Core containment, so it fails closed. Log 2026-10-24 agent: Two more gaps from the U7 Engine port (O0Image-3): (7) no client redirect/proxy policy in Core HTTP; Jetpack follows redirects by hand per hop after the allowlist and refuses relative Locations other than root/scheme-relative. (8) no Directory dup; RemoteCheckout reopens by path and fails closed unless the inode matches. Both need owner-ballot API before Core grows them.

Board burndown 2026-10-22: Not a ballot: every item is already ratified: D-CORE-PROCINHERIT1, D-CORE-PROCREPLACE1, D-CORE-PROCBYTES1, D-FSOPS1 (seek), D-CORE-NETINHERIT1, D-CORE-NETPEER1, D-CORE-HTTPDEST1, D-CORE-HTTPBODYLIMIT1, D-CORE-JSONLIMIT1, D-CORE-TARSTREAM1, D-CORE-ZSTDSOURCE1, D-CORE-CODECSTREAM1. Open point for the owner: this card spells the fd slot as an Int (pass_to(spec, at: Int)) while D-CORE-PROCINHERIT1 says no raw number appears in safe code; implement the decision spelling.

Core lane spelling (CorePort5) for item 1 fd passing, Directory: directory.pass_to(spec: ProcessSpec, at: Int) -[FS, Exec, Env]> ProcessSpec IOError!. Mirrors the Rust CacheLease handle passing (CLOEXEC cleared on a held handle): the held directory is duplicated into the ProcessSpec at descriptor slot at (3 or more), so renaming or closing it here afterwards never changes what the child sees; a slot the spec already passes, or a stdio slot, is IOError.InvalidInput. Shares one implementation with the compiler store bridge (compiler_with_process_directory). Golden io/process_pass_directory: the child reads marker.txt through /proc/self/fd/9 after the directory was closed and renamed; reused slot 9 and slot 2 give InvalidInput.

Core lane spelling (CorePort4) for item 7 zstd: zstd.decompress(data) now decodes every RFC 8878 frame form (compressed blocks, Huffman literals, FSE sequences, repeat offsets and tables, skippable and concatenated frames, windowed frames; dictionaries Unsupported; 64 MiB whole-buffer budget). Streaming: zstd.decoder() -> ZstdDecoder with feed(&self, bytes), read(&self, limit) -> [U8] ZstdFileError! (at most limit bytes; [] when more input is needed or all frames are done), finish(self) ZstdFileError! (Malformed on a truncated frame); zstd.reader(^file: FileReader) -> ZstdReader with read(&self, limit) -[FS.Read]> [U8] ZstdFileError! ([] at end of file). Byte-source design: push decoder (feed/read) for any source, plus an owning FileReader puller; no trait. Window limit 2^27 like the reference decoder default. Golden io/compress_zstd_stream; queued 1792605634-CorePort4.

Core lane spellings (CorePort3): (1) files.stat(path, links: LinkPolicy?{None}) -> Stat IOError!: default describes a final link itself, .Follow describes its target (std::fs::metadata, target nlink), .Refuse is IOError.InvalidInput on a final link; golden io/files_stat_links. (2) json.parse_with_limits(text, limits: EncodingLimits) -> Dyn EncodingError!: caller max_item_bytes and max_depth, mirrors patch_with_limits; golden serde/json_parse_limits. (3) FileReader.seek(position: Int) IOError!: absolute SeekFrom::Start, drops read-ahead; golden io/files_reader_seek. (4) ProcessStdin.write_all(bytes: [U8]) IOError! and ProcessStdoutStream/ProcessStderrStream.read(max: Int) -> [U8] IOError! (empty at EOF, mirrors FileReader.read); native golden pending the ProcessChild.stdout O0 field lowering. Bootstrap note: Core source cannot call new host rows until the next seed (seed E1004), so new native APIs are compiler handle methods or live in new Core modules outside the compiler closure.

Owner approved the batch in principle (2026-10-21): the Core lane designs each of the 7 capabilities to mirror the Rust capability with idiomatic Jet spelling, proves each with goldens, and records each as a ratified decision on this card; the owner may veto any spelling after the fact.

cards.title: Web target on JetIR: a new IR to JS/Wasm backend (A4)
cards.body: The Jet compiler has no live web path: no Jet CLI route constructs JetDriverCompileTarget.Web; web builds today run only through the Rust driver (crates/jet-driver MIRWeb emitter) and Bootstrap/Host/Native.rs, emitting MIR to JS (JetCodegen Emit/Web, 167 functions over 7 files) and MIR to Rust source to rustc for the Wasm bucket. JetIR/JetBackend have no JS or Wasm emitter. A6 S4b deletes Emit/Web with the MIR pipeline, and R7a deletes the Rust driver, so the 113 --target web cases stop running until this lands. Scope: an IR to JS backend (or IR to Wasm replacing rustc), move the JS/Wasm partition facts (web_marker/bucket, on MIR functions today) to checked facts or IR, keep the JS preludes (DOM, game, harfbuzz, timezone). I9: web must carry the same meaning as native. Acceptance: the --target web examples and UI cases pass on the Jet CLI.

cards.title: Secure, current and reproducible systems in the AI-attack era (JetOS and Jetpack)
cards.body:
Owner discussion 2026-10-23: Jet aims to replace Nix. Nix buys reproducibility by pinning, while current security advice (AI shortens patch-to-exploit from weeks to hours) is "update everything fast". These goals conflict less than they seem: a declarative system can make updates atomic, reversible and verifiable, so it should be the easiest system to keep current. This umbrella collects the directions to discuss and plan later; nothing here is scheduled now.

Directions (child cards):
1. Need fewer updates: memory safety (I1) removes the largest CVE class; per-program authority limits blast radius.
2. Make updating cheap and safe: a security lane separate from feature pins, atomic generations, health checks, automatic rollback, exact advisory matching, optional targeted patching (grafts).
3. Make updates trustworthy: capability diffs on update, independent-builder reproducibility checks, signed trust root and transparency log (#2199), hermetic builds with no install scripts (#4760), bootstrappability from a small seed (#4154).
4. Declarative plus imperative: imperative changes write back to the declaration, giving an audit trail, drift detection and attested generations.
5. AI agents as users: capability-limited agent sessions by default.

Owner questions to settle when this is planned (ballot material):
Q1. Should JetOS apply security fixes automatically by default, or only when the declaration opts in?
Q2. Should a dependency update that widens authority (new network, file write, #Unsafe) be blocked until approved, or only flagged?
Q3. Is temporarily breaking bit-reproducibility for patch speed (grafts) acceptable if recorded and reconciled, or should reproducibility be absolute with a faster build farm instead?

Related existing cards: #2199 trust root, #3033 release updates without breaking the app, #3418 inferred effects and policy, #4154 bootstrap resilience, #4195 portable sandboxed app format, #4268 authority and sandbox boundaries, #4760 build hooks in the sandbox, #5070 package effects block.

cards.title: JetOS security update lane: fixes apply within a window, separate from feature pins, with automatic rollback
cards.body: A declaration pins features, but security fixes flow on their own lane and apply within a declared window. Each update builds a new generation, switches atomically, runs health checks (boot, services, declared probes) and rolls back automatically on failure. People skip updates because they fear breakage; this removes the fear. Owner question Q1 on the parent (automatic by default or opt-in). Related: #3033.

cards.title: Exact advisory matching: query whether a system or package is affected using its full dependency graph
cards.body: Jetpack and JetOS know every input a system is built from (lock and closure). Match security advisories against that exact graph, down to the version and build options, so "am I affected?" is an exact query instead of a guess, and the security lane knows exactly what to update. Covers both packages and whole JetOS generations.

criteria.text: `jetpack` answers "is this package affected by advisory X?" from the exact lock and closure, down to version and build options, with a case on a fixture graph that has one affected and one unaffected path (JetOS generations stay out of scope while JetOS is frozen).

cards.title: Targeted security patching (grafts) without a full rebuild, recorded and reconciled in the declaration
cards.body: To ship a fix for a widely used library fast, replace it in existing outputs without rebuilding every dependent (Guix calls these grafts). Trade-off: the result is no longer bit-identical to a from-scratch build. Proposal: the graft is recorded in the declaration and the next full build reconciles it. Owner question Q3 on the parent decides whether grafts are allowed at all.

criteria.text: The owner question on grafts (allowed or not) is a ratified decision; if allowed, a graft is recorded in the declaration, applied without rebuilding dependents, and reconciled by the next full build, proven by a case.

cards.title: Capability diff on dependency update: widened authority, effects or #Unsafe is shown and needs approval
cards.body: Jet tracks authority and effects in the type system, so an update can be diffed by what it is allowed to do, not only by its text. "This update now wants network access" or "this update adds an #Unsafe block" is shown at update time. Defends against maintainer takeovers (xz style), typosquatting and AI-generated or hallucinated packages. Owner question Q2 on the parent (block or flag). Related: #3418, #5070.

criteria.text: Updating a dependency whose new version adds an effect (for example Net.Connect) or a `#Unsafe` block refuses to run until approved, and the prompt lists each widened effect with the dependency function that needs it; the same update under npm, pip and uv runs silently (fixture registry test).

cards.title: Verified reproducibility: independent builders must agree bit-for-bit, published to a transparency log
cards.body: If independent builders produce identical outputs from the same inputs, a tampered binary is detectable. The compiler chain already enforces this for itself (stage 2 == stage 3, 1 thread == 12 threads); extend it to every published package and JetOS generation, and record build attestations in an append-only transparency log anchored at the trust root (#2199), so silent re-publishing is visible.

criteria.text: Two independent builds of every published package from the same inputs are bit-identical, checked by the release gate, and each build attestation is appended to a transparency log anchored at the trust root, with a case that detects a silently re-published package.

cards.title: Per-program authority on JetOS, and capability-limited AI agent sessions by default
cards.body: Every JetOS program and service declares its authorities (files, network, devices, spawn) and is refused anything else, so a compromised component (for example an image parser) has nowhere to go. Software run by AI agents gets a capability-limited sandbox by default, and widening it is an explicit, logged grant, which limits prompt-injection damage. Related: #4195, #4268.

cards.title: Declarative system audit trail: imperative changes write back, drift detection, read-only root, attested generations
cards.body: The planned imperative mode writes every change back into the declaration. That gives an audit trail of what changed and who changed it, drift detection against the last good state, and one-command recovery. Add a read-only system root and boot-time attestation that the running generation matches its declaration hash, so a persistent compromise must defeat the OS on every boot.

criteria.text: Package-level audit trail: an imperative change writes back into the declaration and drift from the last good state is reported, proven by a case (system-root and boot attestation parts wait while JetOS is frozen).

cards.title: Compile speed: 30M lines per second, with per-phase lines/s budgets
cards.body: Owner asked 2026-10-23 for the theoretical maximum compiler speed. Self-compile input: Compiler+Core non-test = 1,263 files, 576k lines, 38.9 MB; output ~55-63 MB. Today about 30 s wall / ~120-150 CPU-s (about 90,000 cycles per token). Reference per-core targets (Carbon toolchain goals): lex+parse 10M lines/s, semantic analysis 1M lines/s; direct x64 emission (no LLVM) can plausibly match about 1M lines/s at O0. Applied: about 1.2 s single-core, about 80-100 ms on 16 cores with near-linear sema/codegen scaling, plus output write/fault cost. Physical floor (memory bandwidth plus a few hundred cycles per token end to end) is tens of ms on 16 cores. Levers: data-oriented compiler data (index-based SoA IR, arenas, no per-node RC or atomics), interned symbols (no string_compare), hashed maps, parallel sema/codegen per function, SIMD lexing, direct emission without a link step, huge pages for output. Work: add per-phase lines/s to the trace report; set phase budgets; card each gap.

The 10M lines/s target needs ~100 ns/line/core, a 64x gap that front-end source changes cannot close: generated code runs a plain byte-test loop at 24 ins/byte (optimised code: ~1) and spends ~35 instructions per small accessor call. The dominant lever is the code quality of the compiler binary: registers across statements, inlined accessors, hoisted bounds checks and stop polls. Next: measure the same profile with an O2-built compiler to decide whether the chain should build the compiler at O2, or the backend needs these optimisations first.

Owner direction 2026-10-23: every improvement that takes the compiler to 30M lines/s must also be applied to codegen, so all code Jet generates is as fast as physically possible without taking control from experts. Rule for the throughput work: each slice is tagged GENERAL (a runtime, codegen or Core mechanism any Jet program gets automatically) or COMPILER-ONLY (a data-structure choice inside the compiler). Prefer GENERAL: implement it once in codegen/runtime/Core and let the compiler benefit as an ordinary Jet program (I8 one mechanism). Examples: non-atomic RC unless shared (#5475), frozen immortal constants (mapfreeze), no reclamation at process end (#5478), escape-proven bump/arena placement (Goose lesson), small-Int fast paths, tag compare (#5473), Shared/queue primitives without futex waits on hot paths, the work-stealing task scheduler, hashed Map instead of binary search (#5474), COW uniqueness at every place (#5480). COMPILER-ONLY wins (interned ids, SoA AST/IR) are each followed by a ticket asking how codegen or Core can give user programs the same (for example Columns<T>/SoA layout, an interned Symbol type, or arenas via escape analysis). Experts keep control via the existing explicit surfaces (layout attributes, #Region, #Unsafe, explicit allocators); defaults stay safe.

criteria.text: A compile-throughput cell measures `jet check` and `jet build` (O0 and --release) of a representative million-line corpus in lines per second on the reference machine, recorded every wave.
Each compiler phase has a lines/s budget, and the budgets compose to 30M lines per second end to end; every phase over its budget names its root on a card.
End metric: `jet build` of the corpus runs at 30M lines per second or faster, with output identical to the slower build.

Owner ruling 2026-11-05, compile model: no incremental compilation. jet run, jet dev and jet test link Core and the runtime as precompiled toolchain pieces built once with the compiler; only the user's program is compiled, fresh each time. jet build compiles from the entry points outward and includes only reached code: unreached Core code is never compiled, so it adds no bytes. Main's notes: the precompiled piece must carry Core's checked interface (not only machine code), because re-checking Core per program is c55's cost; generic Core bodies ship as IR and are specialized per program; it ships with the toolchain and is identified by compiler identity, so it is not a cache; I9 is kept because both paths compile the same Core source, and tier goldens compare them; reachability keeps methods of types used as trait objects, runtime roots, and everything in jet dev (hot reload).

Today suite.sh gives each job 3 GiB because 2 GiB was memory-killed, allows a 6800 s timeout, and the cases runs take hours and were OOM-killed on 2026-11-04. Yet the compiler floor is small: jet check and jet run of a hello program take ~180 ms CPU and 15-19 MB peak (Main 2026-11-04, base 52d3e9cf79, systemd-run accounting). Proof: a per-test wall-time and peak-RSS table for every suite, from a testkit report; every outlier fixed at its root (leak, an unbounded fixture, durable-state fsync stalls, engine or jetpack spawn); and a timed full run that meets the budget.

R3: every compile parses and checks the whole Core closure (66 units, 0.8 s and 700 MiB per call; 72% of ui CPU and 97% of golden CPU). A resident checked Core, or lazy Core modules, make a use core.math check finish under 0.2 s and 150 MiB, with one meaning on every tier. (Also #5910.)

R4: ~270 MiB of each Core compile is Unicode and collation table literals. They become binary assets (embed_bytes relative to Core), with identical results on every tier.

Running one test costs about that test's own time. The testkit's fixed startup cost is measured phase by phase (building or loading the kit, compiling the harness, scanning the corpora, loading Core, starting workers), each phase is listed with its time, and everything that is not the test itself is cut, cached or done once, so a run filtered to one golden entry at --jobs 1 finishes within 0.5 s of that entry's own compile-and-run time. Today a single golden entry pays about 35 s of fixed kit overhead (2026-11-04 gate run: cli_args.jet 3.1 s and fidelity.jet 5.5 s alone, plus about 35 s each run). This also speeds every agent's A/B proof run.

Jet's test runner is the fastest of any language, shown by a peer-matched cell in the canonical performance manifest. The same test corpus (a few thousand small unit tests with assertions, plus a set of whole-program golden tests) is written in Jet and in each peer (Rust with cargo test and nextest, Go with go test, Zig with zig build test, TypeScript with Bun test and Vitest, Python with pytest), and the cell measures, per peer: a cold full run, a warm full run, and the edit-one-test-and-rerun loop, in wall time and peak memory on the same machine. Jet/peer is below 1.00 for every peer in every metric, per the AGENTS performance gate; any loss stays logged here.

Runtime deadlock (found by TestSpeedLead 2026-11-05): with more running tasks than about (cores+8)/2, nested joins hang. Every thread waits in futex_wait on a task that never gets a worker, because the scheduler adds at most 8 workers to cover blocked waits (Compiler/JetRuntime Scheduler.jet:1097). Reproduced by a testkit pool whose entries each join a child and its resident watcher task, on the AOT and run tiers; JET_SCHEDULER_THREADS=256 avoids it. Met when a join on a child that hasn't started yet runs that child on the joining thread (or an equivalent that never deadlocks), a cases fixture nests joins inside a task group whose limit is at least the core count and finishes on O0, O1 and O2, and the testkit's default pool no longer needs its workaround.
