cards.title: Scripts ask once for permissions; -A skips the ask; basics are free
cards.body:
Owner ruling, 2026-10-28. This replaces the old rule where a `#!` first line silently granted every permission.

In plain words: a Jet script gets no extra powers just by having a `#!` line. The first time it needs one (reading files, the network, and so on), Jet asks you in the terminal, once. Your answer is remembered for that exact script. If you already wrote `-A` (allow all), Jet does not ask. Printing, arguments, stdin, time, randomness and exit are always free.

Behavior:
1. A `#!` launch line no longer grants anything implicitly (today `jet_cli_source_invocation` in Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Authority.jet sets `all = true` for any `#!/` file).
2. `-A` (or `--allow=...`) written on the launch line, e.g. `#!/usr/bin/env -S jet -A`, applies as if typed. `./script` and `jet run script.jet` behave the same. `-A` on the command line works as today.
3. Ask once: when the run needs a permission it was not given and stdin/stderr are a terminal, Jet asks before the program starts. Sema already knows the required effects, so one prompt lists every missing permission and its resource, for example "read files under ./data" or "connect to the network". It offers allow once, always allow this script, and no. "Always" is remembered against the script's content hash in the project's single top-level `.jet/` (or the user cache for loose scripts). If the content changes, Jet asks again.
4. With -A present, Jet never asks. Outside a terminal (CI, pipes), Jet never asks either: it fails with the exact-grant error (5).
5. Exact-grant errors name the smallest grant (e.g. `--allow=FS.Read:./data`) and also say that `-A` grants every effect. `jet fix` writes the chosen grant onto the launch line (scripts) or into package.jet (packages).
6. Free basics: stdout/stderr printing, args, stdin, env-free time reads, randomness and exit never need a grant.
7. `--verbose` under -A prints one line listing the effects the run actually used, so users learn what to narrow.

One meaning on every tier (I9): the prompt and grants live in the shared CLI authority path, not per backend.

cards.title: Install Jet with one tested command: release tarball, installer script and a Nix flake package
cards.body:
Today a new user cannot install Jet. The install page says to use Nix, but the repository flake ships no `jet` package, so the documented command cannot work. This card gives Jet one documented install path that a CI job proves on every release.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, DOC-01): Docs/site/dist/install.html names Nix only; flake.nix exports rust-musl-toolchain and musl-linker, no jet package. The channel is chosen by ballot D-INSTALL1 (drafted, filed when this card leaves `later`).

Related: #4154, #5068, D-SEED-DIST1=A (seed published as a release asset for CI and Nix).

criteria.text: D-INSTALL1 is ratified, and the install page documents only the channel it picks.

On a clean Linux x86-64 container with no Nix and no Jet, the documented install command installs `jet`; `jet new hello && cd hello && jet run` then prints the greeting. The release gate runs this on every release.
`nix run github:<org>/jet -- --version` prints the release version: flake.nix exports `packages.<system>.default` built from the pinned seed release asset.
The install page is generated from the tested install script; no page names an install command that the release gate does not run.
The installed `jet` runs `jet run hello.jet` with JET_TOOLCHAIN_ROOT and JET_COMPILER_IDENTITY unset: Core ships inside the binary or the install root (test unsets both).

On a clean Linux x86-64 container, the time from the one-line install to the first `hello` output is below the same flow for the Deno and Bun installers (median of 5, Jet/peer < 1.00), and the downloaded archive is smaller than both (2026-10-28: deno binary 141.7 MB, bun 101.8 MB; jet 76.6 MB plus a toolchain tree).
The same one-line install works on macOS arm64 and on Windows x64 (`irm … | iex`), and `jet run hello.jet` prints the greeting on both, checked by the release gate.

cards.title: New GPU and accelerator support arrives as a library: a public device-provider interface
cards.body:
Jet should run fast on any chip, including chips that do not exist yet. Today each GPU family Jet knows (CUDA, Vulkan, Metal, WebGPU) is wired into Core, so supporting a new accelerator means changing Jet itself. Mojo shows the better model: a hardware vendor ships a library that teaches the language a new device. This card makes Jet work that way.

Owner direction 2026-10-28: replaces the audit's "restore AI/ML / re-scope #3955" proposal. The shape is ballot D-ACCEL-LIB1, hosted here.

Builds on ratified decisions: D-CORE-BOUNDARY1=A (CPU chip instructions are Core library entries, #4565), D-HOST-CAPS1=A (packages add hardware kinds, #4195), D-GPU-PACKAGING1=A, D-COMPUTE1=D and D-COMPUTE-BACKEND1=D (Core owns the compute contract with a CPU reference). Related: #3026, #3028, #4731, #4762, #3955.

log.text: Frozen by owner direction (2026-11-01): cross-platform work is frozen for now. Remaining criteria need CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, Android and iOS device providers.

Merged #3028 "GPU provider matrix and actual cross-target dispatch" into this card (GPU and accelerator providers as a library); its 14 open item(s) are carried as "(was #3028)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T25: KernelIR + DeviceProvider proposal (D-KERNELIR1 and its epic card) folded here by owner direction; no separate ballot or card. Four layers, no MLIR: typed device facts (D-HOST-CAPS1) replace the string devices in Core/Compute/Solve.jet:83-84; #Kernel stays the restricted subset with a CPU reference (D-COMPUTE-KERNEL-SURFACE1=B); a provider implements caps, lower, load, launch, alloc and copy over a public, versioned kernel IR; Core.Compute tensors, autodiff and tiles target that interface. First providers are mined from the Rust-era backends #1144-#1146. Shader stages (#3027) use the same interface.

criteria.text: A package outside Core adds a test accelerator (a provider that runs kernels on the CPU through the provider interface) with no compiler or Core change; device selection finds it from the package's hardware description and runs the CPU-reference conformance suite against it.
The existing CUDA, Vulkan, Metal and WebGPU providers use the same public interface; no provider uses a private path.
A provider that fails the conformance suite is refused at selection with a named failure and is never used silently.

core.compute selects a device by a typed `Device` value built from the hardware description; the string device names in Core/Compute/Solve.jet are gone, and an unknown device kind is a compile error with a registered UI snapshot.

Providers lower from one public, versioned kernel IR (a subset of the compiler IR; no MLIR dependency); `jet inspect` prints a kernel's IR and its version, and a provider that declares an unsupported IR version is refused at selection with a named error (test).

The CUDA, Metal and Vulkan/WebGPU providers are ported from the Rust-era backends of #1144-#1146 (code mined, not re-authored) and pass the CPU-reference conformance suite where the device exists; without the device, selection reports unavailable and never falls back silently.

(was #3028) The existing provider family runs authored compute and graphics across all required Linux/Windows/macOS/browser/Android/iOS routes without adding HIP or a second public API merely for vendor coverage.

(was #3028) Supported NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple and Android mobile GPU routes have actual device execution/readback or presentation evidence. Every required platform has a successful supported route; hardware absence does not count as completion.

(was #3028) CUDA is correctly compute-only; Vulkan, Metal and browser WebGPU carry the matching graphics routes. Receipts identify the actual provider/device/program/profile rather than a generic GPU label.

(was #3028) All adapters consume the same checked program, resource and numeric facts. F32Strict/Reproducible compute and the graphics contract agree with their references across applicable execution tiers.

(was #3028) Loader/capability absence, unsupported precision/format, device loss, queue/allocation failure and invalid lifetime produce bounded typed failures. No implicit CPU/headless replacement or fabricated success occurs.
(was #3028) Existing Tensor .Auto, provider-issued unsafe contracts, system-loader trust, backend lifetimes and I6 dependency boundaries remain intact.

(was #3028) The canonical matrix records exact applicability, source/binary/device identity and focused results. Unsupported but required cells remain open; later broad campaign proof does not replace this card's complete matrix.

cards.title: Workspace roots: check, test, fmt, doc and build act on members; status and parts list them
cards.body:
A workspace is one folder holding several packages. Today `jet check`, `jet test`, `jet build` and `jet doc` at the workspace root refuse with "ambiguous" and exit 2, `jet status` shows a phantom `target run.jet`, and a failing dependency hides its own errors. This card makes the root useful. What root commands act on is ballot D-WORKSPACE-CMD1, hosted here.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-04, mono_probe.sh / notes/mono_probe.log).

log.text: All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: D-WORKSPACE-CMD1 is ratified, and at the root of a three-member workspace `jet check`, `jet test`, `jet doc` and `jet build` behave as it decides with `-p <member>` narrowing; `jet run` still asks which program to start.
`jet status` at a workspace root lists members and their entries (no phantom `target run.jet`), and `jet project parts` lists the members.
E0626 for a failing dependency prints that dependency's own diagnostics inline.

cards.title: Lockfile: committed, machine-independent, and outside the disposable `.jet/` folder
cards.body:
A lock file pins the exact dependency versions so every machine builds the same thing. Today the lock lives in `.jet/lock`, which `jet new` tells git to ignore, and it stores a build timestamp, so it would churn on every commit. This card makes the lock reproducible and places it where ballot D-LOCKFILE1 (hosted here) decides.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-02, LAY-06): generated .gitignore = `.jet/build/ .jet/lock .jet/cache/` (Host.jet:1478); `[build.stamp]` in the lock. Related: D-LOCK1 (spec), D-GENERATED-STORAGE2=B, #3421.

criteria.text: D-LOCKFILE1 is ratified, and `jet new` writes the lock and the .gitignore it specifies.
The lock holds no per-machine state: building the same project on two machines gives byte-identical locks; build stamps live under `.jet/build/`.
The spec lists every `.jet/` subpath and whether it is disposable; files meant to be committed live outside `.jet/`.

cards.title: Tables for data analysis: a dataframe type over Arrow column batches
cards.body:
A dataframe is a table with named columns that you can filter, group and join, like a spreadsheet in code. Data analysts expect one, and Jet has none. Whether Core ships it is ballot D-DATA-FRAME1, hosted here.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, DOMAIN gaps). Builds on D-COMPUTE1=D (dataframes integrate through the compute operation family), D-COLUMNAR-BOUNDARY1 and D-DATA-READER1 (scan into column batches).

criteria.text: Reading a CSV into a frame and running filter, group-by with a sum, join, sort and select by column name works and matches Polars on the same file (golden).
Frame operations run through the shared compute operations; no second kernel path.
In a frame built from `csv.decode<Row>`, a misspelled column name or a column type mismatch is a compile error; the paired Polars and pandas programs fail only at run time (test pairs).
Columns can carry units: adding a `Meters` column to a `Seconds` column is a compile error (test).
Filter, group-by sum, join and sort over a 10M-row CSV run faster than Polars and pandas on the same host (Jet/Polars < 1.00, Jet/pandas < 1.00, numbers logged).
`jet notebook` shows a frame as a table and draws `frame.plot(x, y)` with no package install (test).

cards.title: One manifest per project: fold env.jet and workspace.jet into package.jet sections
cards.body:
A manifest is the file that describes a project. Jet projects can carry package.jet, env.jet and workspace.jet, and a user must learn which setting goes where. Removing the legacy pkg.jet is already decided (D-JPK-LEGACY1=A, #5075). Whether the remaining files become sections of package.jet is ballot D-MANIFEST-ONE1, hosted here.

Evidence (audit 2026-10-28, LAY-05). Related: D-CONF-NAME1 (members live in package.jet).

log.text: Test finding (DeclTypes-3, w22-wave cases, q/sg/cases-w22-wave.txt): 3 env_hook cases FAIL with 'capture prefix line missing': export_changed_definition, export_failed_reload and export_unchanged_directory. A 'module env.dev {prompt}' counts as a typed env (EnvironmentHash.jet:115, environment_names > 0), so an untrusted non-tty export prints 'env.jet here is not trusted' and emits no JETPACK_ENV_HASH line. Whether a prompt-only env needs trust is a trust-law question for this manifest card, not a small fix. The other 16 env_hook rows pass once a jetpack binary is present.

The 10 Core sites stay plain T{x}. Each narrows a value that is masked or built to fit, so the new E3010 stop never fires and their meaning is unchanged. The census found no compiler sites. The Core sites move under c34, once the seed has rotated past Main-13.

c12 patch (Main-13: sema routes an unheld fixed-to-fixed narrowing through the exact Int and CheckedIntToFixed; case tests/cases/numeric_widening/fixed_narrowing_stops_like_int; golden Examples/features/math/fixed_narrowing_stop.jet) is PARKED, not landed: wave 37 on 26fa6cd102 found 2 real regressions. tests/cases/web_build/web_decimal_and_grouped_formatters_use_shared_helpers and tests/cases/checked_text/html_composition_matches_aot_jit_interpreter_and_web fail on the wave and pass on base (rerun on both). Root, from the node wasm stack: Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Int.jet:146 int_fits does U64{int_limb(value, at)} (an I64 to U64 conversion), which is now checked and calls jet_int_checked_fixed, which calls int_fits: infinite recursion. Native passed only because its runtime pack is still built by the older compiler; the next seed would break native too. Verified correct: I64{U64{max}} stops with E3010 on none, basic and full. To finish c12: (1) the runtime's own bit-pattern conversions (about 35 non-literal fixed conversions in Compiler/JetRuntime, e.g. Int.jet:146, Iter.jet:697, IterNumeric.jet:4-8, NativeByteList.jet:12-17) need an explicit wrap-around conversion, and Jet has none (to_bits/from_bits are Float-only; wrapping(...) is ratified for arithmetic operators only), so this needs an owner-ratified spelling or a sanctioned runtime-internal raw cast; (2) the widen-to-Int-plus-runtime-call lowering should become an inline bounds check so hot paths do not pay a call per conversion. Parked patch: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/unitarg/Main-13-parked.patch.

Folded #4886 "List.replace does not have the ratified D-ONCE-VERB1 swap meaning (it clones to a new list)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by CopyPareto1. Ratified D-ONCE-VERB1=A (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:7049): 'replace keeps only the List swap meaning'. Today List.replace is a pure clone-to-new-list in both the registry and the Rust Prelude (~Prelude:3041), not the in-place swap that returns the old value. Fix both tiers to the ratified meaning (in-place replace returning the old element) and migrate every caller in one cutover; regression on both tiers. Check the exact ratified signature first (Tower card for D-ONCE-VERB1).

Folded #4884 "List.sort_by must be O(n log n) on the JetIR route" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found by CopyPareto1 (goal 10), confirmed by NativeReview2 / NativeLead24-2: native O0 List.sort_by computes insertion positions over an index permutation (O(n^2)) and then allocates a replacement element buffer once (Lower/Combinators.jet:523-698/713); it may have replaced an older O(n log n) canonical index-merge. Every native program sorting a large list pays quadratic time. Main-admitted fix: make the canonical List.sort_by kernel a stable O(n log n) sort by reusing the existing canonical stable index-merge + swap-cycle (no second sort implementation), same stability / comparator semantics on every tier; regression with a large list + a stability case + a timing bound. Order: CopyPareto1

Folded #4828 "core.data.sketch: native shared-clone (Arc<Mutex>) violates ratified D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A (sketches are plain values)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: I9 divergence, pre-existing. core.data.sketch {cms, hll, reservoir, tdigest}: the Core source new factories build ordinary value records (a clone copies), while the native seed Sketch.rs uses Arc<Mutex> with SHARED clone semantics (a clone aliases the same sketch), and no source types{} registration exists, so the shipped behavior is the native sharing. Runtime keeps native carriers preserving it for now. Owner decision (ballot D-SKETCH-CLONE1, later): which clone semantics the public sketch types have, and whether the source factories are dead or must change. Raised by CoreReview4.

Folded #4789 "data/plot row_type names differ by tier (I9): Rust type_name vs Jet row names vs none" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: The data/plot row_type naming differs by execution tier: native uses Rust std::any::type_name::<T>() (fully qualified Rust paths), comptime builds checked Jet row names, and the interpreter has no generic type-name marshal at all. The plot factory and the data Rows constructor stay native (uncredited) until a single per-tier type-name contract exists; other plot/data rows port normally (CoreReview4).

Folded #4781 "Lenient untyped JSON decode is declared pure but reads the wall clock and writes to stderr" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: D-JSON3's lenient untyped decode ships with no effects, yet the seed reads SystemTime::now (JSONDataTree.rs:159) and writes an audit line to stderr (eprintln). The Core port (JsonStreams7) keeps today's effect row and ledgers the hidden Time/IO as a truthfulness gap. Fixing it like the JobQueue A' ruling (add the effects; migrate callers) changes public effects, so it needs an owner decision.

Body: Found by CorelibX3 (2026-10-07) while porting the JSON/JSONL streams to Jet. Core.jet's text reader JSONReader(text).next returns DataEvent, while the native file-handle JSONReader.next returns DataEvent?; explicit parameters typed json.JSONReader mean the file handle. One public name has two shapes, so no single Jet class can express it, and users can't tell from the name which next() they get (I8: one mechanism). The port keeps today's behavior: the file-handle reader stays a native nominal boundary (dispatch only; all parse, limit, state and error policy in Jet), recorded in leaves.d. Needed: check the ratified streams/data decisions for the reader contract. Then either make both readers

Folded #4682 "core.collections Counter/OrderedMap/Chain and heap helpers copy on every operation (quadratic)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Source read at dev 595e0dca3: every Counter inc and OrderedMap map_set is an O(n) scan plus a full copy, so counting n words is O(n^2); heap helpers copy the list on each push and are Int-only. Back them with the built-in [K:V] map or retire them for [K:V] methods; heap helpers take &[Int] and sift in place; add a 10^5-insert scale budget row.

Folded #4667 "json.parse is about 460 times slower than V8 on a 2.4 MB document" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Proven: 30,000 records, 2,366,671 bytes; default jet run parse about 12.3 s wall versus Node JSON.parse 26.5 ms (json_probe.jet, node_json.js). Fix: byte-level parser without per-character String/DataTree churn, or a native provider; add a JSON throughput budget (for example 50 MB/s on this shape) to the performance gate. Related: csv.to_string and JSONWriter grow a String by self-interpolation in a loop (csv.jet:77-80, json.jet:208-212), a quadratic copy; collect and join once.

Folded #4611 "Owner ballot candidate: json.parse_with_limits / parse_allow_duplicates_with_limits (custom depth/size limits on parse, mirroring patch_with_limits)" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root idea step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: Found 2026-10-05 by PortIntegrate: the port's Jet sources (seed shared by port/tools and port/compiler) called core.encoding.json.parse_with_limits and parse_allow_duplicates_with_limits, which exist only as unregistered functions in Core/encoding/json.jet (not in Prelude/Core.jet exports, CoreModuleExports, CoreCallRows, docs or conformance). Main ruled: callers use parse()/parse_allow_duplicates() (defaults depth 256, 16 MiB items) and the unregistered functions are removed; if a real caller needs custom limits, ballot the API (precedent: patch_with_limits).

Folded #4602 "One DataTree: owner rulings on duplicate keys, exact numbers, strict typed text and bytes" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root task step of map #5976 (Map: Core data, collections and codecs); 1 criteria, 1 ratified decisions). Body: Owner rulings 2026-10-05 (from Idiom-Runtime3's comparison $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/Idiom-Runtime3/DATATREE-DIFF.md of the ported runtime carrier vs the compiler built-in DataTree; I8: one DataTree, the built-in). (1) Duplicate object keys are a parse error; the explicit parse_allow_duplicates option keeps the later value. (2) Numbers keep their exact text: a Number variant holds the original lexeme (1.50 re-renders as 1.50; 1e400 and integers beyond Int are kept exactly); reading as Int/Float checks range at that point. (3) Decoding is strict: JSON "42" into an Int field is an error. (4) CBOR (and other binary) byte strings decode to a Bytes variant. Reconcile Docs/spec/reference/core-libra

Destination: Every runnable doc block runs in CI; the spec describes only what works.
Notes: Batch DOC of the 2026-10-28 board consolidation (TowerDedup). One worker (sonic), one build, one proof run: the docs-block CI check (#5953) and the unused-grant lint over Examples/ (#5961). Order: #4904 #5953 #3173 #4728 #4800 #5782 #5892 #3195 #5950 #5961 #5962.

Fog: no criteria yet on #5892 #5782 #4800 (proposals in consolidate-plan.json no_criteria).
Out of scope: cards outside this list; other batches of the consolidation plan.

Body: The tooling/sync_crdt example asserts a row policy check (allows(policy, user, row_owner)) and prints the policy (`RowPolicy(table=tickets, expr=owner == user)`). Per D-DBPOLICY1 the row rule belongs to core.db, but the registered core.db API has only policy and policy_audit; the check and display leaves exist only as core.sync rows (Prelude jet_db_policy_allows/show). Golden stem parked until the owner ballot on where these functions live is ratified. Found by GoldenW2b/GoldenFix13, 2026-10-07.

Folded #4663 "core.game.raylib bridge gaps: no draw_line or measure_text, colour channels clamp silently, keys are strings, loaders cannot fail" (CardTrim 2026-10-28: single-root bug step of map #5985 (Map: Domain foundations: games, data, sync, web apps,); 0 criteria, 0 ratified decisions). Body: raylib.jet declares 15 functions, none a line or text measure, so the iprof overlay port from DaJWWePhRsM cannot be written. color(300, -5, 1, 255) silently clamps (raylib.jet:34-36,108-112). raylib.key_down("SPCE") checks clean and returns false (probe g_key.jet); gamepad buttons, axes and sprite names have the same shape (raylib.jet:76-94). Texture and sound loaders return Never! and play_sound returns Bool (raylib.jet:96-106), breaking stdlib law 2. Body: Repro (fc382a23cd discovery jet, jet run): struct S { id: Int }, impl S.Close { fn close(^self) { print("close {self.id}") } }, fn sink(x: S) { print("sink") }, fn run() { sink(S { id: 5 }); print("end") } prints 'sink', 'end' and never 'close 5'. The same happens with a generic fn sink<T>(x: T). With fn sink<T>(x: ^T) and sink(^S { id: 5 }) it prints close 5. So a temporary with a Close impl bound to a read parameter is never closed after the call (a secret would not be scrubbed, a handle not released). Files: $JET_RUN_ROOT/Main/cv/g92b.jet, g92.jet. C6 root cause (BallotDesign at d90660da90): the bodyless child declaration 'module wrap' registers a Module symbol wrap (Registration/Items.jet:1989); 'pub use wrap.wrap' then binds the function wrap in the same namespace, and the duplicate check at Items.jet:3657 reports E0105. Dropping 'module wrap' gives E0610, so the spec's canonical form (spec.md:2232-2243, D-MOD4) cannot compile. Main's ruling, within D-MOD4: a parent's re-export of a child item that has the child module's name replaces the child module name in the parent namespace. The child stays reachable as a path prefix inside use declarations. No separate module and value namespaces.

cards.title: Scripts may read the file you name on the command line, and use a private temp folder, without a prompt
cards.body:
When you type `./wc.jet notes.txt`, you have already said which file the script may read. This card lets that act count as the permission: a `#CLI` field of type `Path` grants reading exactly the path you passed, and a private per-run temp folder (`files.temp_dir`) needs no prompt. Everything else still asks once, as owner ruling #5949 says. Ballot D-SCRIPT-DESIGNATE1, hosted here, decides; this card builds the winner.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T11 items 2 and 3 (the powerbox model: a file picker grants the file the user picked). Writes are not designated; they keep the #5949 prompt.

Related: #5949, D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1=A (#3705), spec.md "Command registry and typed inputs" (`Path` is a supported #CLI scalar), core-library.md `temp_dir`.

log.text: All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: D-SCRIPT-DESIGNATE1 is ratified; the criteria below follow option A and are re-cut in the same change if another option wins.
criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json decision D-SCRIPT-DESIGNATE1: status=ratified outcome=A (typed paths are granted) ratifiedAt=2026-10-30; the card's criteria follow option A

criteria.text: `./wc.jet notes.txt`, where wc.jet takes a #CLI struct with a `Path` field, reads notes.txt with no prompt and no flag; reading any other file still prompts (pty test).
The grant covers exactly the passed path after resolving `..` and symlinks, and only for reading: writing the passed path still prompts (tests for both).
A script that calls `files.temp_dir(prefix)` gets a fresh directory under a per-run root with no prompt, and the root is removed at exit, also after a failure (test).
`jet run --verbose -A` and the prompt list designated paths as granted by argument; the spec and the #5949 basics list are updated in the same change.

cards.title: Checking run at O0 that stops on every aliasing and undefined-behavior class, like Rust's Miri
cards.body:
Rust has Miri: a slow interpreter that catches memory mistakes the type checker missed, such as reading past a buffer inside unsafe code. Jet should have the same safety net. This card adds an opt-in checking run at O0 that tracks extra state for every value and stops with a named error on any aliasing, bounds, release, race or uninitialised-read mistake, including inside `#Unsafe` blocks and at foreign edges.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T06 ("new card for the O0 checking mode if #4726 does not cover it"; #4726 lists results, not a checker).

Related: #4309 (static IR ownership verifier, a compile-time check; this is its run-time partner), #4620 (memory model), #4726 (defined-behavior ledger), D-MEM-HARDEN1=A (shipping run-time checks for unsafe islands and foreign edges).

criteria.text: One documented opt-in on `jet run` and `jet test` (spelling recorded in Docs/spec/cli.md) runs the program at O0 with shadow state and stops on: out-of-bounds access, use after release, double release, a data race on shared memory, a read of uninitialised memory, and writing through an aliased mutable view.

A planted-bug corpus with one program per class, each inside `#Unsafe` or a foreign edge, stops in checking mode with a named runtime code and the source location, and runs without a report in normal mode; the corpus runs in CI.
All in-repo `#Test`s pass under checking mode in a nightly job; the slowdown against normal O0 is measured and logged on this card.

cards.title: `jet test` tries many task orders: seeded schedules over the replay recorder find races and deadlocks
cards.body:
A concurrency bug often appears only in one rare order of task steps, so a test passes a thousand times and fails in production. Rust needs extra tools (loom, shuttle) to search those orders. Jet already records task message and lock order for exact replay (D-REPLAY-ORDER1=A, built in the Rust era as #4252). This card lets `jet test` run a concurrent test under many seeded orders and print the seed of a failure, so it replays exactly.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T07 and T21. The Rust-era replay recorder is a capability row on the not-built census card and must be ported first.

Related: #3239 (task outcomes), #4637 (fair turns), #5468 (stop edges in tasks).

cards.title: One `#Test`: a test with inputs is also a property test with shrinking and a fuzz target
cards.body:
Rust needs proptest, cargo-fuzz and insta as separate add-ons. Jet should need none. A `#Test` that takes inputs runs on generated inputs, shrinks a failure to the smallest case, and can be fuzzed by coverage, all inside `jet test`. D-CLAIM1=C already folds fuzzing into `jet test --grade=generated --iterations=N`, and the snapshot assertion already has one spelling (`expect(...).snapshot()`, syntax-decisions.md). This card builds them on the self-hosted toolchain, mining the Rust-era harness (#4117, #3957, #1916).

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T21. No new syntax.

Related: #4510 (expected stop message), #5899, #5902.

cards.title: Forwarding derive: a distinct type takes its base type's traits in one line
cards.body:
Rust's orphan rule forces wrapper types, and each wrapper must re-implement every trait by hand. Jet's distinct types (`Die: distinct Int(1..6)`) meet the same chore. A forwarding derive lets a distinct type take its base type's traits (equality, ordering, printing, hashing, codable) in one line, through the ratified derive-request law (D-ONCE-DERIVE1=A, D-CORE-DERIVE-HOME1=A). Library API inside existing law; no new marker.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T30.

Related: #3505 (const generics), #4609 (cross-module generics, P0).

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match D-DECL-COLON1=A (`name: value`, no `::`).

criteria.text: A distinct type requests forwarding of listed base traits through the ratified derive-request spelling; the forwarded members behave exactly as the base type's (one test each for equality, ordering, printing, hashing and codable).
Forwarding a trait the base type does not have is a compile error naming the trait and the base type; UI snapshot.
`jet inspect expand` shows the forwarded members as ordinary Jet source.

cards.title: Registry publish policy: short-lived identities instead of stored tokens, and a runnable example per public function
cards.body:
Two rules decide what it takes to publish a package. First, how the publisher proves who they are: in 2025 a worm spread through npm by stealing long-lived publish tokens, and trusted publishing replaces them with a short-lived identity from the CI job. Second, what a package must contain: pages with only type signatures leave users guessing, so each public function could be required to ship a tested example. Ballots D-TRUSTPUB1 and D-REGISTRY-EXAMPLE1, hosted here, decide; this card builds the winners.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T15 and T20. Already ratified and not reopened: the transparency log, TUF metadata and transactional publish (D-JPK-REGISTRY1=D), signing (D-PKGSIGN1), the trust root (#2199).

cards.title: Remote builds and shared cache work with existing build farms
cards.body:
Big teams speed up builds by running steps on a shared farm of machines and sharing a cache of results. Jet has ratified who may use a remote builder and how it is bound (D-JPK-REMOTE1=D: `build.remote` grants, `jet remote bind`), but not the wire protocol. Ballot D-REAPI1, hosted here, decides between the open protocol existing farms speak and a Jet-only one.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T22.

cards.title: Infrastructure as typed Jet: a first-party package where the plan is a value tests can check
cards.body:
Teams describe servers, databases and networks in tools like Terraform, then apply that description to a cloud. Those tools have their own languages, keep secrets in a state file, and make plans hard to test. A first-party Jet package could describe infrastructure in typed Jet, with the plan as a value that tests assert on and apply running only under Net and Secret authority. Ballot D-INFRA1, hosted here, decides whether to build it and whether to reuse Terraform/OpenTofu providers.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T24. Sequenced after the HTTP client and server (audit card 3: #3665, #4957), hence `later`. Fleet and OS deployment are epoch e9 and out of scope.

State is stored as a content-addressed lock, and a `Secret` value never appears in state or plan output (test).

cards.title: Write a typed Jet config out as JSON, YAML or TOML for other tools
cards.body:
Many tools read settings from JSON, YAML or TOML files. Jet lets a project write configuration as typed Jet and can already export a JSON Schema from a type (D-CORE-JSON-SCHEMA1=A). Hand-copying the values into those files repeats them, and the copies drift. Ballot D-CONFIG-EXPORT1, hosted here, decides whether a command writes a checked Jet config value out in those formats. It is not hosted on #4275, whose ratified scope forbids new ballots.

Source: FutureAudit 2026-10-28, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/FUTURE.md T23.

log.text: All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: D-CONFIG-EXPORT1 is ratified; if it is B (library only), this card is frozen with that reason.
criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): tower.json decision D-CONFIG-EXPORT1: status=ratified outcome=A (export command) ratifiedAt=2026-10-28

criteria.text: The export command writes a named config value from a fixture as JSON, YAML and TOML; each output decodes back into the same typed value (round-trip test per format).
With the schema option, the command writes the JSON Schema for the value's type from the same codec metadata, and a value that fails its type is never exported (test).

cards.title: One Jet-native test system: test.jet profiles run every suite through jet test; port testkit and delete the external test scripts
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: Jet must design, build, manage and test all of its suites in one suite, with tools written only in Jet. Needing external tools or other suites to test Jet is a core failing of Jet's testing infrastructure. A package's `test.jet` holds `fn test(t: Test)`, as `build.jet` holds `fn build`. It declares test profiles and suites (quick, golden, ui, cases, jetpack, selfhost, perf, full) and their settings: tiers, jobs, timeouts, memory caps, filters, shards and the baseline to compare against. `jet test` runs them.

Today: ratified D-ROLEFILE1/D-CMDOVERRIDE1 wire `fn test(t: Test)`, but `Test` offers little beyond `t.run()`. D-TESTKIT1 makes `#Test` the only test syntax, with snapshots, fixtures, corpora and golden files as core.testing helpers. Yet Jet's own suites run on a separate testkit program (Tools/testkit) with its own `.case` step language. About 100 Node/shell scripts in Tools/agent and Tools/ci carry lane-check, the Jetpack check, verify-full, shards, censuses and comparisons.

Plan:
(1) Ballot D-TEST-PROFILE1 for the Test profile API, `jet test` flags and the fate of `.case`.
(2) Grow Test and core.testing: corpus suites for examples, UI snapshots and cases; typed settings; parallel by default; per-row result store with a no-lost-rows baseline compare; shards; keep-going; timings.
(3) A root test.jet with the repo profiles.
(4) One cutover: migrate `.case` to #Test plus core.testing, port testkit, and delete testkit and the external gate scripts. Every gate and receipt becomes `jet test --profile X`.

cards.title: Complete the marker API as a metaprogramming rung: every target, typed reflection, one shared API with derives and fn build, library diagnostics, expand/test tooling
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: markers are a rung on the metaprogramming ladder and need a solid, comprehensive API for building and using them; fix the gaps.

Findings (MarkerScout, dev be55563b38, read-only):
(1) User marker bodies expand only on structs, top-level functions and text blocks (Compiler/JetSema Registration/UserTemplates.jet:417-458). Enums, variants, methods, fields, modules and packages are not wired, although built-in markers reach them.
(2) Reflection lacks module and package info and markers on enum variants. Marker arguments come back as untyped MarkerInfo{name, args} (Comptime/Reflection.jet:340), not as the marker's declared typed parameters.
(3) Marker bodies, derives and fn build do not share one reflection and emit API.
(4) There is no way for a library or user marker to register its own diagnostic codes with what/why/fix text (I4).
(5) There is no expand or inspect view or test helper for marker output; jet emit is unwired (#6038).
(6) Wrapping or around behaviour (decorator-like) is absent by design (D-METADEPTH1/2, D-PROCMACRO1), which is a ballot question.
(7) The Data/Syntax Markers.jet name list (25) duplicates part of the Prelude registry (81).
The ladder is: comptime expression, comptime fn, marker, derive, fn build. They share the same reflection and emit API, differing only in scope (philosophy pillar 4).

log.text: Examples concept-area cutover (2c3e68a70b) moved paths this card's criteria cite. Read each cited path as its new home: c8: Examples/features/tooling/declared_text_block.jet -> Examples/Metaprogramming/Attributes/DeclaredTextBlock.jet; c25: Examples/features/effects/effect_declarations.jet -> Examples/ErrorsAndEffects/Effects/EffectDeclarations.jet; c26: Examples/features/serde/user_derive.jet -> Examples/Metaprogramming/Derives/UserDerive.jet.
Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: marker and effect criteria respelled for D-DECL-COLON1=A; retired declarations get no teaching diagnostic or jet fix (owner order).

D-MARKER-INBODY1 A, owner 2026-11-04: markers may be ANYWHERE in the body, not only at the top. Text retargets for the syntax-decisions.md entry (whoever lands #6562 applies them): (1) "The # lines may sit anywhere among the body's members. Position carries no meaning, and jet fmt keeps it." (2) Body members # Path :: value, anywhere in the body, are added to the declaration's marker list when the body closes. (3) The parser collects the # lines from the whole body and applies them when the body closes, where markers above apply today (Items.jet:1906-1909, :2043-2044); Layout, derives, SingleUse and MustUse take effect identically wherever the line sits (#6562 c2). (4) Markers added by tools or templates go right after the declaration's last inside # line when it has inside lines, and above otherwise.

Ballots posted: D-TAG-MARKER1 (tag as a type), D-FACT-MARKER1 (ratified A: keep Fact), D-FIXED-WRAP1 revised. Owner noted that a tag deny setting duplicates the ratified #FX row on types (D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1 A), so D-TAG-MARKER1 was rebuilt: rec A writes a tag as #FX(!Log, !Net) struct CardNumber { impl Marker { sites :: [.TypeUse] } }. D-FACT-MARKER1's illustrative tag sample still shows the old deny setting; the tag spelling follows D-TAG-MARKER1. Tags depend on #FX on types (c09kjhit). Marker struct-form cutover (c10) in progress: struct X { fields; impl Marker { settings; fn expand(self, target: Target) {template} } }; a trailing list field without a default is variadic (Policy, FX; Interrupt has no users). Owner's impl-placement sweep is card #6561.

Owner ruling 2026-10-30: Jet's own diagnostic types live under the jet. prefix (#Allow(jet.UnusedParameter); headers Error [jet.UnusedParameter]). The 1001-row name table (DeclTypes draft, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/DeclTypes/names.draft.tsv) is approved with sensible defaults; retired and reserved rows stay types per D-DECL-TYPES1 rule 13.

Correction: no ballot needed for Gate.Marker(Type). D-GENERIC-TYPEFN1 A (ratified 2026-10-02) already makes types build-time values ('prep fn Pair(T: Type) -> Type', types never reach run time). DeclTypes implements the minimal slice with B6: a type-valued payload or constant only in compile-time values (trait constants, marker args, #Allow), checked to resolve, with the bound checked against the trait, on the same mechanism prep T: Type will use. B2 follows B6.

DeclTypes collect-all for B2 (facts, C12): D-DECL-TYPES1 A rule 12 names Gate.Marker(Type) (e.g. Rights gates :: [.Marker(Unsafe), .Marker(Impure), .Marker(Grant)]), but Jet has no type-valued value (no Type in Core, no type kind among compile-time values), so the decision implies undefined language surface. A ballot is being drafted; B2 stays parked until the vote. Main rulings within the ratified text: one Gate case per escape word, including the unlisted provider, digest, _name, policy allow and manifest rule edit; rule 12 scope (a package does not add new facts) makes the 67 user fact case rows rejection tests, with registered codes for the retired fact word and for a user Fact impl. Order B1, B3, B6, B2.
D-MARKER-DIAG1 A ratified by the owner 2026-10-30; C13 now names its text shape.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

Main note on D-MARKER-USES1=A (ratified): the ballot's code sample wrote 'pub fn routes()' and 'pub struct Route', but pub is retired (E0411). The ratified meaning is unchanged; implement it in today's spelling, 'fn routes() -> [Route.Use] { Route.#uses }' (with HASH1's sigil outcome). The corrected ballot JSON is at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballots/out/markers/D-MARKER-USES1.json.

2026-10-28 MarkerDesign drafts (Audit/drafts6: D-MARKER-TARGETS1, REFLECT1, LADDER1, DIAG1, EXPAND1; PLAN-6039.md) are in review. Defects found that need no ballot: a body on an enum, variant, method, field, module or package is accepted and never runs, silently; a target containing a Char value makes the marker skip silently; tests of rejecting bodies borrow the retired E0927; the MARKER_* constants span six Data/Syntax files, and PreludeMarkers.jet holds an unsynced literal copy of Prelude/Markers.jet. Plan stage 1 (one vocabulary) needs no ballot. The around hook is cited as refused under D-MARKER-LAW1=A, with D-META-COMPILER1 as the expert path.

The Prelude's 46 effects are converted and the effect declaration word is gone.

D-DECL-TYPES1 A: errors are structs implementing Core Diagnostic (D-MARKER-DIAG1 A: what, why and fix are methods whose body is one string literal with {self.field} holes; code, severity (default .Error) and lint_name are trait constants; raised with reject(Value) from expand or a library function, with .Warning silenced by #Allow(pkg.Name)). The library_diagnostic case covers reject(Value), jet explain web.BadPath and #Allow; the retired_allow fix case and the library_rule UI snapshot PASS. jet run -A Tools/agent/DiagnosticRows.jet -- --check prints passed, and jet explain jet.StrayCharacter works. D-TAG-MARKER1 A: a value tag is a field-less struct whose Marker impl has sites: [.TypeUse]; its denials are its own #FX(!…) row (D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1), with no tag-only deny setting; from is a Marker constant used only by tags. A tag with no denial or with a ceiling entry is refused with a registered code and UI snapshot. The four built-in tags are Prelude structs, the copies in EffectsSurface.jet, Taint.jet and the TaintKind enum are removed, the 36 tag declarations are converted, and E0733/E0734 texts are rewritten. Depends on #FX on types (c09kjhit).
D-FACT-MARKER1 A: fact planes stay a separate Fact trait (struct implementing Fact, Prelude-only), converted to the struct form in the same style as markers; no plane setting is added to Marker.

(amend for criterion 10; reflection proposal B6) `target.marker(T)` works on every site kind, including fields, and on named types as `Rock.reflect().marker(T)`. A non-marker argument is a registered refusal with a UI snapshot. String `has_marker("X")` reads (`Sema/Calls/Reflection.jet:232-255`, `Registration/Derives.jet:245-249`) are retired by the `jet fix` rewrite D-MARKER-REFLECT1 names.

(reflection proposal B7) `Entity.reflect().uses` lists every use of a marker with its typed marker record and site (D-MARKER-USES1). It is refused outside the marker's own package with a registered code and UI snapshot, and folds to a constant after checking. Today `Editable.#uses` is E0003/E0107.

D-TASK-WINDOW1 A: a task in a `task.group` may capture a read view or a write window into storage whose owner outlives the group. The capture is a loan held until the group's join. Two live tasks holding overlapping windows, where either writes, are refused with the loan diagnostics (E0204/E0212). So is any use of the owner inside the group. (Found by Builder 2026-11-04 at 37eae4f5d6; pre-existing) User-facing diagnostic text carries no internal ids: the "(#6542)" card ids in Why lines (Parser/Items.jet:620/677/682/714) and the "(I2)" at the end of E3001's Why are removed, and jet test traces print the test name and source position, not internal ids such as module:32:package:15:...::test::name@10685..13401 (I7: no decision or card citations in code text). cards.title: Mutation testing and coverage-guided fuzzing for jet test
cards.body: Split from #6035 by owner answer 2026-10-28 (Q4: own card). The best-in-class evaluation (Audit/drafts4/BEST-IN-CLASS.md) lists mutation testing (peers: cargo-mutants, Stryker, PIT) and coverage-guided fuzzing (peers: libFuzzer/cargo-fuzz, Go native fuzzing, AFL++) as axes where Jet's test system has nothing. Both should climb the same test ladder and use the one settings table, without a second mechanism. Ratified fuzz rows that the CLI refuses today (Front.jet:1023-1027) are built under #6035 S3; this card covers coverage guidance and mutation.

log.text: Moved from G1 to G15 (testing toolkit) by owner order 2026-11-06: G1 keeps only hand-off and durability.
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 4 criteria from archived #2343: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: An owner ballot fixes the surface for mutation testing and coverage-guided fuzzing on the test ladder.
criteria.evidence: D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1 A ratified by the owner 2026-10-30: both on by default; mutate: changed|all|off with stock changed; grade: generated is coverage-guided with a corpus under testdata/fuzz/<test>/.

criteria.text: Each runs on an example package with golden output, and the results appear as rows in the jet test report.

D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1 A, mutation: mutate is a row of the one test settings table (changed stock, all, off). Only functions whose IR changed are mutated by default, all mutants share one build (mutant schemata), each runs only the tests that reach it (last killer first), and the kill matrix is cached in the #6035 store. A cases row proves an unchanged rerun mutates nothing.

D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1 A, equivalent mutants: mutants equal to the original after canonical-IR folding are dropped unrun; an effect-free survivor is proved equivalent by the solver lens or reported with an input that tells it apart, with fuzzing as fallback; effectful survivors are reported as unchecked. A cases row shows each outcome.

D-TEST-MUTFUZZ1 A, fuzzing: grade: generated steers generation by branch coverage, keeps new-branch inputs and shrunk failures under the corpus directory (stock testdata/fuzz/<test>/), and later runs replay them as ordinary rows; a cases row proves the replay.

The stock jet test run with mutate: changed and generated rows on stays fast enough to be on by default: a paired cell in the perf manifest compares the default jet test rerun against the matched peers (cargo-mutants plus cargo-fuzz, Go's test cache plus go test -fuzz) under the performance gate.
(was #2343 c1) A reviewed must-kill catalog names one exact mutation and the expected rejecting layer for every critical silent-data seam class.

(was #2343 c6) The mutation score and survivor list are derived from the catalog and immutable result bundles; manual exemptions, hidden skips, and stale target commits are red [precut audit: no dev test, golden, case or snapshot proves this today]

cards.title: Reuse test results for rows that read files or env, by recording their reads at run time
cards.body: Split from #6035 (D-TEST-PROFILE1 open question Q7, owner asked to card it 2026-10-28). Go's test cache records the files and environment variables a test reads at run time and reuses the result while they are unchanged. Under #6035, rows with undeclared effects are never reused, so file- and env-reading rows lose to Go on rerun time (Audit/drafts4/BEST-IN-CLASS.md). Design this on top of the #6035 S4 result store: what is recorded, how a read is detected under the effect system, and how the reuse key stays exact. A new user-visible setting or flag needs an owner ballot.

log.text: Moved from G1 to G15 (testing toolkit) by owner order 2026-11-06: G1 keeps only hand-off and durability.

c2 scope (Main): the perf manifest has no matched pair for it yet; nothing under Tools/perf has a go test or test-cache row. The criterion defines the pair, so this is build work, not an owner call: add a Go peer suite under Tools/perf that mirrors a fixed golden subset (same programs, same expected outputs, one Go test per golden), plus a manifest row comparing the warm no-change rerun wall time of jet's golden runner against go test with its build and test caches warm, on the pinned Go toolchain. Then measure c2.
D-TEST-READS1 A ratified by the owner 2026-10-30 (foreign code included, no new flag; fresh opts out). C3 added.
All decisions ratified; advanced out of deciding.

criteria.text: A file- or env-reading test row reruns from the store when its recorded reads are unchanged and re-executes when one changes, proven by a cases row for each.
criteria.evidence: dev 616c0dda34 (TestProfiles): cases test_results_rerun_when_a_read_file_changes and test_results_rerun_when_a_read_env_var_changes 2/2 PASS; testing_tiers 12 PASS / 1 KF (#5454); chain s2 from a93d1800d1+patch, fixed point SAME; no KF rows removed

criteria.text: The rerun time of the golden suite with no changes beats `go test` caching on the matched pair in the perf manifest.

D-TEST-READS1 A: reads from foreign code count too. An extern whose declared row has no FS/Env reuses like pure code; under jet test, file reads through the C library are recorded (libc interposition on Linux, libSystem on macOS, ntdll on Windows), and on Linux a seccomp instruction-pointer filter makes a read that bypasses the recorder rerun its row. A foreign env read keys on the whole environment, and a file that changes during the run is not stored. Cases rows prove a fixture test and a core.db/SQLite test reuse and rerun correctly.

cards.title: Memory checks accept every safe program: no over-strict rejections
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: if a program is memory safe, Jet must accept it. Checks must be neither over-strict nor under-strict; only `#Unsafe` blocks opt out.

Known over-strict case: E0221 rejects a type that could form a strong loop at its declaration. It rejects a plain linked list (`next: Shared<Node>?`) and a tree with weak parent links and strong `kids` (probes in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/ballots2/probe/family2.jet). A strong loop can only close when a strong field of an existing shared value is written with a value that reaches it. Building by construction (prepend, a new child) never loops.

Scope: every memory, ownership, borrow, aliasing and resource diagnostic.

log.text: Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: respelled for D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A and D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A; the soundness rule is unchanged.

Merged #6200 "Over-safety audit: every hard error protects soundness, every restriction names its expert way out, and no sealed floors" into this card (memory and safety checks accept every safe program); its 3 open item(s) are carried as "(was #6200)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

Landed 6e013d30c9 (SmallGoals5-g7): immediately called lambda no longer reports E0217; UI row local_cell_guard_immediately_called_lambda_reads PASS. Partial; remaining items unchanged (E0204 nested call, E0212 payload window, E0219/E0220 blocked by #5677, linear-guard Fn lambda E0121).

2026-10-29 Main: landed 3a2f6b469d (SmallGoals5-g5): a non-escaping lambda may read a Cell guard (E0217 only for escaping lambdas). UI test _5 is rewritten to an escaping lambda, and a new test proves the non-escaping capture checks clean. C3 and C4 stay partial; the remaining items are in land/SmallGoals5-g5-cards.tsv.

criteria.text: A census of every memory, ownership, borrow, aliasing and resource diagnostic lists, for each, safe programs it rejects today (probe files with expected output) and unsafe programs it must keep rejecting.

E0221 fires only where a strong loop can actually close (a write of a strong field of an existing shared value whose new value can reach it), never at a type declaration; a strong linked list built by prepend and a weak-parent tree with strong kids compile and run on O0 and O1.
criteria.evidence: Landed cb59b8f072 (E0221 at the write site). On dev cb59b8f072 base jet: tests/ui/shared_weak_parent_tree.jet prints 'Ada has 2 kids' rc 0 under jet run, --optimize=none, --optimize=basic and the built binary; golden Examples/features/memory/shared_graph_building.jet (prepend list + weak-parent tree) PASS o0/o1/o2.

criteria.text: Every other over-strict rejection in the census is fixed in sema, or carded with a ballot if the fix needs new syntax; every unsafe probe still fails with its diagnostic.
UI snapshots and examples cover each changed rule.
(was #6200) A dated audit under Docs/research classifies every active error code (soundness or opinion) with its reason, generated from the diagnostic registry and not hand-listed
(was #6200) Every sealed floor is listed with its location and who can reach it
(was #6200) Every finding has a filed card, and owner-level changes have a ballot that meets the rework bar

Soundness U1 (Prep 2026-11-04, probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/c3836/s64.jet): an escaping lambda that captures a list window of a local that dies owns a materialized copy, so the probe prints 2000|true| on O0, O1 and O2 instead of reading freed memory. The fix is in IR: ir_lambda honors sema's materialized and cloned captures. Sema keeps accepting the program. A case pins it on every tier.

Wrong result L1 (Prep 2026-11-04, probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/c3836/s36x.jet): writes inside a loop in a non-escaping lambda reach the captured variable, so the probe prints 3|6|3 on O0, O1 and O2 instead of 3|3|0. A case pins it on every tier.

(S1, I1 soundness) A refill write 'self.r = next(self.r)' (next takes &&) on a &self receiver, where next can stop (panic), never closes the moved value twice. Today both the callee frame and the caller's owner close it: probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/bal2/p/stop_refill.jet prints 'close a' twice before E3001 on -O0 and -O1 (refill-move path, Checking.jet:583-584). Rule: while a write place is empty, nothing that can stop may consume the moved value; sema rejects it or the place is refilled before any stop. The probe becomes a tests/cases case that closes once on O0/O1/O2, and the 8 repo sites of 'x.f = g(x.f)' (g takes &&) (CheckProgram.jet:5580/5581/6385/6529/7346, Host.jet:2553, Review.jet:282, Loops.jet:177) check clean or are migrated.

Probes are under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/ until they become repo cases. D-TASK-WINDOW1 A: a task in a `task.group` may capture a read view or a write window into storage whose owner outlives the group. The capture is a loan held until the group's join. Two live tasks holding overlapping windows, where either writes, are refused with the loan diagnostics (E0204/E0212). So is any use of the owner inside the group. The element type must be sendable, and IR holds the window by address (BuildExpr.jet:6297-6300). Proof: prep/c6066/bal/task_a.jet prints 6 on O0, O1 and O2; today it is E0631 at 9:17 and 9:27 (Lambdas.jet:2171-2184). prep/c6066/bal2/task_overlap.jet (both tasks write window `a`) and task_owner.jet (`print(v[0])` inside the group) are refused, each with a UI snapshot. All three become tests/cases cases.

Probes are under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/ until they become repo cases. D-MAPSLOT-WINDOW1 A: `&map[key]` at a `ViewMut<V>` destination is a one-value window over the entry's value, read as `w[0]`. IR builds the header from the entry's value address with length 1, as ir_list_window does. A missing key stops exactly as `map[key]` does. Adding or removing entries while the window lives is refused by the existing loan check (today that is E0220 at slot_grow.jet 8:5). Proof: prep/c6066/bal/slot_a.jet prints 1 on O0, O1 and O2; today it is E0108 at 2:5. prep/c6066/bal2/slot_grow.jet is refused at 8:5, with a UI snapshot. prep/c6066/bal2/slot_missing.jet stops with `the map has no entry for key "z"` on every tier. All three become cases.

Probes are under $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/ until they become repo cases. D-INDEX-COMPOUND1 A: `xs[i] op= v` and `map[key] op= v` mean the long form, with one lookup. - E0164 is retired: Prelude/Diagnostics.jet:157 becomes a retired row, and the Statements.jet:5835 refusal is removed. The Dyn-path refusal at Statements.jet:5961, which shares the code, moves to its own registered code with the same text. - Proof: prep/c6066/bal/idx_a.jet prints 2 then 2 on O0, O1 and O2. - prep/c6066/bal2/idx_missing.jet stops with E3001 `the map has no entry for key "z"`. idx_range.jet stops with E3010 `the list has 2 items, so position 5 doesn't exist`. Both match their long forms, idx_long_missing.jet and idx_long_range.jet. - tests/ui/compound_index_target becomes a run case. - The E0164 text is amended in spec.md:1449-1452, syntax-decisions.md:264-265 (S17) and architecture.md:834-835. - The comments at Statements.jet:6158 and :6221 are corrected, and so is the fixture comment at tests/cases/l0503_behavior/…/prefer_compound_assign.jet:20. L0503 itself does not change.
criteria.evidence: aaa6331fc0 release candidate kit (chain s2 98d89707fb97975a): tests/ui/compound_index_target.jet PASS. This row is the proof the precut audit named for this criterion.

criteria.text: D-WRITE-TAKE1 A (ratified 2026-11-04): core.mem has swap<T> and replace<T> (-[!Panic]>), named by the prelude with no import, while a user swap or replace still wins; List and Map gain swap. Sema tracks each moved-out gap behind E0121: an exit or a call that can stop inside a gap is E0201, and its fix offers swap or replace. IR moves the value back on every stop path inside a gap. An example with goldens on o0, o1 and o2, and UI snapshots for E0201.

Definite initialization accepts a fixed array `[T#N]{ uninit }` that a counted loop fully writes before any read; today it reports E0420. The census covers each fill shape (counted loop, while with index, fill call) and each lands as a case. Found by the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation (dev 0ccdff27ea).

cards.title: Jet one-liners: jet -e, jet run - and input through plain Core names that beat Perl and awk
cards.body:
Scripting audit 2026-10-28 (Docs/audits/scripting-peers-2026-10-28.md, row D03). Jet has no one-liner mode. Probes on commit 8fbf094: `echo 'fn run() { print("x") }' | jet run -` gives E2105 "Can't securely read the file `-`"; `jet run -e 'print(1)'` gives E2105; `jet eval 1+2` gives E2104. Perl (`perl -lane`), Ruby (`ruby -ne`), awk and nushell own this use. No card covers it: #4720's `jet eval` is pure and evaluator-only.

Design that beats them. `-e CODE` is the body of `fn run`, checked by sema exactly like a file, so a typo fails before any input is read. `-n` wraps the body in `loop line in stdin.lines()`; `-p` also prints `line` after the body; `-a` binds `words: [String]` split on whitespace (`-F,` sets the separator); `--begin`/`--end` run code before and after the loop; `-i` edits named files in place. The step Perl and awk cannot take: `--csv Row` or `--json T` decodes each record into `row: Row`, a struct declared inline or in a file, so a misspelled field is a compile error, while awk and Perl print an empty string. Compiled one-liners are cached by content hash like any script, so the second run uses native code. Piped source follows #5949: never remembered, always asks.

Spelling is decided by ballot D-SCRIPT-ONELINER1 (cards/DECISIONS.md). Map: #5981.

cards.title: Upgrades need no hand edits: every breaking change ships a `jet fix` rewrite, and last release's code builds on the new one
cards.body:
Scripting audit 2026-10-28 (row D28). `jet --version` on commit 8fbf094 prints "release readiness: not-ready" and "1.0 compatibility policy: future-1.0 (planned; not active)". Go 1 (compat promise plus `go fix`) and Perl 5 are best in class: old code keeps running. Python 2 to 3 took twelve years because most changes needed hand edits.

Design that beats them. Jet keeps greenfield freedom (AGENTS.md) but makes every break mechanical: a change that makes accepted source fail `jet check` must register a `jet fix` rewrite in the same change. CI proves it on the previous release's Examples/ and on a fixed corpus of scripts. Go fix covers a subset of changes; Jet's rule covers all of them, so users never hand-edit to upgrade. No card owns this: #5071 removes editions and retired forms but does not gate migrations. Map: #5982.

A change that makes previously accepted source fail `jet check` without registering a `jet fix` rewrite fails the guard (planted-break test).
`jet fix --from <version>` applies only the rewrites added since that version and prints one line per rewrite kind with a count (UI snapshot).
Across every release since the guard turned blocking, the number of hand edits needed to move the corpus forward is 0; the count is logged on this card per release.
The `1.0 compatibility policy` line of `jet --version` reads from Docs/spec/release-policy.md, and the policy names the release in which the guard became blocking.

cards.title: Port the Python bridge and the PyPI/npm providers to the self-hosted toolchain: `use py.X` in a loose script, each foreign package fenced by its grant
cards.body:
Scripting audit 2026-10-28 (row D06, ecosystem size). Python has 600k+ PyPI packages and JavaScript 3M+ npm packages; Jet's own registry has no public content, so Jet loses on reach by count. The ratified design already answers this. D-FFI-PY1=A (Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:4166): `use py.X` talks to a supervised sidecar CPython with a typed message boundary and the `-[FFI.Py]>` effect; `py@embed` is the opt-in in-process mode. D-JPK-EXTPROV1=A (:4185): PyPI, npm and SwiftPM are first-class providers, fetched, hash-pinned and offline after the first fetch. D-DATA-BRIDGE1=A (:5964) reserves the `py.*` and `r.*` roots. Both were built in the Rust era (#180, #937 done) and never ported: probe on commit 8fbf094, `jet run -A b/pyuse.jet` with `use python.numpy as np` gives E0603 "The imported module is not present in the package source snapshot". No open card owns the port (#5984 is a map with no criteria).

Why this beats every peer rather than tying. Reach becomes a superset: PyPI plus npm plus Jet packages, where Python reaches only PyPI and Node only npm. Safety is better than at home: a PyPI package runs in a sidecar whose OS access is fenced by the script's grants, so a package that reads ~/.ssh is refused unless FS.Read for that path was granted. pip, uv and npm run package code with the user's full authority. Mojo also imports Python modules but runs them in-process with no fence.

Scope: the self-hosted `py.*` binder (sidecar default, `py@embed` opt-in), the PyPI and npm providers in the resolver behind #4833's fetch path, typed stubs from `.pyi` files where present, and the authority wiring. The R bridge (D-FFI-R1) follows the same sidecar path and is out of scope here.

criteria.text: A loose script with `use py.numpy as np` and `print(np.mean([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))` prints 2.0 under `jet run`; the first run fetches and hash-pins numpy from PyPI, the second run works with the network disabled (test). Today E0603 (probe `jet run -A b/pyuse.jet`, commit 8fbf094).

Reach census: of the 100 most-downloaded PyPI packages, at least 90 import and pass a one-call smoke test through `use py.X` on Linux x86-64 (script and table checked in; the failing ones are listed with the reason).

Fence test: a fixture PyPI package that opens ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 at import is refused with an authority error naming FS.Read and the path, unless that grant was given; the same package under `pip install` plus `python3 -c 'import fixture'` reads the file (paired test).
The #5949 prompt lists `FFI.Py` and the Python package names when a script first uses `py.*`, and a dependency update that adds a new Python package asks again (#5459 rules).

Call cost: with `py@embed`, 100k calls of a small pure Python function finish in less than 1.5x the time of the same calls made inside CPython; with the sidecar default, the median round trip is below 20 microseconds (numbers logged per release).

A manifest dependency in the D-JPK-EXTPROV1 form (`leftpad: npm@"1.3.0"`, syntax-decisions.md:4186) fetches, pins and is called through its typed first-party stub package (:4220); the second run works offline (test).

cards.title: Benchmark Jet's build and package system against Nix, and beat it
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-28: Jet's build and package system must be lightning fast, substantially faster than Nix, more powerful, and easier to use, audit and reason about. Nix is a required peer for the build, package and configuration cells.

Compare like with like: the same project or package set built hermetically by both, on the same machine, cold and warm. Nix evaluation and store operations count, and so do Jet's check, store and cache.

log.text: KitSpeed first receipt 2026-10-28 (5 samples, interleaved; Jet/Nix medians with the SemanticIndex O(n²) fix): eval 0.77, noop 20.4, incremental 4.87, cold_cache 5.21, scratch 3.88 — all lose. Causes: 73% build-plan query (whole-package Interpreter check, eager ProgramInfo, third Doc-mode recheck); no build stamp or artifact cache (JET_CACHE_DIR unread); Core rechecked per process (~150 ms). Fix plan: build stamp, plan cache + per-module interface/object caches, CAS under JET_CACHE_DIR, build-program closure scoping + one shared check + lazy ProgramInfo, persisted Core interface. Receipt: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/land/kitspeed-nix-peer-receipt.txt

criteria.text: The canonical performance manifest lists Nix as a required peer with paired cells: config evaluation (`nix eval` vs `jet check` of the build program), no-op rebuild, one-file incremental rebuild, cold build from a populated cache or substituter, and a from-scratch hermetic build of the same medium project; each cell has a harness and committed receipts.
Every cell meets the gate (Jet/Nix below 1.00) and the evaluation, no-op and incremental cells reach Jet/Nix at most 0.25; losses stay on cards with their cause.

A side-by-side note shows the same project in Nix and in Jet: lines and concepts a reader needs, how each declares and audits inputs and effects, and reproducibility (bit-identical output on two machines or two clean stores).

cards.title: `Set` is a sorted array with a memmove per insert
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R3 (cells: w13 wall/CPU). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `Set` is a sorted array (`Compiler/JetIR/Source/BuildSets.jet:1-7`). Each insert shifts the tail with memmove (`ir_set_insert_body`, `:65-95`, memmove `:77-88`). Building a set of 2 M lines is O(n²) moves.

Evidence: perf: `jet_rt_mem_move` 80.0 %, `jet_rt_string_compare` 5.8 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 18,666 ms vs PHP 733.1 ms, Python 1,363.8 ms.

log.text: W13 root (CardClose-1, perf on a 200k-line subset, base s1 release): jet_ir_set_insert → jet_rt_mem_move is 88.5% self, string_compare 4.0%. Set<String> is a sorted array (Compiler/JetIR BuildSets.jet:65-95, ir_set_insert_body). Each new key is binary-searched, then the tail is memmoved, so n distinct keys cost O(n^2) shifting: 200k keys take 3.5 s, 2M lines 87 s. Fix: a hashed Set index like BuildMaps' hash/capacity, or insert-then-sort for bulk adds.

ScriptBench w13 on dev 69a987b5a6, wave-21 s1 (CardClose-1, sbench/w13-dev.json): LOSS against every peer. jet-bin 86.9 s wall, 79.1 s CPU, 220 MB RSS. Wall ratios: 249x python, 78.6x ruby (the closest), 241x php. jet run 56.5 s; that run may have overlapped other jobs, so it is not yet evidence of an inversion. The root is not profiled yet.

criteria.text: The cause above is removed at its root, and the probe cited in the evidence scales linearly or shows the gap closed (receipt with the command and numbers).
criteria.evidence: c375bc9af5 (a Set or Rank of hashing keys inserts and finds by hash): release gate of a0_036 at 8a85d45051 (candidate s2, 2026-11-08 01:10, all suites 0 lost, 0 untracked failures). PASS: collections_and_methods/set_inserts_by_hash_in_linear_time (TIMEOUT on a0_035, PASS on the candidate).

criteria.text: ScriptBench workload w13, measured with the BENCH.md method (hyperfine -N, interleaved, same machine), beats every measured peer on warm wall, CPU and peak RSS (Jet/peer below 1.00), on the built binary and on `jet run`; same output on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: JSON decodes through a `Dyn` tree and refuses typed input over 16 MiB
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R4 (cells: w06 wall/CPU/RSS). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: JSON parses to a `Dyn` tree first, then decodes the tree to the typed records in a second pass (`Core/Encoding/Json.jet:93`). Typed `json.decode<T>(text)` refuses input over 16 MiB (`Json.jet:81`, `:718`), so a 44 MB file must take the two-pass path. Every node is allocated and freed.

Evidence: perf: `jet_rt_alloc_8` 12.5 %, `jet_rt_free_8` 10.4 %, `jet_rt_alloc` 6.2 %, `jet_rt_dyn_to_native` 4.2 %, `jet_rt_dyn_from_native` 3.7 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 9,785 ms and 1,950,092 KB peak vs Bun (TS) 395.8 ms / 289,728 KB, Python 1,502 ms / 403,264 KB.

log.text: G1Lead b7ff715849 fixes the a0_039 gate regression from option D (c1dd8c7b26). A migration block now loads core.encoding, and E0105 never names a generated __ helper. G1Lead proof on a dev-built compiler: golden Examples/Data/Migrations/run.jet PASS on O0, O1 and O2; ui migration_change_via_ok PASS; ui marker_module_ambiguous PASS on its original snapshot; all 12 ui migration* and 6 marker_module* rows PASS; golden CryptoMigration, DecodeMigration and DBMigrationProof PASS on O0 to O2; cases filter migration 6 PASS and 3 known, decode 30 PASS and 8 known. Main re-cuts a0_039 at this commit.

G1Lead landed option D as dev c1dd8c7b26: typed json.decode<T> reads the document in place through one generated reader per type; decode(tree) is the same body over the tree source. Worker verify: check/build/selfcheck rows 0; filters encoding_parity 27, json 91, codable 13, serde 4, decode 29, corelib_parts_encoding_streams 4, all PASS. General-mechanism proof on a second program (package index, 50k+100k packages, identical output): 1648-1719 ms / 444 MiB vs 2922-3268 ms / 1.20 GiB. w06: 1633-1822 ms / 505 MB vs 3593-4058 ms / 1.46 GB. Main runs the c1/c2 peer measurements with the next seed.

Owner correction 2026-11-08 (to Main), superseding the process in the previous entry: NO ballot. The owner ratifies D directly: engineer away the downsides (hand-written impl migration, Flatten/untagged without a second semantics, error-order parity with the tree path, public Decode change size, code size and compile time), then build D. A design pass that removes each downside comes first inside the build; no owner gate before building.

Owner direction 2026-11-08 (to Main): option D. The generated Decode body reads an abstract format-neutral reader interface; Dyn is one reader and a JSON byte cursor another, so there is one copy of the decode rules (SerdeItems) and every format streams with no intermediate tree. The downsides must be engineered away before presentation: the migration of hand-written Decode impls (adapter or one cutover), Flatten and untagged enums (buffering or lookahead without a second semantics), the size of the public Decode change, the beginner surface, and error-order parity with the tree path. Process: a ballot draft with exact surface and same-program alternatives, then an adversarial design review in Docs/audits (serde Deserializer/visitor and Swift Decoder as the strongest existing designs, with measured probes), then a redesign until it holds, then owner ratification, then build. Options A/B/C are superseded.

Main 2026-11-08 06:10 c1 is owner-gated. Every #Codable decode is a Sema-generated body over `tree: Dyn` (Registration/SerdeItems.jet: field lookup, defaults, presence/E2410, DenyUnknownFields, validate, Flatten, migration, tagged/untagged enums). JetIR ir_dyn_decode only dispatches to it, so a one-pass decode needs a second, generated, per-type decoder over a byte cursor. Options (G1Lead scoping): (A) a hidden codec slot on the Prelude Decode trait, `__decode_json(cursor)`, whose default materializes the subtree and calls decode. SerdeItems emits the streaming body beside decode with shared helpers, and Flatten, untagged, migration and hand-written impls use the fallback, unchanged. This changes a public trait shape (Prelude Traits.jet, the OwnedTraitRows ratchet), so it needs a ballot and an adversarial review. Recommended. (B) a compiler-generated free function per type over a Core-private cursor. It needs a privacy exemption for generated items in Sema/Calls/Core.jet, which is frozen, so the freeze must be lifted. (C) JetIR synthesizes the readers from type rows plus TSerdeAttribute, duplicating the SerdeItems semantics in IR. That is a second mechanism (I8), the largest and riskiest; not advised. Any option must keep per-field errors in declaration order, and a syntax or duplicate-key error anywhere must replace the field errors, as the tree path does. Separately in scope now: dropping the 16 MiB typed-decode refusal (typed decode over 16 MiB then works through the tree path). That is not the root fix.

Main 2026-11-08 00:00: PortsLead-2 found c1 needs a streaming Decode path. The Prelude trait is decode(tree: Dyn) and SerdeItems derives it, so every typed decode builds the Dyn tree first. Meeting c1 needs a language-level change to the Decode trait and its derive, not a library fix. It needs a design (and a ballot if it changes the public trait) before code. Deferred out of the overnight G4 push.

W06 root (CardClose-1): json.parse_with_limits (Core/Encoding/Json.jet:93 → parse_value/object/array, 392-672) builds the whole 40 MB document as a Dyn tree: one allocation per value and key, plus a positions map per object. Person.decode then walks it again (dyn_to_native, string_clone). Typed json.decode<T> refuses input over 16 MiB, which forces this path. Fix: a typed streaming decode from bytes straight to the target type, with no Dyn tree.

Correction (CardClose-1, perf stat -r 3, sbench/w06-evsym.txt): there is no O0-vs-full inversion. --release 4.06 s, 18.0G cycles; --optimize=none 4.06 s, 17.5G; jet run 5.22 s, a third of it compile. The earlier jet-bin 5961 ms was load noise. Root: per-value allocation and the Dyn round-trip. jet_rt_alloc_8, free_8, alloc, dyn_from_native, string_drop and free make up about half of all cycles, all in the runtime pack, which --optimize does not touch.

ScriptBench w06 on dev 69a987b5a6, wave-21 s1 (CardClose-1, sbench/w06-dev.json): LOSS against every peer. jet-bin 5961 ms wall, 5640 ms CPU, 1.26 GB RSS. The closest peer is python (4.09x wall, 3.93x RSS); bun is 46.6x wall and 9.0x RSS. jet run (4468 ms) beats the optimized binary, the same inversion seen on w05.

criteria.text: The cause above is removed at its root, and the probe cited in the evidence scales linearly or shows the gap closed (receipt with the command and numbers).
