cards.title: CSV builds fields byte by byte, re-validates UTF-8 per field and materializes every row
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R5 (cells: w05 wall/CPU/RSS). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: CSV pushes each byte into a `[U8]` (`Core/Encoding/Csv.jet:341-441`), then makes each field with `String.from_bytes(field.copy())`, which validates UTF-8 again per field (`:382`, `:390`). All rows are materialized before the caller sees one, so peak memory grows with the file.

Evidence: perf: `core_encoding_csv_parse_rows_with` 12.7 %, `jet_rt_free_8` 10.3 %, `unit_numeric_int_parse` 7.5 %, `jet_rt_alloc_8` 6.8 %, `unit_text_bytes_utf8_error` 5.4 %. Timed warm: jet-bin 1,976 ms and 719,540 KB peak vs LuaJIT 498.8 ms / 2,768 KB, Python 2,136 ms / 11,848 KB.

log.text: w05 streamed with csv.reader: 204.4G -> 33.9G instructions:u (6.0x), 26.6 s -> 5.2 s, RSS 151 MB (csv.rows: 850 MB); same totals Landed in wave 32 as dev f251c88891 (Codegen-1-55).

2026-11-01 c2 measured on 360e470044 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/sbench/h360-report.md): FAIL every cell; jet-bin 1057 ms / 879 MB, closest peer php 1.08/1.07. Root: csv.rows materializes [CSVRow] (Csv.jet:62/400); perf self: numeric_trim_start 18.9%, parse_rows_with 18.9%, int_parse 12.5%, sentry enter/leave 6.6%.

Codegen-1 root analysis on dev bb770de593 (w05, 1M rows, instructions:u / ms / RSS):
- csv.rows as written: 9.35G / 1323 ms / 850 MB, because every row is materialized.
- Streaming csv.reader + next(): 204G / 26.5 s / 149 MB. encoding.__read_byte runs once per byte, at about 7000 instructions per byte.
- With an unlanded Core fix (CSVReader reads buffer_bytes chunks via __read_into, charges the budget once per buffer, and has a bulk path for unquoted bytes): 33.9G / 5.2 s / 151 MB.
- Remaining cost: per-field stream.charge/reserve and the AllocationBudget guard edits.
- The fix is parked in Codegen-1's lane (w28 Core). It is not lane-checked yet.

ScriptBench w05 on dev bb770de593 (wave-28 tree s2, BENCH.md method, 2026-11-01 13:38): still FAIL c2. jet-bin 1646 ms wall / 1548 ms cpu / 873,200 KiB peak RSS; jet-run 1939 ms / 872,504 KiB. Loses on every peer (deno wall 0.69x but cpu 2.25x; RSS 3.6x-310x worse: perl/lua/luajit/php hold ~3-10 MB). The RSS shows every row is still materialized. Log: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb-w05w11.log

W05 profile (CardClose-1, 69a987b5a6): Core Csv.jet:383 materializes [CSVRow] (871 MB). Int.parse is 31% of cycles and the per-field #Unsafe sentry scope in field_text (Csv.jet:376) is 11%. The fix is still the streaming CSV path in Core/encoding logged earlier; the sentry scope per field is a second, separate cost.

Correction (CardClose-1, perf annotate sbench/w05.perf.data): unit_numeric_trim_start already exits on a printable ASCII byte (IntParse.jet:13). Its 21% self time is two cache misses, the text-length load (34.6% of samples) and the first data byte (44.6%), on cold field Strings. The root is csv.rows building every row up front (871 MB, about 870 B/row). The fix is a streaming or field-view csv path in Core/encoding, not a runtime fast path.

ScriptBench w05 on dev 69a987b5a6 (CardClose-1, sbench/w11-w05.json): LOSS. jet-bin 1653 ms wall, 1532 ms CPU, 871 MB RSS; vs bun wall 9.58x, RSS 3.80x; RSS loses to every peer (lua 310x). jet run (1168 ms) is faster than the optimized binary. Roots (perf, --optimize full): Int.parse 31% inclusive with numeric_trim_start 21% self; csv parse_rows_with 50% inclusive; sentry scope enter/leave 11%; mem_move 8.6%. RSS: csv.rows materializes all 1M rows with per-field Strings (about 870 B/row) where peers stream.

cards.title: Waiting for a child process polls in 1–10 ms slices (~10 ms per spawn)
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R6 (cells: w07 wall). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: Waiting for a child polls. The collector waits in 1 ms slices (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/ProcessExecutionCollect.jet:190`); the waiter yields in 10 ms scheduler waits (`:225-229`, comment: "polling remains the seed's 10ms scheduler wait"). About 10 ms per child; w07 runs 100 children.

Evidence: Timed: jet-bin warm 1,057.9 ms (≈ 10.6 ms per child) vs Bun 129.3 ms, Python 141.2 ms. CPU is much closer (jet-bin 216 ms vs Bun 132 ms), so most of the wall time is waiting.

log.text: Owner cut the agent count to 2. MechD-3 stopped. Unlanded: its c2 (w07) work and inline-run drafts in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MechD (patch-g5 landed as c639365c56). c2 is not started.

c1 follow-up (MechD-3): on the CardClose-54 base c66f96253f, strace -f -c over 1000 run() calls shows 1000 poll calls, one per run, each returning on pipe HUP or pidfd readiness, and 0 nanosleep or clock_nanosleep. The 1-10 ms sleep slices are gone.

c2 remeasured on 2ba0d540c4 (base jet, ScriptBench copy $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb/scriptbench with imports migrated to 'use X :: core.X'; bun is 1.3.13 because 1.4.4 is no longer substitutable; receipt $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sbench/w07w11.json). w07 FAILS, so c2 stays open. jet-bin 110.8 ms wall, 5920 KiB; jet-run 116.3 ms, 9684 KiB. Losses: php wall 1.09 / cpu 1.14 (php 101.6 ms); perl cpu 1.01 and rss 1.00; rss vs lua 1.35, luajit 1.34, bash 1.16. jet-run also loses to python cpu 1.01, bun wall 1.02, perl wall 1.01, php wall 1.14, and rss vs perl, lua, luajit and bash. Roots: per-spawn cost (about 1.1 ms vs php's 1.0 ms) and a 5.9 MiB resident floor against 4.4-5.1 MiB for lua and bash.

2026-11-01 c2 measured on 360e470044 (BENCH.md, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/sbench/h360-report.md): FAIL. jet-bin 192.9 ms loses wall/cpu to php 1.30/1.33, perl 1.12/1.10, python 1.11/1.11. Root: run_spec starts a collector thread (192 MiB stack, clone/join), 3 pipe2 pairs capturing unread stdio, /dev/null, 23 extra parent syscalls per child; peers inherit stdio.

ScriptBench w07 on dev 1620f05362 + tools (wave-27 tree s2, BENCH.md method, 2026-11-01 12:35): still FAIL c2. jet-bin 191.1 ms wall / 187.4 ms cpu / 4140 KiB for 100 children; loses to php 146.3 ms (1.31x) and perl 175.4 ms (1.09x); jet-run also loses on rss to perl and lua. The 1-10 ms poll is gone (c1); the remaining ~0.45 ms per child is spawn-path CPU (the child already uses clone(CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK)). Log: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb-w07w10.log

Landed on dev at undefined in CardClose-54 (patch row: criterion/count 1): Root removed (tsc s1, runtime pack 827b3c1660d49fda = dev 69a987b5a6 + d4f3932172): the waiter's park slot is woken by the collector when it sets done, and the idle collector sleeps on the child's pidfd instead of 1-10 ms slices. Probe: 1,000 sequential run_spec(cmd(["true"])) take 11165 -> 3815 ms under strace, and timed park waits ending on the timeout fall from 1291 to 261 (re-parks; 0 lost wakes). ScriptBench w07 jet-bin 1037.6 -> 133.9 ms wall (7.7x), jet-run 1052.7 -> 128.6 ms; O0/O1/O2 print children ok=100.

Correction (CardClose-1): process_execution_env_remove (ProcessExecutionPrepare.jet:26) is about a third of the jet process's own samples, or 17.4% of all samples, not 38%. No other jet function is above 4%.

W07 root after CardClose-54, on 69a987b5a6 + CardClose-54 (CardClose-1; confirm on the wave-24 HEAD). Each spawn builds the child environment twice: once to prepare (Compiler/JetRuntime ProcessExecutionPrepare.jet:240) and once for the receipt identity, only to read PATH (ProcessExecutionReceipt.jet:250). Each build copies the inherited environment through process_execution_env_set (ProcessExecutionPrepare.jet:45), which removes by key linearly for each var. With 169 vars that is about 14k string_eq per build, plus 4 allocations per var: 38% of user samples. The inherited keys are already unique, so the fix is to move-push them and read PATH directly. Pinned to one CPU, jet equals python (0.23 s); php and bun remain ahead. Handoff: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/HANDOFF-scriptbench.md.

cards.title: `para_map` runs one worker per 64 items and ignores `limit:`
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R8 (cells: w11 wall). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `para_map` splits work into fixed 64-item ranges (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Parallel.jet:24-26`, `:90`) and starts at most one worker per range (`:94`). w11 has 100 URLs, so only 2 workers run, each doing up to 64 blocking GETs in a row, whatever `limit:` says.

Evidence: Timed: jet-bin warm 1,356.9 ms vs Bun 222.5 ms, Python 312.5 ms; 64 × 20 ms server delay = 1.28 s.

log.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Q19): A. Public Core gets core.tasks.cpu_ns() -> Int (CPU time used by the current task) and core.tasks.current_task() returns a real task id; the compiler trace uses that public surface rather than a private route.

SchedLead commit 1/7 landed as afe2acc8c8: tasks run on fibers that park instead of blocking their worker thread; closed InlineAsm rails X64_FIBER_SWITCH and X64_GS_BASE_WRITE, gated by IRProgram.asm_rails. Its receipt: precommit rc=0, VERIFY OK, LaneCheck CHECK OK; focused task/cancel/generator/para/deadline/sleep cases and the concurrency goldens equal to baseline. #6403 r08: the quick task finishes in 98.7 us (base 2.9 s). 100000 cancel/timer/wake race rounds all accounted on every tier (base hangs). No leak over 3 x 10000 cancelled parked tasks. About 5.7 KB per parked task. w11 still loses to bun on wall (105.95 vs 94.66 ms); the root is the para_map limit cap at the core count, which is commit 2. Open: the ~32k live-fiber cap (vm.max_map_count) must degrade or diagnose, never crash; a 100k-task case is requested. #6403 c4 names a function that was removed; it gets reworded to the offload stats at c6.

Owner decision 2026-11-08 (to Main): build the async-I/O scheduler redesign now, no ballot. Tasks are multiplexed on few threads, with the epoll wait run on the waiting thread (the D-PARA-LIMIT1 path) instead of an OS thread per in-flight wait plus a poller-thread hop. Scope covers the same root in #6403 (a blocked task holds its worker) and #6440 (generator yield is a park/wake, about 20 us). Engineer away the downsides (task/channel/cancellation semantics unchanged on every tier, blocking foreign calls and OS waits offloaded, fairness and deadlines, I9 parity, debuggability), then build. Target: w11 beats every peer on wall, CPU and RSS (bun 9.25 ms CPU; jet 19.5 ms after fixes 1-4).

Main 2026-11-08 04:55 w11 fix 3 landed bee6af85ed (inet_pton for literal hosts, no getaddrinfo): perf task-clock -r30 25.4 -> 21.2 ms CPU, hyperfine user+sys 20.7 -> 17.7 ms, wall unchanged at 87 ms (G1Lead). Fix 2 (persistent epoll registration, 21.2 -> 20.9 ms) is queued in lane-commit; fix 1 (wake after unlock, 20.9 -> 20.3 ms) passed VERIFY and is next. bun stays at 9.25 ms CPU; c2 still fails pending the scheduler redesign.

Main 2026-11-08 04:40 w11 c2 profile (G1Lead, dev at 15e01b1474, perf stat -r30, nice 19, busy box): bun 9.25 ms CPU and 89.2 ms wall against jet-bin 25.8 ms CPU and 87.2 ms wall, so Jet wins wall unpinned and loses CPU 2.8x. Pinned to 12 cores Jet wall is 187 ms (para_map worker cap). Breakdown: 25 para workers spawn and join in 1.6 ms. 100 sequential GETs take 11.1 ms, about 110 us per request against about 40 us for bun, from 22 syscalls per request: 6 futex poller hops, 4 epoll_ctl ADD/DEL on every wait, 4 setsockopt, and a musl getaddrinfo mmap/munmap even for 127.0.0.1. Parallel overhead adds about 9 ms: 1401 of 2090 futex calls hit the HostNetPoller root mutex, which is held while waking ParkSlots and around epoll_ctl. The server delay adds about 4 ms. Approved bounded runtime fixes, to land after the next seed, in this order: Jet-side IP literal parse, register once with MOD re-arm, wake after unlock (prototype 25.8 -> 24.5 ms), then shard the root lock if still hot; estimated 19-21 ms total. The verdict: bounded fixes cannot reach bun 9 ms. The floor of the current model is one OS thread per in-flight request plus a poller hop (2 context switches) per wait. Closing c2 needs the D-PARA-LIMIT1 async-I/O path (waits multiplexed on few threads, epoll on the waiting thread): a scheduler redesign needing owner scope.

Main 2026-11-08 04:15: 7bf10da106 by PortsLead-2 does not meet c2. It resolves IP literals through getaddrinfo AI_NUMERICHOST on the caller thread, adds a word-sized Int division fast path for boxed operands, and reads the clock through vDSO clock_gettime with the replay env parsed once. w11 jet-bin instructions:u 104.4M -> 32.8M, task-clock 45.1 -> 24.7 ms; jet run 164.6M -> 92.4M; clones 126 -> 26, clock_gettime 2909 -> 0. On a loaded machine (15 runs, wall/CPU ms): jet-bin 85.5/19.2, jet-run 99.0/33.2, bun 87.1/8.1, deno 112.8/38.6. Still loses to bun on CPU; the rest is futex/thread-park, about 14 ms of system time, which is a scheduler redesign. A quiet-window measure is queued in proofq as Main-PortsLead-w11-measure.sh.

Spreading receipt for 9177db37e4, same compiler (seed-built from d405d4cb6c). Probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/para/para16.jet: 16 items of a 20M-step LCG kernel; under the old 64-item chunks all 16 ran on one worker. Built with jet build --release: ser wall 0.430 s (cpu 0.44 s); para_map wall 0.042 s (cpu 0.50 s), 10.2x. jet run (O0): ser 1.139 s, par 0.068 s. Every mode prints total 6472. c2 (ScriptBench w11) waits on the ScriptBench rebuild.

dev 9177db37e4 (Main): an unlimited para_map, para_filter or para_partition now passes PARA_EVERY_WORKER (1073741824) instead of -1 (BuildParallel.jet). The runtime caps it at the available parallelism, so chunks are the items spread over the pool, at most 64, and a short list of costly items reaches every worker. para_fold keeps -1 and its 64-item chunks (merge-tree contract). Compile-time code keeps cap 1, so the same value. The Parallel.jet comment and core-library.md core.tasks were updated; 4df47ce6da has the c5 paragraph. Proof is queued for the dev s1 batch: the 16-item probe at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/para/para.jet should show the parallel run well under the serial one, with every result 508760, plus goldens Concurrency/Parallel and ParallelIter.

Finding for c2 (Main 2026-11-07): an unlimited para_map over fewer than 64 items is one chunk, so it runs on the caller thread (Parallel.jet:22-26 keeps 64 items per chunk when limit < 0). 16 items of a 20M-step kernel: built binary par (map+fold) real 0.893 s, user 0.992 s = serial x2. para_fold's 64-item grouping is its contract (BuildParallel.jet:570-573), but para_map, para_filter and para_partition could spread a short list over the pool the way the limited path does (parallel_chunk_size). w11 passes limit: 32, so it already takes the spreading path.

Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT); the Rust-free toolchain (Jet suites and tests/cases rows replace cargo tests and .rs sources).
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 3 criteria from archived #3672: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

c2 remeasured on 2ba0d540c4 (same setup and receipt as #6084: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sbench/w07w11.json; bun 1.3.13). w11 FAILS, so c2 stays open. jet-bin 106.8 ms wall, 21.8 ms cpu; bun 93.4 ms wall, 21.2 ms cpu: jet-bin/bun wall 1.14, cpu 1.03. jet-run/bun wall 1.23, cpu 1.45; jet-run/deno wall 1.03. All other peers are wins. With a 20 ms server delay and 32-way concurrency the ideal is about 4 rounds x 20 ms = 80 ms, so Jet spends about 27 ms of wall outside the server wait against bun's 13 ms: the per-request concurrency path, not CPU, is the gap.

2026-11-01 c2 measured on 360e470044 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/sbench/h360-report.md): FAIL vs bun only (wall 1.46, cpu 2.18). Root: parallel_limit (Parallel.jet:11-16) caps limit:32 at the CPU count, giving 20 chunks of 5 blocking GETs; each http.get starts its own thread (121 clones for 100 requests).

ScriptBench w11 on dev bb770de593 (wave-28 tree s2, BENCH.md method, 2026-11-01 13:39): still FAIL c2, only against bun. jet-bin 143.6 ms wall / 38.7 ms cpu / 1,860 KiB; jet-run 150.9 ms / 56.0 ms / 15,424 KiB. Loses to bun on wall (1.31x) and cpu (1.75x); beats it on rss; wins against every other peer. The floor for 100 fetches at 32 at a time with a 20 ms answer is 4 rounds (~80 ms), so ~60 ms is scheduling/spawn overhead. Log: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb-w05w11.log

ScriptBench w11 on the wave-24 tree (a34ef0affd content, s2), BENCH.md method, measured by Main 08:15 EST while two suites shared the machine: FAIL. jet-bin 231.8 ms wall, 43.5 ms CPU, 2368 KiB RSS; jet run 438.8 ms, 67.9 ms, 13976 KiB. Results: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sbench/run/res/w11-r1.json.

cards.title: `fs.walk` collects and sorts every entry before yielding
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R10 (cells: w02 wall/CPU/RSS). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: `fs.walk` collects every entry, then sorts the whole list by path (`Core/Files/Files.jet:1501-1530`, sort at `:1529`). The program then stats each file again for its size.

Evidence: perf spread over `core_files_walk_impl`, `jet_rt_string_compare`, alloc/free. Timed warm: jet-bin 113.6 ms vs Lua 59.6 ms, Bash 65.6 ms, LuaJIT 65.6 ms.

log.text: 412154ebff (G1Lead): fixes the I2 ICE at its root, in JetIR ir_call_row. An argument widened to a union is boxed as the callee parameter's own union, registered by the callee signature, rather than a union respelled in the caller's scope. New case core_path_foundations/core_path_calls_core_files_on_every_tier passes on O0/O1/O2 (9 core.files.path functions plus missing paths); seed a0_038 fails it with 8 ir.build faults. A census of Core union parameters (String|Path 46 sites, [String]|HTTPCorsOrigins 1, Int|ServiceWorkflow 7, LocalDate|DateTime 1) is covered by the same fix. Open structural finding, I8: Core declares Path twice (the Core/Compiler/Lang.jet builtin and core.files.path), so user code `files.exists(path.of("x"))` fails with E0112. Making it one Path is a Core API design call that waits for a ballot. Also seen: CoreSurfaceLedger --check fails under the seed on core.files.__walk_release (seed against tree; it clears with the next seed).

Lander gap closed (Main, 2026-11-08): the precommit census (the lander's census-snap.sh) checked Compiler/JetCli but never Core, unlike Land.jet census selfcheck-core, so a Core spelling no compiler accepts landed in 863e3d6b4e. The census now runs `jet check --threads 12 Core` with keep-going using the compiler it just built, and precommit requires `selfcheck-core rc=0 rows=0`. Probe: dev Core gives rc=0 rows=0; a copy with the old Path.jet:410 spelling gives rc=1 with the same 2 rows (E0047, INCOMPLETE) the a0_039 preflight reported; about 3 s per run.

cd58a15b81 (G1Lead): Core/Files/Path.jet walk unwraps each entry with `entry ?? return Err(err)`. The old `entry?.path` spelling checks under no compiler (E0047 on a0_038 and on dev sema), and it landed because precommit does not gate selfcheck-core; that lander gap is Main's. A Core census under a0_038 and B2 is clean after the fix (0 rows), and the walk cases pass 11/11. Found while fixing it: no case calls core.files.path walk, and every core.files.path function passing path.raw to a `String | Path` parameter ICEs in ir.build ("union String | core.files.path::Path without a definition") on a0_038 and on dev, an I2 violation. Routed to G1Lead ahead of #6082 D: fix the root in lowering, add an O0/O1/O2 case, and census the other Core parameter unions.

Phase 2 landed as 863e3d6b4e (62 files, lane-commit precommit passed). G1Lead reports peak RSS, old vs new, of 13.4/40.2/160.6 MB vs 15.0/15.0/14.4 MB on 20k/80k/323k entries, identical path order, and the Iterable-loop authority fix (E1803/E0740). Main could not re-check this with the a0_038 seed: a probe built inside the dev checkout came out byte-identical to one built outside any checkout and still reported no FS requirement, so the seed does not pick up the checkout Core. c1 is to be measured with a compiler built from 863e3d6b4e or later, in the next batch verification. Scripts: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/walk6086/ab2.sh.

Owner decision 2026-11-08 (to Main): option A, no ballot. walk/walk_files become lazy, with per-entry results: each entry or its own IOError is yielded as the walk goes, break/drop closes the handles, and memory is bounded by depth. One greenfield cutover migrates every caller (G1Lead census: 52 files: Examples using .len()/index, Path.walk() -> [Path], the L0522 lint, docs); collecting is explicit. Engineer the downsides away in the build (error visibility for callers that only want a list, ordering identical to today, the beginner path), then build.

Main 2026-11-08 05:45 c1 is owner-gated (public API). Since e3e314c953 the walk is depth-first and sorts one directory at a time, so the collect-then-sort-everything cause is gone; what remains is the collected result in the public signature: walk/walk_files return [WalkEntry] !IOError (core-library.md). Today a failed directory drops its subtree, the walk continues, and the earliest failure is the Err of the whole walk. A stream cannot keep that contract, because it has yielded entries before the Err exists. Options (G1Lead census, 52 files touched by A: Examples using .len()/index, Path.walk() -> [Path], the L0522 lint, docs): (A) walk/walk_files become a lazy per-entry-fallible stream, and every caller migrates in one cutover; (B) keep the list API and add a streaming twin (new surface, against I8 one mechanism); (C) keep the list: linear time per e3e314c953, peak memory proportional to the tree, and c1 is reworded to time-linear. Needs an owner ballot (with an adversarial review before A/B is built). G1Lead builds whatever is ratified.

MechD-3 stopped (2-agent cap); nothing of this landed. Its proposed design: add fs.walk_iter(root, ignore:) and walk_files_iter, which return an Iterable of Result<WalkEntry, IOError>, walk depth-first keeping only the open directories on the current path, and sort siblings per directory, so the order is by path component (the order __walk_before uses for errors, and walkdir's sort_by_file_name). walk and walk_files keep their signatures and collect over it, which removes the BFS queue and the global string sort. Visible change: 'a/b' now sorts before 'a.txt' and 'a-c'. walk_iter is new public API and the order change is product behavior, so this needs an owner ballot before it is built.

cards.title: Plain `jet run` keeps an unoptimized program, slower than `--release`
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R15 (cells: `jet-run` warm cells that do real work (w03, w05, w06, w14)). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: Plain `jet run` builds with the stock options; only `--release` adds `optimize: full` (`Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Front.jet:755-757`, `:777`, `:799-801`). So the kept script program is unoptimized, and a warm `jet run` is slower than the `--release` binary of the same file.

Evidence: Timed warm, jet-run / jet-bin: w03 18,572 / 14,790 ms (1.26), w05 2,747 / 1,976 ms (1.39), w06 12,223 / 9,785 ms (1.25), w14 135.7 / 74.1 ms (1.83). (w09 13.8× and w10 2.3× are mostly R12 start-up; w04 0.83 and w13 0.99 are within their ± 34 % / ± 11 % spread.)
cards.probe: jet run Tools/gauntlet/entries/text-script/jet/run.jet

log.text: Main 2026-11-08 04:05 regression (blocks the a0_037 release): a kept program reused by plain jet run runs as a child of a waiting jet run that does not forward SIGINT, so `kill -INT <jet run pid>` leaves the program running. A fresh compile runs the program in-process, and SIGINT ends it. Lost cases: corelib/core_os_interrupt_delivery_matches_aot_jit_and_interpreter and core_os_interrupt_callback_forms_match_dev_tiers. Repro: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/intr/probe2.py. G1Lead is fixing it by making the kept launch take the same in-process path, one mechanism.

Main: c6's tier-trace test and interp/deopt rows have no meaning without an interpreter; c6 now proves native byte-exact runs on every level. c8's 'evaluator' is compile-time code, which runs natively at O0 (I9). CardCleanup Q(c).
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).
#6563 c1 precut audit re-added 7 criteria from archived #2862, #2864: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

ScriptBench w15 on dev 69a987b5a6 (CardClose-1): the jet run path costs 16.8 ms CPU and 9.5 MB RSS to launch the kept program, against 1.8 ms and 0.25 MB for the built binary. jet-run cells therefore lose to luajit (CPU 7.01, RSS 3.75), perl (CPU 4.23), php (CPU 2.69) and bash (RSS 1.30), while jet-bin beats every peer. These cells are report-only under D-PERF-RUNCELL1=B. The root is the run-path launch overhead this card and D-RUN-TIER1 cover.

Ballot D-RUN-TIER1 drafted (A: jet run at basic; B: first run at none, a reused script is rebuilt once at full; C: keep, use --release), rec B, at $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/ballot-run-tier1.json. Not posted yet: it needs the cross-family adversarial review pass first.

Ballot input (UiGreen-1, INFERENCE, not measured): (b) costs one kept --release image per script (it replaces the none image, so the net cost is the size difference) and one full-optimize rebuild per script source, about a jet build --release, on the first reuse (2nd run) or in the background after the 1st; the cold run is unchanged. Card warm ms, jet run (none) / jet-bin (release): w03 18572/14790 (1.26x), w05 2747/1976 (1.39x), w06 12223/9785 (1.25x), w14 135.7/74.1 (1.83x).

UiGreen-1 2026-10-31 23:50: owner gate. Plain jet run optimizing none is ratified (Docs/spec spec.md:3815-3816, D-BUILD-DEFAULT1=B, syntax-decisions.md:5713). Fix options for a ballot: (a) jet run stock = basic (cold compile cost; run cases re-key); (b) cold jet run stays none, and the kept script program (ScriptCache) is rebuilt at full once warm (tier-up on reuse, same meaning per I9); (c) keep as is. UiGreen-1 leans (b). Parked until the owner rules; Main is preparing the ballot.

cards.title: Get-push-store grouping copies the whole group per row, silently
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R17 (cells: w10 (first Jet version; fixed before the timed cells)). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: The obvious grouping idiom `group := by_dept.get(k) ?? [Person]{}`, `group.push(p)`, `by_dept[k] = group` copies the whole group list, strings included, on every row: the list is still shared with the map, so the push makes it unique first. `jet check` gives no warning. The in-place form `by_dept[k].push(p)` (after `has_key`) avoids the copy.

Evidence: `perf record` of the first version: `jet_rt_string_clone` 24.7 % (21.2 % under `jet_ir_unique_*`), drop 20.1 %, `jet_ir_unique_*` 7.1 %. Paired run, `hyperfine -N --runs 30 --warmup 3`, cores 16-19: old 10.3 ms ± 2.3, in-place 4.3 ms ± 1.1 (2.37×). `jet check probes/w10_old.jet` → "has no problems".

log.text: Probe 2026-11-07 (Main, a0_034 on dev a5476b82af, built binary --release): $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/grp/grp.jet, N rows into 10 String groups. get-push-store (group := m.get(k) ?? [String]{}; group.push(x); m[k] = group): N=20,000 0.095 s, N=200,000 9.887 s (10x rows, 104x time: quadratic). In place (has_key, then m[k].push(x)): 0.005 s and 0.050 s (linear). At 200k the idiom is 198x slower. Rewrite hazard for any fix that turns the get into a take: a statement between the get and the store-back that can exit early (?, return, break, panic) would leave the map missing key k where today it keeps the old group. So the rewrite must hold only when nothing in between exits early or reads or writes the map, or when the map is dead on every early exit.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A and D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A (no call-site marks; `&&` marks a take).

criteria.text: Either the get-push-store form no longer copies the group (in-place update through the map), or `jet check` reports it with a registered diagnostic whose fix rewrites it to the in-place form; a UI snapshot or case proves it.
criteria.evidence: 10ce9aab90 (on dev): jet check reports the get-push-store form as L0534 jet.MapGroupRoundTrip with a NeedsReview fix-it to the in-place form. Proved with the census-built dev compiler at 15b9773dee (check, build, runtime and selfcheck rc=0, 0 rows): jet test Compiler --profile ui --filter map_group_round_trip PASS 1/1; on a copy of tests/ui_lint/map_group_round_trip.jet, jet check gives 1 L0534 before, jet fix --all rc=0, and jet check gives 0 L0534 after; jet run of the rewritten file rc=0 (prints 2, 2).

criteria.text: The cause above is removed at its root, and the probe cited in the evidence scales linearly or shows the gap closed (receipt with the command and numbers).
criteria.evidence: 2d77541df1 (G1Lead): `group := M.get(K) ?? F; S; M[K] = group` lowers to the canonical &M[K] write window when S cannot observe the difference (no read of the map root in S, no early exit or ?, an immutable key root, group unnamed after the store, no closure cell). L0534 is narrowed to the shapes where the copy is semantically required. Probe receipt (--release, best of 3, taskset one core), times in s: N=25k/50k/100k/200k/400k: old 0.005/0.009/0.017/0.035/0.071, header 0.005/0.010/0.018/0.036/0.072, call 0.006/0.012/0.023/0.045/0.090, hand-written in-place 0.005/0.010/0.018/0.038/0.073, so linear and equal to the in-place form (the a0_036 seed was 0.149/0.595 at 25k/50k, quadratic). Front insert is quadratic only through its own memmove and equals the hand-written in-place insert (1.905 vs 1.914 at 400k). Checks: verify-tree OK; ui_lint map_group_round_trip PASS; golden MapGroupGrowsInPlace o0/o1/o2 PASS; a new case (an update left half way shows the same map on every tier) agrees on run/none/basic/release.

cards.title: Every lazy-iterator pull locks a global mutex to charge comptime fuel
cards.body:
ScriptBench 2026-10-28 root cause R18 (cells: w10 jet-bin wall/CPU vs Lua and LuaJIT). Report: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Audit/scripting/bench/BENCH.md.

Cause: After R17, the rest is text splitting and iteration. Every pull of a lazy runtime iterator calls `jet_rt_iter_charge` (`Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Iter.jet:277`), which locks and unlocks a global mutex to charge compile-time fuel even when no compile-time evaluation runs (`IterCharge.jet:4-21`).

Evidence: `perf record` of the timed w10 binary: `jet_rt_native_iter_string_split` 12.1 %, `jet_rt_iter_charge` 8.8 %, `main_run` 6.3 %, `jet_rt_alloc` 5.4 %. Timed: jet-bin cold 4.3 ms / warm 5.3 ms vs LuaJIT 2.7 / 2.7 ms, Lua 4.8 / 3.4 ms; every other peer is slower.

log.text: 2026-11-01 c2 measured on 360e470044 ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CardClose/sbench/h360-report.md): FAIL. jet-bin 25.4 ms loses to php 1.66/1.59, bun 1.13/1.05, luajit wall 1.01. Root: alloc/free per split piece (280k each); needs a borrowed-view split lowering (sbench/w10-root.md).

ScriptBench w10 on dev 1620f05362 + tools (wave-27 tree s2, BENCH.md method, 2026-11-01 12:36): still FAIL c2. jet-bin 19.3 ms wall / 19.9 ms cpu loses to php 12.0 ms (1.61x) and bun 13.0 ms (1.49x); ties luajit. The global fuel mutex is gone (c1); the rest is line/word splitting cost. Log: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/sb-w07w10.log

criteria.text: The cause above is removed at its root, and the probe cited in the evidence scales linearly or shows the gap closed (receipt with the command and numbers).
criteria.evidence: Iter.jet iter_pull calls jet_rt_iter_charge only when the compile-time request's active word is set; ScriptBench w10 (n=15) jet-bin 15.6 ms vs jet-base 15.9 ms on a34ef0affd + this patch; REF-SAME 48/48; lane-check CHECK OK (jet-lane-check.spRDYt) Landed in wave 25 as dev 367eaf8f0d (Codegen-1-44).

cards.title: Port the deleted Rust tests coverage to Jet tests (202 tests, 64 areas)
cards.body: RustOut7 2026-10-28: the tests/**/*.rs suite (37 files, 56.7k lines) could no longer compile (no root Cargo.toml; it imports deleted crates) and is deleted under #4717. Of its 769 tests, 202 have no Jet counterpart: 169 have no port, 32 were ported only on origin/port/main, and 1 was never audited. Each criterion names one area. The full per-test lists are in the mapping TSVs ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/RustOut2/out/rust-tests-uncovered.tsv and rust-tests-mapping.tsv, archived with the deletion commit). The behavior is planned coverage, so it stays on the board until a Jet test covers it.

log.text: c65 root 2 (closed-list guard) fixed on dev: dace302873 (SchedLead), 2e4142d89c (SpeedLead) and 72e3e2cd78 (QuickLead). The precommit tests/guards run on 72e3e2cd78 gives 122 passed, 0 failed. The Main precommit now runs tests/guards with an empty baseline, so any new closed-list problem fails a commit. Also landed: 8b040ecdba (#6696: the libc census prints on demand; generated table removed from Docs).

Correction to the P15 note above (SchedLead measurement; buildsample with rusage). CPU did not regress: cold jet build Compiler is user 106.7 s plus sys 10.0 s on a0_038 at c902740d37, and user 107.7 s plus sys 9.7 s on a0_039 at b7ff715849. The trace accounting broke: Request.jet keeps span stacks and item cpu_ns by OS thread, and since afe2acc8c8 tasks resume on other carriers. The a0_039 trace has B=10147 against E=10086 (61 spans never closed), nested phases count as top-level, so whole-process CPU is summed per carrier, and item cpu_ns differences two threads clocks. The jet check wall difference is fsync stalls on the cache store (9.9 s and 12.7 s per strace), the known store journal cost SpeedLead fixes after c6. A task-heavy program (4000 tasks) shows no spin. Fix: SchedLead does opt-in per-fiber CPU accounting in the runtime and keys the Request.jet stacks by task; the surface for the task clock and id is owner Q19.

P15 root measured (Main, cold traced jet build Compiler checked by Tools/perf/budget/Check.jet at 225K). a0_038 on c902740d37: wall 59.3 s, work sum 108.8 s, P15 0.08 s, P4 comptime 2.42 s (508 us per item), P8 8.67 s. a0_039 on b7ff715849: wall 53.1 s, work sum 498.6 s, P15 305.2 s, P4 25.8 s (5.4 ms per item), P8 18.5 s. Cold jet check of Compiler/JetFoundation: a0_038 real 43.8 s, user 293 s; a0_039 real 91.0 s, user 56 s, so parallel check lost its parallelism. The suspect range includes the fibers commit afe2acc8c8 (#6085 c2). Routed to SchedLead as top priority, with p15.sh as the proof harness. Guard rows: dace302873 (SchedLead) and 2e4142d89c (SpeedLead) landed; only QuickLead three extension lists remain.

c65 run 6 follow-up (Main). (1) The BuildGraphRules fix landed as 9cd852f2bf. (3) JetCli/Tests passes when re-run under the full profile in the same home (all its rows pass), so the exit -1 in run 6 was not reproduced; a load or OOM-kill flake, watched in run 7. The re-run reused the run-6 home and state, and 14 Jetpack Engine, Environment, Publication and Services rows that passed in run 6 failed there, so that re-run is not clean evidence for them. (4) P15 is a real regression, not only load: self-compile total work went from 95.6 s (run 5, c902740d37) to 297.8 s on the quieter re-run, with the residual at 223.7 s against a budget of 800 units. Main is timing a cold traced jet build Compiler at b7ff715849 to find which interval grew.

c65 run 6 roots (Main repro in the same clean home at b7ff715849 and on a dev export at d17bb32500). (1) BuildGraphRules.jet:198 still asserts that .file(found) fails, which 4a44ce3b8e made legal; Main lands the one-line removal (fixed tree: JetBuildSession/Tests 17/17). cards.title: Effects on types: packages, targets and the compiler as effect-typed types (end-state proposal)
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-29, after a talk by Simon Peyton Jones on types that control which effects they may interact with and how: "if we can define the usable and not usable effects on a type, then we can make packages and the compiler types themselves, which then echoes effects on types." This is the mechanism behind pillar 5, "The Language Is A Library", but it is not itself a pillar (owner, 2026-10-29).

The owner wants the exact end state first: every semantic rule and every spelling, as it will look once built, so he can fix it before any work starts. Main writes the proposal in Docs/proposals and links it here. The owner then corrects it, and the corrected surface becomes ballots on this card.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match D-DECL-COLON1=A (`name: value`, no `::`).

Defect found 2026-11-04 (Prep, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/mv/m12b.jet): the ratified D-META-REFLECT2 ballot code '@FUNCTION(advance)?' is stale. A bare ? is E-ERR-PROPAGATE and @FUNCTION is E0102; the current reflection surface is T.reflect() and reflect.of(x). Any spec or example copying it must use the current surface.

Merged #6137 "Effects on types: library-defined effects built on kernel effects" into this card (effects on types); its 8 open item(s) are carried as "(was #6137)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1 A ratified by the owner 2026-10-30: #FX above a struct, enum or trait caps everything done in the type's name (methods, trait impls in any package, closures inside them, inherited default methods and Close impls). Method rows may only tighten it, and parameter work belongs to the caller, so there is no tail rule. C9 rewritten; C31 added.

Merged #6141 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Effects on types: spec page, diagnostics registry and teaching examples. Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (sections 12 and 14). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). Sema owns every check (I3); rows are erased in codegen and the same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Write the durable spec for effect rows on every rung (replacing the proposal once implemented), register every new code with what/why/fix text, and add one beginner-path and one expert-path example.

Merged #6140 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Effects on types: build action reuse decided by the action's row. Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (section 9.4; relates to D-BUILD-REUSESET1 and D-REAPI1). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). Sema owns every check (I3); rows are erased in codegen and the same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Make an action reusable exactly when its row is pure apart from declared `Build.Input`; never reuse actions with ambient effects. Remote execution ships only reusable actions.

Merged #6138 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Effects on types: build targets are typed declarations with rows and facts. Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (section 8 and ballot C4; relates to #6126 and #5006). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). Sema owns every check (I3); rows are erased in codegen and the same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Declare targets in Core as library code in the ratified form (ballot C4), each with a row and hardware facts. Check code reachable from each artifact's entry against that artifact's target row (new code, proposal E0763). Expose target facts as `$build.target.*`.

Merged #6136 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Effects on types: package rows and dependency grants checked against inferred rows. Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (section 7.1-7.3 and ballot C6). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). Sema owns every check (I3); rows are erased in codegen and the same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Treat the package `authority:` block as the package type's row. Compute each dependency's inferred row and check it against the depending package's `grants` (new code, proposal E0762) with the call path and the version that widened it. Implement the ratified `jet add` behavior (ballot C6). Retire the unenforced `policy: { effects: … }` in one cutover.

Merged #6135 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Effects on types: module rung (file-head and inline `#FX`). Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (section 6 and ballot C2; supersedes the module rung of D-EFFECT-RUNGS1). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). Sema owns every check (I3); rows are erased in codegen and the same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Accept `#FX(...)` at a file head and before an inline `module`; it bounds every item in the module, nested modules included. Module values stay named-only unless ballot C2 on this card says otherwise.

Merged #6134 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Effects on types: trait rows bind every impl and make trait-value calls precise. Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (section 5). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). Sema owns every check (I3); rows are erased in codegen and the same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Allow `#FX(...)` on trait declarations as a ceiling on every impl in every package; keep the per-method bound (D-EFF3) as the rung below. A call through a trait value uses the trait's row; without one, the union of the built program's impls.

Merged #6133 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Effects on types: rows of generic types and the type-parameter tail. Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (section 4.3 and ballot C1). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). Sema owns every check (I3); rows are erased in codegen and the same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Compute a generic type's row per instantiation, adding row(T) wherever T's methods are called. Implement the ratified spelling for naming a type parameter's effects in a ceiling (ballot C1 on this card).

Merged #6132 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Effects on types: `#FX(...)` rows on struct, enum and union. Body: Design: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (sections 3, 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 13). Owner direction 2026-10-29: implement effects on types in the near future; ballots for the proposal's choice points are attached to the cards they govern. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). Sema owns every check (I3); rows are erased in codegen and the same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Parse and register `#FX(...)` on struct/enum/union declarations (same list grammar as function rows). Infer each type's row as the fixed point of its methods (inherent and trait impls), function-typed fields, and field types. Check the inferred row against a written ceiling (E0712 widened) and denials (E0749 widened); report field-path overruns as a new code (proposal E0760). Calls through a value of the type add its row as today.

Owner 2026-10-29 08:31: ballot choice points C1-C7 and card all effects-on-types work for near-term delivery. Implementation cards #6132-#6141 filed under this card in e16; folding stays #6125. Ballots attach to: C1 #6133, C2 #6135, C3+C5 #6137, C4 #6138, C6 #6136, C7 #6139, core model #6129.
Main: end-state proposal written: Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md (queued to dev as 1793274134-Main). Seven owner choice points C1-C7 in section 15.

criteria.text: A proposal in Docs/proposals states the complete end state: the syntax and semantics for effects on types, packages as types, targets as effect types, and compiler parts as public types. It includes worked examples, every diagnostic, the inference rules, how existing mechanisms are absorbed or kept, and what is retired.
criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 2026-10-31 (wave 9b tree): Docs/proposals/effect-types-2026-10-29.md exists at a16a86d88f, linked to card #6129 on line 3. It covers everything the criterion asks for. Syntax and semantics: §3 Spellings, §4 Types (#FX rows on struct/enum/union, generic `..T`), §5 Traits, §6 Modules, §7 Packages are types, §8 Targets are types, §9 The compiler is types (extension points as function types with rows). Inference rules: §2 design rules ("inferred ⊆ ceiling", denials) and §4.2 "Using a type spreads its row". Worked examples: the #FX code blocks in §4-§8. Every diagnostic: §12 table, E0749/E0712/E0747 widened plus new E0760-E0765. Absorbed, kept or retired mechanisms: the §11 table, e.g. `policy: { effects: { deny } }` Retired, advanced compiler opt-in Replaced by `Compiler.*`.

criteria.text: The owner has reviewed the proposal and recorded his corrections; each new surface is on a ratified ballot on this card.
criteria.evidence: The owner ratified every effects-on-types ballot: D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1, D-EFFTYPE-USES1, D-EFFTYPE-KERNEL1, D-EFFTYPE-TARGET1, D-EFFTYPE-GRANT1 and D-EFFTYPE-MODVALUE1 are all ratified A.

criteria.text: (from #6132 Effects on types: `#FX(...)` rows on struct, enum and union) A type's inferred row covers its methods, function-typed fields and field types, including recursive types (fixed point); a sema test pins each source of effects.

(from #6132 Effects on types: `#FX(...)` rows on struct, enum and union) Ceiling and denial violations on a type report E0712 and E0749 at the offending method or field with the type's `#FX` as the secondary label; a field-path overrun reports its own registered code; each has a UI snapshot.
(from #6132 Effects on types: `#FX(...)` rows on struct, enum and union) A type with no `#FX` behaves exactly as before: a case pins an unmarked type's inferred row and calls on O0, O1 and O2.
(from #6133 Effects on types: rows of generic types and the type-paramet) A generic type's row is computed per instantiation; a test shows `Box<Pure>` is pure while `Box<Logger>` carries `Log`.

(from #6133 Effects on types: rows of generic types and the type-paramet) Per D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1 A there is no tail spelling: what a type or function parameter does belongs to the caller and is checked where the instantiation (Traced<Parser>) is written; an example with golden output on every tier shows Traced<Parser> doing Traced's work plus Parser's.
(from #6133 Effects on types: rows of generic types and the type-paramet) Violations through a type parameter name the instantiation in the diagnostic, with a UI snapshot.
(from #6134 Effects on types: trait rows bind every impl and make trait-) `#FX(...)` on a trait checks every impl, including impls in another package (new registered code, UI snapshot).

(from #6134 Effects on types: trait rows bind every impl and make trait-) A call through a trait value (`[Shape]`, `s: Shape`) gets the trait's row when written, else the union of the program's impls; sema tests pin both.

(from #6134 Effects on types: trait rows bind every impl and make trait-) Per-method trait bounds keep working unchanged; an example shows trait and method rungs together with golden output on every tier.

(from #6135 Effects on types: module rung (file-head and inline `#FX`)) A file-head `#FX(...)` and an inline `#FX(...) module m { }` bound every item inside, with E0749/E0712 reported at the offending item and the module marker as secondary label (UI snapshots).
(from #6135 Effects on types: module rung (file-head and inline `#FX`)) An example with golden output on every tier shows a deterministic offline module (`#FX(!Net, !FS, !Exec, !Time, !Rand)`).
(from #6135 Effects on types: module rung (file-head and inline `#FX`)) The ratified D-EFFTYPE-MODVALUE1 outcome (A) is implemented, with a case on O0, O1 and O2.

(from #6136 Effects on types: package rows and dependency grants checked) A dependency whose inferred row exceeds its grant fails the build with a registered code naming the dependency, the effect, and the call path (UI snapshot).

(from #6136 Effects on types: package rows and dependency grants checked) `jet add` behaves per the ratified D-EFFTYPE-GRANT1 outcome (A), and a Jetpack test proves it, including an upgrade that widens a row.
(from #6136 Effects on types: package rows and dependency grants checked) `policy: { effects: … }` is removed from the manifest model, docs and examples, with no shim.
(from #6136 Effects on types: package rows and dependency grants checked) An example package with a dependency and a grant has golden output on every tier.

(from #6138 Effects on types: build targets are typed declarations with ) Core declares at least the native host, web and GPU targets in the ratified form, each with a row and facts (word size, pointer size, cache line, CPU features).

(from #6138 Effects on types: build targets are typed declarations with ) Code reached from an entry built for a target that denies an effect it uses reports a registered code naming the line and the target (UI snapshot).

(from #6138 Effects on types: build targets are typed declarations with ) One `fn build` builds the same source for two targets and each artifact is checked against its own row; an example with golden output proves it.
(from #6138 Effects on types: build targets are typed declarations with ) `$build.target.<fact>` reads work in `comptime if` and in code, with a test.
(from #6140 Effects on types: build action reuse decided by the action's) A pure action with declared inputs is reused on an unchanged rebuild and rerun when an input changes; a test proves both.
(from #6140 Effects on types: build action reuse decided by the action's) An action with an ambient effect is never reused; a test proves it.
(from #6140 Effects on types: build action reuse decided by the action's) The reuse rule is the only reuse switch: no separate verify or trust flag remains for it.

(from #6141 Effects on types: spec page, diagnostics registry and teachi) Docs/spec states the rung rule, spellings and inference once, linking to the registry and examples instead of listing behavior.
(from #6141 Effects on types: spec page, diagnostics registry and teachi) Every code from the effects-on-types cards is registered with what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot.

(from #6141 Effects on types: spec page, diagnostics registry and teachi) A beginner example (no rows written, a dependency upgrade error) and an expert example (module, type, trait and target rows) have golden output on every tier.

D-EFFTYPE-MODEL1 A: #FX above a type also bounds closures written inside its methods, inherited default methods and its Close impl, and a method row may only tighten it; concrete calls, trait-value fields and fixed-row function fields count against the cap (no laundering); a cases row per path proves each on o0/o1/o2, and the check is erased before IR.

(was #6137) A library effect with its relied-on kernel effects parses, checks, is qualified outside its package, and is blocked by a denial of any kernel effect it relies on; sema tests pin each rule.
(was #6137) A body that uses a kernel effect not listed for its library effect reports a registered code with a UI snapshot.
(was #6137) The kernel effect list matches the ratified D-EFFTYPE-KERNEL1 outcome (A); the moved effects are Core declarations, with a case on O0, O1 and O2.
(was #6137) An example (a small `sql`-style library effect) has golden output on every tier.
(was #6137) (was #6139) core.compiler exposes the extension-point function types with their rows; a marker or lint that exceeds its row reports a registered code (UI snapshot).
(was #6137) (was #6139) The advanced compiler API is gated only by `Compiler.*` effect grants; the old opt-in spelling is gone with no shim, and a test proves a grant enables and its absence refuses.

A module #FX limit also covers methods inside struct and enum bodies and trait default bodies in that module; a function row wider than its module limit is an error; and a file-head #FX above use lines applies to the file instead of being dropped silently. Each has a UI or case proof.

cards.title: Ballot: are Core's generic bodies checked against the selected target?
cards.body:
Finding B10 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core's generic bodies are checked without the selected target's no_os fact; user bodies are checked with it (Sema/Scopes.jet:492-498).

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9).

cards.title: Ballot: does Core ship as a versioned package?
cards.body:
Finding B15 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). Core comes from the toolchain beside the package graph (JetDriverCompileRequest.core_sources, Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/Identity.jet:180-218), is keyed by `<corelib>/` (Sema/Diagnostics.jet:20-22, Loader.jet:2659), and has a private core.<area>.runtime namespace (E1001, Loader.jet:3616-3625) that packages cannot mirror.

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9).
cards.plan: Implement the ballot's answer. Under A, Core resolves through the package graph with a version, and the `<corelib>/` predicates are deleted once F01-F12 land.

criteria.text: The ballot is answered; under A, `jet` resolves Core as a package with a version shown by `jet inspect`.
The core.<area>.runtime privacy uses a rule any package can use (UI snapshot for the refused import).

cards.title: Core declares its own host leaves; delete the compiler's twin of Core's API
cards.body:
Finding F01 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). The compiler keeps a twin of Core's API. Core members are typed and dispatched by compiler tables (Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet:1-4, CoreCallExtensions.jet; generated Registry/CoreCallRows.jet:10 with 1,998 rows; hand-written Registry/CoreSignatures.jet:88, CorePlatformSignatures.jet:229, CoreHostSignatures.jet:22, CoreValueSignatures.jet). A native row wins over the Core declaration (Sema/Calls/Core.jet:264-270). A package can reach the host only through C FFI.

Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9).
cards.plan: Add one public declaration for a host-provided function, usable by any package, whose signature, effects, failure and sink facts are read from the declaration. Move every Core member that has a CORE_CALLS row to that declaration in Core source. Delete Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet's member rows, CoreCallExtensions.jet, the generated CoreCallRows table and the hand-written signature tables in one cutover. The spelling of the declaration is ballot A on this card.

OWNER 2026-10-30 asked what Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet is ('looks nothing like jet ... some weird kind of table or config file'). Facts at dev 216cac590b: 2546 lines in a custom line format, not Jet: 1938 dispatcher_row lines (1791 of them embed literal Rust constructor text, CoreCallRecord::new(...)), 343 ambient_route, 115 module export lists, 113 source_module owner lists, 7 format_row and 4 bootstrap lines. The module, export and owns rows restate what Core/*.jet already declares. It is read by about 10 compiler registry files, Compiler/Bootstrap/generate-core-sources.mjs and Tools/agent checks, and its header still names deleted Rust tables. C2 deletes its member rows; under D-DECL-TYPES1 A (ratified) the remaining runtime-symbol and ambient facts become markers on the Core functions themselves, so the file goes entirely.

Merged #6163 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Build core.build and the fn build host on the public compiler library. Body: Finding F16 of the #6128 census (Docs/audits/2026-10-29-language-is-a-library-census.md; line numbers at dev 25f9dee58f). core.build is implemented inside the compiler: Compiler/JetBuildSession/Source/Session.jet:1-4 (private compiler service linkage), Keys.jet:1-5 (Rust v2 key contract), Declarations.jet:1-2 (Rust runtime_bridge positional contract); Compiler/JetEval/Source/BuildServices.jet:1-3; Build and BuildPlan methods are dispatched by member-name strings in Compiler/JetDriver/Source/Driver/BuildAdapter.jet:36-81. Pillar 5 (Docs/spec/philosophy.md): Core is ordinary Jet that uses only mechanisms any package can use, and every tool calls the compiler library instead of keeping its own copy of a language rule. Every new or widened diagnostic ships with a registered code, what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot (I4). The same program means the same thing at O0, O1 and O2 (I9). Plan: Make core.build ordinary Core source over the public compiler library's typed extension points (#6139). The fn build host calls those functions; delete the string dispatch in BuildAdapter.jet and the private session linkage.

Plan: Give packages the same private `__` name rule #5978 settles for Core, or remove Core's exception; then lex and parse Core with the ordinary job. Fold this into #5978's plan if Main prefers.

cards.title: Odin-level array programming: element-wise array operators, swizzles on any small array, matrices
cards.body:
Owner 2026-10-29 (direct): Odin's built-in array support (array arithmetic with + - * / that just works, swizzling, strong support for 3D and graphics) must ALL be added to or verified in Jet. This amends D-VECARITH1 (element-wise operators closed to compiler-provided lane and linalg types) and widens D-SWIZZLE1.

Today: swizzles work only on five hard-coded Core type names (F32x4, F64x2, Vec2, Vec3, Vec4; Sema/Expressions/Places.jet:679), with x/y/z/w only and no rgba. Element-wise arithmetic is limited to compiler-provided lane and linalg types. Fixed arrays `[T#N]` (S76/D-FIXARR1) get no element-wise operators or swizzles.

Odin reference set to audit row by row: fixed arrays of numbers with element-wise + - * / % and bit ops between arrays and with a scalar (broadcast), and unary minus; == and !=; swizzles .xyzw and .rgba for N<=4 (read, write and repeat-read); swizzle on the result of an expression; built-in matrix types with * as matrix product, matrix-vector product, transpose and the like; quaternions; #simd vectors; #soa struct-of-arrays layouts; array-to-slice conversion; `len` as a compile-time constant; and compile-time evaluation of all of the above.
cards.plan:
1. Audit: write a table of every Odin array, matrix, quaternion, simd and soa feature (cite the Odin docs/spec) against Jet today, with each row PASS, PARTIAL or MISSING and a probe program. Send the table to Main before implementing; any new spelling needs an owner ballot (I7).
2. Implement every MISSING and PARTIAL row whose spelling is already ratified or needs no new syntax: element-wise operators on [T#N] numeric fixed arrays (array op array, array op scalar), swizzles on [T#N] with N<=4 plus rgba on every swizzleable type, driven by a type fact instead of hard-coded Core names.
3. One runtime meaning on all tiers (I9), with lowering to SIMD where the backend has it.
4. Examples/features/lowlevel goldens; UI snapshots for length mismatch, a non-numeric element and an invalid lane.
5. Pair each new performance-relevant surface with a two-program perf cell against the plain loop (AGENTS.md performance gate).

log.text: Array ballots on Tower: D-ARRAY-CORENAMES1, MATRIX1, KEYED1, LAYOUT1. Drafted by KitSpeed-2; adversarial reader Ballots-4. Ratified conflicts fixed (card #1437 matrix family INDEX1=E, MUL1=F, LIT1=E, BCAST1=E, SOLVE1=B, HOME1=D; D-LANES1=A; D-SPACE-GEOMETRY1=A; ..= is E0318). Readings for the owner to confirm: MATRIX1 treats Matrix*Vec as the transform product, with BCAST1 limited to repeating operators; LAYOUT1 says push through a window is refused where visible and stops otherwise. Main replaced alias declarations in MATRIX1 with the #6176 form.
Correction to the audit counts (KitSpeed-2): 87 rows, of which 25 PASS, 6 PARTIAL, 55 MISSING and 1 bug.

Audit (KitSpeed-2, 2026-10-29, 78 probes at O0 and full on 25f9dee): 19 PASS, 7 PARTIAL, 49 MISSING, 1 bug. SIMD S1-S11 is ratified but unbuilt (E2104 cites #5984). Swizzle write is broken (lowlevel/swizzle.jet FAILs on all tiers). Rows needing no new syntax are in implementation; B0-B10 go to owner ballots.

criteria.text: A dated audit in Docs/audits lists every Odin array/matrix/quaternion/simd/soa feature with Jet status and probe; every row is PASS or has a linked card or owner ballot.

Numeric fixed arrays [T#N] support element-wise + - * / % and bit operators with another [T#N] and with a scalar, unary minus and ==, as goldens on O0/O1/O2; length or element mismatches are registered diagnostics with UI snapshots.

Swizzles .xyzw and .rgba (read, write, repeated read) work on every [T#N] with N<=4 and every vector/lane type, decided by a type fact rather than hard-coded Core names; invalid lanes are E3110/E3111 with snapshots.
Matrix and quaternion operations the audit marks as Odin built-ins have a Jet equivalent proven by goldens, or a linked card or ballot.
The golden, UI and cases compares lose 0 rows; lane-check CHECK OK.

Integer lane types (`I8`..`I64`, `U8`..`U64` lanes) support element-wise `<<`, `>>` (arithmetic for signed, logical for unsigned), `.bit_and`, `.bit_or`, `.bit_xor` and `.bit_not`, with a lane or a scalar right side. Output matches the scalar fold at O0/O2, and a UI snapshot covers a float-lane shift error. Found by the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation (ratified, not built; compiler 0ccdff27ea).

Paired performance cell for a checked lane gather (draft ballot D-LANES-GATHER1, held until this passes): in the canonical performance manifest, two programs do the same Doom-style two-stage byte lookup (texture byte, then light-table byte) over the same tables and positions with the same output and the same bounds-checked safety, one with a checked Lanes<U8, N> gather and one with plain checked scalar reads. The cell records target, compiler commit, optimization level, cycles and bytes, and proves equal output. The gather ballot is posted for ratification only after the gather form strictly beats the scalar form; a loss stays logged on this card.

cards.title: Portable wasm seed: bootstrap Jet from the repo alone with a C compiler (jet compiler as wasm + tiny C wasm interpreter)
cards.body: Split from #4154 step 3 (owner-approved plan, 2026-10-01; split approved by Main, 2026-10-29). #4154 closes on steps 1–2 (the tagged chain and per-release seed binaries). This card owns the third leg: a portable seed checked into the repo and refreshed occasionally, like Zig's zig1.wasm. It is the Jet compiler built to WebAssembly plus a tiny C wasm interpreter, so any machine with a C compiler can bootstrap from the repo alone, with no downloads and no older Jet binary. Today the self-hosted backend emits only x86-64 (Compiler/JetBackend/Source/X64). The wasm32 target triples exist only as target-machine facts (TargetMachine.jet wasm.browser / wasm.wasi), with no wasm code emitter. So the first prerequisite is a JetIR → wasm32 core-module emitter. The wasm decoder and validator from the plugin engine (#5487, Docs/proposals/plugin-wasm-engine-2026-10-29.md) are reusable for checking the emitted seed. Related: #5455 (bootstrappability from a small seed as the trusting-trust answer).
cards.plan: 1. A JetIR → wasm32 core-module emitter (wasm 1.0 + bulk memory + multi-value), with a minimal WASI-like host import set (args, environ, fd read/write/seek, path open/stat/readdir, clock, exit) that is exactly what jet build needs. 2. Build the compiler (Compiler/ workspace, JetCli) to jet.wasm and check it with the #5487 validator. 3. A small C99 wasm interpreter (one file, no dependencies) that implements that import set over POSIX. 4. A bootstrap script: cc the interpreter, run jet.wasm to build native s1 from the repo, then s2 = s3 fixed point against the released seed. 5. Check the seed in (compressed, with recorded sha256) and document the refresh: who regenerates it, and when.

Lower JetIR functions, calls, linear memory, globals, data segments and the function table (indirect calls) to wasm 1.0 + bulk memory + multi-value. Define the stack and heap layout and the C-ABI-like call convention. Add `jet build --target=wasm32-wasi`. Grow coverage from the golden examples up to the Compiler workspace.

cards.title: Value passing is physically optimal: named-tuple returns in registers, last-use moves are true moves, and large read-only values pass by address
cards.body: Owner direction (2026-10-29): multiple returns (Jet named tuples) and value passing must be maximally performant, optimal and efficient. Last-use moves are ratified (D-COPY-DEFAULT1=A, D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A; spec.md ~1103-1150). Calls carry no marks; a take is declared && in the signature (D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A) and an early move is written x.move(), including for fields, values with cleanup, type parameters and lambda captures. Nobody has verified that the generated code actually achieves this. The nbody profile (#3039 C6) already showed hidden heap boxes and copy/drop helpers on hot paths.
cards.plan: Write a small benchmark and inspect corpus (jet inspect code, D-CODE-INSPECT1) at O1/O2: (1) functions returning small named tuples (2-4 scalar fields): the result must come back in registers, with no heap and no stack round-trip beyond the ABI; (2) last-use moves of List/String/struct locals into take parameters and receivers: no copy, no extra retain/release; (3) large read-only struct parameters: passed by address, with no copy; (4) the `^`-required exception cases: confirm each is required for meaning, not for a codegen limitation. Fix every gap in the backend and IR. Add each case as a paired perf cell against the C/Rust equivalent per the performance gate.

log.text: Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A supersedes D-CALLSITE-MARK1=A's ^ exceptions.

The old 'Rust <= 1.05' band is retired.

C4 measured on f75020e91d (IrTypes-2, one build slot, 7 runs pinned to CPU 31, clang-21 -O2 / rustc 1.97 -O3, loaded machine): LOSES. Jet/Rust and Jet/C at O2: multi-return 2.86 / 3.12, recursion-aggregate 2.82 / 2.85, fixed-return-64 1.50 / 2.79, destructure-move 0.82 / 3.02. At O1: 3.15/3.44, 5.16/5.24, 2.40/4.45, 0.66/2.45. Table: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/IR/IrTypes/perf/m1.txt, runner perf/fb.sh. multi-return's O2 IR is fully scalar-replaced, so the gap is arithmetic: floordiv/mod use idiv plus a floor fixup, % 13 gets no magic multiply, every division has a trap check, and every loop iteration has a stop_poll. cards.title: Research: modularity, scalability and extensibility of every layer of Jet, then one extension-architecture design
cards.body: Owner direction (2026-10-29): every level, semantic, syntax, feature and scope of Jet must be analysed through the lens of modularity, scalability and extensibility, so that every domain can grow indefinitely the way D-CORE-BOUNDARY1 makes hardware a library change and D-INFRA1 makes infrastructure typed Jet code. Hardware and FFI are two drops in that ocean. A dedicated research agent (owner-approved) does this.
cards.plan: Write a dated research document in Docs/research that covers every layer: lexical/syntax, the type system, semantics (effects, memory, errors, concurrency, evaluation, comptime), the compiler pipeline, the runtime, tooling, build/packages, every standard-library domain, deployment/targets, and evolution over time. For each layer: what is closed today and where (file:line, measured), the possible extension mechanisms, prior art with citations, costs (performance, tooling, readability, safety, I8 one mechanism, I9 tiers), and what the evidence favours. Then draft one extension-architecture design meeting the ballot rework bar, and specify a 'no closed lists' gate.

cards.title: Native struct layout is physically optimized (reordered and packed) on every type, and C interop works with that optimized layout
cards.body: Owner direction (2026-10-29): always keep the compiler's memory-layout optimization, unlike Rust where #[repr(C)] turns field reordering off. C interop and FFI must be confirmed working with the optimizations on. Current state (Main probe on dev bb9c74e522): a default struct reports kind "default", guarantee "physical layout unspecified" and no size fact (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Comptime/Reflection.jet:682-723; `Mixed.$layout.size` is empty). The same 5-field struct {U8, Int, U8, Int, U8} under #Layout(c) is 40 bytes, while the optimal order is 24. Runtime record glue (e.g. JetRuntime/Source/DataPlotFlat.jet:68-92) stores each field in its own 8-byte word in a jet_rt_alloc block. That suggests default records are heap blocks with a word per field, the same cost the nbody profile showed for [T#N] (#3039 C6).
cards.plan: 1. Measure the real native representation of default structs (stack vs heap, word-per-field vs packed) at O0/O1/O2. 2. Make the default layout physical and optimal: fields ordered by alignment then size, small fields packed, niches used for optionals (D-MEM-UNBOX1), inline (not heap) for value structs, and a defined $layout size/offset fact. 3. C interop with optimization on: a Jet type exported to C emits its C declaration in the optimized field order, so C sees the same bytes with zero copies. A type imported from a C header keeps that header's layout because it is a C type. Today's 'wire mirror' copy at the boundary (syntax-decisions D-PLACE1 text) is removed wherever the layouts already coincide. 4. #Layout(c) remains only for matching an externally fixed layout; if its public meaning changes, that part goes to the owner through the ballot bar. 5. Prove it with a C round-trip test: C reads and writes Jet-exported optimized structs, on every tier.

log.text: OWNER RULING 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'keep field order unchanged' for hand-written #Layout(c) structs that mirror an outside layout. Final rule: every struct defined in Jet source is layout-optimized, including ones exported to C (C gets a generated declaration in Jet's order). #Layout(c) marks a layout owned elsewhere and keeps its written field order, as do C types imported by use from a header or C source.

OWNER DIRECTION 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'if we define the layout in our source, then we should optimize it. If we are pulling it from elsewhere we shouldnt change it.' Applied: every struct defined in Jet source is layout-optimized, including ones exported to C (C gets a generated declaration in Jet's order). Types pulled from elsewhere, such as C structs imported from a header or C source by use (D-FFI-CINPUT1 A), keep the foreign layout unchanged. Open edge sent to the owner: hand-written #Layout(c) structs that mirror an outside layout (Jetpack HeaderParser structs, embedded MMIO register blocks) count as 'defined in our source' by the literal reading, which would reorder them.

Landed bc8aba3913: C1 C2 C3 C5 met. C4 (perf cell vs C/Rust for the packed layout) stays open; the struct-packed cell is ready in IrTypes-2's tree, measurement paused by the owner's overnight priorities.

Main reading of the owner direction (reported for confirmation): every Jet-owned struct gets the optimized layout, including structs exported to C, which get a generated C declaration in offset order (C3). #Layout(c) keeps C declaration order, because it marks layouts the foreign side owns (Jetpack HeaderParser structs and the embedded MMIO register blocks); reordering those would break them. No new marker is added. If the owner wants #Layout(c) reordered as well, the foreign-owned layouts would need a different spelling, which is a ballot.

Correction from IrTypes-2's measurement (e6, jet emit --ir at none/full plus O2 objdump): default user structs are NOT heap. They are one IR Aggregate in a stack slot on every tier, laid out in declaration order with natural C alignment (Mixed {Bool, Float, U8, I32, Float} = 32 B; reordered and packed = 24 B). The word-per-field heap glue is the runtime's 163 hand-written jet_rt_record_new_*/jet_rt_handle_* shims for specific Core types (boxed records at the Core/runtime boundary), not user structs. Read-only by-value params already pass by address. Returns copy from a frame temp into the caller's sret (#6201 C6). The remaining scope of this card is reordering/packing, the  size fact, C export in the optimized order, and whether those boxed runtime records should become plain aggregates.

cards.title: Effect vocabulary has three disagreeing copies (Prelude Effects.jet, Core Compiler/Lang.jet, Registry CoreCalls.jet) plus a leaf copy missing Mem.Alloc/Mem.Rc

cards.title: Lambda is an unnamed function: `fn(n: Int) -> Int { n * n }` (ballot D-LAMBDA-FN1)
cards.body: Owner idea (2026-10-29): a lambda is a function without its name, just as `A | B` is an unnamed enum (D-UNIONTYPE1). Today `->` starts the result type in `fn f(x: Int) -> Int {}` and in the type `fn(Int) -> Int`, but starts the body in a lambda `(n: Int) -> n * n`. So `(n: Int) -> Int { n * n }` silently parses `Int{n * n}` as a typed value, and adding a line makes it E0399. Census at d345e35902: 4,768 lambdas in 1,194 files, 59.1% relying on E0801 inference. Ballot D-LAMBDA-FN1 decides the form.
cards.plan: After ratification: parser (fn + `(` in value position parses an unnamed function, reusing the callable signature parser), sema (written result/error types checked against the expected type; the declaration rules apply when there is no expected type), a `jet fix` migration of all lambdas, and updates to the spec, the syntax registry, editor grammars, examples and diagnostics in one cutover.

cards.title: Debug info for optimized builds: DW_TAG_inlined_subroutine entries and location lists for locals at -O1/-O2
cards.body: Found by RustOut7-2 while probing lldb on a native jet build at 236cd9310c for #6221 P1. At the default optimization level, inlined functions (e.g. `area`) leave no inlined_subroutine entries, and most locals have no location, so `--release` binaries can't be debugged meaningfully. #6221 P1 covers aggregate type DWARF and makes `jet debug` build with optimize=none/inline=off. This card covers the optimized tiers, which C compilers support (gcc/clang -O2 -g).
cards.plan: Emit DW_TAG_inlined_subroutine with call-site file/line for every inlined call, and location lists for locals across register allocation. Verify with lldb on a -O2 probe: break in an inlined function, show frames, print locals.

cards.body: Found by BallotDesign (probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext). Compiler/Prelude/core/prelude.jet:21-22 declares `fn check(text: String) Error! -[]>` and `fn encode_hole<T: Printable>(value: T) String -[]>`. In user code `String -[]>` is E0003 (only `-[]> String` is accepted), and user traits cannot declare bodiless methods at all (E0081 '`fn name` has no body'). Pillar 5: Core may use no form a package can't write.
cards.plan: Make the Prelude use the user grammar (`-[]> String`). Decide whether user traits may declare required (bodiless) methods; if the ratified trait design allows required methods, lift E0081 for trait declarations. Otherwise the Prelude must use the same form users use. Cutover in one patch.
