Merged #6183 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: A local trait implemented through `impl labels.Tag.Mine` passes coherence, but calling its method gives E0102. Body: Found by IrTypes-2 while working on g10 (#6170/#6171/#6172, 2026-10-29) on jet-u13 / dev 36825b7a15; the repro is in the IrTypes-g10 msg. Not fixed by g10. A local trait implemented with a module-qualified head (`impl labels.Tag.Mine`) is accepted by coherence, but a call to its method is refused with E0102, so the impl can never be used. Plan: Reproduce from the g10 msg. Make method resolution find impls registered under a qualified head, using the same key that coherence uses. Add a case test.

Merged #6181 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: `Mat3<Int>(...)` silently ignores its type argument; a missing static method on Mat3 reports E0107 "Nothing named Mat3". Body: Found by KitSpeed-2's #6177 Odin array audit (2026-10-29; probes in kitspeed/w6177/probes, run at O0 and full on 25f9dee, with both tiers agreeing). (1) Writing a type argument on a non-generic Core math type, `Mat3<Int>(...)`, is accepted and the argument is silently discarded, so the program builds a Float matrix. It should be a registered diagnostic. (2) Calling a static method that doesn't exist on Mat3 reports E0107 "Nothing named `Mat3`" instead of E0311 naming the missing method. Plan: Reproduce with the audit probes. In sema, reject type arguments on non-generic types (registered code, UI snapshot), and route missing static methods on an existing type to E0311.

Merged #6285 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: `[T]{}` means the empty list in an expression but is E0003 as a field default (`values: [DBValue]{}`). Body: Found by BallotDesign (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext/holes_b_default.jet). A field default `values: [DBValue]{}` is E0003 'Expected a value'; only `[DBValue]{[]}` parses. In expressions, `[DBValue]{}` is the empty list. The same text should mean the same thing in both places. Plan: Accept `[T]{}` as the empty-list default in field position (one grammar rule shared with expressions). Migrate any `{[]}` defaults if the ratified spelling is `{}`.

Merged #6284 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: A static trait method cannot return `Self`: `-> Self` gives E0108, and `-> Cypher` gives E0913. Body: Found by BallotDesign (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext/self_static.jet). In an impl of a trait whose static method returns Self, writing `-> Self` and returning `Cypher{...}` reports E0108 'This needs Self, but the value is Cypher'; writing `-> Cypher` reports E0913 (signature mismatch). Self must be the implementing type inside an impl. Plan: In sema, resolve Self to the impl's target type in static trait methods (signature and body), consistently with instance methods. Add a golden and a ui snapshot for a true mismatch.

Merged #6283 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Two spellings of unit success: `Ok(())` and `Ok()` in the corpus. Body: Found by BallotDesign: Examples/ has 13 lines of `Ok(())` and 12 of `Ok()` (for example web/state_surface.jet:42). Reaching the end of an `E!` body already succeeds. One meaning needs one spelling (I8). Plan: Pick the canonical form from the ratified decisions (or ballot it if none decides), migrate every caller in one cutover, and make the other spelling a diagnostic with a jet fix.

Merged #6282 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Impl methods do not inherit the trait method's declared effect row (E0907 asks to restate `-[]>`). Body: Found by BallotDesign (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/bd/probe/ext/unit_norow.jet). An impl of CheckedText.check without `-[]>` gets E0907 'must be pure. Declare this CheckedText method pure', even when the body is pure. The trait's declared row is not used as the impl's row. Under D-EFFECT-OMIT1 rows are inferred, and an impl should take its row from the trait (a pure body checks; an impure one reports E0907 at the effect). Plan: In sema, an impl method with no written row takes the trait method's declared row as its ceiling and checks the body against it. Update the E0907 snapshot to point at the offending effect.

Merged #6257 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: Is Float Comparable? The generic bound `T: Comparable` admits Float, but `#Comparable` on a Float field is E0905 and Solver.jet:258 says Float isn't Comparable. Body: Found by Ballots-4 for #6174 (probes $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/b4/p74/gen2.jet, gen3.jet). TypeRelations.jet:1168 treats Float as a member of the scalar family at generic bounds, so min/max over Float work and NaN propagates. Deriving #Comparable on a struct with a Float field is refused (E0905), and the solver has a Float-specific 'isn't Comparable' fix text. One meaning (I8) needs one answer: either Float is Comparable everywhere, with NaN-propagating comparisons (the generic-bound behaviour min/max now relies on), or nowhere (and min/max over Float need a separate ordering such as total_cmp). Plan: Pick the meaning that matches the ratified Comparable contract (Docs/spec, D-CORE-LAWS1 laws for Comparable). Make the bound, derive and solver diagnostics agree, and add UI tests for each path. If the contract is silent and a choice is needed, it is an owner ballot.

Merged #6252 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: `return` inside a braced lambda passed to generic `map` is checked against the enclosing function (E0113) instead of the lambda. Body: Found by Ballots-4 while probing for D-LAMBDA-FN1: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/b4/lamp/p12.jet. A `return` inside a braced lambda body passed to a generic `map` is type-checked against the enclosing fn's result type and reports E0113. The retired Rust test sort_comparator_early_return_is_local_to_lambda expected `return` to be local to the lambda, and spec S47 says return leaves the lambda. Plan: Make lambda bodies a return scope in sema for every call shape, including generic callees whose result is solved from the body. Port the Rust test as a case/golden.

Merged #6199 into this card (one card per stream). Its title: A comma between enum cases gives a misleading E0003 ("Expected a name for a variant name", fix "e.g. `main`"). Body: Found by Main (2026-10-29, dev bb9c74e522). `enum Color { Red, Green, Blue }` reports E0003 "Expected a name for a variant name, found `,`". The Why is "Names start with a letter or `_`" and the Fix is "e.g. `main`, `count`, `_tmp`". The real cause is that enum cases are separated by whitespace or newlines, not commas, and every user coming from Rust, Swift, TS or C writes the comma. The diagnostic must name the actual rule and offer a machine fix that drops the commas. If the owner changes the separator rule (enum comma question, 2026-10-29), this card follows that outcome instead. Plan: In the enum case parser, detect a `,` where a case name is expected after a case and report a dedicated registered diagnostic (what/why/fix: enum cases are separated by spaces or newlines; remove the comma) with a structured fix. Add a UI snapshot. Re-check after the owner's separator ruling.

cards.title: Ratified GC opt-in is unbuilt: `#Policy(gc)` still reports E0221, and `!Mem.Gc` is E0750
cards.body: Probes q/bd/probe/gc (BallotDesign, dev 94df799429, all non-empty): cycle.jet gives E0221 "This write can close a strong `Shared` cycle through `Person`" twice (correct without opt-in). cyclegc.jet (file-level `#Policy(gc)`) and optb.jet (`#Policy(gc) { }` block, ratified D-OPTGC1) give the same two E0221s, so the opt-in lifts nothing. nogc.jet: `!Mem.Gc` (ratified D-DENY-COST1=A / D-MEMREF-LIFE1=A) is E0750 "`Mem.Gc` isn't a declared effect". Which items the opt-in covers is on ballot D-GC-OPTIN1 (types vs code); under every option the opted program must stop reporting E0221 and collect its cycles.
cards.plan: After D-GC-OPTIN1 is ratified: register `Mem.Gc` in the effect tree; make the opted scope lift E0221 per the outcome and route opted cycle-capable values to the collector (D-GC-WHEN1 timing); keep E0221 for non-opted code.

cards.title: Rebuild Tower in Jet: the board's CLI, store, server and web UI become a Jet web application (stress test for Jet as a web domain language)
cards.body: Owner order 2026-10-30: 'Rebuilding tower in jet rather than TS/JS will be the goal as a stress test for jet as a web domain language.' Tower today is a Node application under Tools/tower (63 .mjs/.js files: CLI tower.mjs, app/store.mjs, app/server.mjs, the web UI and tests). The rebuild uses Jet's web stack end to end (Core web, HTTP server, routing, live UI, storage), so every gap it finds is a Jet defect or missing capability, recorded as a criterion here or a gap card. The board data in Tools/tower/.tower/ keeps its format unless the owner rules otherwise, so the cutover needs no data migration. The owner runs tower serve; agents use the CLI.

log.text: #6563 c1 precut audit re-added 46 criteria from archived #519, #667, #773, #1195, #1203, #1375, #2331, #2332, #2338, #2924, #2929, #3513: each was not proven on 9c7ddf1359. Row verdicts and reasons: Docs/audits/precut-2026-11/PRECUT-AUDIT.tsv (ff5dd7fd7b).

Merged #5962 "Tower hygiene report: cards without epoch or criteria, stale cards, blocked by done cards, near-duplicates" into this card (Tower in Jet); its 3 open item(s) are carried as "(was #5962)" criteria. Owner ruling 2026-10-30: merge duplicate and superseded cards into one survivor.

criteria.text: A gap census: every capability Tower uses (HTTP server and routing, file-backed JSON store with atomic writes and locking, CLI argument parsing, live web UI, markdown rendering, the test suite) is mapped to a Jet Core API that exists or to a named gap, committed under Docs/research with file:line evidence.

The Tower CLI is a Jet program with the same commands, flags, output and exit codes; Tools/tower's own test suite, ported to jet test, passes against it, and the board files it writes are byte-identical to the Node version's on the same operations.
tower serve is a Jet web application serving the same board UI and live updates; a scripted browser test drives the main flows (cards, criteria, decisions, ballots, questions) on the Jet server.
Cutover: Tools/tower holds no .mjs/.js/.ts outside generated browser output (per the #5201 rule); AGENTS.md, skills and docs name the Jet commands; nothing falls back to Node.
A Tower workload cell in the perf manifest compares the Jet server with the Node one (request latency and memory) under the performance gate.

cards.title: Cache control and visibility: give programs control over L1/L2/L3 use and show where code leaves cache for RAM or disk
cards.body:
Owner question 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'Cache hits are critical -> how can we give control over L1,2,3 cache, visualize when we are no longer in cache & go to RAM or HDD/SSD?'

Starting facts: D-CACHE-CONTROL1 A is ratified (mem.prefetch(place, .Read|.Write, level: .L1), mem.stream_store, the build fact for the cache-line size, each needing a paired gauntlet cell). #Layout(c, align(N)) and D-PLACE1 cover alignment; #Layout(columnar) covers SoA. Whether any of this is implemented is unproven; this card measures it.

log.text: Update: the full original cache-control1-wip.patch is recovered (31 files, 71,012 bytes, the same size as the original): $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/recovery/6312/cache-control1-wip.patch, with SOURCES.md. Recover integrates it under c5.

Recovered 2026-11-04 by Prep-2: the compiler half of cache-control1-wip was replayed from the MemDesign agent transcript (MemDesign.jsonl) with 0 mismatches; the Encoder file's blob hash matches the original. 24 hand-edited files plus the 3 tests: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/recovery/6312/cache-control1-hand-27files.patch. It applies to 67fd7fdc47 and conflicts in 7 files on dev; generated rows are to be regenerated. The Recover lane integrates it under c5, and its landing also corrects Tools/tower/held/6312/README.md, which still says the compiler half is gone.
The 3 surviving cache-control test files are now in the repo at Tools/tower/held/6312/ (landed e07c1b85ae). c5 integrates them; the Recover lane is rebuilding the missing compiler half now.

Lost-work status (owner 2026-11-04: recover it, or record it as incomplete so it is never reported done): cache-control1-wip.patch (31 files, 783 lines, base 67fd7fdc47; D-CACHE-CONTROL1 A) is gone. Its three test files survive in $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign/t1: Examples/features/memory/cache_line_padding.jet, Examples/features/memory/stream_store.jet and tests/conformance/corpus/core/mem/stream_store.jet. The compiler half (IR StreamStore, the x64 movnti plus sfence encoder, registry and Core rows, the Core/Mem wrapper, the $build.cpu.cache_line fact and #Layout align() parsing, E1105 text) is missing; the search of agent transcripts and git objects continues. It adds $build.cpu.cache_line (registry fact, align() parser, E1105 text) and mem.stream_store (IROp.StreamStore, x64 movnti plus sfence, Core rows, conformance fixture, two examples, core-library.md). cards.title: Type conversions: make explicit conversion clean (owner asks about Int{myFloat}-style constructor casts)
cards.body:
Owner question 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'Type conversions generally need casts, how can we make this clean? Should casting be done by wrapping the value to cast in a type literal constructor? like Int{myFloatVar}?'

Starting facts: D-SHAPE-CONVERT1 A (ratified 2026-07-14, #566) makes conversion destination-owned: Target.from_source(value) (U8.from_int(n) ?? return, UserId.from_int(raw)); checked narrowing is fallible; safe widening is implicit; casts, to_* and convert() are refused. D-JAI-SMALL1 A adds #As member conversion. Type{...} braces already mean typed literals and field defaults (String{""}, ANSI{"..."}), so Int{x} would overlap them.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match the owner order that a retired spelling gets no teaching diagnostic, UI snapshot or jet fix rule.

Owner 2026-10-30 on float to int: 'for integer, let's do the swift/rust style. we have advanced APIs with variadics and optionals and defaults and named vs positional etc. but dont think we really use them, but this may be a good place for that.' Direction for the ballot: separate exact conversion (fails unless the value is whole and in range, like Swift Int(exactly:) and Rust TryFrom) from the deliberate lossy forms (truncate, round, saturate), and use Jet's named, defaulted and optional parameters for the lossy choices.

OWNER 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'what about casts as a kind of generic trait that can be implemented? then using the Int{myFloatVar} would detect that you are trying to construct an int literal and detect the type of the internal type, then use the implemented conversion trait implicitly? Thoughts'. Main's findings: Type{x} conversion already exists for scalar heads under D-DOTCTOR3 and its 2026-09-28 amendment (#3739; syntax-decisions.md:1187-1229): Float{n}, U8{i}, F32{v}, Int{I64{v}} work, and Int{myFloat} is deliberately E0112. Those rules are compiler-builtin while from_* (about 2821 call sites) is a second mechanism. The #6313 ballot leads with the owner's trait design.

criteria.text: A dated Docs/research note answers the owner's question: the current rule and how it reads in real code (counted call sites in Core, Examples and Compiler), the pain points with evidence, how Int{x} would interact with typed literals, field defaults and checked text, which conversions are lossy (float to int rounding, narrowing, sign) and how each must be spelled, and prior art (Rust as/From/TryFrom, Swift Int(x), Zig @intCast, Odin cast, Go T(x)).
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-type-conversions.md (SurfaceDesign-docs.patch): current rule with file:line (BuiltinStatics.jet:175/212, Checked.jet:389), probes m6313/m6313b/m6313c/m6313p o0=o1=o2; lossy cases (float->int truncation, Float.from_int rounding, narrowing wrap, sign); typed-literal and checked-text interaction; census of from_float/from_int/_rounded/round sites in Core, Examples, Compiler; prior-art table (Rust as/From/TryFrom, Swift, Zig, Go, C, Java, C#, Python, Kotlin, JS)

criteria.text: A ballot-ready Tower decision presents same-program alternatives (keep Target.from_source; Int{x}; Int(x); others the research finds), each with exact spelling for widening, checked narrowing, rounding, saturating and wrapping, and the beginner and expert paths; it states which earlier decisions it amends.
criteria.evidence: D-CONVERT-TRAIT1 added to Tower on card #6313 (ballot-ready: Tower decision add validation passed, readycheck READY, plaincheck PLAIN OK, recommendation losses []).

criteria.text: After ratification the chosen spelling is the one canonical form: every caller, example, test and doc is migrated in one cutover, the old spelling is not Jet syntax and gets no diagnostic, UI snapshot or jet fix rule (owner order), and the examples pass on o0/o1/o2.

impl Celsius -> Float no longer gives the self-contradicting E0113 naming the internal errconv_Celsius_to_Float; after ratification the declaration follows the D-CONVERT-TRAIT1 outcome with a user-facing diagnostic and a UI snapshot.

cards.title: Custom allocators and struct-of-arrays: native, complete support and its interactions
cards.body:
Owner questions 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'How can jet support custom allocators? What does this feature intefere with? Does this overlap with anything? Can we just support it natively? what about soa data types? We should support those.'

Starting facts: D-REGION1/D-ALLOC1/D-ALLOC2 (mem.Arena, scope-bound views, E0631/E0632), D-FIXED-BACKING1 (mem.Fixed), D-ALLOCFAIL1 (try_alloc family, AllocError), D-ALLOC-DEFAULT1 A (Jet-written size-class mem.Heap), D-TARGET-ALLOC1, D-SOA1/D-SOA2A-D (#Layout(columnar), whole-struct only, E1107-E1109), D-SOA-SITE1 A and D-SOA-TIER1 A. Core/Mem/Mem.jet declares empty struct Arena {}, Bump {} and Pool<T> {}. #6109 (Arena/Bump .alloc) closed; #6310 is an allocator-view ICE; #5042/#5043 are allocator speed cards.

log.text: D-SOA-SITE1 A retired the #Layout(columnar) marker in favour of Columns<T>; the criterion named the retired spelling.

criteria.text: A dated Docs/research note answers each owner question with evidence: what is ratified versus implemented (each allocator and columnar surface probed on o0/o1/o2, file:line), whether a user can write their own allocator today and through which trait, what custom allocators interfere or overlap with (ownership and drop, collections, Close resources, threads and tasks, FFI, the GC opt-in, comptime, the runtime heap), and prior art (Zig allocators, Odin context allocator, Rust Allocator API, C++ pmr, Jai SoA, Odin #soa).
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-custom-allocators-and-soa.md (MemDesign.patch): allocator and columnar surfaces probed o0/o1/o2 (a1-a14, s1-s12, api/ 22 ops) with file:line; user allocator today (no trait); interference: regions, Mem effect, try_, drops, tasks, FFI, Close, GC opt-in (D-OPTGC1), comptime, runtime heap; prior art Zig, Odin context and #soa, Rust Allocator, C++ pmr, Jai SOA, Zig MultiArrayList.

criteria.text: Ballot-ready Tower decisions for every owner choice found, for example a public Allocator trait users implement, how collections take an allocator, and any SoA surface beyond #Layout(columnar) (per-field columns, SoA slices, partial SoA), each drafted to the ballot bar with same-program alternatives.
criteria.evidence: Ballots $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign/ballot/D-ALLOC-TRAIT1.json and $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign/ballot/D-ALLOC-SITE1.json; plaincheck-file.mjs -> PLAIN OK for both; SoA beyond whole structs has no ballot by evidence (Columns<T> absent: s3 E0003, s8 E0302), stated in the note section 3.

criteria.text: Every ratified allocator and SoA surface is implemented natively in Core and the compiler: a user-written allocator backs List, Map and String, and Columns<T> (D-SOA-SITE1 A, which retires #Layout(columnar)) supports the full logical-list API; each has examples with golden output on o0/o1/o2.
Each allocator and SoA surface has a paired two-program perf cell against the plain spelling (default heap, array of structs) recorded in the canonical manifest, and strictly beats it before closing.

A dated Docs/research note compares Jet with Zig's MultiArrayList and SoA practice: layout, field-slice access, append and grow cost, iteration codegen (vectorization), and the ability to take a pointer or reference to one element's field inside a column and mutate through it; each probed on o0, o1 and o2 with timings.
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-soa-vs-zig.md (landed 1b8925fb9f): layout and growth (lines 15-18), field-slice access (20-), references to an element field probed o0/o1/o2 (ref1-ref8, E0204/E0220, lines 51-63), append/sweep/update timings at n=2M best of 5 (73-102), vector-code counts (108-111).

criteria.text: A paired perf cell set shows Jet SoA (Columns<T> or the ratified form) at parity or better against Zig MultiArrayList on the same workloads (field sweep, append, element-field update through a reference), recorded in the canonical manifest; any loss stays open on this card.
Any owner choice the Zig comparison raises (for example element references into columns and their safety rule) is a ballot-ready Tower decision with recommendation.losses = [].
criteria.evidence: No owner choice raised by the Zig comparison: every gap is implementation under ratified D-SOA-SITE1 and D-ARRAY-COLUMNS1; stated with evidence in Docs/research/2026-10-30-soa-vs-zig.md section "Owner choices".

cards.title: Terminal control API: broad, deep core.term so no external terminal library is needed
cards.body:
Owner order 2026-10-30 (verbatim): 'I want to ensure it is easy to use Terminal "commands" like "execute(term.clear_buffer, term.enable_raw_mode, term.enable_alternate_screen, term.hide_cursor)" with an excellent, broad and deep API so external libraries would not be needed'.

Starting facts: Core/Term/Term.jet (64 fns) and Core/Tui/Tui.jet (62 fns) exist; D-TUI-ANSI1 A (ANSI{...} checked text plus cursor, clearing, alternate-screen and mouse helpers returning one checked value), D-TERM-INCREMENTAL1 A (one lossless key decoder), D-CORE-TERMSTDIN1 A (is-a-terminal), D-CORE-PROCGROUP1 A. #6147 is an open ballot on whether the terminal UI leaves Core; this card's API must agree with its outcome. A grep finds no raw-mode or alternate-screen function in Core today.

cards.title: Make a := binding that is never reassigned an error
cards.body: Owner order (2026-10-30): a mutable binding (:=) that is never reassigned or mutated must be an error, so name: value (D-DECL-COLON1=A) is the only spelling for a value that never changes. Design only until the owner asks for implementation.

log.text: Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: restated in the spellings of D-DECL-COLON1=A (: replaces ::), D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A (no call-site marks) and D-MOVE-SIGIL1=A (x.move() replaces ^x).

criteria.text: A dated Docs/research note answers the owner's question with evidence: what Jet does today with a := never reassigned (any lint, its code and level), what counts as reassignment or mutation (&x calls, field writes, loops, closures, conditional paths, compile-time code), how Rust, Swift, Go, Zig and Kotlin handle it, and how many sites in Core, Examples, tests and the compiler would change. Each Jet claim is probed on o0, o1 and o2 or cited to code; ratified versus implemented is stated per item.
criteria.evidence: Docs/research/2026-10-30-never-reassigned-binding.md (SurfaceDesign-docs2.patch): today's rule with file:line; L0528 row with no emitter; old Rust rule loop_lints.rs:396-538; probes m6324/m6324b/m6324x o0=o1=o2 for each write kind; census about 6,372 never-written local := out of 40,600 (b2/census6324.mjs); prior art Zig 0.12 error, Rust unused_mut, Swift, Kotlin, Go

criteria.text: Every owner choice the research raises is a ballot-ready Tower decision (same-program alternatives, exact syntax and behavior, beginner and expert paths, edge cases), with recommendation.losses = [] and Tower's readiness check passing.
criteria.evidence: Ballot $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/SurfaceDesign/ballot/D-MUT-NEVER1.json: PLAIN OK, READY. A: any write anywhere in scope counts, error plus Safe jet fix := to ::. B: only reachable writes count. C: error for plain locals only

criteria.text: D-MUT-NEVER1=A, in the spellings of D-DECL-COLON1=A and D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A: a := name never written in its scope is a registered error with what/why/fix text and a Safe fix that rewrites := to : (name: value). A write is =, a compound assignment, a field or index write rooted at the name, passing it to a & parameter, or calling a method that takes &self; a write inside any lambda, branch, loop, ?? block or compile-time block counts even if it never runs. Reading, x.move(), passing by value and writing through Shared are not writes. UI snapshots per case; every in-repo site migrated in one cutover; golden, UI and cases compares lose 0 rows.

cards.title: Binary size: Jet's default build must produce the smallest output of any language, for every program, by design rather than per-program tricks
cards.body: Owner (2026-10-30): 437 KB for hello world is far too big. Measured by Main on this machine (x86-64 Linux, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/q/hello): Zig 0.15.2 ReleaseSmall 10,720 B (static), Zig ReleaseFast stripped 18,744 B, C gcc -O2 stripped 14,440 B (dynamic glibc), C musl static stripped 17,696 B, Rust 1.97.1 -O stripped 394,032 B (dynamic). Jet with #6106 C1 (per-function sections plus gc): 437,416 B with .text 387,880 B (IrTypes-2 measurement); dev before #6106 C1: 5,210,576 B. A hand-written static ELF hello is a few hundred bytes. The size comes from runtime code that startup and print reach (allocator, task and thread setup, panic and formatting machinery), not from the program.

log.text: Warm jet run driver profile (SchedLead, 2026-11-08, dev c2be1e72ac, 20 warm runs of ScriptBench w11, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/SchedLead/prof/run-g.data): the jet driver is 32.6% of all cycles (the program 65.8%). Inclusive, as a share of the driver: package-root search 27.6% (manifest root 24.0%, workspace root 10.8%, entry_has_workspace 12.3%, the same search done three times), production receipt env 26.6%, plan/resolver 18.3% (authority walk 12.6%), pinned toolchain 15.3%, script cache 12.5%, launch 10.2%, C-header bind refresh 8.1% (reads headers with no binding declared), list_dir 8.0%. About 20% self is string copy and alloc/free. Fix in the general driver path (item 4 of the startup plan): find the root once per invocation, skip the header bind when nothing binds, and remove the copies. Routed to QuickLead.

Main 2026-11-08 07:00 owner adopted the no-cache startup plan and its recommended fixes: (1) Core/Prelude precompiled inside jet (new criterion), (2) a single-threaded compile for small programs (new criterion), (3) close the #6527 compiler phase budgets (throughput, which also makes edit-runs fast without incremental state), (4) a leaner jet process start (lazy init, a smaller touched page set), (5) remove the kept-program cache once the cold path beats it (new criterion). c18/c19/c20 are reworded to no-cache runs; #5949 c17 (incremental re-check) is retired as obsolete. Target: jet run at or below one exec plus a user-code-only compile, about 0.2-0.3 ms for hello, below luajit 0.58 and lua 0.75.

Main 2026-11-08 06:45 startup census (a0_037, x86-64 Linux, hyperfine -N; the machine was loaded by a running release, so these are min/median of 60 runs, cold 15): hand-written static ELF hello (write+exit, 182 B) 0.140/0.155 ms; Jet AOT hello binary (jet build, 37,504 B) 0.155/0.175 ms, within ~13% of the ceiling; luajit 0.547/0.582; lua 5.4 0.707/0.751; `jet --version` (exec of the 95.9 MB jet binary) 0.463/0.492; `jet run hello.jet` warm (kept-program cache hit) 8.87/9.57 ms (user 3.9, sys 5.6); cold (no cache or store at all) 17.5/17.8 ms (user 9.9, sys 8.7). strace -c: warm makes 2,255 syscalls (519 statx, 125 getdents64, 268 openat, 440 close: the toolchain and Core source scan to compute the keep key) plus thread-pool futex waits; cold makes 2,999 (501 futex across the parallel compile threads). So the program and runtime startup are at the ceiling, and the whole gap is the jet run front end: the toolchain and Core scan, the thread pool for a tiny program, re-processing Core and Prelude every run (most of the cold 9.9 ms user), and the compiler throughput gap (#6527 phases 3.9x over budget in total). Physical floor for running from source with no cache: one exec (about 0.15 ms) plus a compile of the user code only, against a Core/Prelude shipped precompiled inside the jet binary (an immutable toolchain artifact, not a cache) at about tens of us for hello, plus the in-process run (about 0.02 ms): about 0.2-0.3 ms, below luajit 0.58 and lua 0.75.

Owner 2026-10-30: wants to win every metric including final binary size. Hello world must be the smallest of all languages by default, even without aggressive size optimization. 437 KB is a symptom of an underlying design issue; fix the root, never work around it for one example.

criteria.text: A size breakdown of the Jet hello binary at o0, o1 and o2 lists every runtime symbol and data object over 1 KB with the root that keeps it alive (startup, print, panic, allocator, tasks), recorded in a dated Docs/audits note.
criteria.evidence: Docs/audits/2026-10-30-hello-size.md: hello 437,416 B, identical at default/o0/o1/o2/--release; all 111 runtime functions over 1 KB listed, each with its size, held bytes and root path (startup, init_array, _start/EH, print, exit); no data object reaches 1 KB; liveness recomputed over jet_runtime.pack.o matches the binary (749 sections)

criteria.text: Runtime startup and print pull in only what the program uses: a program that never spawns tasks, allocates or formats links none of that machinery, by liveness and lazy initialization, with one meaning on o0, o1 and o2 (I9) and no change to panic or error behavior.

Jet's default build (jet build, no size flags) of hello and of every required perf workload is strictly smaller than each peer's smallest output for the same program (Zig ReleaseSmall stripped, C musl static -Os stripped, Rust opt-level=z stripped, Go -ldflags=-s -w, Odin -o:size), measured on the same machine; o0 (jet run/jet dev output) and --release are smaller still or equal, never larger.

Final binary size is a required metric in every required perf cell of the canonical manifest, and the gate fails any cell where Jet's default build is not strictly smaller than every peer; a hello-world cell and a small CLI cell are among them.

The size win comes from the root design (pay-for-what-you-use runtime, lazy runtime initialization, liveness through every runtime and Core layer, no unconditional startup machinery), with no hello-world special case, no per-program flags, no stripping or compression tricks that peers are denied, and no change to panic, error, safety or I9 behavior; the receipt shows the same mechanism shrinking a non-trivial program.

Owner order 2026-10-30: for every program in the size corpus (hello plus one program per required perf cell, each with a hand-written, optimized x86-64 assembly reference committed beside it), the default jet build is within 2x of the assembly reference size (target 1.5x). Every byte category above the reference is listed with the reason this program needs it.

(was #5478) Fast process exit: no memory reclamation when the process ends; user cleanup and secret scrub only

(was #5476) With no kept program, cache or incremental state, `jet run hello.jet` (a fresh process, nothing reused from an earlier run) shows a lower mean than `luajit hello.lua` under `hyperfine -N --warmup 3 --runs 30` on the same host (Jet/LuaJIT < 1.00); the final target is at or below one exec plus a compile of the user code only (the hand-written ELF hello is 0.155 ms on the reference host). Baselines 2026-11-08 (a0_037): cold 17.8 ms, luajit 0.58 ms, lua 0.75 ms, Jet AOT binary 0.175 ms.
(was #5476) Peak RSS of `jet run hello.jet` with no kept program or cache (GNU time %M, median of 10) is below `lua hello.lua` on the same host.

(was #5476) After a one-line edit to a 30-line script that uses core.files and core.regex, `jet run` prints its first output sooner than `python3` runs the equivalent script (hyperfine with a prepare step that applies the edit; Jet/Python < 1.00), with no kept program, cache or incremental state: an edited run costs what any run costs.

(was #5949 c16) Script startup beats Lua: on one host, the same-run median of `jet run hello.jet` and of `jet run` after an edit are each below lua 5.4 hello.lua, by design rather than by reusing a kept program or incremental state (owner 2026-11-08: do not rely on incremental compilation or caching to win; the final target is the hand-written machine-code ceiling). Baselines in the #6328 log, 2026-11-08.

Core and Prelude ship precompiled inside the jet binary: checked interfaces and machine code produced when jet is built, part of the toolchain identity and immutable (no runtime cache, nothing to invalidate). `jet run` reads, scans and re-checks no Core or Prelude source: strace -c of `jet run hello.jet` shows no statx/openat/getdents64 on the toolchain tree, and the cold user time for hello is spent on the user code. One meaning on o0/o1/o2 (I9).

A small program compiles on the calling thread: `jet run` starts compile worker threads only when the work justifies them (by a measured threshold), with identical output either way; strace -c of `jet run hello.jet` shows no thread-pool futex traffic.

Once the no-cache `jet run` beats the kept-program path on every ScriptBench workload, the kept-program cache (Compiler/JetCli ScriptCache: keep slots, background full builds, the stdin entry cache) is removed in one cutover, with every caller, case, doc and setting migrated; `jet run` has one launch path.

cards.title: Fixed strings and a growable builder: should String be unchangeable, with a separate mutable type, and what are both called
cards.body: Owner, 2026-10-30: "Relook at string types: string should be constant, not flexible, and string builders (don't love the name). String builders are the mutable version that can grow, shrink, change, etc.; strings should generally be fixed. Maybe strings would be like Odin string builders and text would be static unchangeable constant strings? Open to suggestions for both concepts' names." Today Jet's one text type is String (about 2,250 uses in Examples), and D-STRING-EMPTY1 covers reusing it. Owner: SurfaceDesign (design only).

log.text: Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: c5 restated for D-DECL-COLON1=A (fixed names are name: value) and D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A (edits are plain calls).

C5 root (CardClose-1): D-TEXT-FIXED1=A names String.with_capacity(n) and s.capacity(). The runtime has rt_text_builder_with_capacity internally but exports only jet_rt_string_builder_new() with no capacity. Needs a runtime export (jet_rt_string_with_capacity), a BuiltinMethods static row and a TBuiltinOp lowering.

cards.title: A portable target better than WASM: a Jet bytecode or IR plus a hardware-capability API so sandboxed code can use tensor cores, SIMD and GPUs
cards.body: Owner, 2026-10-30: "Mojo has a bytecode/VM effectively which supports portability. One of Jet's goals is to effectively replace WASM as a portable target, so we need to investigate deeply. One issue with WASM is that it doesn't expose the hardware, like tensor cores, so it is a lowest-common-denominator system. We need to improve on that: some kind of metadata API that lets portable code leverage the hardware capabilities exposed by the host running the Jet sandbox." cards.title: Greenfield proposal: the best possible FFI design for calling and being called by almost any language
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-10-30: a terse but thoroughly engineered, robust proposal for a theoretically perfect FFI that beats every existing one, designed greenfield with no Jet limitations, then judged for adoption into Jet. It must follow the composition principle: a complete primitives layer that can express everything, plus high-quality wrappers for the common cases.

**The proposal:** Docs/proposals/ffi-perfect-boundary-2026-10-30.md (commit e99e795e4c). Section 9 maps every idea onto Jet; three owner ballots follow from it: D-FFI-PRIMS1 (public primitives layer), D-FFI-ISOLATE1 (isolation as a placement option) and D-FFI-EXPORT2 (rich exports).

## Plain summary

- **The idea.** Every foreign boundary is described once, as a *boundary
  contract*. That is a typed list of functions and types, plus the facts a C
  header cannot say: who owns memory, how long a view lives, how errors come
  back, which thread may call, and whether a call is async.
- **Readers and writers.** A reader package builds the contract from whatever
  the other side has (a C header, a Rust crate, a `.d.ts`, a WIT file, a JVM
  class, Windows metadata, a GPU shader). A writer package turns the same
  contract into bindings for whoever calls *us*. Both directions share one
  model, so N languages cost N readers plus N writers, not N×N bridges.
- **Two layers.** A small, complete, unsafe *primitives* layer can express
  every boundary: layout, symbols, calls, memory, callbacks, errors, threads,
  async, isolation. Pareto *wrappers* sit on top: `use "png.h" as png`,
  `#Export`, and typed imports for Rust, Python and JS. Every wrapper
  expands into primitives that you can inspect, so the expert path is a ladder,
  not a cliff.
- **Safe by default.** A call is safe when its facts are checked, vouched for
  in a named `#Unsafe("reason")`, or *isolated*. Isolated means the same import
  runs in a wasm sandbox or a separate process, with no source changes.
- **Zero cost.** A crossing whose types already match costs one direct call.
  When the foreign source is visible, the optimizer can inline across the
  boundary.
- **For Jet.** Most of this is already ratified: header import, C source import,
  binder packages, ownership sigils at the border, vouches, both embedding
  artifacts, and the hardened profile. The new pieces are a public primitives
  layer, isolation as a placement option, and rich exports. Each is one ballot.
  Inline C stays, and becomes a thin wrapper over C-source import, which
  removes the "two ways to bring in C" loss that D-FFI-ONE1 recorded.

This builds on, and does not replace, the boundary audit
[`Docs/audits/ffi-owned-source-and-boundaries.md`](../audits/ffi-owned-source-and-boundaries.md)
(#2933), which covers project arrangements and workflows. This document is the
mechanism underneath them.

cards.title: API design principle: strong composable primitives first, pareto wrappers on top, full use of variadics and named/positional arguments
cards.body: Owner direction 2026-10-30: wrappers solve some problems but often make everything outside their case harder. Jet's APIs need a very strong primitives layer that can express everything, then pareto-level high-quality wrappers for the common work. Jet's API tools (variadics, named and positional arguments, defaults) are barely used today and should be, to make APIs more powerful and more streamlined. This must become a fundamental design element of the project, with a review that checks the APIs follow it.

(was #6023) The acceptance checks of #1915 are ported and pass with the self-hosted `jet`: a C host links libjet, loads a Jet module, calls a function and gets its result.
(was #6023) The wasm component runs the same module in wasmtime with the same output (test).
(was #6023) The embedding header is generated, and its doc page carries a runnable C example checked by a test.

(was #6023) The runtime a host links for a guest that uses only core.text and core.math is smaller than the Lua 5.4.7 interpreter (329,248 bytes), and 10M host-to-guest calls of a small function finish faster than `lua_pcall` on the equivalent Lua function (Jet/Lua < 1.00).

(was #6023) The host passes an Authority value: a guest module that calls files.read without an FS.Read grant is refused at load time with a named error, before any guest code runs (test). Lua can only sandbox at run time by removing globals.

cards.title: Build `reject(Diagnostic)` (D-MARKER-DIAG1=A): library compile-time checks raise their own error codes
cards.body: Found by #6385 on dev 59213de00f. D-MARKER-DIAG1=A ratified that a library error is a struct implementing Core's Diagnostic trait (what/why/fix as one-literal methods) and that `reject(err)` raises it while compiling, from a marker's expand or a helper. `reject` is not built: probes/zig/z05_reject.jet reports `E0102 Nothing named 'reject' exists here`. Today a comptime check can only `panic`, which gives E3010 with a message but no code, why, fix or `jet explain` page. This is Jet's version of Zig's @compileError, done better.

cards.title: A task blocked in an ordinary OS wait or foreign call holds its worker thread, so ready tasks stall
cards.body: Found by MemDesign-5 for #6376 (release-notes research: Java 21 virtual threads pinned their carrier inside synchronized and native calls, which made libraries rewrite their locks, until JDK 24's JEP 491; Go releases the P on every syscall and cgo call). D-ASYNCRT1=A promises Go's model: "blocking calls yield automatically; no call-site annotation". Only runtime park points call `scheduler_blocking_wait_enter` (Condition, Shared, Task, TaskGroup, Realtime, Generator, AsyncEvents, SharedTransactions, Scheduler). Raw host calls do not: `jet_sys_waitpid_raw` issues wait4 directly (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/HostProcess.jet:166-177), and foreign calls have no hook. Repro $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/MemDesign-4/probes/rel/r08_child_wait_block.jet: 96 tasks each run `sleep 1` through core.process, then one trivial task is spawned and joined. On jet 03c64ad0c4 (soft address-space limit raised to 16 GB, see the 192 MiB stack card) it prints "quick task done after 3023780905ns". Compensation costs a thread start today (Shared.jet:46-50 notes hundreds of thousands of such threads in one compiler pass), so the fix has to be cheap on short calls, like Go's hand-off after a call has blocked for a while.

(was #6404) A program's worker threads use a stack size chosen for programs, not the compiler's 192 MiB floor. The compiler's own stages keep their larger stack through their own setting. The sizes are documented in the runtime docs.

(was #6404) When an extra worker or compensation thread cannot start, the scheduler goes on with the threads it has. Only a failure to start the first worker stops the program, and that stop names the resource limit (for example RLIMIT_AS) and is not reported as a program panic. UI snapshot registered.

cards.title: core.compute port: devices, streams, sparse tensors and transfer receipts need storage in the registered compute vocabulary
cards.body: The R1 port of core.compute to Jet source (Core/Compute/Compute.jet) cannot express on_device and transfer to non-CPU placements, transfer_show, streams, sparse CSR, VJPRun or deserialize receipts. The registered types have no storage for them (core-library.md:4289-4291 makes the registered vocabulary their only owner). ComputeDevice, ComputeStream and SparseTensor are opaque to users today (E0119 on a literal, E0302 on field access), so their storage is added as private core_only field rows. Tensor is a 5-field literal that users can read and assign today (a.requested = "Metal" changes compute.placement), so where its reason and transfer receipts live is the owner ballot D-COMPUTE-TENSOR-STORE1 on this card.

cards.title: Run time: default codegen must be borderline equal to hand-written optimized assembly for every program
cards.body: Owner order, 2026-10-30: performance should be borderline equal to hand-written assembly with default codegen, not with flags or per-program tricks. Binary size has the same goal, and #6328 owns size. This card owns speed. Every program in the perf corpus (one per required perf cell plus the codegen kernels: loops, bounds-checked indexing, string length and iteration, slices, calls, closures, records, allocation, I/O write) gets a hand-written, optimized x86-64 assembly reference, committed with a harness that measures cycles and instructions (perf stat, best of N, pinned CPU). The gap is closed in the code generator and runtime design (instruction selection, register allocation, bounds-check elimination, inlining, layout), never by weakening safety, semantics or diagnostics (AGENTS.md performance gate).

log.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (chat, Q17): SpeedLead takes run-time codegen (#6414, #6478, #6472, and the TlsLead and G1Lead roots logged here) when it finishes the build.jet work on #6682. No new lead.

Evidence from G1Lead (#6688 c4, 7639370892 and b53d287e41; Jet libm against musl with identical bits, O1 perf-stat cycles per call: sin 81.8 vs 64.8, cos 80.5 vs 64.7, exp 56.7 vs 39.9, log 63.4 vs 41.1, pow 169.3 vs 113.9). Roots, all general codegen: (1) index math on a proven-small Int keeps an inline add plus jo overflow test, 2 to 3 per access; a comptime table read goes through its static list header (len and data-pointer loads) with a bounds check and a list_bounds_stop call with xmm spills, about 15 instructions per access (exp 2, log 4, pow 5 accesses). (2) FloatBits and FloatFromBits (BuildLibrary ir_reinterpret) and Float abs (BuildRoutes:3489) go through a stack store and reload instead of movq; 14 percent of pow samples sit on one reload. (3) At O1, Float and shifted constants are neither folded nor hoisted: movabs plus movq at every use. (4) A || chain is materialized as bools through stack slots, about 25 instructions at pow entry. (5) A small struct return (LibmReduced) goes through sret, and a small helper (libm_rem_pio2_near) is not inlined. Same family as the TlsLead hash findings above; ownership is owner Q17.

Evidence from TlsLead (#6694 S1, b53a78981d), the emitted x64 of core_crypto___jet_hashes_dcompress (portable SHA-512 compress, about 935 ns per block against about 280 ns for mbedtls): (1) 4670 instructions, 2564 mov and 1209 rbp spills, about 6 GPRs used (#6478); (2) no rol or ror: a constant rotate lowers to a shift-by-cl pair plus and 0x1f, and there are 107 shl or shr 0x20 U32 zero-extends; (3) per call 65 jet_rt_list_bounds_stop, 76 jet_ir_stop_poll inside fixed-trip loops (#6472), 32 cleanup enter and leave, 43 jet_rt_int_drop; (4) wrapping(U8{x}) from an out-of-range Int costs about 260 ns (global masks, boxed-Int drops, jo checks) against 9 ns for U8{x %% 256}; (5) list copy and push cost 1.5 to 2 ns per element; (6) a fixed-list global is re-materialized on every access (64 stores); (7) hash_start plus Close costs about 256 ns. Each is a general codegen root; the crypto engine is the second program for the perf rule.

criteria.text: A perf corpus with a hand-written optimized x86-64 assembly reference per program, plus a measurement harness (cycles and instructions, perf stat best of N on a pinned CPU), is committed under Tools/perf and listed in the canonical perf manifest.
For every corpus program, `jet build` (default flags) runs within 1.10x of its assembly reference in cycles, with identical output; any program over that bound has a named codegen root on a card.

The perf gate fails any corpus program over the bound, and a plan document (Docs/proposals) names the codegen and runtime design changes, with modelled gains, that close the gap without per-program tricks.

criteria.text: Every G10 kernel beats Rust (Jet/Rust < 1.00, same run) and is measured against the best hand-written assembly for the workload, with the gap to that ceiling reported per kernel and closed largest-first (owner order 2026-10-31).

Owner order 2026-10-31 (supersedes the 1.10x bound in C2 and the Rust 1.05 band in C22, C28): the canonical manifest (Tools/gauntlet/matrix.json strict_performance_policy) encodes two stages per required cell and metric: the peer floor (Jet/peer < 1.00 for every matched peer, Rust included) and the machine ceiling (Jet/hand-written, maximally optimized machine-code reference <= 1.00 in cycles and in bytes). The harness reports both verdicts and fails any required cell without a ceiling reference as uncovered.
criteria.evidence: CardClose-1 verdict 2026-10-31: With CardClose-8 (wave/14/in) applied, Tools/gauntlet/matrix.json strict_performance_policy v3 carries a `ceiling` block with stages peer_floor (initial) and machine_ceiling (final, meet "<=1", metrics cycles and bytes). It also has peer_win_closes_cell=false and missing_reference "uncovered", which is listed in failure_statuses. run.mjs reports peer_verdict and ceiling_verdict per cell. The new test "a peer win never closes a cell whose machine ceiling is unmet" asserts blockers of the form "fixture.cell/machine-ceiling/runtime_wall_seconds: metric uncovered (no hand-written machine-code reference names this cell)". Manifest and status tests pass 32/32 on rebase12; lane-check CHECK OK.

cards.title: Core APIs that are not built yet: Bytes, Path.walk, timer channels, browser automation, config decode, Parquet/Arrow, Stream windows and the Vulkan provider
cards.body: Core APIs that the spec ratifies but the self-hosted runtime still answers with E2104 "not built yet". Their goldens and cases rows carry KNOWN-FAILING links here (owner ruling 2026-10-30). sys.decode (#5992), mod.load (#5993), service.tree and ws (#4957) keep their own cards. GoldC-3 owns Bytes.

log.text: Goal set to G3 only (was G1,G3). The two open rows, c7 (Parquet/Arrow reader beating pyarrow/polars) and c9 (Jet-runtime Vulkan provider), are Core completeness. They are not hand-off or durability, and they don't block a fresh clone from continuing work. The rows are unchanged.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

cards.title: raylib leaves Core: Core/Game/Raylib.jet and UiRaylibMetadata.jet go to a first-party `raylib` package
cards.body:
Move card for #6149 (D-RAYLIB-FONT-HOME1=A, ratified 2026-10-31: "Moves under A, one card each").

- Moves: Core/Game/Raylib.jet and Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/UiRaylibMetadata.jet to the
  first-party battery Jetpack/Provider/Batteries/raylib/. It ships with Jet at its version
  (D-JPK-RINGSHIP1=C), and `jet add raylib` writes the one dependency line.
- Keeps the typed backend value of D-GAME-BACKEND1=A, so `game.run(scene, backend:)` still
  takes it. GPU device providers stay with card 5964.

log.text: Examples concept-area cutover (2c3e68a70b) moved paths this card's criteria cite. Read each cited path as its new home: c1: Examples/features/game/raylib_canvas -> Examples/Apps/Game/RaylibCanvas [new path does not exist yet: the criterion still has to create it].
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match D-DECL-COLON1=A (`name: value`, no `::`).

Retargeted c1 (owner order 2026-11-02: an invalid criterion is retargeted to a valid one). Old text: `use raylib as rl` builds and runs Examples/features/game/raylib_canvas, raylib_shapes, raylib_indexed, raylib_sprites and battery, with the same golden checksums on o0/o1/o2. Why: the criterion spelled the retired `use raylib as rl` import form; the current form names the alias first (`use rl :: …`), as every game example spells it today.

Core/Game/Raylib.jet and its rows in Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet, CoreCalls.jet, CorePlatformSignatures.jet, CoreSurfaceInventory.jet and StructureRegistry.jet are gone, and the generated Core registries are regenerated.
The package uses only mechanisms that any package can use (pillar 5): no Core-private power and no compiler row that names the package.

cards.title: UI cases where the Jet checker reports nothing: diagnostic families the Rust checker emitted
cards.body: CoverPort census of the wave-6 ui suite (2026-10-31; table $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/CoverPort/out/report5-nodiag.tsv with count, code, stage, registry meaning, Jet emit files and example ids): 157 tests/ui rows expect an error diagnostic that the Jet checker never reports (lint rows L0xxx belong to #6006). Each is a missing sema check, not text. Two kinds: (1) the code has a Jet emit site that misses this case (largest: Sema/Ownership/Checks.jet E0204 x10, E0121 x6, E2305 x5, E0209 x4; Effects E3403 x6; Calls E0112 x5; Control E2402 x5; Registration E3203 x5; E0119, E0926, E0999, E2960 x4 each; E0907, E1206 x3); (2) whole families with no Jet emit site (E1293, E2806, E2807, E1402, lint-policy E1201/E1208/E1211/E1212/E1213/E1216, E0619, E0996, E0997, E2967, E-OSTARGET-*, E-WEB-RUN, a11y E2931). cards.title: Each generator yield is a scheduler task park and wake, about 20 us per value
cards.body: Measured by IrTypes-3 2026-10-31 (IrTypes-25b timing): a generator pull hands off through the task scheduler (park the consumer, wake the producer, and back), about 20 us per yield. The iterloop kit case does 3M yields plus 1.28M channel pulls and takes 79 s. A generator that runs on the consumer thread needs no scheduler: a direct stack switch or a compiled state machine costs nanoseconds, and C/Rust/Zig iterators cost one call or less. This is a structural cost on every program that iterates a generator. Related: #6089 (lazy pulls charging comptime fuel through a global mutex).

criteria.text: A generator pull that stays on the consumer thread costs under 50 ns per value (a direct switch or a compiled state machine, no scheduler park/wake), measured same-run on the iterloop kit case and a 10M-yield microbench; every generator golden is unchanged on O0/O1/O2.

cards.title: stdin reads one byte per syscall: cat-style programs run ~3,300x slower than Rust
cards.body: Floor-1 same-run measurement on df84 (2026-10-31, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Floor/out/pareto-speed.md): the cat cell is about 3,300x Rust by task-clock, because terminal/stdin reads go one byte per read syscall (Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/RouteTerm.jet:19-51). stdout writes need the same check. Fix the root in the one shared runtime: buffered stdin and stdout with correct flush semantics (line-buffered for a TTY, block-buffered otherwise, flush at exit, flush before reading interactive input), with one meaning on every tier.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match the AGENTS.md Performance gate (Jet/peer < 1.00 with no Rust band, then the asm-parity ceiling).

Main-34 folds print's LF into host_stdout_write (one locked write per print line). cat cell vs rust-O3, perf stat medians: HEAD 7c67280960 runtime 435M cycles / 94.3 ms task-clock (Rust 395M / 89.3 ms: 1.10x cycles, 1.056x task-clock); with Main-34 430M / 93.3 ms (about -1.1%). Output byte-identical; cases --filter stdout|print match the HEAD baseline; golden suite adds no new failures versus HEAD (18 missing-stream rows are #6538, stack_overflow o2 tier-split is pre-existing at HEAD). Rejected: a 16-byte unroll of stdin_line_scan (+3.8% cycles). Remaining gap per profile: sync_sole_enter about 14% (about 15 cycles per elided call), copy about 14%, SWAR scan about 10%, stdout write about 22%; mostly runtime codegen quality (stack spills) and call overhead. Card stays open: the gate requires Jet/peer < 1.00.

Main 2026-11-01 09:05, dev 367eaf8f0d base jet, release build of Floor cells/cat/run.jet on a 200,000-line (10.7 MB) pipe input: output byte-identical. strace shows 165 stdin reads (64 KiB each) and 1,398 stdout writes (about 7.6 KiB each), so the one-byte read root is gone. hyperfine -N, 40 runs, load average 18: Jet 33.2 ms (user 25.7), Rust O3 20.1 ms (user 9.8), C gcc O2 3.9 ms. Jet/Rust is 1.65, down from about 3,300. Criterion 1 is still open. The remaining cost is per-line user time: lines() makes one String per line, UTF-8 is checked per line, and print adds its own work. Next: a borrowed line view or a bulk copy for the lines-to-print path, still with one meaning on every tier.

AsmPar-1 2026-11-01 01:05: the one-byte read root is fixed on wave 18 (strace of the cat cell: 1,086 reads of 64 KiB for 71 MB). The cell is still 3.3x Rust in cycles (0.78G vs 0.24G); the remaining gap is a per-line alloc/free in the lines iterator plus stdio_checkpoint.

Landed on dev at undefined in AsmPar-13 (patch row: criterion/count 2): AsmPar-13 (partial; criterion stays open): cat's final string drops skip the lock. Locked instructions retired 3.535M -> 3.303M (-6.6%, release); the remaining locks are retains and shared drops.

Landed on dev at undefined in AsmPar-12 (patch row: criterion/count 1): AsmPar-12 (partial; criterion stays open): the cat cell's per-line UTF-8 validation no longer calls rt_text_valid_width for each ASCII tail byte. cat: 2581.4M -> 2453.6M instructions (-5.0%, release, r15 vs r16 s1).

Landed on dev at undefined in IrTypes-31 (patch row: criterion/count 1): PARTIAL, criterion NOT met (card stays open): IrTypes-31 drops the line's trailing LF/CR inside jet_stdin_line_raw (in place, after the UTF-8 check), and Core read_line no longer round-trips each line through [U8] (stdin_chomp removed). Floor cat cell, jet --release: 6,485 M instr / 252-312 ms -> 3,963 M / 150.6 ms task-clock; matched Rust peer (cells/cat/main.rs, now BufRead::lines + BufWriter) 752 M / 58.8 ms, so Jet/Rust is 2.56x (the raw block copy moved to cells/catblock). CRLF transcript byte-identical to the old chomp on 5 inputs, default and --release; 88 stdin/terminal/prompt/io_/print cases have the same status as on IrTypes-30. Left: per-line Result/Option boxes and the String alloc in the lines iterator (codegen, sent to Codegen-1).

Landed on dev at undefined in IrTypes-30 (patch row: criterion/count 1): PARTIAL, criterion NOT met (card stays open): IrTypes-30 buffers stdin (one shared 64 KiB buffer under the stdin lock) and stdout (print flush 0: line-buffered on a tty, 8 KiB blocks otherwise; flushed before stderr, every stdin read, children, exit). Floor-1 cat cell: jet --release 35,612 ms -> 252 ms task-clock (wall ~= task), rust-O3 10.2 ms, zig 9.3 ms same run, so Jet/Rust ~24x, not <= 1.05. strace: stdin reads max 65,536 B, mean 65,424 B (1,086 reads; was 1 B each); stdout 9,198 writes (was 833,335). Every stdin/stdout/prompt/terminal/print/io_/no_args/runtime_stop_goldens/build_option_ case has the same status as the pre-patch jet (cases/repl/ differs only by the harness's E2104 stdin-write race); terminal/stdin_lines_emit_before_eof and stdout_write_bytes_ordered_with_print pass by hand on default and --release. The remaining ~300 ns/line is the per-line String (Core StdinHandle.read_line: checkpoint, jet_stdin_line_raw copy, stdin_chomp's [U8] round trip, alloc/drop), which needs a borrowed line view in the lines loop to reach Rust's raw 64 KiB copy.

Main 2026-10-31: IrTypes-30 (wave 11) buffers stdin/stdout: cat cell 35.6 s -> 252 ms, 64 KiB reads, corpus 52/52 identical. The Floor-1 Rust peer was an io::copy block copy, so it was not matched. Against a matched BufRead::lines + BufWriter Rust (64 ms, 752M instr), Jet is 4.2x in time and 8.5x in instructions (7,894 vs 928 Ir per line). Roots: Core stdin_chomp round trip 30%, jet_stdin_line_raw 27% (UTF-8 validated twice), per-line lazy_line_next boxes 18%, print 8%, String drop 5% ($JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/IR/IrTypes/c6328/d44/cg/ATTRIB.md). Next: runtime strips CR/LF (IrTypes-31); per-line boxes and String alloc go to Codegen-1. Criterion 1 is not met yet.

criteria.text: The cat cell (Floor-1 cells/cat) is faster than Rust same-run (Jet/Rust < 1.00) by wall time and task-clock, strace shows reads of at least 64 KiB per syscall on a pipe, and every stdin/stdout golden and interactive REPL case is unchanged on O0/O1/O2.

cards.title: The gauntlet measurement manifest has no slot for a matched Rust peer, so Jet/Rust ratios cannot be gated
cards.body: Found by Codegen-1 on 2026-10-31. Tools/gauntlet measurement-manifest.json entries carry jet and python programs only, and axes need a status and harness. There is no field for the matched Rust peer, so the AGENTS.md performance gate (Jet/Rust <= 1.05 per cell and metric, strictly below 1.00 against every other peer) cannot be encoded in the manifest, only in prose and lane notes (Floor cells, Codegen-1 corpus). The manifest must name every required peer per entry, with the matched program, and the gate must fail any required cell where a peer is missing or the comparator fails.

log.text: Main 2026-10-31: the gauntlet matrix gives each cell exactly one owning entry (measurement-manifest.test.mjs:744), and matrix.json is owner-approved. So the wordfreq 200k-unique-key variant (Codegen-1: gen.py seed 42, input sha256 43e32ccc…, matched Rust collect+sort_by) cannot be added as an entry without a new matrix cell plus a loss_owners source card. Until the owner approves a text.kernel scale-variant cell, its numbers live in the Codegen-1 Map patch msg as lane evidence. Baseline: Jet 26.45 s vs Rust 0.08 s at 200k; Jet 0.63 s vs Rust 0.05 s at 10k (wave-11 s1, --optimize=full).

criteria.text: measurement-manifest.json names the matched Rust, C, Zig and Go peers per entry, where they apply; the gate script fails a required cell whose peer is missing, unmatched, or fails the AGENTS.md comparator; wordfreq 10k/200k and cat are recorded with matched peers.

cards.title: Function-local Result/Option boxes from runtime routes stay heap-allocated (binparse 25% alloc/free)
cards.body: binparse run builds a jet_rt_alloc(16,8) Result box around each reader route (4 per record in the loop) that never leaves run. perf on the register-return build: free_8 12.4% + alloc_8 8.8% + alloc 4.3% = 25.5% of 257M cycles (~66M). The register-return pass does not reach these boxes. Fix: escape analysis in JetIR: a function-local box used only by Load/Store at offsets, the unique test, free and Drop becomes a stack slot, and scalar replacement then puts it in registers. General: applies to every non-escaping small heap allocation. Full text: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/IR/IrTypes/c6328/d53/CARD-REQUEST-local-box.md.

cards.title: Sound quiet-runtime-route table so no stop poll follows a runtime call that cannot stop
cards.body: Every runtime route except the hand list in Build.jet ir_route_can_stop is followed by a stop poll. RUNTIME_STOP_EXPORTS cannot decide it as generated: it is the named-call closure from scheduler_panic_publish_record only (cancel/deadline publish via scheduler_native_publish; dynamic code-word calls excluded; 24 scalar route exports such as jet_time_sleep_until are not Jet runtime exports). Generate the closure from scheduler_control_publish, seed every function calling through a non-rail code word, and emit the complement (quiet exports), in both gen-runtime-stop-exports.mjs and RuntimeGenerators.jet. Then ir_route_can_stop answers from that table and the hand list goes. Full text: wave/16/in/Codegen-1-27.msg.

criteria.text: Default build: a loop's stop poll costs at most 2 hot instructions per iteration, with the poll call out of line (objdump of the asm-parity hot loops).

cards.title: Cross-package IR inlining of small Core bodies (runtime-routed Core leaves are opaque to OptInline)
cards.body: Runtime-routed Core leaves (jet_std_math_*) are prebuilt in the runtime pack, so OptInline never has their IR; OptInline also refuses cross-file callees holding located (stop-capable) ops because the trap site is tied to the source file. Ship the IR of small Never! runtime leaves with the runtime pack (or compile them from Core source into the module), and carry the source file per located op so an inlined cross-file op keeps its trap site. Measured motive: fft/tensormap still call Core fabs via to_bits/from_bits after the ir_leaf_route table (-9.1% instead of 12-16%). Full text: wave/16/in/Codegen-1-27.msg.

criteria.text: Small runtime-routed Core leaves are inlinable across packages (their IR ships with the runtime pack or compiles from Core source), and an inlined cross-file located op keeps its trap site.
fft and tensormap no longer call Core fabs through to_bits/from_bits; their cells improve by the measured 12-16%, with identical output.

cards.title: Hoist constant Regex{} construction out of every evaluation
cards.body: sema_expression_typed_literal_regex (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Expressions/Constructors.jet) lowers every Regex{"…"} literal to a runtime core.regex.compile(pattern) on each evaluation, although the pattern is fixed and checked at compile time. With the budgeted DFA (GoldC-59, #6474) a typical compile costs ~44 µs instead of ~3 µs, so a literal inside a hot loop now pays that per iteration. Build each constant Regex once per program (comptime constant: Regex values already materialize, see comptime_diff/reusable_regex; or a once-initialized global). Proof: a loop with a Regex literal shows one compile per program in a profile; regex cases and goldens unchanged on o0/o1/o2.

cards.title: Register allocator: live-range splitting so density-based spills keep hot loop values
cards.body: IrTypes-37 (floats in xmm2-15) found that a pure density spill rule wins nbody (1.65G -> 0.62G cycles) but evicts collatz hot loop variables for short temporaries (6.97G -> 10.82G instructions). The landed safe rule (evict only lighter ranges) keeps collatz exact but gives nbody only -36% (1.64G -> 1.05G). Split long live ranges around hot loops so the density rule can keep both. Proof: nbody at or under 0.62G cycles and collatz at or under 6.97G instructions in the same s2, every other ceiling cell flat or better, s2 chain + FULL cases.

cards.title: Pareto census: profile every cell, attribute every gap to a root, and plan each root
cards.body: Owner order 2026-10-31 20:00: binary size and speed are still far from the hand-written ceilings. Profile every cell (not cherry-picked): every asm-parity ceiling cell, every gauntlet cell against every peer, and a seeded random sample of programs from the example/workload corpora with peer versions. For each, record cycles, instructions and bytes as ratios to the ceiling and to each peer, plus perf hotspots and a size breakdown by symbol and section (runtime, glue, user code). Attribute every gap to a root (e.g. startup, RC/locks, bounds checks, spills/regalloc, missing loop opts or vectorization, inlining, allocation, runtime size, dead code). Rank the roots by total gap mass across cells. Separately, compare the JetIR/backend pipeline with the LLVM O2 pipeline (SROA, GVN, LICM, InstCombine, SCCP, jump threading, loop unroll/vectorize, inliner cost model, register coalescing, shrink-wrapping, tail dup, code layout, LTO dead stripping) and list the missing ones with their expected reach. Output: a dated audit under Docs/audits with the TSV, and one Tower card per root with an owner, proof terms and the cells it moves.

cards.title: Beyond the hand-written ceiling: survey optimizations that beat expert asm (Goose language claims, whole-program specialization, superoptimization, data-layout transforms)
cards.body: Owner order 2026-10-31: once every program meets the hand-written asm ceiling in cycles and bytes, the next goal is to BEAT it. Survey with sources: the Goose language (its claimed speedups over Rust and C, what mechanisms produce them, which are verified, and which fit Jet semantics and I9), whole-program specialization and monomorphization budgets, superoptimization of hot blocks, automatic data-layout transforms (AoS/SoA, field reordering, small-value packing), allocation elision and region inference, comptime evaluation of input-independent work, and cache-aware code layout without PGO. Output: Docs/research/beyond-asm-ceiling-2026-10-31.md ranking each idea by expected gain across ALL programs (not one example), implementation cost and semantic risk, with cards proposed for the top items. No claim without a source or a measurement.

log.text: Owner, 2026-11-08: reaching the theoretical bound requires unbounded hill climbing, so it is a horizon goal and not a short-term one like today's speed and size goal (G11). It stays distinct, blocks no current card or work, and is treated as research. This card stays in G13 (Hillclimbing) at P3, tagged research. Its bound and report criteria (c4-c6) are research targets and are never a gate for G4 or G11 or any card there; the G11 gate stays peers below 1.00 and the hand-written reference at most 1.00.

Owner direction, 2026-11-08: default Jet should outperform everything and land just above the theoretical maximum. That maximum is not only optimized machine code, but the best result the problem allows, reached by rethinking phasing, ordering, logic and advanced techniques. For real-world cases, hit the real-world maximum. The owner chose "Record it": every required cell gets a written, reviewed theoretical bound; reports show Jet against the peers, the hand-written reference and the bound; the gate stays peers plus the reference; the design targets the bound. Each technique that adds user-visible behavior still needs its own ballot and adversarial review.
Owner 2026-10-31: the Goose material is in our prior-art notes (mined about 1-2 weeks ago): https://github.com/aardappel/goose. Start there.

criteria.text: The survey lists every technique known to beat expert hand-written assembly (Goose-style stack-based execution, whole-program specialization, superoptimization, data-layout transforms and others), each with sources and a runnable probe.
Each technique that wins its probe gets a card with a paired two-program cell under the performance gate rules.
End metric: required cells beat their asm-parity ceilings (Jet/ceiling below 1.00 in cycles and bytes) with identical output, and every cell that does not is on a card.

Every required gauntlet and ScriptBench cell has a written theoretical bound per metric, derived only from the workload's stated contract: wall time from the critical path (unavoidable latencies and dependency chain); CPU time from the larger of bytes moved over memory or disk bandwidth and minimum operations over machine throughput; RSS and bytes from the minimum working set and image. The derivation is committed beside the cell and reviewed adversarially, so a bound cannot be made easy.

The performance reports show, for each cell and metric, Jet against the best peer of each tier, Jet against the hand-written reference, and Jet against the theoretical bound, on the binary and on `jet run`. The bound ratio is the design target and never relaxes the gate (every peer below 1.00, the reference at most 1.00).

The survey covers the schedule-level techniques that move Jet toward the bound and that typical runtimes do not apply by default: effect-aware early I/O (sema-known opens, DNS, connects and fetches issued at process start); concurrent execution of effects sema proves independent, longest expected chain first; syscall batching (io_uring, writev, readahead) and zero-copy; elimination of unread outputs and stage fusion; compile-time initialized startup images; speculation limited to repeatable effect-free reads. Each gets a probe, a paired two-program cell, and observable behavior preserved (output, the order of visible effects, workload limits such as "at most 32 in flight"; no caching of results the program must compute).

cards.title: FFI v3 gallery: C libraries (libm, zlib, libpng)
cards.body:
Three complete programs that call C through `use c.<lib>`. None contains `#Unsafe`, a pointer or a binding file.
The `cbind` package (root `c`) reads each header with pinned clang, derives facts with evidence, and writes a Jet
module. Outputs are design targets, not observed runs. Design: `ffi-v3.md` in the FFIDesign v3 lane, sections 4
and 5; ballots D-FFI-LANG1, D-FFI-PRIMS2, D-FFI-FACTS1.

## Simple: libm

What it shows: a system library, scalar rows, zero overhead. Each call lowers to the same `call` C emits.

```jet
use m: c.math

run: fn() {
    print(m.cos(0.0))
    print(m.hypot(3.0, 4.0))
    print(m.fma(2.0, 3.0, 1.0))
}
```

```text
1.0
5.0
7.0
```

What the binder wrote (`jet inspect bind math --row hypot --expand`):

```jet
#ffi.Facts(Effects([]))                       // link evidence: libm imports nothing with effects
hypot: fn(x: F64, y: F64) -> F64 {
    ffi.cross("hypot")
    ffi.extern<fn(F64, F64) -> F64>("hypot", EV_MATH_H_168).call(x, y)
}
```

## Medium: zlib file compression

What it shows: lists passed as pointer and length from `counted_by` facts; a C status turned into a Jet error by
the reviewed zlib pack; owned output; text copied from a static C string.

```jet
package: {
    name: "squeeze"
    deps: { z: c@nixpkgs:zlib }
}

use z: c.zlib
use fs: core.files

squeeze: fn(path: String) -> Int !z.ZError {
    data: fs.read_bytes(path)
    packed: z.compress(data, level: 9)          // pack: compressBound + compress2, status -> ZError
    fs.write_bytes("{path}.z", packed)
    restored: z.uncompress(packed, size: data.len())
    assert(restored == data)
    packed.len()
}

run: fn() {
    print("zlib {z.version()}")                   // const char*, static: copied once
    size: squeeze("notes.txt")
    print("compressed to {size} bytes")
}
```

```text
zlib 1.3.1
compressed to 1184 bytes
```

If the zlib pack were absent, `z.compress` would still exist in its raw-but-safe shape:
`compress2(dest: &[U8], dest_len: &U64, source: [U8], level: I32) -> I32`, because zlib's header documents
lengths for both buffers through its `uLongf *destLen` and `uLong sourceLen` pairs and the binder's pairing rule
matches them. Only the error mapping and `compressBound` sizing come from the pack.

## Complex: libpng thumbnailer

What it shows: a reviewed pack giving handles with `Close`, `setjmp` error handling turned into Jet errors, a
refused row with its fix, a project overlay supplying a missing fact, and the audit.

```jet
package: {
    name: "thumbs"
    deps: { png: c@nixpkgs:libpng }        // c-png-pack is found by header hash
}

use png: c.png
use fs: core.files

#Import module c.png {
    // The project states the length fact for one row; Jet checks it at the call.
    #ffi.Facts(Count(row_pointers, num_rows))
    png_read_rows: fn(r: &Reader, row_pointers: &[[U8]], display: ?&[[U8]], num_rows: U32)
}

thumbnail: fn(path: String, out: String, scale: Int) !png.PngError {
    img: png.Image.read(path)               // pack: png_create_read_struct + png_destroy_read_struct as Close
    small := png.Image.blank(img.width / scale, img.height / scale, img.format)
    loop y in 0..<small.height {
        loop x in 0..<small.width {
            small.set(x, y, img.pixel(x * scale, y * scale))
        }
    }
    small.write(out)                          // longjmp inside libpng becomes PngError via the pack's error hook
}

stream_rows: fn(path: String) !png.PngError {
    reader: png.Reader.open(path)
    rows := [[U8]]{}
    loop i in 0..<reader.height -> rows.push([U8].zeroed(reader.row_bytes))
    png.png_read_rows(reader, rows, .None, reader.height)    // checked: rows.len() >= height
    print("read {rows.len()} rows")
}

run: fn() {
    loop f in fs.list_dir("photos") {
        if !f.ends_with(".png") -> next
        thumbnail("photos/{f}", "thumbs/{f}", 4) ?? print("skipped {f}")
    }
    stream_rows("photos/cat.png")
}
```

```text
read 480 rows
```

Without the overlay, the `png_read_rows` call would stop the build:

```text
Error [E3241]: `png_read_rows` takes pointer `row_pointers` with no known length.
  --> thumbs.jet:31:5
 Why: Jet cannot tell how many elements C will read or write through it.
 Fix: Use `reader.read_rows()` from the libpng pack, or state the length with
      #ffi.Facts(Count(row_pointers, num_rows)) in #Import module c.png.
```

The audit of this program (`jet audit foreign thumbs.jet`) lists `png_read_rows` with
`Count(row_pointers, num_rows)  source overlay thumbs.jet:8`, and every pack row with its reviewers and the header
hash it was checked against.

### Best competitor equivalent

```zig
// Zig: one line to import, then raw C everywhere; setjmp errors need a C shim.
const c = @cImport(@cInclude("png.h"));
var png_ptr = c.png_create_read_struct(c.PNG_LIBPNG_VER_STRING, null, null, null) orelse return error.Png;
defer c.png_destroy_read_struct(&png_ptr, &info_ptr, null);
c.png_read_rows(png_ptr, rows.ptr, null, height);      // no length check
```
