cards.title: FFI v3 gallery: isolation (wasm, process, hardened profile)
cards.body:
Three complete programs that move foreign libraries out of the program's memory with one `isolate:` line and no
call-site change (D-FFI-PLACE1). `.Wasm` compiles a source library to wasm and runs it inside the process with its
own linear memory. `.Process` runs a closed binary in a supervised child and batches calls through a shared-memory
ring. Jet already has the pieces: the wasm plugin host (`PluginHost.jet`) and the worker supervisor
(`WorkerSupervisor.jet`). Costs are inferences from published sandbox reports, marked as such. Outputs are design
targets.

## Simple: a C image decoder in wasm

```jet
package: {
    name: "avatars"
    deps: { stb: c@nixpkgs:stb_image }
    isolate: { stb: .Wasm }
}

use img: c.stb_image

run: fn() {
    pic: img.load("upload.png")                     // same call as in-process
    print("{pic.width}x{pic.height}")
    evil: img.load("crafted.png")                   // a heap overflow inside stb traps in its sandbox
    print(evil.width)
}
```

```text
640x480
Error [IsolateError.Trapped]: stb_image trapped: out-of-bounds memory access
  in wasm  stb_image.h:4877   stbi__parse_png_file   [placement .Wasm]
  -- crossing: c.stb_image load  (binder cbind 3.0.1, rule emit_plain) --
  in Jet   avatars.jet:10:13  run()
```

Jet memory is untouched; the sandbox is discarded and recreated on the next call. Cost: about 1.1 to 1.5 times
the native decode time inside the library [INFERENCE from RLBox reports], nothing at the call.

## Medium: a closed codec in a child process

```jet
package: {
    name: "transcode"
    deps: { codec: c@"vendor/oldcodec" }   // a local directory: library plus header
    isolate: { codec: .Process }
}

use codec: c.oldcodec
use fs: core.files

transcode: fn(path: String) -> Int !(IsolateError | codec.CodecError) {
    dec: codec.Decoder.open(path)                   // a handle living in the child; Close sends the release
    out: fs.create("{path}.raw")                 // a Close file handle
    frames := 0
    loop {
        frame: dec.next_frame() ?? break            // Bytes cross through the shared ring, no copy per frame
        out.write(frame)
        frames += 1
    }
    frames
}

run: fn() {
    print(transcode("clip.old"))
    // If the child crashes, the call fails with IsolateError.Crashed, the supervisor restarts it,
    // and handles from the dead child fail with IsolateError.Stale instead of touching freed memory.
}
```

```text
2400
```

Effects are enforced: the child runs with only the grants the codec's link evidence needs (`FS.Read` on the input
directory). A codec update that adds a `connect` import shows up as a lock diff before it can run.

## Complex: hardened profile and audit

```jet
package: {
    name: "upload_service"
    deps: {
        stb: c@nixpkgs:stb_image                  // source
        zlib: c@nixpkgs:zlib                      // source via nixpkgs
        codec: c@"vendor/oldcodec"
        exif: py@"exifread==3.0"                    // pure Python
        pillow: py@"pillow==11.0"                   // native extension
    }
    isolate: { stb: .Wasm, codec: .Process }
    profile: { release: { foreign: .Hardened } }
}

use img: c.stb_image
use z: c.zlib
use codec: c.oldcodec
use exif: py.exifread
use pil: py.PIL.Image
use fs: core.files

handle: fn(upload: Bytes) -> Bytes !(IsolateError | codec.CodecError | z.ZError) {
    tags: exif.process_bytes(upload)                       // in-process: pure Python
    pic: img.load_memory(upload)                           // .Wasm
    thumb: pil.from_rgba(pic.width, pic.height, pic.pixels).resize([128, 128])   // .Process under .Hardened
    z.compress(thumb.png_bytes(), level: 6)                  // in-process, hardened clang build
}

run: fn() {
    out: handle(fs.read_bytes("upload.jpg"))
    print(out.len())
}
```

```sh
$ jet audit foreign upload_service.jet --placement
  stb       .Wasm        source jetpack:stb_image@2.30      effects enforced: []
  zlib      in-process   source, hardened build             effects proven:   []  (link evidence)
  codec     .Process     closed binary sha256:44c1…         effects enforced: [FS.Read]
  exifread  in-process   pure Python                        effects proven:   []
  pillow    .Process     native extension, hardened profile effects enforced: [FS.Read]
  trusted in-process native code: zlib (hardened: -fbounds-safety, _FORTIFY_SOURCE=3, auto-var-init=zero, CFI)
$ jet build --profile release
  ok
```

Removing `codec: .Process` under the hardened profile fails the release build:

```text
Error [E3243]: `codec` is a closed native binary running in-process under the hardened profile.
 Fix: Add `codec: .Process` to isolate:, or grant trust with a reason, a trust_grant gate:
      trust: { codec: "vendor-audited build, ticket SEC-114" }   (D-FFI-PLACE1)
```

### Best competitor equivalent

```cpp
// Firefox RLBox: each call and each returned value is rewritten and verified by hand.
rlbox_sandbox<rlbox_wasm2c_sandbox> sandbox;
sandbox.create_sandbox();
auto tainted_w = sandbox.invoke_sandbox_function(stbi_load_from_memory, buf, len, w, h, n, 4);
int width = w.copy_and_verify([](int v) { return v > 0 && v < 65536 ? v : 0; });
// Chrome: decoders run in a utility process behind a .mojom interface and generated bindings.
```

cards.title: FFI v3 gallery: Python (statistics, numpy, pandas with matplotlib)
cards.body:
Three complete programs that call Python through `use py.<package>`. The `pybind` package (root `py`) runs the
pinned CPython with its `jetpy.describe` module to read type hints, stubs (`.pyi`), classes and exceptions, and
emits Jet types. Typed functions get Jet signatures; untyped ones get `Dyn` values that decode on use. Placement is
decided by facts (D-FFI-PLACE1): pure Python runs embedded in-process; native extensions run in-process by default
and in a child process under the hardened profile. Outputs are design targets.

## Simple: the standard library's statistics module

```jet
use stats: py.statistics                     // ships with the pinned CPython; no dependency line needed

run: fn() {
    xs: [2.0, 4.0, 4.0, 4.0, 5.0, 5.0, 7.0, 9.0]
    print(stats.mean(xs))                       // list[float] hint -> [F64]
    print(stats.pstdev(xs))
    print(stats.median(xs))
    print(stats.mean([]))                       // StatisticsError -> stats.StatisticsError
}
```

```text
5.0
2.0
4.5
Error [stats.StatisticsError]: mean requires at least one data point
  in Python  statistics.py:430   mean()
  -- crossing: py.statistics mean  (binder pybind 1.0.3, rule emit_call) --
  in Jet     main.jet:8:11  run()
```

## Medium: numpy arrays shared, not copied

What it shows: PEP 3118 buffers over Jet list memory, so numpy reads and writes Jet data in place; dtype and shape
facts from numpy's stubs; in-place operations take a writable input in the binding's signature, so the call stays plain.

```jet
package: {
    name: "signal"
    deps: { numpy: py@"numpy==2.1" }
}

use np: py.numpy

run: fn() {
    wave: loop i in 0..<1024 -> (Float.from_int(i) * 0.05).sin()
    samples := wave.copy()
    spectrum: np.fft.rfft(samples)                  // reads samples in place; returns an np.Array<Complex128> handle
    peak: np.argmax(np.abs(spectrum))
    print("peak bin {peak}")

    np.multiply(samples, 0.5, out: samples)          // writes into Jet memory through the buffer
    print(samples[20])

    m: np.Array<F64>.from(samples).reshape(32, 32)   // an owned ndarray handle
    print(m.shape)                                      // [32, 32]
    print(np.linalg.det(m.slice(0..<3, 0..<3)))
}
```

```text
peak bin 8
0.4207354924039483
[32, 32]
-0.0
```

## Complex: pandas report with matplotlib, async I/O and a placement choice

What it shows: a DataFrame as an opaque handle with typed column access; Python exceptions as Jet errors;
an `async def` turned into a wait point; a Jet callback passed to `DataFrame.apply`; the hardened profile moving
native extensions to a child process with no call-site change.

```jet
package: {
    name: "sales_report"
    deps: {
        pandas: py@"pandas==2.2"
        mpl: py@"matplotlib==3.9"
        aiohttp: py@"aiohttp==3.10"
    }
    profile: { release: { foreign: .Hardened } }       // pandas, numpy and matplotlib run in a child process
}

use pd: py.pandas
use plt: py.matplotlib.pyplot
use http: py.aiohttp

#Codable
Rate: struct {
    currency: String
    to_usd: F64
}

fetch_rates: fn() -> [Rate] !http.ClientError {
    session: http.ClientSession.new()                 // async with -> Close at scope end
    resp: session.get("https://rates.example/today")  // coroutine -> wait point
    resp.json<[Rate]>()                                 // coroutine -> wait point; decoded into Jet records
}

run: fn() {
    rates: fetch_rates()
    df: pd.read_csv("sales.csv", parse_dates: ["day"])
    df.assign_column("usd", df.apply((row) -> {          // call-scoped Jet callback
        currency: row.get_text("currency")
        rate: rates.find((r) -> r.currency == currency)?.to_usd ?? 1.0
        row.get_f64("amount") * rate
    }, axis: 1))
    monthly: df.groupby(pd.Grouper(key: "day", freq: "ME")).sum_column("usd")

    fig: plt.figure(figsize: [8.0, 4.0])
    ax: fig.add_subplot()
    ax.bar(monthly.index_text(), monthly.values_f64())
    ax.set_title("Revenue (USD)")
    fig.savefig("revenue.png", dpi: 150)
    print("months: {monthly.len()}, best: {monthly.idxmax()}")

    bad: pd.read_csv("missing.csv")                    // FileNotFoundError -> pd.FileNotFoundError
    print(bad.len())
}
```

```text
months: 12, best: 2026-07
Error [pd.FileNotFoundError]: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'missing.csv'
  in Python  pandas/io/parsers/readers.py:1026   read_csv()
  -- crossing: py.pandas read_csv  (binder pybind 1.0.3, rule emit_call, placement .Process) --
  in Jet     report.jet:46:12  run()
```

`jet audit foreign report.jet --placement` shows pandas, numpy and matplotlib in `.Process` (native extensions,
hardened profile) and aiohttp's pure-Python parts in-process.

### Best competitor equivalent

```mojo
# Mojo: Python interop through PythonObject; every value is dynamically typed, errors are raised Python exceptions.
from python import Python
def main():
    pd = Python.import_module("pandas")
    df = pd.read_csv("sales.csv")
    print(df.groupby("month")["usd"].sum())
# Julia PythonCall.jl is similar: pyimport, Py values, conversion with pyconvert.
```

cards.title: Declare Encode, Decode, Equatable and Comparable as Core traits in Jet source (D-EXTEND-ARCH1)
cards.body:
The codec and comparison traits are synthetic: Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/Calls/Methods.jet:333 lists them by name and Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Facts/Checked.jet:20 maps them. Core declares only two traits in Jet source (Compiler/Prelude/core/prelude.jet:19, Core/Math/Math.jet:3590). A package cannot add a format the way Core does.

Done when: the traits are declared in Core source; the synthetic list is gone; derives for `#Codable` and friends produce ordinary impls visible in `jet inspect expand`; a test package adds a new format codec with the same form.

Research: Docs/research/declarative-jet-2026-10-31.md (card #6513). Citations are at dev 68c87ae07b. Section 3.4.

criteria.text: Two `ID<T>` values compare with `==`/`!=` by slot and generation, as D-POOLID-API1=A says. A live id equals itself, and an id taken before `remove` differs from the id `add` returns for the reused slot. Golden at O0/O2, plus a UI snapshot proving E0312 is no longer raised for `ID<T>`. Found by the 2026-11-05 Doom port investigation (defect against a ratified rule; compiler 0ccdff27ea).

cards.title: Package diagnostics, lints and rewrite rules as values; retire hand-written marker name switches
cards.body:
The registry has 874 diagnostic rows; 80 carry a structured fix and 71 a lint name (DiagnosticRows.jet). Marker names are matched by hand in the parser (Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Items.jet:1593) and in sema (Compiler/JetSema/Source/Sema/MarkerRules.jet:918), and re-declared as strings (Compiler/JetFoundation/Data/Syntax/CoreSurface.jet:160). Packages cannot register codes.

cards.title: `ffi.binder`: declared type maps, handles, error conventions and refusals derive a binder's expand loop
cards.body:
Every binder in ffi-v3.md section 4 repeats the same loop: run a tool, map types with an if chain, refuse and stub, emit a template (ffi-v3.md:234-263). Add a Core kit that takes declared tables (`types`, `handles`, `errors`, `refuse`, `names`) and derives `expand`. Hand-written `expand` stays for complex binders.

Done when: the libm binder from ffi-v3 section 4.2 is written as tables only; a handle row derives a close and single-use; a missing type mapping is a registered refusal; `jet inspect expand` shows the derived module.

Depends on the `trait Language` card. Research: Docs/research/declarative-jet-2026-10-31.md (card #6513). Citations are at dev 68c87ae07b. Section 3.2.

cards.title: Read package.jet, project.jet and env modules through the prep evaluator into typed Core records

cards.title: Pipelines as values, and a declared restart policy on service trees

cards.title: Typed task channels: `Receiver<T>` instead of `Receiver<Int>`
cards.body:
Every channel function in Core/Tasks/Tasks.jet:17-141 is typed `Receiver<Int>`, so typed pipelines must encode values as integers or go through services.

Done when: `Receiver<T>` carries any sendable type on native, O0/O1/O2 and web; `after`, `interval`, `recv`, `waitall` and `waitany` are generic; a case sends a record through a channel at every tier.

Research: Docs/research/declarative-jet-2026-10-31.md (card #6513). Citations are at dev 68c87ae07b. Section 3.6.

log.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Q3): recommended option. interval stays Receiver<Int> tick counts (no interval<T>); waitany on an empty list is a precondition panic.

G1Lead landed 9b21994eb3: typed task channels. recv, get, result and wait return T? (None means closed and drained), and the -1 sentinel is gone. waitall returns [T?]; waitany returns (index, T?); after<T> carries any value. interval stays Receiver<Int> pending the owner (c1 question). Case task_state_tiers/typed_task_channels_carry_records_on_every_tier: PASS on O0, O1, O2 and web for a plain channel. The task parts have no web step, because tasks are not available on the web target yet. Finding, not changed: on native, closing a receiver never sets the cancelled flag, so is_cancelled is always false; the web Channel.js sets it. Also, Core in-file #Test blocks cannot run: jet test Core refuses with E1355.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (asked by Main): a generic `recv` returns `T?`; none means the channel is closed and drained. `waitall` returns `[T?]`; `waitany` returns the index plus `T?`. The -1 closed sentinel is removed, and every existing Int caller, case, example and doc migrates in one cutover on O0/O1/O2 and web. Build scope as scoped by G1Lead 03:50 (runtime after/interval value route, web Channel.js, row regeneration); no ballot needed for the return shape.

Main 2026-11-08 03:50 (G1Lead scoping): this is not a Core-only edit. channel<T> is already generic in Core, but the runtime after_value/interval routes carry exact-Int words with a fixed Int element meta (JetRuntime RouteAInterval.jet). A generic after<T>/interval needs an IR special case that passes the value slot and element meta (as ir_channel_new does), a new runtime route, the web Channel.js path, row regeneration, and cases on O0/O1/O2/web. A generic recv/waitall/waitany cannot keep the -1 closed sentinel and must return T?, which changes behaviour for existing Int callers and needs an owner ruling before the build. Several hours plus a compiler rebuild; out of the overnight pareto pass.

criteria.text: Receiver<T> carries any sendable type; after, recv, waitall and waitany are generic, and interval(period) -> Receiver<Int> delivers tick counts 1, 2, 3 (owner ruling 2026-11-08, Q3 A: a caller wanting a payload maps the tick); a case sends a record through a channel on O0, O1, O2 and web.
criteria.evidence: dev 5987d18926 (b1): tests/cases/task_state_tiers/typed_task_channels_carry_records_on_every_tier.case PASS with the b1 s1 compiler (jet test Compiler --profile cases --filter typed_task_channels: PASS 1 FAIL 0); a record crosses a typed channel on O0/O1/O2 and web

criteria.text: Generic `recv` returns `T?` (none = closed and drained), `waitall` returns `[T?]`, `waitany` returns the index plus `T?`; the -1 sentinel and every Int-only channel signature are gone, with all callers migrated in the same cutover (owner 2026-11-08).
criteria.evidence: dev 5987d18926: Core/Tasks/Tasks.jet generic recv -> T?, waitall -> [T?], waitany(receivers: [Receiver<T>]) -> (index: Int, value: T?); callers migrated in the same batch, census clean

criteria.text: waitany on an empty list stops with a precondition panic whose message says waitany needs at least one receiver (owner ruling 2026-11-08, Q3); a case proves it on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Self-compile wall regressed from the best measured 9.62 s; get it back below, then keep improving
cards.body: Owner 2026-10-31: the best measured self-compile was 9.62 s. Track major regressions and fix them through the ongoing optimization work. History, from seed rotation s2/s3 builds of the compiler at the default level on a reserved slot: a0_019 (Oct 24) 11.3/9.4 s; a0_020 (Oct 28) 10.7/11.1 s; a0_021 22.6/16.8 s; a0_022 (Oct 30) 12.9/12.4 s; wave 17 chain s2 (Oct 31) 22.8 s. Today's dev compiler (wave 17 s2), fresh tree, 24 pinned CPUs, load 35-48: O0 19.9 s wall/56.5 user-s/6.6 GB; O1 (default) 54.7 s/91.9 user-s/6.9 GB; O2 175 s/143 user-s/5.3 GB, binary 83.4 MB (O1 69.0 MB). cards.title: Core #Test blocks have no runner: tests inside Core modules never execute
cards.body: Found 2026-11-01 00:10 (GoldC-3, #6457). Core modules carry #Test blocks (for example Core/Data/Data.jet:2785), but nothing runs them. jet test Core/Data/Data.jet stops with E0067 on __-prefixed names, testkit has no core suite, core-conformance.mjs runs a corpus under tests/conformance, and core-module-check.mjs only runs jet check per module. So every Core #Test is unexecuted, and card criteria that cite them cannot be proven. Fix: one runner (a testkit core suite or jet test over Core with Core-internal names allowed) that executes every Core #Test on o0/o1/o2, gated in lane-check or the wave report, plus a census of the blocks that fail today.

log.text: Main 2026-11-08: priority raised. The ports under #6687 (TlsLead #6694, SqliteLead #6695, G1Lead #6688) need it to prove private Core parts, and 73 Core files hold #Test blocks that never run. Assigned to QuickLead after #6686. Until then, port vectors go in tests/cases.

criteria.text: One runner executes every Core #Test on O0, O1 and O2 (Core-internal names allowed), it is gated in the lane check or the release gate, and a census lists the blocks that fail today, each on a card.

A gated row runs the Core #Tests, among them the Dyn kinds #Test at Core/Encoding/Encoding.jet:384 (from #4306 c4). Today jet test Core/Encoding stops with E1355, because the root project's env.dev imports textkit, so no Core #Test can run alone (CoreCliLead-2, 11-07, dev c83db9e70f).

A gate type-checks every Core function body, reached or not. Today Tools/agent/CoreModuleCheck.jet (VerifyFull) and LaneCheck's Core path (47fbc5b2a5) use a one-import probe that checks only the bodies the module reaches. A type error injected into Core/Encoding/Encoding.jet bytes_to_hex passes both, and surfaces as a user error at <corelib>/Core/Encoding/Encoding.jet only when a program calls it (TestSystemLead-2, 11-07). Fix: a Loader mode that checks a Core-row entry whole. Proof: the injected error is red in LaneCheck and CoreModuleCheck, and HEAD is green.

jet test on a Core module runs its #Test blocks: today jet test Core/Encoding/Cbor.jet refuses every __core_* import with E0067 ReservedDunderName (found by CoreCliLead-2 at 2ce486d9bf). A Core module's own reserved imports are allowed when the module under test is Core.

A Core module that imports an unknown __core_* part gets one registered diagnostic from both jet check and jet build or run, never an ICE. TlsLead repro on dev d17bb32500 with seed a0_039: add `probe: __core_crypto_probe` to the use block of Core/Crypto/Crypto.jet; then jet check of a user program importing core.crypto says ok and exits 0, while jet run exits 101 with "the Jet compiler stopped before finishing" (I2, I3). The same use line in user code gives E0067.

cards.title: Startup cost: dynamic symbol binding, setlocale and env capture dominate short programs (hello 8.8x, taskfile 22x asm)
cards.body: asm-parity on dev 45ab3b5ef5 (perf record cycles:u, $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/asmpar-45ab/hot.sh): hello's cycles are ld.so symbol binding (do_lookup_x 24%, _dl_lookup_symbol_x 23%, _dl_check_all_versions 15%) and glibc tunables init (24%). taskfile spends 14% in check_match, 13% in _nl_intern_locale_data (a setlocale/locale load), 12% in jet_rt_host_env_capture, 12% in strcmp and 12% in record_in. Every cell pays this startup cost. Within the current dynamic-libc model (static linking is the owner ballot #5088): import only the libc symbols the program reaches, avoid eager binding of unused imports, don't load locale data the program never uses, and capture the environment lazily (#6493 is in wave 22). Proof: asm-parity hello and taskfile cycles columns drop, no cell worse in bytes or cycles, and output is identical.

log.text: Linux syscall leaf loads its arguments straight into the syscall registers (no push/pop glue): asm-parity hello 2942 -> 2681 instructions:u (-8.87%) default and release on a34ef0affd + this patch; REF-SAME 48/48; lane-check CHECK OK (jet-lane-check.z6u8Iv) Landed in wave 25 as dev 367eaf8f0d (Codegen-1-47).

jet_rt_alloc_init maps the allocator root and size-class table in one mmap (one startup syscall fewer per process) and the JET_CHECKED_ALLOC envp walk no longer spills its cursor; REF-SAME 48/48 and asm-parity bytes -8/-16 default on a34ef0affd + this patch; lane-check CHECK OK (jet-lane-check.mGwHm2) Landed in wave 25 as dev 367eaf8f0d (Codegen-1-46).

Jet-owned main indexes envp on the first environment read instead of at startup: asm-parity taskfile default 2,715,178 -> 1,394,992 instructions:u (-48.6%), release -48.9%, every runtime-linked cell -220K, on a34ef0affd + this patch; REF-SAME 48/48; lane-check CHECK OK (jet-lane-check.WJt5mR) Landed in wave 25 as dev 367eaf8f0d (Codegen-1-45).

CORRECTION (Codegen-1): the ld.so, tunables and locale rows in Main's hot.sh came from the taskset wrapper (perf record -- taskset BIN profiles taskset's own dynamic startup before exec). The asm-parity binaries are static, with no dynamic section and no libc. Real hello cost: 7,212 cycles:u / 2,642 instructions, about 1,200 of them the JET_CHECKED_ALLOC env scan that environment.md requires; the rest is syscalls and page faults (TLS, 12K stdout buffer, 256K sigaltstack, 4 sigactions, ioctl). taskfile: host_env_capture (#6493), alloc/free, stop_poll and thread_attach. The scope of this card is now those real startup costs. The long-running cells' profiles (fft, wordfreq, nbody, binparse, tensormap) are unaffected; taskset is negligible there.

criteria.text: The asm-parity hello and taskfile cycles:u and instructions columns drop against dev 45ab3b5ef5 (instructions, plus the median of at least 21 interleaved runs for cycles). No asm-parity cell is worse in bytes or cycles, and output is identical.
End metric: startup is as fast as physically possible: exec-to-exit cycles and instructions of the hello and taskfile cells match their asm-parity references within noise.

cards.title: Function-value copy: does f.copy() of an escaping closure share its captured state, give an independent copy, or get refused?
cards.body:
Question (owner/ballot): spec.md:889-905 ("Captures and escaping lambdas") says an escaping lambda owns its captures. Copy values are copied at closure creation, clonable values are cloned, and owned non-clonable values move. It never says what a *function value* does when it is copied (`alias: counter.copy()`) or bound twice.

Witness: tests/cases/run_regressions/shared_and_closure_owner_topology_is_preserved.case, fixture tests/fixtures/shared_owner_topology.jet:82-87.
  counter: make_counter(live)   // returns `(value: Int) -> { bucket.values.push(value) ... }` over a `:=` Bucket it owns
  alias: counter.copy()
  print(counter(1)); print(alias(2)); print(counter(3))
The ORACLE-LITERAL output (run_regressions.rs:174, never re-bless) is 102 / 202 / 302. bucket.values.len() grows 1, 2, 3 across counter and alias, so the alias **shares** the one captured environment, as a refcounted closure would.

Today: sema refuses with E0211 "`fn(Int) -> Int` can't be copied" (360e470044).

Alternatives:
- A: A function value is a cheap handle. `.copy()` (and implicit copy) shares the captured environment, as `Shared<T>` handles do (spec.md:1426-1431). Matches the oracle 102/202/302. Needs closure env refcounting in IR/runtime and a spec sentence.
- B: `.copy()` deep-clones the captured environment, so each copy has its own state. Requires every capture to be clonable, or E0211. The oracle would become 102/102/202 (re-blessing an ORACLE-LITERAL needs owner sign-off).
- C: Function values that own mutable captured state are not copyable (today's E0211). The spec gains that sentence, and the case's alias line is removed with owner sign-off (oracle lines 11-12 change).

Acceptance: spec.md "Captures and escaping lambdas" states the chosen rule. The fixture then runs on every tier with the decided output, and shared_and_closure_owner_topology_is_preserved passes (or is rewritten per C with a cited spec line).

Related fixture repairs already staged by CardClose-1 (CC-66 follow-up, not yet landed because this blocks the run):
- bare-block scopes become helper fns (S6-R, syntax-decisions.md:3949)
- `fn(Int) Int` becomes `fn(Int) -> Int` (spec.md:857)
- `String!` becomes `Err!` (E2417)
- untyped-lambda `return x` becomes the tail value
- SharedSnapshot `.value` becomes `.value()` (Main ruling, SharedOwner.jet:429)
- `!= .None` now type-checks (CC-66 sema fix, D-FLOWTYPE1)

cards.title: Jet web framework: full breadth and depth parity with the best frameworks, with their downsides designed out
cards.body:
## Outcome

Owner direction: Jet ships a first-class, native web framework (the Core web modules, compiled by Jet, with no JavaScript runtime or wrapped library). It has full breadth and depth parity with every element of the best frameworks, and every known downside of those elements is engineered away in the Jet design rather than inherited. The framework gets its own Jet name; no repository path or user-facing text keeps a third-party framework's name.

## Scope

Parity is judged element by element against the best framework for that element, not against one framework. The reference set covers at least: TanStack (Start, Router, Query, Form, Table, Virtual, Store, DB, devtools), Next.js, Remix / React Router, SvelteKit, SolidStart, Qwik, Astro, Nuxt, Angular, Phoenix LiveView, Rails (Hotwire), Laravel (Livewire), Django, Leptos and Dioxus, htmx and Elysia/Hono. Elements include routing and typed search params, data loading and caching, mutations and optimistic updates, forms and validation, tables and virtualization, state stores, rendering modes (SSR, SSG, ISR, streaming, islands, resumability, CSR), server functions and actions, real-time and live views, auth and sessions, i18n, images and assets, styling, testing, devtools, error boundaries, deployment and edge targets, and the dev loop.

## Method

1. A dated audit (Docs/audits) with one row per element: the best framework for it, what Jet has (by code path and executable example, not prose), the gap, and each known downside of the best implementation with the Jet design that removes it.
2. One ballot per owner choice the audit raises (new syntax, public API, product behavior), with same-program alternatives.
3. One child card per gap, each closing with an executable example and golden output on every applicable tier (I5, I9), and a performance cell where the element is performance-relevant.

## Known downsides to design out (seed list, the audit extends it)

Hydration cost and mismatch bugs; client bundle growth; waterfalls between nested loaders; cache invalidation by hand; stringly-typed routes and search params; server/client boundary leaks of secrets; framework lock-in to one host; slow dev rebuilds; runtime-only type errors in forms and APIs; opaque magic in file conventions; duplicated validation between client and server.

## Current state

Examples/features/web/tanstack_start/run.jet is a reference app over the Core web modules (router, query, forms, table, virtual, store). Its web build is being repaired under #5990 c13. It is evidence of coverage breadth only; depth parity is unaudited.

cards.title: Native code faults (SIGSEGV at 0x0) seeking a handle bound by '&executables[i].file == .Val(input)' in store_reuse_executable_lease_members
cards.body: Repro (Linux, admitted compiler 657d0c5553 and HEAD 83c4c6521b runtime alike): assemble the Engine unit (JETPACK_BOOTSTRAP_AREAS=$(node Jetpack/Bootstrap/areas.mjs closure Engine) JETPACK_BOOTSTRAP_OWN_AREA=Engine node Jetpack/Bootstrap/assemble.mjs aot), then in its project run: jet test src/jetpack.jet "realize verified round trips". The claim 'store broker realize verified round trips through broker and fails closed on auth' (Jetpack/Store/Tests/Broker.jet) FAILs with Fault [SIGSEGV] invalid memory access at address 0x0; backtrace compiler_fs_error <- store_reuse_executable_lease_members (Jetpack/Store/Source, line '&input.seek(0)' after 'if &executables[index].file == .Val(input)') <- store_reuse_build_lease <- store_snapshot_lease_unlocked <- store_snapshot_lease <- store_realize_verified. Safe code must never fault (I1): either the borrowed-pattern binding of an Option field through an indexed borrow lowers a null handle, or the File handle in SnapshotFile is dropped early. The claim is not listed in Tools/testkit/known-failing.tsv. Found by Main while proving #6426.

log.text: QuickLead receipt, 2026-11-08 (seed a0_038, source dev 759775d626): the Engine-unit claim passes on every tier. Steps: Jetpack/Bootstrap/Assemble.jet areas closure Engine; Assemble.jet aot (560 sources, 559 claims, no E1271); then jet test --optimize=none,basic,full src/jetpack.jet "realize verified round trips" gives 1 passed, 0 failed at each of none, basic and full. The minimal repro is the b75e525782 case borrowed_list_of_optional_handles. Main reruns this exact proof before meeting c1.

b75e525782 repro half: cases --filter borrowed_list_of_optional_handles PASS 1/1 (seed-built d405d4cb6c + 8405a508b0). The Engine-unit claim (store broker realize verified round trips) still waits on a locked jetpack source (E1271).

a0_034: minimal repro of the faulting pattern (a [SnapshotFile] with FileReader? handles passed by value to a loop, then twice through '&executables[i].file == .Val(input)' seek+read) prints names 3 / bytes 12 / again 12 on O0, O1 and O2: no fault, handles stay open. The Engine-unit claim still needs its jetpack env run.

Likely root: #6677. The faulting statement compares '&executables[index].file == .Val(input)': it widens the borrowed FileReader into an Option union, and before 060bbcd0f1 and 8ac163916e the widened value was moved and dropped, which closes the caller's handle (the 'corrupt after' bisect). Re-run the claim with a0_034, the first seed carrying both fixes, before any other work on this card.
Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match I9 tiers O0, O1, O2 and web (D-EXEC1, D-EXEC2=A: no interpreter or JIT).

Bisect (assembled Engine unit, s1 of 60324f013d, scratch edits to the assembled copy only): the SnapshotFile FileReader is valid (stat ok) before store_reuse_create_exec_wrappers and corrupt after it; the corrupt handle sends seek/stat into compiler_fs_error, which faults at 0x0. The general FS error path works in the same unit (open of a missing path reports NotFound). A probe placed right after 'ready :: store_reuse_keeper_line(&child)' faults, a probe after the spawn hides the fault, and probes at every step hide it (claim passes). --checked-alloc also hides it (passes). So the damage happens in or around the first keeper_line call (loop line in child.stdout.lines() -> return line: early return out of a shared process-lines iterator, IterSources.jet iter_source_node shared clone/release) and is heap-layout dependent. A standalone repro of that pattern (spawn sh, keeper_line twice, stat a FileReader between) runs clean on jet run. Next: build that standalone with --checked-alloc and run to main return (sweep catches write-after-free), then shrink inside keeper_line. Parked for the owner's marker work.

criteria.text: The Engine-unit claim 'store broker realize verified round trips through broker and fails closed on auth' passes under jet test on the assembled Engine unit (O0, O1 and O2 tiers), and a minimal tests/cases repro of the faulting pattern passes on O0/O1/O2.

cards.title: Types contain their impls: jet check --style flags a detached impl and jet fix --style moves it into the type body
cards.body:
Owner direction: across all Jet code (Core libraries, the compiler, Jetpack, examples, tests and tools), a struct or enum contains its own impls. A separate top-level impl is allowed only when it has to be somewhere else. Struct and enum bodies already accept methods and nested `impl Trait { … }` blocks (Compiler/JetParser/Source/Parser/Items.jet:1947-1952 and :2035-2042), so this needs no new syntax.

Census at dev 2d8aea4762: 1,335 top-level impls sit in the same file as their own struct or enum, in 580 files. By tree: Compiler 282, Core 368, tests 436, Examples 179, Jetpack 42, Tools 27, Docs 1.

Allowed exceptions (each must be named by the lint's own rule, not by an allow list): the type is declared in another file, module or package; an error conversion `impl A -> B`; a protocol side `impl X.Client` or `impl X.Server`; a target-specific impl; an impl a derive or generated source writes; an impl the type body cannot hold (for example `impl T.Trait using field` until the nested form accepts `using`).

Flag: `--style` turns on opt-in style checks on `jet check` and applies their fixes on `jet fix`. Impl placement is the first member. The marker cutover on #6039 already writes markers in the nested form.
cards.plan: 1. Parity: nested impl blocks accept everything a top-level impl does that a type body can hold (assoc types, constants, operator right-hand types, #Commutative, and `using` delegation if feasible). 2. Lint: a registered lint code with what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot. It is off by default and on under `jet check --style`, and it flags an `impl T` or `impl T.Trait` in the same file as `struct T` or `enum T` outside its body, unless an exception rule applies. 3. Fix: `jet fix --style` moves each flagged impl into the type body. Inherent methods become `fn` members and trait impls become nested `impl Trait { … }`, keeping comments and order. Re-check after the move, and skip it with a reason if checking fails. 4. Formatter keeps nested impls in place. 5. Sweep the whole tree with `jet fix --style` in collect-all mode, one commit per top-level tree. 6. One line of style guidance in Docs/spec/contributing/agent-engineering.md.

log.text: Deconfliction 2026-11-06: reworded to match D-DECL-COLON1=A (`name: value`, no `::`).

Main 2026-11-04: C4 retargeted as criterion 6 (jet check DIR checks only the entry, not every file). Prep finding: nested impl Trait {} blocks do not receive the trait's default methods (E0102) while the top-level form does (probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/prep/nested_parity.jet); the parity step must fix it before any sweep. The lint skips impl heads that already carry an error (E0321, E0003, E0908) as a named rule of the lint; this is covered by the card's own exception rule, so no ballot is needed.

criteria.text: A registered lint, off by default and on under `jet check --style`, flags every top-level `impl T` or `impl T.Trait` in the same file as `struct T` or `enum T` unless a named exception rule applies. It has what/why/fix text and a UI snapshot.

`jet fix --style` moves each flagged impl into its type body (inherent methods as `fn` members, trait impls as nested `impl Trait { … }`), keeping comments. The moved file checks, formats unchanged and runs the same, proven by a fixture test with a golden.
Nested impl blocks accept every member a top-level impl accepts that a type body can hold, or the lint's exception rule names the missing one.

cards.title: Every closed card is durable: no work lives only on the scratch disk
cards.body: On 2026-11-04 Main's $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT cleanup deleted lane work that open cards still cited (for example #6442's held patches). A closed card or met criterion is a promise that its change is on dev or master. Evidence that names only a scratch path, ~/.cache, /tmp or a commit outside dev/master/rust breaks that promise, and card merges carry such evidence forward unchecked. Owner order: durable work lives in the repo, and only throwaway output stays on disk.
cards.plan: 1) Audit every done card and met criterion, live and archived (audit-closures.mjs): DURABLE, SHA-NOT-IN-BRANCHES, SCRATCH-ONLY, NO-COMMIT. 2) Re-verify each non-durable code closure against dev content, and reopen any whose change is absent, with the reason. 3) Move durable out-of-repo work into the repo: unlanded patches under Tools/tower/held/<card>/ (base commit, state, next step), research and proposals into Docs/research and Docs/proposals, ballot drafts into Tower. 4) Tower refuses card close and criterion meet unless the evidence names a commit reachable from dev or master; scratch-only evidence is rejected. 5) Commit the board to master regularly.

cards.title: Pipe syntax: steps read top to bottom with the value written as it (D-PIPE1)
cards.body: The owner asked for pipes to be researched and proposed (2026-11-04), knowing they duplicate a named value used once. The study (Docs/research/2026-11-04-pipes.md) finds about 950 repo sites where steps are functions rather than methods, so dots cannot fix them. The ballot D-PIPE1 chooses the spelling. Nothing is built before it is ratified.

log.text: Regression from 8405a508b0: a value table over an &place subject lost its write window, because sema_expression_window_source only knew __jet_switch_subject_N names. Jetpack CacheLease.jet:470 gave FieldWriteWithoutMarker (it reproduces on the 8405 compiler with the extended case). Fixed in 15b9773dee: the generated it (AST_NODE_GENERATED) is a window source; a written it never is. Proof with the census-built compiler: case switch_on_listed_optional_reader_closes_it_once (extended: the payload passes on through a &FileReader parameter) PASS; core_files_opaque_handles 9 PASS, 1 known-failing; golden Basics/ValueDispatch 3/3; hosted Jetpack check OK.
Owner deconfliction 2026-11-06: respelled for D-DECL-COLON1=A.

criteria.text: Precondition, a wrong-meaning bug found by the pipes study: inside a bindingless loop body, a subject table over a computed value (if .age * 2 == { … }) must give its arms its own subject as it, not the loop item. Fixed with a golden on o0, o1 and o2 before any pipe work starts.
criteria.evidence: dev 8405a508b0 (Main). A value table over a subject that is not a plain name or a place now binds that subject to it in a frame of its own: a generated grouping from parser_expression_form_parse_dispatch_table, hoisted by sema even with one arm. Its binding is pushed into that frame (as the statement form's is), so a nested table's it shadows the enclosing one. A bindingless loop body's table therefore reads its own subject, not the loop item. Examples/Basics/ValueDispatch.jet has the loop case (loop people -> if .age /% 10 == { 3 -> "in the 30s" ... }) and a top-level age_band. Its golden matches on O0, O1 and O2 with a compiler the seed built from the patch (jet run --optimize=none|basic|full, cmp against ValueDispatch.out). Precommit census of the landed tree: check, build and runtime pack OK, compiler self-check rc=0 rows=0. The first attempt's 7 self-check rows (nested tables reading the outer it) are fixed by the frame-scoped binding. Nested probe $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/it/nest.jet prints b1 s1 / b7 inner err 7 / outer err -1 on O0 and O2.

criteria.text: After D-PIPE1 is ratified: the ratified spelling is registered in the syntax registry, parses, and lowers each stage to a hidden name: value binding before type checking. A paired IR test proves the pipe and the hand-named form give identical IR at O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Comments: the comment sigil ballot and the comment defects found by its study
cards.body: Owner question 2026-11-04: should comments move from // to ##? The study recommends keeping //, with a typed warning for Python 7 // 2 (ballot D-COMMENT-SIGIL1). cards.title: Leak freedom is structural: safe Jet cannot leak
cards.body: Owner rule, 2026-11-05: Jet never leaks memory. Leak freedom is part of the memory-safety guarantee (I1); only an expert #Unsafe block may leak, so the language must structurally prevent leaks rather than fix them case by case. On 2026-11-05 three lowering families leaked in safe code (c8a 5037b3ce72: a reassign after a move; c8b 2d712dd94a: a field read off a fresh call result; c8c: a loop over or an index into a fresh List or Map), found only because jet repl grew 6.2 GB over 9 turns. This card makes such a defect impossible to ship: the compiler checks its own output, and the suites fail any program that leaks.
cards.plan: 1. An ownership verifier pass after IR lowering. 2. A leak gate in the golden and cases suites, plus the compiler itself, using the checked allocator. 3. Fix every leak the two find, by lowering family. 4. An audit of every construct that could leak in safe code (shared values and cycles, tasks parked at exit, channels, globals, closures) with a structural rule for each, or an owner ballot where the rule is a language choice. 5. I1 in AGENTS.md states leak freedom.

log.text: Golden leak-gate census, 2026-11-05 on dev 02602250cc (s1 with the checked allocator; runtime process roots tagged; under --checked-alloc the runtime runs the entry's drops instead of the exit shortcut): about 1170 of the golden programs leak (o0 1164, o1 1162, o2 1161 rows; about 100 more rows leak on only some tiers). On o0, 610 rows leak only runtime init roots (jet_rt_*_init, TLS keys), so the runtime frees or tags those at shutdown; 507 have real library or user leaks. Leak-gate rows: 3492 of 4715. Starting point for c2 and c3 when G19 is worked.

c3 progress (invariant fixes), f2ba7d34bf: the fresh-temporary-never-dropped family. loop x in make(), make()[i], make_map()[k], every non-mutating Map/Set builtin on a fresh receiver, and Set.from(make()) (buffer) now end the temporary. Before: 100-520 MB VmRSS per 40,000 rounds per shape on O0 and O2. Three new cases FAIL->PASS, one guard case PASS on both; every shape clean under --checked-alloc on O0 and O2; chain FIXED_POINT; golden A/B 267 = 267; cases A/B over 284 ids. Probe audit of the flat shapes (match, if pattern, struct method, String chains, ?. and ??, slices, tuple fields) is in the guard case.

criteria.text: After IR lowering, a verifier checks that every owned value, temporaries included, is dropped or moved exactly once on every path out of its scope, outside #Unsafe. It runs on every compile at O0, O1 and O2; a violation is an internal compiler error (exit 101), never a user diagnostic. A negative-control case shows it catching each of the 2026-11-05 leak shapes when the matching fix is reverted.

The golden and cases suites run their programs with the checked allocator and fail any row whose program exits with a live owned block allocated outside #Unsafe, at o0, o1 and o2. The compiler itself passes the same check: jet check and jet build over Core and over the compiler's own sources end with zero leaked blocks, and 9 jet repl turns of repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins stay flat.
Every leak the verifier or the leak gate finds is fixed at its root, per lowering family, each with a case per shape; the full suites then run with the leak gate on and show zero leak rows.

An audit, committed under Docs/audits, lists every construct that can keep memory alive in safe Jet (shared values and reference cycles, tasks or generators parked at exit, channels, globals and caches, closures and captures) and states the structural rule that prevents a leak for each, with a case; any rule that is a language choice goes to an owner ballot.
AGENTS.md I1 states that safe Jet cannot leak memory (only #Unsafe may), and Docs/spec/philosophy.md's memory-safety guarantee says the same.
criteria.evidence: 520bfbfa0f: AGENTS.md I1 says memory safety includes leak freedom: safe Jet cannot leak memory, and only code inside an #Unsafe block or function may. Docs/spec/philosophy.md design priority 1 says safe Jet cannot leak memory: every value it allocates is freed, and only #Unsafe code may leak.

criteria.text: (moved from #6035 c8) Root found by Prep 2026-11-04 for c7 (report $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/briefs/6035-c7-perf.md; measured at 5 jobs: ui 256 s, golden 678 s, cases OOM at 16G and 856 s for its last 826 entries at a 19.7 GiB peak). R1: jet repl keeps every turn's compile in memory (Repl.jet:338-348): 773 MiB at 1 turn grows to 5.6 GiB at 9, and suite repl cases reach 4.7-8.3 GB. Per-turn memory stays flat: 9 turns of repl_core_data_query_plans_and_typed_joins under 1 GiB, with a test. (Also #6543.)

A runtime leak and double-drop witness proves leak freedom per program: today JET_MEMORY_LEDGER records only unsafe sentry events (not leaks or double drops), and the counting allocator cap does not trip on String allocations (a 32 MB copy ran under a 48 MB cap; found by CoreCliLead-2 on #6677). A safe-Jet program run under the witness reports live allocations at exit = 0 and any double drop as a failure, on O0, O1 and O2.

cards.title: Close rate: one source of truth per fact, structural checks, criteria sized to close
cards.body: Owner 2026-11-05: cards take too long to close; a well-designed codebase should take a change in one place. Measured on 2026-11-05: a compiler rebuild to fixed point takes about 5 minutes (147 s s1 + 132 s), and a lander batch averages 129 s over 111 batches, so build and landing are not the bottleneck. The causes are copies of one fact that drift (a diagnostic lives in the Prelude row, the generated DiagnosticRows, the coverage baseline, the snapshot, the explain page and spec prose: retiring two codes touched 10 files, and ui --coverage found 137 drift errors), checks that are found serially instead of structurally (three leak families found one at a time; 1170 leaking golden programs), unported Rust behavior that is porting work rather than edits (82 KF-UNPORTED ui rows over about 60 codes, 23 more Rust-only codes, 294 open G15 criteria), and criteria merged from old cards that each hold a whole feature.

cards.title: Remove interpreter residue: jet run and comptime are native O0 in memory (D-EXEC2=A, I9)
cards.body: Owner reminder 2026-11-05: jet run, jet dev and compile-time code run natively at O0 from memory, like a JIT, never through an interpreter. That is built: JetBackend Image/Loader.jet maps the linked image through a memfd; JetCli Host.jet:1431 runs it in place of jet (single-threaded) or in a child; JetEval IR/Native.jet runs comptime batches in a compiler child; Pipeline.jet:1600/1619 calls jet_eval_native_load/run. Residue to remove in one cutover: (1) Pipeline.jet:951,1646-1662 diagnostics say 'comptime interpreter'; (2) ComptimeIR.jet:104 TTargetApplicability field 'interpreter'; (3) InspectGates.jet:64 still classifies a '--interpret' session flag; (4) Host.jet:353 and EffectsSurface.jet:630 comments; (5) Host.jet:1433-1434 writes the image to a file when it can't run from memory, which D-EXEC2=A forbids: make it an ICE (exit 101) or a report, never a written executable.

criteria.text: No compiler source, diagnostic text, registry field or CLI flag names an interpreter for jet run, jet dev or compile-time code (Pipeline.jet comptime messages, ComptimeIR TTargetApplicability.interpreter, InspectGates --interpret); UI snapshots updated in the same commit.
criteria.evidence: dev 3b17b1be65 + c788d573db: the debug tier wire value is jet-dev-replay, E2202 (jet dev step budget) retired, comptime/ComptimeIR/InspectGates interpreter names removed, CoreCallRecord.interpreter_route deleted, DiagnosticStage.Interp gone from the generated CoreEnumRows; the core enum generator --check now verifies each exported enum against its source enum declaration (fails naming DiagnosticStage with Interp restored); full chain FIXED_POINT, LaneCheck CHECK OK (SemaParity)

criteria.text: jet run never writes an executable: when the image can't run from memory (Host.jet:1433), the run reports a registered diagnostic or an exit-101 internal error instead of writing the file; a case proves it.
criteria.evidence: Owner ruling D-EXEC-NOEXEC1 (c): when the system forbids runnable memory, jet run writes the same code to a file and runs it, same output and real signal. The Host.jet:1433 file fallback is the ruled behavior, not residue.

cards.title: Soundness: a struct holding a clone:false handle (WsConn) copies implicitly and double-drops (SIGSEGV)
cards.body: Found by BallotLead on dev 070ba19ad7 while porting core.web.browser. A struct whose field is a non-cloneable handle (clone: false, e.g. WsConn) is copied implicitly instead of moved or rejected, so both copies drop the handle and the program segfaults. Browser works around it with Shared<__BrowserWire>. Fix in sema: a type that holds a clone:false field is itself non-copyable, so an implicit copy is a move or a registered diagnostic. Add a case that segfaults today, then remove the Shared workaround.

criteria.text: A value holding a WsConn is non-copyable: an implicit copy is a move, and copying it from a read param or self is a registered diagnostic with a UI snapshot (tests/ui/ws_conn_holder_is_not_copied). Golden tests/run/Net/WsConnHolderMovesItsSocket passes on O0, O1 and O2, and core.web.browser no longer has Shared<__BrowserWire>.
criteria.evidence: 34290833a9 release candidate kit (chain s2 613ff4f17287d935): tests/ui/ws_conn_holder_is_not_copied.jet PASS. This row is the proof the precut audit named for this criterion.

criteria.text: One rule for every clone:false handle, not a WsConn special case: every type holding a clone:false field is non-copyable in sema, with the WsConn-specific check removed. Receiver is classified by its real semantics: if its copies soundly share one reference-counted queue, it is not clone:false and its registration says so; otherwise Core/Tasks moves it instead of copying. The Core runtime pack builds, and every clone:false holder in Core either moves or is rejected.

cards.title: Moving a handle field out of an aggregate (^x.f) does not transfer ownership
cards.body: Reported by JetpackStore. Expressions like close(^outer.owner), ^verified.lease.release() and lease: ^parts.lease consume a field. The consumer's drop is a no-op, and the fd or flock closes only when the source aggregate drops. Repro: struct Outer{owner: Holder{lock: FileLock}}; close(^outer.owner) leaves the fd open until outer's scope ends. Closing the whole value works. Hits Jetpack Store leases (LeaseSnapshot.jet:243: the owner lock dies with prepared). Related: #6581 (a clone:false handle in a struct double-drops). Fix: a partial move transfers drop responsibility to the consumer, and the source aggregate skips that field's drop on every tier.

cards.title: A BuildError from an implicit-contract fn build loses its identity and reports E3502
cards.body: Found by JetpackEngine on dev 7de2280131. A BuildError returned from an implicit-contract fn build reports 'fn build returns nothing' (E3502) instead of the typed build error. JetIR BuildTypes.jet .Typed conversion calls the Prelude impl BuildError -> Err { Err("{self}") }, dropping typed_identity and details, so jet_eval_build_failed_diagnostic (BuildServices.jet) returns None. Three non-known-failing cases fail on base because of it: criterion9_programmable_build_cli_human_and_json_reports_match, ..._implicit_failure_preserves_build_error_identity, ..._error_union_widens_build_error_without_losing_identity. Fix at the conversion so the typed identity survives on every tier.

criteria.text: A BuildError from an implicit-contract fn build reports its typed identity and details, proven by the three criterion9 build_entry cases
criteria.evidence: dev d6c1a293bc (JetpackEngine): the IR .Typed conversion takes the BuildError's own Err record via BuildError.into_err and the evaluator writes it as a native JetErr (the inverse of jet_eval_ir_err_data), so typed_identity and details survive. On s1 of HEAD+patch, cases build_entry/criterion9_programmable_build* pass 6/6, including cli_human_and_json_reports_match, implicit_failure_preserves_build_error_identity and error_union_widens_build_error_without_losing_identity (all FAIL on base). Other build_entry/package_outputs/comptime rows match base; known-failing row duplicate_generated_modules_fail_before_any_file_is_written now passes and is removed.

cards.title: Compiler segfaults in codegen on &opt_handle == .Val(x)
cards.body: Found by JetpackEngine on dev 12da3c76b5: compiling a comparison of a borrowed optional handle against .Val(x) (&opt_handle == .Val(x)) crashes the compiler with SIGSEGV in codegen. Two #3590 c190 known-failing Store rows hit it. I2: checked code the backend cannot lower must be an internal compiler error (exit 101), never a crash, and this shape should lower. criteria.text: A switch on a borrowed optional no-clone handle in a list element closes it exactly once and exits, proven by a case on O0/O1/O2 (an I1 safety fix: no double close on freed state)
criteria.evidence: dev 137704d910 (GoldenRoots3): root cause was a double close. Sema hoisted the switch subject into a generated Let that moved the no-clone handle out of its List element, and ir_bind_pin's box alias also armed a close, so the second close locked freed FD state and hung in a futex (no signal, one thread). Fix: a hoisted generated Let over a place whose value has a drop and no clone reads the place in place, and an ir_bind_pin box alias never arms a close. cards.title: A child's stdout line reaches the parent only after the child exits
cards.body: Found by CoreOwnership on dev d1e6c214e1: in golden foundations/storage, crash_recovery waits for a child to print 'ready' while it keeps running, but the parent receives the line only after the child exits, so the program panics. Streaming a running child's stdout must deliver each line as it is written (no buffering until exit), on O0/O1/O2. Add a case where the parent reads 'ready' from a child that then waits for the parent.

log.text: Restated (CoreOwnership, Main): the runtime follows ratified D-STDOUT-BUFFER1=A (spec.md:321-325: pipe stdout is written when its buffer fills, or before a stderr write, stdin read, child start or stop; Host.jet host_stdout_write). The foundations/storage child printed 'ready' into a pipe and slept without flushing, so the example is wrong, not the runtime. Fix: the example flushes stdout after 'ready', plus a case where the child prints ready, flushes and waits, and the parent streams the line on O0/O1/O2. Line-buffered pipes would need an owner re-ballot of D-STDOUT-BUFFER1.

criteria.text: Under D-STDOUT-BUFFER1=A, the foundations/storage example flushes its ready line and passes on O0/O1/O2, and a case proves a flushed child line reaches the parent while the child waits
criteria.evidence: dev bd4d5bb844 (CoreOwnership): the storage crash writer flushes its ready line; golden foundations/storage added, o0/o1/o2 PASS; new case process_sessions/flushed_child_line_reaches_the_parent_while_the_child_waits PASS on O0/O1/O2 and the built binary.

cards.title: First jet cc pack install hashes the 450 MB tree about four times with pure-Jet SHA-256
cards.body: Found by Builder5 on dev b44941163a: the first jet cc toolchain pack install takes about 290 s, about 90% of it in the Store hashing the 450 MB unpacked tree about four times with core_crypto_sha256 (pkg_try_output_hash_of, store_record_realized_mode, publish_object, seal). Hash each tree once and reuse the digest across those steps, and bring core_crypto_sha256 throughput to the machine ceiling (SHA-NI where available) per the performance gate.

log.text: Main 2026-11-08 06:00: phase 2 landed as a08ffb93e2 (G1Lead). Core sha256 runs blocks through the runtime __sha256_blocks (SHA-NI where the CPU has it) in a private module. Receipt: release build, on a host with sha_ni, best of 3, 64 x sha256 over 1 MiB takes 0.38 s against 1.43 s on dev (3.8x). A differential of 302 inputs (lengths 0..299, 4109, 1048583) against node crypto shows 0 mismatches on none and release. Golden Crypto/ 39 PASS, Jetc 3 PASS, cases crypto 43 PASS (1 known-failing E2702, 1 SKIP-HOST), argon2id 2 PASS; 12 ratchets --check pass on a0_037. With phase 1 (591744cc94 hash-once, 3058b17fff SHA-NI) that completes the build. c1 still needs the timing: a first `jet cc` pack install under 60 s on the reference machine, measured on a quiet machine with the next seed (it must contain a08ffb93e2; a0_037 does not).

Main 2026-11-08 03:45: c1 progress by G1Lead. The hash-once half landed in 591744cc94. SHA-NI phase 1 landed in 3058b17fff: x64 SSE/SHA template forms (12 SDM encodings plus 3 rejections, tested), the leaf os_sha256_block_i64 behind cpuid with the scalar fallback kept, jet_crypto_sha256_blocks, and the core.crypto.__sha256_blocks row. Phase 2 (the Core sha2_256 and JETC2 stream through sha256_blocks) waits for a seed built from 3058b17fff or later, since the seed resolves Core dunders from its compiled-in rows. Lane rows with phase 2: SHA-256 of 16 MiB 435 ms -> 43-52 ms (about 9.4x); 302/302 differential rows against node sha256/sha224 at O0/O1/O2; crypto cases 43 PASS, 0 FAIL; jetc 5/5.

Main 2026-11-07: g13 landed as 591744cc94 (a cold fetch-toolchain hashes once; 20.6 s cold on the home NVMe, 1131 s before) and b1f1abe895 (the shared-CAS pass reseals a tree left writable). The Jetpack Engine+Environment aot jet test (seed a0_034): baseline eaa085b237 and fixed tree have the same 13 FAIL rows (empty diff), none from #6592: 2 lease recovery (recover_stale_leases and store_recover_hangar give 0, expected 1); 1 clean-plan quarantine (closure record has no dependency references); native runtime split (the test expects Rust `fn main()`, the generator emits `main: fn()`); 8 recipe sandbox rows (E1238 instead of E1236/E1237/E1275: the sandbox cannot start inside the test systemd scope); shared_hostile_corpus (Assemble does not copy tests/fixtures/build_sandbox/hostile-corpus.tsv). None is in the a0_034 full-profile run. Logs: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/PortsLead/g13/tests-base.log and tests-fix.log.

PortsLead-2 AFTER numbers, g13 batch (link CAS, parallel fsync pool, hashing on worker tasks, one tree pass with a memo), not yet landed. Cold `jetpack env fetch-toolchain --json` from an empty HOME and state: 20.6 s wall on the home NVMe; 43.4 s on the contended scratch NVMe, and 96.6 s on a rerun at load 10, where the fsync writeback of 442 MB dominates. BEFORE was 1131.1 s. Tree hash unchanged: sha256-700385c9c906 (5931 files, 442377517 B); CAS 4019 entries, linked. Scratch split: verify 2.2 s, untar 7.1 s, seal 1.2 s, parallel hash 16.6 s, publish fsync 24.1 s, hangar 0.6 s. core.crypto SHA-256 runs at 45-50 MB/s at O1/O2, about 10x slower than a scalar native implementation (~500 MB/s) and 40x slower than SHA-NI; that work is on #6681.

PortsLead-2 measured a cold fetch-toolchain before the fix at 135.6 s on its own s1. The c65 fresh run spent about 45 minutes in the same phase (17:10-17:55) under heavy machine load. The gap is unexplained: the per-file sync alone may not account for the 45 minutes.

Root cause of the 45-minute cold fetch-toolchain (c65 run 4df47ce6da, 17:10-17:55; PortsLead-2): AdmissionTransaction.publish_object → store_fsync_tree fsyncs every file and directory of the pack, about 1,900 journal commits at about 1.4 s each. Fix: write everything, one filesystem flush, then the publish rename. That needs a public Core function, because a Core  seam is reserved outside Core (Spellings.jet:13, Sema/Calls/Core.jet:514); ballot D-FS-SYNC1 (A: files.sync_filesystem, B: parallel fsync_tree, C: no API). Internal commit A (runtime syncfs export plus seam rows, no public surface) lands meanwhile; commit B (public function, store change, conformance case) waits on the ballot and the next seed.

criteria.text: The first `jet cc` pack install hashes each tree once and reuses the digest, and core_crypto_sha256 uses SHA-NI where available; the install takes under 60 s on the reference machine.

D-FS-SYNC1 = A is built: core.files.sync_filesystem(path) IOError! -[FS.Write]> (syncfs on Linux, sync where no per-filesystem flush exists, IOError where neither does) with a conformance case, and the store publishes with one sync_filesystem before the publish rename.

cards.title: JSON event reader drains a document about 10x slower than parse
cards.body: Measured by GoldenRoots3 on dev aeeb2c479c (golden serde/json_selective, 1.05 MB document, --release): draining every event from the JSON reader takes 1.37 s against 80-123 ms for parse, and decode<Small> builds the whole Dyn tree before projecting (129 ms, 84 MB peak vs 67 MB for parse). Bring the event path to at least parse speed, let typed projection skip unselected fields without materializing them, and add a paired cell with a ceiling reference per the performance gate.

log.text: Main 2026-11-08 03:35: reader speed slice by G1Lead, landing now. On the 1.09 MB 20-field doc (CPU time), the reader drains in 51 ms against 52-72 ms for parse; it started at 1110 ms. Per kind, reader vs parse: ints 24/36 ms, strings 30/40, objects 88/94. Remaining plan, set aside for cheaper G3 criteria per the pareto order: (a) typed projection, about 2-3 h. A compiler-private intrinsic encoding.__decode_keys<T>() gives the generated Decode its demanded wire keys, wired through CoreSignatures, CoreCallRows, the Sema backing gate and JetIR lowering. __decode_typed then skips the other root fields with a validating, non-materializing skip. (b) the paired performance cell. A gauntlet entry (e.g. formats.json-kernel) with a fixture, expected.out, and peers in rust, c, zig, go, python and node, plus a hand-written Tools/perf/asm-parity ref.S ceiling, about several hours.

criteria.text: Draining every event from the JSON reader is at least as fast as parse on the 1.05 MB serde/json_selective document, typed projection skips unselected fields without building a Dyn tree, and a paired perf cell with a ceiling reference records it.

cards.body: Found by GoldenRoots3 on dev 41ad578550 and present on the base too: linking the program built by run-process-witnesses.mjs fails with an undefined reference to jet_rt_fault_report. Every runtime symbol a generated program calls must come from the one shared runtime (I9). log.text: Owner 2026-11-06: script porting, the pairing bars and full removal of non-Jet languages are G4 work (#5072), not G1/G2; c5 keeps its original goal.

c3 and c4 added from TestRot's #6595/#6609 findings (no new card): runtime import ledger drift and 6 s5 witness-loop rot rows.

Finding (Builder5): with the process-wide atexit queue built, main-run worker-fatal still loses every handler. A worker's fatal stop runs in stop domain 2, and Trap.jet trap_exit routes only domain 1 through the root. Every other domain takes trap_defect_exit, a raw exit_group with no main_exit_claim, no cleanup and the report written straight to fd 2. This looks like a regression since 114e150cba. Ruling (Main): a fatal stop in any domain under a live jet_rt_main claims the process exit (single winner), runs main_exit_cleanup, then writes the captured report. Report text and exit code 70 are unchanged; a stop during cleanup aborts; hosts with no live jet_rt_main keep the defect exit. The golden is re-recorded to all four handlers in registration order, then the report, once the fixture's registration order is deterministic. Builder5 owns Trap.jet and Scheduler.jet for this fix.

Ruling (Main) on run-main-fixtures worker-fatal: make the os.atexit queue process-wide. Today it is per-thread TLS (Task.jet task_exit_queue), and main_exit_cleanup drains only the main thread's queue, so a worker's handlers are dropped. core-library.md:1875,2073-2079 and spec.md:1069-1077 define atexit as a process-boundary registration run in registration order, so that's a runtime defect. Same change: core-library-native-contract.md:573-575's thread-exit drop is rewritten; the scheduler fixture asserts survival; a new case covers a handler from a worker that exits normally; the lock covers only append and claim. The LIFO goldens (exit2exit1) are re-recorded as exit1exit2 to match spec registration order.

cards.title: Witness harnesses that count frees through --wrap=jet_rt_free never see runtime frees
cards.body: Found by GoldenRoots3 on dev e8bf2c763d: the runtime object binds its internal calls section-relative (objdump shows R_X86_64_PC32 .text-4), so -Wl,--wrap=jet_rt_free never intercepts frees made inside the runtime. About 50 *Witness.c harnesses count frees that way, so their leak and double-free assertions prove nothing; TerminalProcessWitness fails its free-count assert because of it. Give the witnesses a counting route that sees every runtime free (for example a runtime test hook or symbol-relative calls in the test build), keep one mechanism, prove it with a negative control that leaks one buffer and fails, and rerun every witness.

cards.body: Found by CoreOwnership on dev 668a296d5c (#4717 c8, goldens ui/battery and ui/surface, 14 lowering faults on checked code, an I2 and I9 defect). (a) bb9c74e522 made UIHostError, UIClipboardText, UICapabilityFacts, UIShortcut(Binding), UIFileDialogRequest, UIFSGrant and UIAccessibility Jet structs and enums in Core/Ui/Host.jet, but the JetIR RuntimeRoutes rows and the JetRuntime Ui*.jet carriers still treat them as opaque JetUi* handles, so ir_is_handle refuses them (BuildRoutes.jet:4263/4493/4609; 9 faults). (b) The native runtime exports no jet_ui_host_* service (clipboard, drag, IME, shortcuts, capabilities, open/save file) or jet_ui_text_input; only Prelude/Web/Core/Ui.js implements them, while the CoreCall rows mark them aot_direct (4 faults). (c) The UINode handle has field routes only for label, width and height, so .accessibility has none (1 fault). Fix at the root by finishing the Jet-source cutover: remove the handle carriers and Handle route rows for these types, and implement the native host services as source-owned Jet over a headless provider that returns CapabilityUnavailable, with the same meaning on every tier (I9). A native-tier rejection would split meaning by tier and is not the fix. Proof: ui/battery and ui/surface pass on o0/o1/o2 and web, and no lowering fault remains in a core.ui sweep.

cards.title: Native-era collect-all launch gate: check in the preflight that AGENTS.md requires
cards.body: AGENTS.md (Find every issue at once) says expensive launches start only through tooling that refuses to launch without a collect-all preflight receipt for that exact commit, naming $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/Main/preflight.mjs enforced by prepare-sharded-chain.mjs. Neither is usable: prepare-sharded-chain.mjs does not exist in the repo or scratch, and preflight.mjs depends on the retired Rust-era jetc0 factory, hostJet and proof-source.mjs. In practice the gate today is chain full reaching FIXED_POINT plus the keep-going census, but nothing enforces it, and a fresh clone can't follow the contract. For a commit it runs, in collect-all mode: parse, imports, sema (JET_KEEP_GOING=1), the lowering sweep (JET_DEBUG_LOWER_ALL=1), the generator checks and the comptime-host count against the last admitted compiler. It writes a receipt keyed to the commit in which every row is clean or carries a written disposition. The seed-cut and release launchers refuse to start without a matching receipt. Then point AGENTS.md at the checked-in path in the same cutover.

cards.title: jet front accepts any registered flag on any command: jet init --check silently writes
cards.body: Found by JetpackEngine (#6418 c9). The CLI registry scopes --check to fmt ("With fmt:"), but the JetCli front accepts any registered flag on any command. So jet init --check ignores the flag and writes package.jet. A flag outside a command's registry scope must be a usage error that names the commands which do take it. Silently ignoring a flag that promises no writes is a safety bug.

cards.title: Every CLI flag must also be a setting: non-build commands (registry publish --force and others) have no settings home
cards.body: Standing owner order: every CLI flag is also a setting. The only flag↔setting table is JET_BUILD_OPTIONS (build profiles, fn build, pins), which only build, run and dev read. jet registry publish --force (CLICommands.jet:796; it also gates E1218 per #6600) and every other non-build command flag have no setting. First census every registered CLI flag against its setting home. Then ballot where non-build command settings live (e.g. package.jet publish: {…} vs a per-command settings table in jet settings), with same-program alternatives. Then build it, with one flag↔setting mechanism for all commands.

log.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Q24 A): one registry. Every CLI command flag row gets a key <command>.<flag>, readable from package.jet settings and the user settings file; precedence flag, then package, then user (the JET_BUILD_OPTIONS mechanism). Destructive flags are marked not persistable and setting one is refused with a registered diagnostic. ScriptLead builds it.

Census (c1 first half), Main 2026-11-07, dev eb47eb7277 on seed a0_034. Method: jet help for all 49 commands and every action of the group commands (117 help pages), parsing each flag a usage line or flag row lists. A flag counts as homed when its long name is a JET_BUILD_OPTIONS row (Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuildOptions.jet, 7 rows) and its command reads that table (build, run, dev). Result: 429 command-flag rows over 76 commands and actions. 21 are homed: build, run and dev each have 7 (backtrace, bounds, inline, libs, optimize, os, small). The other 408 rows (157 distinct flags) have none. The most common homeless flags are --json x52, --color x44, --quiet x44, --live x8, --verbose x7, --profile x6, --set x6, -p x6, --gate x5, --release x5, --target x5, --threads x5, --trace x5, --dry-run x5 and --allow x4. Rows per command: test 57, build 34, run 32, dev 26, inspect 26, new 17, cc 16, c++ 16, jobs 15, check 12, fmt 11, self 11, budget 9; registry has 7, including publish --force and --no-sign. Flags with a neighbouring but non-flag-keyed home (--allow/--deny to package authority, --target to package targets, --profile to build profiles) count as homeless, because none goes through one flag-to-setting mechanism. The census is regenerated on demand by $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/burn/flags/{collect.sh,census.mjs} (scratch; the porting home is the CLI registry, not a committed table). Next: the ballot on where non-build command settings live, then one shared mechanism.

criteria.text: A census lists every registered CLI flag with its setting (or none); after the ratified ballot, every flag has exactly one setting through one shared flag-to-setting mechanism, with a cases row per command family proving that flag and setting have the same effect

cards.title: Test kit runs cases with the real HOME: suites write ~/.jet (registry index, keys)
cards.body: The cases kit does not isolate HOME per case, so suite runs (pkg and vendored filters) modify the owner's ~/.jet: registry-index was modified on 2026-11-06 at 04:11 during agent suite runs. A probe with the real HOME also overwrote ~/.jet/keys/jet.ed25519 at 04:23. Every case must get its own fresh HOME (and JET_HOME, XDG_* dirs) under its scratch directory, unless the case explicitly declares a home fixture. log.text: Suspect runs that modified the owner's ~/.jet on 2026-11-06: DeclColon's ui suites, jetpack builds and generators (03:30–04:45); GoldenRoots3's tests/cases/pkg A/B (04:00–04:36); JetpackEngine's pkg/vendored filters and its registry keygen --force probe (04:23). GoldenRoots3's pkg profile also deadlocked on the base compiler (all threads in futex waits, no children), probably contention on the shared real ~/.jet/.jetpack.lock across agents. A planted case that writes $HOME/.jet/probe leaves the real home untouched (proven by stat before and after a full pkg-filter run). The kit refuses a run whose HOME resolves to the real user home.

Two full --filter=pkg cases runs with HOME, JET_HOME and XDG_CONFIG/DATA/STATE pointed at a stand-in home holding .jet/lock, .jet/keys/jet.ed25519 and a registry-index row: a recursive lstat+sha256 digest is identical before and after both runs (4be57bd3..., f99c92c7..., 13 entries each), so package cases that write HOME/.jet leave the invoking home untouched.
