cards.title: Test suites run in seconds: fix the slow programs, the timeouts and the per-program cost
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-06: suites should finish in seconds or minutes, not take a long time; the golden suite once took about 15 minutes at most.

Measured on vb5 (dev 7f0b3d03ed, s1, 32 cores):
- golden: 4766 rows, about 4 minutes wall, median 0.28 s per row. The 4655 rows under 5 s alone sum to 74 CPU minutes, so per-program cost sets a floor of about 2.3 minutes even with perfect parallelism.
- cases: 4501 rows, about 13.5 minutes wall, median 0.10 s; 284 rows of 5 s or more account for 97 of 131 CPU minutes; 12 rows hit the 60 s wall-clock limit.
- ui: 2412 rows, about 1 minute wall.

Slowest golden programs (all tiers): concurrency/job_queue 248 s, foundations/storage 177 s, foundations/text 161 s, crypto/file_seal_jetc 153 s, game/raylib_indexed 148 s, foundations/realtime 100 s.
Timeouts: cffi/concurrent_bridges_share_one_target_publish_without_racing, cffi/ffi_capability_boundary_is_safe_only_inside_unsafe, ffi_rust/rust_extern_std_round_trip_uses_the_canonical_descriptor, fixtures_crypto_bridge_entropy/jetc_v2_record_boundaries_are_canonical, fmt_project/top_level_jet_fmt_delegates_non_jet_file_to_realized_formatter, jetpack_nix_index/index_backed_nixpkgs_repairs_only_missing_transitive_object, jetpack_nix_index/static_publication_resolves_signed_index_and_nix_objects, jetpack_tool/use_ephemeral_execs_inside_and_outside_project_without_path_projection, repl/repl_tty_prompts_and_reuses_exact_session_tuple, ui_fixes/ownership_ui_fixes_compile_ffi_companions, unsafe_and_runtime/ffi_capability_edge_uses_shared_sentry_prelude, web_dev/embedded_devserver_rejects_hardlinked_source.

For every slow row, first record where the time goes (compile front end, Core/Prelude re-check, code generation per tier, link, the program's own run, or a fixed sleep or timeout in the test), then fix that root. Never raise a limit, drop a tier or move a row out of the default profile to make a number.

log.text: Moved from G1 to G5 by owner ruling 2026-11-07. a0_033 release kit timings (parallel, under load): golden 1479 programs, median 528 ms, 420 at 5 s or more, rows sum 5037 s; cases 4637, median 156 ms, 524 at 5 s or more, sum 8201 s; ui 2252, median 66 ms, 9 at 5 s or more, sum 939 s. c4's shared per-run Core check is compiler work, the same as #6623 and #6647.

c4 progress: MechD-3's 59d955887b (store capacity checks replay a footprint tally instead of scanning every entry) cut golden wall from 1086 s to 118.7 s on fab74a230c s1, all rows passing (4318 PASS, 0 FAIL). The per-program median is 348 ms over 3 tiers, about 0.12 s per tier, against the 0.1 s target. About 90% of each tier is re-checking Core identically for every program; caching checked Core by content key is the remaining c4 lever, and df runs about 6 times per build. c5 still needs a run on the batch machine (118.7 s against the 90 s target).

criteria.text: Each of the six slow golden programs (concurrency/job_queue, foundations/storage, foundations/text, crypto/file_seal_jetc, game/raylib_indexed, foundations/realtime, or their successors after the Examples cutover) runs in under 5 s per tier on the batch machine, with the root cause of its old time recorded on this card.
The 12 cases rows that hit the 60 s wall-clock limit on vb5 are root-caused and each passes, or fails for a recorded unrelated reason, in under 10 s.
criteria.evidence: 85dea10ff4 (TestSystemLead-2). The 12 vb5 60 s rows, rerun at HEAD (release jetpack aaa6331fc067, cargo and bwrap on PATH). Root causes, from reproducing each on 7f0b3d03ed: cffi/concurrent_bridges was a jet check futex deadlock (PASS 3.0 s); ffi_rust/rust_extern_std was an ICE 101 (PASS 2.7 s); fixtures_crypto_bridge_entropy/jetc_v2 was an fsync stall in jbd2 on loaded ext4 scratch (PASS 3.1 s); fmt_project/top_level_jet_fmt was the old jetpack hanging in env -- nixfmt (PASS 0.26 s); jetpack_nix_index static_publication and index_backed_repairs were the old jetpack hanging in env --prep (PASS 4.4 s and 9.5 s); web_dev/embedded_devserver_rejects_hardlinked_source was jet dev watching until the limit (now KNOWN-FAILING #6386, 2.2 s). cffi/ffi_capability_boundary (1.4 s), unsafe_and_runtime/ffi_capability_edge (0.3 s) and ui_fixes/ownership_ui_fixes_compile_ffi_companions (2.6 s) pass; the first two now declare requires tool:cargo/rustc and report SKIP-HOST without cargo. jetpack_tool/use_ephemeral is KNOWN-FAILING #3594 (8.0 s); repl_tty_prompts is KNOWN-FAILING #5949 with its limit lowered to 6 s (6.1 s). Row lists: lanes/TestSystemLead/kf82.txt, kf84.txt, kf85.txt.

criteria.text: Every cases row that took 5 s or more on vb5 (284 rows) runs in under 5 s, or this card records why its work is inherently longer (for example a real network or Nix fetch) and that row moves to a named opt-in profile that the default run does not include.

Per-program cost: a profile of a typical golden row splits its time into Core and Prelude checking, the program's own front end, code generation per tier, link and run. Any work repeated identically for every program (for example re-checking Core) is done once per suite run and shared, and the median golden row drops to 0.1 s or less.
On the batch machine the golden suite finishes in under 90 s wall, the cases suite in under 3 minutes and the ui suite in under 30 s, measured on the same commit and recorded with the commit.

The two step timeouts set for #6651 c2 are removed and both rows pass on the default 60 s step limit under full-kit load: tests/cases/compiled_workloads/compiled_workload_gate_self_check.case (19 s alone; warm 11.6 s splits into contract 2.2 s, synthetic report 2.1 s, 33 check_report calls with about 63 ms of start-up each, then tier, peer, sample and tier-receipt checks) and tests/cases/comptime_sequence_parity/repl_list_and_fixed_list_sequence_methods_are_exact.case (50 REPL turns at about 0.4 s each).

The packages suite on a fresh clone finishes in under 5 minutes wall: the hosted Jetpack engine build overlaps the package runs (2a5ad087af), and the engine unit's claims, which run serially because they share process state, run in under 1 minute.
Every corpus suite (golden, cases, ui, packages) runs as wide as the machine's cores and memory allow, with no fixed job cap below that.
Excluding the toolchain fetch, jet test Compiler --profile full on a fresh clone finishes in under 10 minutes on the batch machine. A per-phase timeline is recorded with the commit.
The cold toolchain fetch inside that run (#6592) takes 30 s or less, so the whole fresh-clone run finishes in under 11 minutes.
The fresh-clone full profile's startup (building the test runner and assembling before the first suite row; about 4 minutes on 2026-11-07) is measured by phase and cut to under 30 s.

cards.title: Passing a read parameter to a method's owning argument copies silently, while a plain call reports E0201
cards.body:
Found by SyntaxOwner during the #6586 sweep (2026-11-06, dev 529e9d9ddd). With a read parameter `item: [Int]`, `rows.push(item)` is accepted silently: the list is copied into the owning argument. Passing the same value to a plain function whose parameter owns it, `keep(bag)`, reports E0201 MissingMoveMarker. One meaning must have one mechanism (I8): an owning argument position needs the same move or copy rule whether it belongs to a method call or a plain call, and sema decides it (I3).

First establish from the ratified ownership decisions (D-CALLSITE-MARK2, D-MOVE-SIGIL1, #6586) which behaviour is correct for a non-copyable value from a read parameter, then make both call forms follow it.

log.text: Follow-up on c78da98b1b: the a0_030 candidate also rejects Core sites that the compiler build never reaches (Core/App/App.jet:307,310,312; Core/Web/Storage/Local.jet:22 and Session.jet:22; Core/Web/Browser.jet:1428), which broke 4 golden examples at o0-o2.  only reaches Core bodies a program calls (an import-everything probe, even with JET_DEBUG_LOWER_ALL=1, reports nothing), so no tool today can census a sema rule change across all of Core. Main is sweeping every Examples/ and tests/run program with the candidate s2 and lands one batch fix.

Owner ruling 2026-11-06: A, calls never copy. Method owning arguments (push/add/extend…) are take parameters like keep(item): a read parameter or later-used name gives E0201/E0209 unless written .copy(). This follows D-CALLSITE-MARK2=A ('a call never copies on its own'). Cutover: the sema rule plus a collect-all codemod inserting .copy() (>=958 sites at census), in one commit. [item] and Box{items: item} are not covered by this ruling.

criteria.text: A UI fixture shows `rows.push(item)` on a read parameter `item: [Int]` and `keep(item)` with an owning parameter giving the same result: the same registered diagnostic and snapshot, or both accepted with the same copy rule, whichever the ratified ownership decisions require.
A tests/cases row covers method calls, plain calls, operator hooks and trailing blocks with an owning argument taken from a read parameter, and passes with the admitted jet.

cards.title: Tool symbol paths use `.`, not `::`: inspect, find, semindex, docs and the impact selector
cards.body:
Owner 2026-11-06 chose A: with `::` gone from source (D-DECL-COLON1=A, #6586), tool symbol paths switch from `module::name` to `.`, matching source qualification such as `alias.Type.method`. This changes the public JSON and text output of jet inspect, jet find, the semantic index and jet docs, and the user-typed selector of `jet inspect impact <file> <symbol>`. Greenfield cutover: no `::` reader stays behind.

Sites found by the syntax owner at c92bf872eb:
- User-typed: the jet inspect impact selector (Inspect.jet:1580).
- User-visible JSON or text: semindex identity, summary and call_path keys (SemIndexBuild.jet 149/1481/1526/1530/2151, Sema SemanticIndex.jet:422, InspectOutput.jet:32; the case semindex_projects_omitted_inferred_effects expects `inferred_effect_signature::announce`); inspect rights keys (InspectRights.jet 142/168/173); inspect shapes (InspectShapes.jet:422); find (Find.jet:308); docs `parent::name` (Docs.jet:279); codemod and try identities (Codemod.jet:1371, Try.jet:242).
- Internal parsing: ArchitectureAdvice.jet:47, Fill.jet:80, SemIndexBuild.jet:1797, and the ComptimeIR.jet:103 and Pipeline.jet:2712 cache keys.
- Real Rust paths in RustForeign.jet:210-232 are foreign syntax and stay.

Module paths contain dots (`core.process`), so a tool must know where the module path ends. The tools have the module graph, so a reader resolves the longest prefix that names a module, and the rest is the member path. Writers emit the same form.

log.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-06 (chat, second cut questions): c1 stands as written: every `::` in Compiler/ goes, internal keys included (~3,800 sites), not just the tool-visible paths.

criteria.text: Every tool output and selector listed in the body writes and reads symbol paths with `.` (for example `inferred_effect_signature.announce`), with no `::` writer, reader or fallback left except real Rust paths in RustForeign.jet; a repo search for `::` in Compiler/ outside Rust-foreign code and dated docs finds none.

Readers split a dotted path at the longest prefix that names a module in the program's module graph; a case proves `jet inspect impact <file> core.process.spawn`-style selectors and an ambiguous or unknown prefix gives a registered diagnostic with a UI snapshot.

The affected cases, snapshots and goldens (semindex_projects_omitted_inferred_effects and every inspect, find, docs, codemod and try row that names a symbol) are updated in the same commit and pass on the default tier; the spec text that documents these outputs shows the `.` form.

cards.title: jet fix renames a used loop variable to _n and skips the real := fix (E0111)
cards.body:
Repro on a0_029 (release binary, empty HOME): oops.jet is
run: fn() {
    total: 0
    loop n in 1..3 -> total = total + n
    print(total)
}
`jet run` correctly reports E0111 (total was made with `:`; Fix: declare it with `total := ...`). `jet fix oops.jet` then says 'applied 1 fix, skipped 1 suggestion for review'. The applied fix renames `n` to `_n` as if unused, although `total + n` uses it, so the program is now wrong. The real E0111 fix (`:` to `:=`) is the skipped one. Probe: $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT/lanes/Main/readme-probe/fresh/oops.jet.

criteria.text: `jet fix` on the oops.jet repro applies the E0111 `:` to `:=` fix and never renames a used variable; a test proves both.
criteria.evidence: 01c7879e02 (+4337521436 for uses inside unresolved calls); batch vb10 (dev e4756389a9, s1 kit): cases cli_parts_surface/fix_applies_e0111_and_keeps_used_loop_variable, e0102_and_e0111_typed_fix_edits_apply and fix_safety_tiers_are_reported_and_applied PASS.

cards.title: Every effect is allowed by default; code denies, and a run warns when its effects change
cards.body: Owner ruling 2026-11-06 (chat): 'I think by default, we should consider all effects allowed. Packages, functions, types, etc can deny them. When a script or program is first run it warns about the effects that are used unless using the -A flag.' Approved with Main's four refinements: (1) the notice repeats whenever the program's effect set changes, not only on the first run; (2) a written authority row is a ceiling and silences the notice for what it lists; (3) jetpack records each dependency's effect row and reports widening, and --locked refuses it; (4) code run straight from a URL or the registry asks before its first run. Decision D-AUTH-DEFAULT1. This supersedes the prompt model of D-AUTH-AMBIENT1, D-AUTH-AMBIENT3 and D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1 (spec.md 'Application authority'). Greenfield cutover: the prompt path, its diagnostics and every caller migrate in one change.

log.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Q33 a): D-AUTH-DEFAULT1 covers the REPL. The REPL follows the program model: every effect allowed, a notice when the session effect set widens, --deny wins. Its separate TTY prompt (once/session/deny) and the piped E1803 are removed in the same cutover. EffectsLead builds it with the c2 docs.

Ballot D-JET-RUN-REMOTE1 posted for the owner (Q25a B): the command that runs code straight from a URL or the registry and asks before its first run. Options A jet run <https-url|name#ver|name> (recommended), B a jet x verb, C jet fetch then run the stored path. c8 applies to the ratified form.

Owner rulings 2026-11-08 (Q25). a: B, ballot a command that runs URL or registry code (jet run <url> or pkg@ver) now; c8 applies to it. b: A, --allow=R acknowledges R (left out of the notice) and resource-qualified rows still confine through Landlock. c: A, the ambient floor (IO, Mem.Alloc, Exec.Args) stays inside every written ceiling and leaves only through an explicit deny. FYI items (jet new writes no authority row; scripts lose the #! -A rule; the notice omits floor effects) stand, no objection.
Assigned 2026-11-08 by Main: EffectsLead (G8), starting with the c1 adversarial review. Also on EffectsLead: #6206, #6551 (ballot draft for c1) and #6129 for direction.

criteria.text: A dated adversarial review in Docs/audits attacks every claimed strength of D-AUTH-DEFAULT1 (allow-by-default against Deno's deny-by-default prompts, Node's opt-in permission model, and Python, Go and Rust having no authority model) and ends with a holds verdict; every gap it finds is on a card or ballot. No build criterion below starts before this one is met.

spec.md 'Application authority' and syntax-decisions.md state the new model in one cutover; D-AUTH-AMBIENT1, D-AUTH-AMBIENT3 and D-SCRIPT-CONFIRM1 are marked superseded by D-AUTH-DEFAULT1; no prose still describes the Run it? prompt.

With no written authority, jet run grants every effect and, before the program's first instruction, prints the program's inferred effects in plain words on stderr. A rerun with the same effect set prints nothing, and a rerun whose effect set changed prints the notice again. Proof: a UI snapshot plus a case that runs the same program three times (first, unchanged, after adding an effect).
-A (--allow-all) suppresses the notice, and --deny=<RIGHTS> still wins over every grant (E1803 before host state changes). Proof: a case per flag.

A written authority row (package.jet, a script's inline package block, a module, a type or a function effect row) is a ceiling: reaching an effect outside it fails at check time with E0749, and the effects it lists no longer appear in the notice. Proof: a UI snapshot and a case.

A deny written on a package, module, type or function prohibits the denied effects for everything inside it, transitively, at check time (E0749). The existing deny rows keep passing, and a new case covers a deny on a type.

jetpack records each dependency's inferred effect row in the lock. An update that widens a dependency's row prints which package gained which effect, and --locked refuses the widening with a registered diagnostic that has a UI snapshot. Proof: a jetpack case.
Code run straight from a URL or the registry asks before its first run in a terminal. Without a terminal it stops, and the Fix names the -A command. Proof: a case for each path.
Without a terminal or a writable state store, the notice prints once per run on stderr, and --json carries the effect list as structured detail. Proof: a case.

The Run it? prompt path, the always grant writer, and every diagnostic used only by the old model are removed; every in-repository caller, test, snapshot and example is migrated in the same change (no alias, fallback or second path). Proof: a census in the closing commit shows no remaining caller.

Soundness (found by the c1 review, EffectsLead 2026-11-08): a written #Import(c) or other foreign import records FFI.C (or its language leaf) and, with no declared effect row, is treated as reaching every effect, so deny rows and written ceilings apply to it. Probe: deny:[FFI, Exec, FS] plus a C system() call that writes a file is refused at check time. Proof: a case per path.

Soundness (found by the c1 review): the run and entry effect list is sema sound row: open-world calls through function values (fn-value reference edges, values stored in lists or records) count as maximal, so the notice, --deny and ceilings never miss an effect. Probe p6/hidden2.jet (a file read through a list-stored fn value, listed as IO only) reports FS.Read. Proof: a case.

cards.title: D-HOST-LEAF1=E: the runtime is an ordinary library that Core uses
cards.body: Owner ratified D-HOST-LEAF1 option E on 2026-11-06. jet_runtime becomes an ordinary library: Core and any package write use rt: jet.runtime.time and call rt.sleep_ns(duration.ns). No marker, no symbol string, no hand-written manifest. Internals stay hidden by pub. Amended by the adversarial review (Docs/audits/2026-11-06-d-host-leaf1-option-e-review.md): a declared effect row on a pub runtime function introduces its effects, and the interface is generated from source with the runtime pack. This card builds the runtime side. The #6151 criteria (c4-c41) and #6111 c1/c2 that waited on the host-leaf ballot are unblocked by E and stay on their cards: they remove Core's privileges, which E's ordinary-library model makes possible.

log.text: Defect found by TestSystemLead-2 at 56e30acfcf: an #Import(c) call to the runtime symbol jet_rt_process_exit lowers into jet_rt_unreachable. The program prints 'internal error: entered unreachable code:' and exits 101 whatever code it passed. Repro: a 10-line program that imports raw_exit: fn(code: I64) = "jet_rt_process_exit" and calls it. Sites hit: Compiler Host.jet:1563 jet_cli_defect_exit, the JetTestKit fixture compiler.jet, and Compiler/JetTestKit/Assets/no_nix.jet. It belongs to c6 (reaching a runtime C symbol through #Import(c)): the imported call must exit with its argument and print nothing.

criteria.text: Docs/audits/2026-11-06-d-host-leaf1-option-e-review.md is on dev and its verdict holds within the stated limits; its two amendments (declared effect rows on pub runtime functions are the introducing leaves; the runtime interface is generated from source with the runtime pack) are part of E.
criteria.evidence: Docs/audits/2026-11-06-d-host-leaf1-option-e-review.md landed on dev as a8ca8c0f63 (lane-commit, CHECK OK). Verdict: holds within limits, with the two amendments (declared effect rows on pub jet_runtime functions are the introducing leaves, proven equal to CoreCallRows effect_kind/effect_leaf at cutover; the runtime interface is generated from source with the runtime pack and embedded). The web-tier gap (Compiler/Prelude/Web/Core/Realtime.js reimplements runtime functions) is c7 on this card.

criteria.text: A census lists every CoreCallRecord field (borrow_mask, fallibility, effect_kind, effect_leaf, capability contract, pure_route, coverage, aot_direct, native_int_result, frame_accesses, sink_class, ui_capabilities, marker, authority) and gives each either its home in the runtime's Jet signature or a proof that nothing reads it, so it can be deleted.

Building the runtime pack also generates the jet_runtime interface (each pub function's Jet signature and effect row) from the runtime source and embeds it in jet. A check fails the pack build when the interface and the source disagree. No hand-written copy exists. The measured compile time of a hello-world jet check with the interface loaded is recorded and no slower than before the change.

Every runtime function Core calls is a pub function of jet_runtime with a Jet name, Jet types (Int, not I64; typed handles) and a declared effect row. A generated comparison over every bound function proves each declared row equals the effect_kind and effect_leaf the compiler row held before the cutover, with zero differences.

Core reaches the runtime only through ordinary use of jet.runtime modules. The dispatcher_row lines in Compiler/Prelude/Core.jet, the bound CoreCallRows, the IRRoute carrier rows for those functions and their RuntimeStopExports entries are deleted, and every in-repository caller is migrated in one cutover. Goldens prove o0, o1 and o2 for one call in each Core module that called the runtime.

A safe package that names a runtime function that isn't pub fails with the ordinary visibility diagnostic, and reaching a runtime C symbol needs #Import(c) inside #Unsafe. Proof: a UI snapshot for each.

The web tier provides no runtime function as a JavaScript reimplementation: it runs jet_runtime compiled for the web, or its JavaScript host only marshals values into the same runtime code (I9). Until then, no public text says every tier runs one runtime.

cards.title: Verify batches see self-compile miscompiles before a release does
cards.body: a0_030 (e32b979063) failed its release gate on an I2 regression that only the release's s2/s3 show: an ICE exits 1 instead of 101. Root (CoreCliLead): b4e29635ce made the runtime map a user program's process.exit(101) to status 1 (101 is reserved for ICEs). The compiler exits through the same Core call, so a jet linked with a pack built from post-b4e2 runtime source (s2/s3 link pack1) loses its 101. s1 links the seed's (a0_029) pack and still exits 101. Main's vb batches build and test s1 only, so every runtime change reaches the compiler's own behaviour unseen until the release run (33 minutes here). Fix the batch so a cheap probe runs on every batch: a jet linked with the batch's own runtime pack, on the rows most exposed to runtime changes in the compiler (ICE exit codes, process exit codes). Don't add a full s2 suite to each batch.

log.text: 2026-11-06 a0_030 retry on 2edea7b26a: census-snap preflight passed (rc=0) but the chain's s2 stopped with 19 jet.MissingMoveMarker errors in Core/Http, Core/Net/Tls and Core/Web. The rule came from c78da98b1b (#6611, calls never copy); the preflight and LaneCheck both check with the a0_029 seed, which lacks that rule, so a sema change that tightens Core is invisible until s2. Gap: the preflight needs a candidate pass (build s1, then a keep-going s1 check of Compiler, Core and Jetpack) before a release launches.

cards.title: One receipt kind for results, goldens, budgets and API snapshots
cards.body: A design card: decide whether test results, goldens, budgets and API snapshots share one receipt format, then build it. Starts with a design and an adversarial review.

criteria.text: (was #2112 c1) Test results, goldens, budgets and API snapshots are all stored as receipts of one kind (moved from #6035 c25)

A jet check of a small program returns within 1 s of its result being known, even on a contended disk, and its receipt stays durable. Today one check writes .jet/receipts and records as 4 objects plus a records index, each made durable separately: 0.35 s of compile, then 49-84 s of fsync under lane load on $JET_SCRATCH_ROOT (after_close_reader, 11-07). Make the write cost one barrier per check: the objects first, then one fsync of the directory and index, or the write handed off with the next command waiting on it. A measured row pins the time under write load, and a kill during the write leaves either the old index or the complete new one.

cards.title: Alloc cache gating disagrees between alloc and free (Alloc.jet:1012 vs :1056)
cards.body: Found by MechD 2026-11-06 while fixing the JetRuntime plain transport (#6594). Compiler/JetRuntime Alloc.jet:1056 gates the cached free on alloc_root+200 (the tracked count) while the allocation fast path at :1012 gates on alloc_root+144 (mode). When anything is tracked, frees bypass the cache but allocations still pop it. Confirm with a runtime test that tracks one allocation and then cycles cached sizes; fix so both paths read the same gate.

criteria.text: A runtime test tracks an allocation and cycles cached sizes; alloc and free gate on the same root field, and the test passes on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: Not a bug: the two gates differ on purpose. Compiler/JetRuntime/Source/Alloc.jet:1012 jet_rt_alloc takes the cache only when the counting mode word (alloc_root+144) is 0, so every allocation in counting mode is tracked. :1056 jet_rt_free takes the cache only when the tracked count (alloc_root+200) is 0. Policy restore (:887) turns the mode off while tracked blocks stay in the side table, so each of those frees must still reach alloc_untrack. Gating free on the mode would skip the untrack and leave the ProgramAllocator facts stale. Gating alloc on the count would skip tracking the first counted block. The comment at :995-997 documents the split. Verified by Main from MechD-3's analysis.

cards.title: Scripting speed and startup: beat Lua, LuaJIT, Python, Node, Bun, Deno and Perl
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-06: Jet scripts beat every scripting language on run speed and startup.

criteria.text: A matched script cell family (hello, a 50-line text-processing script, a JSON transform, a directory walk, a subprocess pipeline) runs `jet run` against Lua 5.4, LuaJIT, Python 3, Node, Bun, Deno and Perl, measuring exec-to-exit wall time, cycles and peak RSS, Jet compile included, cold and warm reported separately.
End metric: Jet wins every cell and metric against every peer (Jet/peer below 1.00), cold and warm; every loss names its root on a card.

cards.title: Reasoning about code: Jet beats every language on how well readers and tools can reason about a program
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-06: beat all other languages on the ability to reason about code.

criteria.text: A reasoning benchmark defines task families (predict the output, find every effect of a call, show two values never alias, find every caller, find what a change breaks, find where a failure can come from) over matched programs in Jet, Rust, Go, Python, TypeScript, Zig and C++.
Each task is scored for readers (human or model: accuracy and time) and for tools (what `jet inspect` and the language server answer mechanically versus each peer toolchain).
End metric: Jet scores best on every task family; every loss names its root on a card.

cards.title: Concision and builtins: the shortest correct code for common tasks
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-06: lean toward less code for an equivalent task, with builtins good enough that common scripts are very short.

criteria.text: A matched task corpus of at least 50 common scripting, data, CLI and service tasks has idiomatic solutions in Jet, Python, Ruby, Lua, Go, Rust, TypeScript and Kotlin, measured in tokens and lines.
End metric: Jet is shortest or tied on every task family without giving up safety, diagnostics or clarity; every loss names the missing builtin or convenience on a card.

cards.title: Expert performance APIs: every technique the asm-parity ceilings use is expressible in Jet
cards.body: Owner order 2026-11-06: advanced APIs so codegen can produce the equivalent of the best hand-optimized machine code.

criteria.text: Every technique an asm-parity reference uses that Jet code cannot express (SIMD lanes, prefetch, alignment and layout control, branch and cold hints, non-temporal stores, syscall batching and others) is listed with the cells that use it.

Each missing technique gets an owner ballot with its plain and expert spellings (expert control by explicit opt-in) and a paired two-program cell; it ratifies only when it strictly beats the plain form.
End metric: every required cell can be written in Jet with its ceiling's technique, and codegen emits that technique.

cards.title: comptime: a pure generator that only yields fails E3410 at compile time

cards.title: core.files: exists() is true for a broken symlink
cards.body: files.exists(path) follows the link target's existence inconsistently: on a symlink whose target is missing it returns true. The contract must state whether exists follows links, and the code must match it.

log.text: 8583f858a0 made files.exists follow a final link, and core_files_metadata_predicates_follow_links_and_keep_errors_false passes in vb13. Still missing for c1: a doc comment on Core/Files/Files.jet exists and lexists stating the rule, a lexists assertion on the broken link (true), and an O2 (--release) step; the case covers only jet run and jet build. criteria.text: A case creates a symlink to a missing target: files.exists follows the link and returns false, and the link-level query (the Core API that does not follow links) returns true. The rule is stated in the core.files doc comment. Passes on O0, O1 and O2.
criteria.evidence: 8583f858a0 made files.exists follow a final link. 1cac917708 adds doc comments on Core/Files/Files.jet exists (follows the link, so a broken link is false) and lexists (the link itself), a lexists assertion on the broken link in tests/cases/core_files_foundations/core_files_metadata_predicates_follow_links_and_keep_errors_false.case, and a jet build --release step with checked stdout beside jet run (O0) and jet build (O1). log.text: Back to G5. CoreCliLead-2 measured it: JetLSP and JetDevserver are about 35k lines of Rust transliterated into Jet that have never compiled. cards.title: E3510 GeneratedModuleShadows is registered but never emitted
cards.body: From #6638 c3 (MechD-3, ffff735682). tests/ui/build_generated_collision pins E0603 because nothing emits E3510 GeneratedModuleShadows. Either the generated-module collision reports E3510 (and the snapshot moves to it) or E3510 leaves the registry (I4: every registered code has an emitter and a snapshot).

log.text: MechD-3 (2026-11-07): nothing can emit E3510 today. Loader.jet ~1646 reports E3502 for a generated module aliasing another source, but generated paths are under .jet/generated/ and the source scan skips dot-directories (Request.jet:420, :1269), so no handwritten source unit can sit at a generated path. The fixture fails earlier with E0603 (run.jet is both build file and importer; the use of ./.jet/generated/... resolves before generation). The only real collision is write_generated: on overwriting a handwritten file (InspectBuild.jet:174-180). An emitter needs a rule for 'handwritten' (exists, bytes differ, sha256 differs from the lock's [[comptime_inputs]] row; but the lock row is written only after targets compile, so a failed build would flag its own output), E3510 at that write site, a --write-generated=on ui directive, and a fixture. Alternative: drop E3510 from the registry and spec.md:5076.

criteria.text: tests/ui/build_generated_collision snapshots E3510 GeneratedModuleShadows from the generated-module collision (or E3510 is removed from the registry with no remaining reference); diagnostics_snapshots guard PASS.

cards.title: LaneCheck cannot check Compiler/Prelude or Compiler/JetRuntime files: it checks them as standalone units
cards.body: Tools/agent/LaneCheck.jet checks a touched file's package as a normal unit. Compiler/Prelude is embedded, so checking it alone gives 1539 ReservedDunderName errors in Core.jet, including on untouched files such as CoreSurfaceInventory.jet. Compiler/JetRuntime is assembled by the chain, so checking it alone gives 2874 UnknownFunction os_store_i64 errors across 153 files. Workers editing either tree therefore get CHECK FAILED whether or not their change is good, which makes the receipt meaningless for the two most sensitive trees. Found by TestSystemLead-2 in 332eb41d18 and 83859ebe1c. d16f96e61e skips both in the packages suite for the same reason.

log.text: c4 isn't met yet: at dev HEAD 963f74b975 the lander's precommit (looping over Land.jet ratchets with seed a0_033; 10 checks in 23 s) fails Tools/agent/DiagnosticRows.jet --check on Docs/site/dist/e/E-ERR-PROPAGATE and E1206. Diagnostics.jet hasn't changed since 78aa137994, so the output depends on the jet running the generator. TestSystemLead-2 is fixing the root. The other 9 checks pass.

Ruling on c1: option B. The compiler gains a check mode that checks Compiler/Prelude files as generated prelude source (lex_generated plus the same unit context the compiler embeds them in), and LaneCheck uses it once a seed has it. Until then LaneCheck reports a touched Prelude file as unchecked ('needs a seed with the prelude check mode'), never as CHECK OK. The row-DSL inputs (Core.jet, CoreSurfaceInventory.jet, CoreSourceParts.tsv) are checked by their generator --check, which is their real consumer. No baseline-diff gate. c3 added for the duplicated raw-string copies.

cards.title: Transpile Jet to other languages through target libraries that implement one trait (C and Rust first-party, any language by a package)
cards.body:
Owner request 2026-11-07, re-scoped the same day: Jet transpiles a program to another language, and any language can be added as an ordinary Jet library implementing a target trait. Seeding and bootstrapping the compiler are a separate, frozen question on #6683; this card comes first.

Why: interop (Jet code inside C, Rust, Lua or JavaScript projects), reach (platforms with no Jet native writer), and the language-is-a-library priority.

Design: ballot D-EXPORT-TARGET1. The recommended shape: one shared pass makes every meaning explicit, and core.compiler exposes a versioned program view. A Target trait has required operation methods, host leaves and optional idiom hooks. Capabilities are checked first, and `jet test --to <target>` checks every executable example against `jet run`.

log.text: Ballot D-EXPORT-TARGET1 posted and ready. The fresh adversarial review (PortsLead-2, against dev 964e737fcc) broke the first draft's recommendation. Today's IR still leaves exact-Int spill, trap and stop meaning to each writer (X64Select.jet, Web/Select.jet). The runtime's platform layer is 75 #FFI(asm) leaves plus 383 raw x86-64 syscall sites. Comptime and the only native writer are x86-64, so a C seed cannot rebuild itself elsewhere. --target already means a platform. Recommended now: staged A, with a Wasm seed from the existing web writer (C syscall host, evaluator comptime), then a shared pass that makes every check explicit plus jet build --emit c, then third-party emit libraries once the form is declared stable. If ratified, the criteria follow the ruling.

Ballot D-EXPORT-TARGET1 drafted (owner request: challenge, refine, improve). Options: A target libraries over the compiler's final lowered form, with C and WebAssembly first and a C seed every release (recommended); B readable source-level transpilers per language; C WebAssembly seed only (Zig's approach); D prebuilt binaries only. It passes Tools/agent/ballots/Validate.jet except the review pass. Tower needs the adversarial review even for a draft, so the fresh review (PortsLead-2) is in progress, and the ballot is posted once its findings are folded in.

criteria.text: An adversarial design review in Docs/audits tests every claimed strength of the ratified D-EXPORT-TARGET1 design (library-defined targets for any language, one meaning across targets, readable output through idiom hooks, interop) against Haxe with Reflaxe, Fable, Kotlin's shared IR, Nim, Gleam and LLVM targets. Every gap it finds is on a card or ballot.

A ratified Tower ballot fixes the command's name and flags, the target-library API (what a target receives from the checked program and how it emits text), and the first-party targets, with same-program alternatives and beginner and expert paths.
criteria.evidence: D-EXPORT-TARGET1 ratified A (2026-11-07): one public core.compiler.target Target trait over the explicit program, with required op methods, host leaves and optional idiom hooks; capability errors before output; jet build --to <target>; jet test --to conformance; C and Rust first-party.

criteria.text: A target is an ordinary Jet library that any package can write, using only public compiler-library seams. A third-party test target built outside the repository exports a program as well as a first-party one does.

Exporting a program to C and building it with a stock C compiler gives the same stdout, stderr and exit code as jet run at O0, O1 and O2 for every executable example, with memory safety, fault reports and error behavior unchanged.

cards.title: A borrowed argument widened into a union parameter is moved and dropped by the callee (I1)
cards.body: Found by CoreCliLead-2 on an s1 seeded from B2 phase 1 (dev ee7e360461 + phase 1): passing a borrowed resource handle to a parameter of union type (handle: FileReader | FileWriter | Directory) gives the callee an owned union value that drops the payload on return. That closes the caller's handle: spec.keep_open(directory, at: Val(300)) succeeds, and a second keep_open(directory, ...) returns IOError.Closed. A borrowed argument must stay borrowed when it widens into a union (or be copied when the payload is a value type). It must never move, because the caller still owns it and drops it again. With a heap payload this is a double drop.

log.text: Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (Main asked; owner chose): add dir.duplicate(), a new Core call on Directory that returns a fresh, independent handle to the same directory. keep_open keeps its ratified take (D-CORE-PROCINHERIT1=A). Census (QuickLead): the only caller that reuses one handle is Jetpack CacheLease.pass_into (CacheLease.jet:174, reached from ShellEnv.jet:172 and StoreCache.jet:337); it migrates to keep_open(lease.directory.duplicate()), and Directory.pass_to is removed in the same cutover. FileLock arm: phase 1 refuses it with IOError.Unsupported until a seed carries core.files.__lock_fd; c3 is met only after phase 2.

c3 state at dev 8405a508b0. Done: the per-type core.files.__keep_open_{reader,writer,directory} bodies and every JetSema routing by handle type are gone; grep finds keep_open in no JetSema or JetIR lowering source. 94775580e5 and a5476b82af (#3594 c8 phases 1-2) leave one raw bridge, core.process.__keep_open_raw, plus core.files.__reader_fd and __writer_fd. Missing: the public PROCINHERIT1 method ProcessSpec.keep_open(^handle: KeepOpen, at: Int?{None}) over the union. Today only Directory.pass_to(spec, at) and compiler_with_process_directory reach the bridge, so a FileReader or FileWriter cannot be passed. c3 closes with #3594 c8 phase 3: one Core keep_open body over the union, which takes the handle's descriptor (__reader_fd, __writer_fd or __directory_fd) and calls __keep_open_raw. Directory.pass_to then becomes a caller or goes. Batch proofs at the same compiler (seed-built d405d4cb6c + table-it): golden --filter Systems/Process PASS 54/54; cases --filter held_directory is still KNOWN-FAILING under #6386 (jet debug DAP), unchanged.

c3 landed in dev a5476b82af (Main): Core/Files/Files.jet calls core.process.__keep_open_raw; jet_process_spec_with_directory_raw (export, IR route, host signature, dispatcher row, surface inventory, generated rows) deleted, witness calls the one name. CoreSourceRows, RuntimeGenerators, CoreSurfaceLedger and UnsafeRatchet --check pass on the tree. Proof queued for the next dev-built batch.

Owner cut the agent count to 2. CoreCliLead-2 stopped with c1, c2, c4 and c5 met (060bbcd0f1, 8ac163916e). c3 (keep_open on one Core body) waits for a seed that carries them; a0_034 is being cut from c639365c56.

The c5 audit found the same leak in two more carriers: Ok(handle) passed to a Result parameter, and a tuple literal (d: dir, n: 1) passed to a tuple parameter (probe t5 printed closed: false). CoreCliLead-2 is fixing Option, Ok and tuple in one pass in the ir_call_row lend path, and c5 covers all three.

Root (CoreCliLead-2): in ir_call_row, a read argument widened to a union is boxed through ir_union_box, then ir_store_at, then ir_own. That clones a value that has a clone (every borrowed String passed to a union parameter is copied) and moves one that has none (a handle gets closed under its holder), and the box is dropped after the call. Struct fields, ? and returns already own their value through ir_own, matching the non-union paths. The named-fn value adapter (BuildExpr around 6725) has the same widening. Fix: a lent union box (payload bits stored with no owner; after the call only the box is freed), about 80 lines in BuildTypes/BuildExpr, with no new IR representation.

criteria.text: Root fix in sema/lowering: a borrowed argument that widens into a union parameter stays a borrow (the union carries a borrowed payload), or is copied when the payload is a plain value. It never moves, so the caller's drop is the only drop. No per-API routing or special case. The other places a borrowed value meets a union (return position, struct fields, optional widening) are checked and fixed in the same pass.
criteria.evidence: 060bbcd0f1: ir lends a borrowed argument to the union or trait box of a read parameter, not moved or copied. A .copy() of a lent box is a retain, handled by a release check plus copy fixup at the box end.

criteria.text: A #Test or golden proves it on O0, O1 and O2: a borrowed Directory passed twice to a union-typed parameter stays open for both calls and closes exactly once, and a borrowed heap payload (String in String | Int) passed to a union parameter is neither freed by the callee nor double-freed (run with the memory ledger, 0 leaked and 0 double-dropped).
criteria.evidence: 060bbcd0f1 on its s1: cases union_argument_is_lent_not_copied and union_argument_box_is_freed_after_the_call PASS checked-alloc at o0/o1/o2 (filter _argument_: 25 PASS, 1 known-failing #5454 unrelated); ui ownership/lent_union_handle_cannot_outlive_the_call PASS; golden Types 210/210 at o0/o1/o2.

criteria.text: ProcessSpec.keep_open uses one Core body over the approved union parameter, with no JetSema routing by probed handle type and no per-type core.files.__keep_open_{reader,writer,directory} bodies.

The same lend applies to ir_trait_box: a borrowed handle boxed into a trait object for a call is lent, not moved (sibling found while fixing #6677), with a row proving a borrowed Directory passed twice to a trait-typed parameter stays open.
criteria.evidence: 060bbcd0f1: cases trait_argument_is_lent_not_moved PASS checked-alloc at o0/o1/o2; LaneCheck CHECK OK on BuildTypes, BuildExpr and BuildTraits.

criteria.text: The optional-wrapping path lends too: Val(folder) passed where a Named? (Option of a trait) is expected no longer leaks or moves the borrowed Directory (ir_present/ir_store_at). A case row proves the handle stays open across two such calls and closes once. The other ir_present/ir_store_at widenings of a borrowed operand are audited in the same pass.
criteria.evidence: 8ac163916e: at a read call a borrowed argument is lent to the Option, Ok/Result or tuple carrier built there. On its s1: case memory_semantics/carrier_argument_is_lent_not_moved runs Option, Folder?, Named?, Result and tuple under --checked-alloc at o0/o1/o2 (each handle open across two calls, closed once); cases filter _argument_: 26 PASS, 1 known-failing #5454 unrelated; golden Types 210/210; LaneCheck CHECK OK on BuildExpr and BuildTypes.

cards.title: Web builds ship a 4.4 MB rt.wasm: the hello bundle grew 6.1x over its gate baseline
cards.body: Found by PortsLead-2 porting Tools/perf/WebBundleCheck.jet (#6035 c3) on seed a0_033 at dev 3e4998fcca. jet build --target=web now writes .jet/build/ with a second partition, rt.wasm (4,437,521 bytes), named in web.manifest.json. Bundle bytes (app.wasm + rt.wasm + app.js + jet_dom_runtime.js): hello 4,484,465 (baseline 729,206), counter 4,484,612 (baseline 798,637), todo 4,484,474 (baseline 729,395). The baseline's wasm was about 611 KB. The DOM runtime js also grew from 35,834 to 43,654 bytes. Every app pays the whole runtime partition whatever it uses.

log.text: fc0de36c7c: Tools/perf/WebBundleCheck.jet now counts every file web.manifest.json names, rt.wasm included, and keeps the committed byte budgets. Against them it fails honestly: rc=1, 12 size regressions over hello, counter and todo. It passes (rc=0, 3 workloads) only against a scratch baseline at today's sizes, which is not committed.

criteria.text: Root found: why rt.wasm carries 4.4 MB (whole-runtime partition, no dead-code removal, debug sections, or table literals), named with a size breakdown by section and by runtime module.

The web bundles of hello, counter and todo are at or below their WebBundleCheck baseline (729,206 / 798,637 / 729,395 bytes total), measured by the gate with every file web.manifest.json names counted, and the gate passes on its unchanged byte budgets.
The web tier keeps one meaning (I9): the same examples' goldens pass on web after the size fix.

cards.title: Test results are reused across runs: the full profile and the admit skip rows whose compiler and inputs are unchanged
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card this; no cached or incremental work now.

Measured: a fresh-clone `jet test Compiler --profile full` took about 2 hours (engine 4 min, cold toolchain fetch 45 min, suites 64 min). The release admit then reruns every suite for the same commit, about 40 more minutes. Corpus rows total 248 CPU minutes (golden 160, cases 79, ui 9).

criteria.text: The admit of a commit reuses the full-profile results recorded for that exact commit and compiler identity, and reruns only rows whose inputs changed.

A row's reuse key covers its source files, fixtures, the compiler identity, the Prelude and Core it builds against, and the environment it reads. A change to any of them reruns that row and the rows that depend on it, and a targeted test proves each part of the key.
With an unchanged tree, a second `jet test Compiler --profile full` finishes in under 1 minute and reports the same rows and verdicts as the first.

cards.title: The compiler's default thread count is fixed at start from the instantaneous load, so a build started on a busy host runs on one core
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card this; do not build now.

`jet_cli_default_threads` (Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Request.jet) reads procs_running from /proc/stat once at start and drops to one thread when the host is busy. The thread count then never grows. In the full profile, the hosted Jetpack engine build started beside four package runs took about 13 minutes on one core; it took 184 s when it started on a quiet host.

criteria.text: A build's parallel width follows free cores while it runs, instead of being fixed by the load at start.
The hosted Jetpack engine build started beside 8 concurrent package runs finishes within 1.5x of its quiet-host wall time, measured on the batch machine and recorded with the commit.
The quiet-host self-build wall time does not regress (compared on the same machine and commit range as #6527).

cards.title: core.crypto SHA-256 runs at 45-50 MB/s; a scalar native implementation does about 500 MB/s and SHA-NI about 2 GB/s
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: card this; do not build now.

Measured on #6592: pure-Jet core.crypto SHA-256 runs at about 45-50 MB/s at O1 and O2, and a hand-unrolled Jet version gives the same speed. The backend has no SHA-NI path. Toolchain install hashes about 450 MB, so hashing alone costs about 9 s per pass on one thread.

log.text: Measured on #6592 (PortsLead-2, 2026-11-07): pure-Jet core.crypto SHA-256 at 45-50 MB/s at O1 and O2; a hand-unrolled Jet version is no faster. Parallel hashing of the 442 MB toolchain tree still takes 16.6 s, the largest remaining fetch phase after fsync.

criteria.text: An asm-parity cell under Tools/perf/asm-parity is the SHA-256 ceiling reference: SHA-NI where the CPU reports it, and the best scalar code otherwise.
core.crypto SHA-256 at O1 and O2 meets that ceiling (Jet/ceiling at most 1.00 in cycles and bytes) on both paths, and beats every gauntlet peer.
The digest is identical on every tier (O0, O1, O2 and web), held by the existing SHA-256 conformance vectors.

cards.title: Compiler/build.jet declares the whole project: every artifact, generated table, toolchain, chain stage and profile is one build graph
cards.body:
Owner direction 2026-11-07: make full use of Jet's customizable build function for this project; card it, do not build it now.

Today Compiler/build.jet declares one target, the jet executable. Everything else is assembled outside the build graph, each piece in its own serial step: the self-host chain (Tools/agent/chain/chain.sh), the runtime pack (cc-pack and pack, with musl found through JET_PACK_MUSL_LIB), the Jetpack engine (Jetpack/Bootstrap/Assemble.jet, then a separate jet build inside the packages suite: 3 min quiet, 13 min under load), the generated registry tables (regenerated by hand and checked at precommit; a stale CoreEnumRows failed a landing on 2026-11-07), and the test and release tools.

The Build API already offers add_executable, add_library, add_test, add_package, add_publish, add_install, add_doc, action, generate, toolchain, probe, signing and embed, the registered build options, and core.build graph receipts with receipt_diff.

log.text: SpeedLead: build.jet cannot list a folder at plan time (b.find returns files only, walks into .jet, and is not recorded as a plan input; #4833 known-failing). So c6 keeps STAGE_FOLDERS and STAGE_FILES as a kernel.tsv row, plus a tests/guards check that every top-level entry of a split stage package (except Generated and dot entries) is listed, so the list cannot go stale silently. The .jet/deps alias hole touches 5 to 6 files in two packages and is now its own criterion; c6 does not depend on it.

c6 layout ruling (Main): the build-graph contract stays. SpeedLead moves the 4 kept generated sources into <pkg>/Generated/ (JetFoundation PreludeMarkers, JetSema PreludeDerives and PreludeUnits, JetLexer KeywordSpans). Stages read those packages top-level entries minus Generated/, derived at plan time, not a hand list, plus the kept files through .reads. The rejected alternative (narrow folders plus about 105 explicit files) would be a stale-prone closed list. Owner Q20 is withdrawn. Validator defect found by SpeedLead: both validators compare spelled folder paths, so a dependency bound at .jet/deps on the same real folder escapes the rule. It is fixed in the same patch by comparing resolved folders, with a #Test.

c6 blocker (SpeedLead): the self-host stages read the 17 Compiler folders whole, and the build-graph rule (Graph.jet:109-121, Jetpack Validation.jet:173-177, spec.md:5050, E3502) refuses step outputs inside them: the runtime step outputs under JetCli/.jet/build, and the c5 kept outputs (Prelude copies, KeywordSpans.jet). Main ruling: an output under a .jet or .git part being outside the folder read is a defect fix (one meaning with the folder snapshot, Cache.jet build_folder_skipped). SpeedLead lands it with a BuildGraphRules #Test. Allowing an output inside a read folder when the reader also reads it changes the spec contract, so it is owner Q20. SpeedLead is costing the keep-the-rule alternative.

c4 landed on dev as 42d3bedfe8 (SpeedLead lane-commit; precommit census on a0_039: check, build, runtime from jet build Compiler, self-check, Core self-check). It is the owner (A) stopgap shape (host cc plus musl), removed under #6687. On master as merge cb5a55054d, the exact tested dev tree. A cherry-pick conflicted in the generated Docs/spec/safety.md and would have given master an unbuilt tree, so the merge also carries 1f8f46177e (#6690) and 775f3b07ae (#6686). Main updated its precommit census for trees where jet build Compiler writes the pack. c5 (generated tables as kept build outputs) is next, and c6 (s2 and s3 as build actions) is approved.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 on commit 4: "A as stopgap but removed when we have 100% jet." So c4 lands in the (A) shape: a fresh clone builds with the dev shell or a host cc plus static musl, and ReuseSeedRuntime.jet is deleted. The host C requirement goes when #6687 (no C dependency) closes; the fresh-clone criterion there proves it. Landing waits for a0_039 to be the current seed, because a0_038 rejects the new build.jet (Build.folder arity). SpeedLead holds the tested patch (LaneCheck CHECK OK on dev c884e9421c).

Commit 4 is held for an owner question (2026-11-08). Under c4, `jet build Compiler` builds the runtime pack, so it needs cc plus a static musl libc.a. A fresh clone with neither stops at the probes, so bootstrap.md "From a fresh clone: no Nix" (seed build plus ReuseSeedRuntime) stops being true. Using the toolchain own jet cc inside build steps needs new public build API: steps run sandboxed (bwrap, cleared env, no net) and see only the builder folder and probe results, not the Hangar cc pack. The pack also lacks nm (RuntimePack symbol gate) and ships compiler-rt instead of libgcc.a/libgcc_eh.a. Main ruling, commit 4: `.file(b.found(p))` accepts a find_program result too (it already accepts find_folder), within the approved D-BUILD-GRAPH1/D-BUILD-TREES1 surface, so no ballot. The found program gets the same sandbox visibility it gets as a step tool; the action key covers its bytes and its probe fact; the old refusal and its snapshot go; a cc case proves it. The runtime pack logic moves to Compiler/Toolchain/RuntimePack.jet, run as one b.run step. Also fixed: staged inputs lost the exec bit.

Commit 3 landed as 74bbf2a07c (the find_folder probe, with no caller; E3505 with a UI snapshot). Main decided commit 4: flatten jet-runtime/ to fixed paths, with the identity in native.key. It is an internal pack format, one cutover across the CLI lookup, ReuseSeedRuntime, the chain store, the pack cache and publishing, with no fallback reader; the alternative was a new public step.output_folder API (I8). The vendored C is reached through source-less foreign packages at Core/Vendor/Sqlite3 and Core/Vendor/Mbedtls (not a Core/package.jet, which would mark Core as its own project); this needs a side-effect census first. A flake.nix LIBRARY_PATH export is allowed only with a host glibc-link proof.

Owner ruling 2026-11-08 (asked via Main): Compiler/build.jet builds jet with Core embedded, the committed generated tables (D-BUILD-ROWS1 = A, kept: true) and the runtime pack (jet-runtime: Core/Vendor C compiled with cc, static musl linked) as one complete toolchain. Main 2026-11-08 02:00, BuildLead final handoff (slot ended). Landed: C4 profiles 3af734e9cb; step 1 b.run/b.found/action_timeout ccf9915f44; b.action and b.legacy retired 74942e812c; step 2 b.host/b.jet/one parallel graph c9c3ce97a6; gate fix 8a85d45051 (a b.jet() step gets the running compiler's identity); step 4 receipts, times and jet inspect build --times 64f57f1583; step 5 b.dependency(name).file(path) 509708b651; step 6 b.image(target) a749167d57; step 7 a step never overwrites a file no build made 4361eec2f4; closed-list kernel rows ec519cce83. BuildLead builds it, in this order: b.run with declared inputs and outputs and Duration timeouts; b.host and b.jet; the one-graph executor; times.json; b.dependency().file; b.image and b.found. b.run replaces b.action in all 51 callers, with no alias.
