attempts: Define structural declaration/index order, independent of initializer spelling, reassignment time and physical layout.
designAway.result: No runtime acquisition ledger; state clearly that reverse order means reverse structural positions.

designAway.loss: A partial move might clean a field twice or falsely reorder its destination.
attempts: Apply order only to still-owned fields at each existing cleanup point and leave moved bindings under ordinary local law.
designAway.result: No new move permissions or lifetime changes; exactly-once ownership remains shared law.

decisions.title: Capitalized code paths, lowercase imports
decisions.situation: Jet programmers currently meet two folder styles: capitalized words in the compiler and lowercase words in the standard library. You asked for every code folder and file to use PascalCase, which capitalizes each word and keeps acronyms fully capitalized. This ballot records that direction and decides whether imports change too. We recommend keeping imports lowercase, so existing code reads the same while folders become uniform.
decisions.gist: Should code folders and files be capitalized while imports stay lowercase?
decisions.lesson: PascalCase capitalizes each word, as in MathLibPure. Acronyms are names made from initials, such as JSON, and keep their capitals. An import tells Jet which file supplies code; its dotted name need not copy the file's capitalization.
decisions.explainer: One naming rule covers Jet's own code, user projects, and published packages. The examples show the same three files under every option. Shared work: rename paths safely, update tools and references, and reject names that collide on another operating system.
decisions.story: Maya copies a lowercase library folder into her project, then sees capitalized compiler folders and wonders which style her package should follow.
decisions.inWild:
// Jet today: two styles for code paths
Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/AST/Items.jet
Core/text/fmt.jet
use core.text.fmt as fmt
decisions.detail:
Owner instruction, 2026-10-05: 'all paths in Jet code should stay PascalCase with capital acronyms, so Core/**/runtime should be Core/**/Runtime/**'. Main reports the owner has chosen A and supplied implementation card #4613, c0itvqcw. This payload remains OPEN for the owner's recorded vote; it is not a ratification or a Tower write.

What needs a vote: D-ONCE-CASE1=A already settles one naming lexicon across source, CLI, manifest keys, and file names. Fixed acronym casing is settled by D-ACRO-CASE1=A and D-ACRO-LEX1=A. They do not specify this complete directory/import mapping. This ballot records the owner's path direction and makes that mapping explicit, rather than reopening the lexicon.

Observed inventory, 2026-10-05: Core has 46 immediate area directories, all lowercase. Examples are Core/text/fmt.jet:1-3 and Core/math/math.jet:1-11. Compiler and Jetpack predominantly use PascalCase source directories and files. Examples: Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/AST/Items.jet, Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Collections.jet:1-11, and Jetpack/Foundation/Source/TreeHash.jet:1-9.

'Already PascalCase' is not universal: Compiler/JetCli/package.jet:1-11 and Compiler/JetCli/main.jet are lowercase exceptions that the cutover must also rename. Bootstrap helpers such as assemble.mjs are not .jet source files.

Ported units are staged separately, not present in the inspected root Core tree. RuntimeLead identified .agent-worktrees/idiom-runtime on idiom/runtime at 1833b8ca2, with units under Core/<area>/runtime/<snake_case>.jet. Inspected file: .agent-worktrees/idiom-runtime/Core/math/runtime/top_math_lib_pure.jet:1-8. It imports core.math.runtime.kernel_complex and core.math.runtime.kernel_float_policy.

Runtime wiring is staged in .agent-worktrees/runtime-wiring at 2acfe41a7. There, crates/jet-foundation/src/CoreSourceParts.rs:70 maps core.math.runtime.top_math_lib_pure to Core/math/runtime/top_math_lib_pure.jet. crates/jet-sema/src/CoreSourceTexts.rs:120 embeds that path. Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/CoreSources.jet:127 mirrors it. Handoff: $JET_STATE_ROOT/scratch/RuntimeWiring/HANDOFF.md:3-6,15-32.

Source module names are lowercase dotted, with snake_case inside multi-word segments. Core/text/fmt.jet:3 names core.text.fmt; Core/math/math.jet:2 names core.math. The staged runtime example is core.math.runtime.top_math_lib_pure.

The blessed abbreviation list in D-API-LEN1=A is closed: len, fmt, args, env, mem; additions require a ballot. They render Len, Fmt, Args, Env, Mem, not LEN or FMT: abbreviations are not acronyms. This ballot does not authorize new abbreviations or rename public domains. Other ratified vocabulary rows remain authoritative in the single lexicon.

D-ACRO-LEX1=A treats initial-letter names as acronyms regardless of pronunciation: JSON, SQL, HTTP, CLI, ABI, HTML, CSV, OS, IO, DB, FS, GPU, JS, TLS, SMTP, IP. Contractions such as Wasm and Bindgen stay ordinary words. D-ACRO-CASE1=A joins an acronym to an ordinary word, as HTTPClient. Touching acronyms require an underscore, as HTTP_API. That rare underscore is the existing PascalCase law, not a new path exemption.

Scope is Jet source paths, not every directory in a repository. Include directories from each declared Jet source-tree root, and every .jet file stem. Keep the .jet extension lowercase. Checkout locations, dependency caches, non-source assets, foreign source trees, and helper-file extensions keep their own contracts. Source folders gain no per-project casing overrides. Package names and dependency aliases retain their logical-name law; they are not raw filesystem names.

options.name: Capitalize paths, keep imports lowercase
options.detail: Every Jet code directory and .jet file stem uses PascalCase with capital acronyms. Imports stay lowercase dotted, with underscores separating words inside a segment. Users write use core.text.fmt as fmt or use core.encoding.json as json. Their own app.http_client import finds App/HTTPClient.jet under the declared source root. The same rule applies to published packages and their source files.
options.technical:
Exact forward mapping: split a logical module name on dots into path segments. Split each segment on underscores into word tokens. Look up each token in the shared naming lexicon. Emit its fixed acronym spelling when it is an acronym; otherwise uppercase its first letter and preserve its canonical remaining letters. Digit suffixes stay attached: utf8 becomes UTF8 and base64 becomes Base64.

Join tokens without separators except between adjacent acronym tokens, where the ratified underscore is retained. Join segments with '/', then append '.jet' for a source file. Examples: core.text.fmt maps to Core/Text/Fmt.jet. core.math.runtime.math_lib_pure maps to Core/Math/Runtime/MathLibPure.jet. core.encoding.json maps to Core/Encoding/JSON.jet. app.http_client maps to App/HTTPClient.jet. app.http_api_client maps to App/HTTP_APIClient.jet.

Apply declared source-root and package-root resolution before segment conversion. A dependency alias names its resolved package, not a directory guessed from its alias. Keep existing root-module entry selection: core.math still selects its registered owning source, now Core/Math/Math.jet. Do not replace the package loader with an assumed one-file-per-package model.

Reverse generation splits PascalCase word boundaries and capital runs using D-ACRO-CASE1=A, honors underscore boundaries, and emits lowercase tokens joined with underscores. Reject paths whose reverse/forward round trip is not canonical. Do not scan case-insensitively for another file or invent a per-directory translation table.

The requested MathLibPure example removes the Rust layout prefix top_ during port-name cleanup. This is a lexical rename, not capitalization: top_math_lib_pure would mechanically become TopMathLibPure. Rename that logical unit to math_lib_pure and its imports/generated aliases together; the resulting lowercase import is core.math.runtime.math_lib_pure. No retired alias remains.

Other lexical changes must be approved lexicon rows, not guesses by the casing function. Runtime paths remain private to Core; users import core.math, never core.math.runtime.math_lib_pure.

User package manifests become Package.jet; the already-ratified entry stem run becomes Run.jet, without reopening the canonical entry stem. Compiler main.jet exceptions migrate to the canonical entry contract, not a second entry convention. Update manifest discovery, explicit path imports, entry paths, and dependency paths. Literal paths show real capitalization: use "App/HTTPClient.jet" as client. Logical imports and ordinary value aliases stay lowercase.

Portability: reject files or directories differing only by case, including JSON.jet versus Json.jet and Runtime versus runtime, before reading or publishing a package. Compare all source entries with the package portability case-fold rule even on Linux. Never let an OS choose between logical targets. Canonical-name errors show the supplied import, expected real path, and actionable rename. This covers case-insensitive macOS/Windows configurations without assuming every installation is case-insensitive.

Tooling consumes one mapping function and lexicon, shared or generated into both compiler halves. jet fmt formats logical imports to canonical lowercase spelling but does not silently move filesystem entries. Rename/refactor tooling migrates directories and files, updates literal references and generated rows, and reports its plan before applying it.

Case-only moves use a temporary intermediate name after collision preflight; the final tree keeps no temporary names. Diagnostics, completion, navigation, and package publication show the same logical import and physical path. No new CLI verb or flag is minted here.

One greenfield cutover covers Core including staged Runtime units, tests/Tests and fixtures, Examples, Compiler, Jetpack, and all Jet source-root directories. Update generators, source manifests, include_str paths, embedded source tables, bootstrap rows, both loaders, golden/UI paths, package fixtures, commands, and documentation examples together.

Preserve non-Jet harness directory contracts outside Jet source roots. Regenerate derived files from existing authoritative homes; remove obsolete lowercase paths, lookup fallbacks, and aliases. A preserves D-SHAPE-CASE1=C's lowercase module-path rule and extends the settled lexicon to the owner's path contract.

options.name: Capitalize paths and imports
options.detail: The same files use PascalCase, and every dotted module segment uses that spelling too. Users write use Core.Text.Fmt as fmt and use Core.Encoding.JSON as json. A project's logical App.HTTPClient names App/HTTPClient.jet. Ordinary local aliases can stay lowercase. Readers see matching words and capitals in imports and folders.
options.technical:
Use A's lexicon, acronym seams, file scope, Package.jet/Run.jet contract, port-prefix cleanup, portability checks, and migration machinery. Dotted module segments become PascalCase, including MathLibPure and HTTPClient. Core-only runtime imports become Core.Math.Runtime.MathLibPure. This explicitly amends D-SHAPE-CASE1=C for module paths, not functions, fields, or local aliases. Rewrite every logical import, module declaration, module reference, registry key, and generated source name alongside the filesystem cutover.

Errors teach use Core.Text.Fmt as fmt. jet fmt enforces PascalCase module segments; rename tools move files and update callers. Dependency aliases used as module roots need the same module-casing amendment; manifest identity strings otherwise keep their existing contract. Case-fold collisions are rejected before package publication exactly as in A.

options.name: Capitalize only new folders
options.detail: New directories, including the runtime folder, use PascalCase; existing lowercase library directories and files stay unchanged. Existing imports stay lowercase. This minimizes changes to paths already named by scripts and examples, but newcomers must learn which folders predate the rule.
options.technical:
The same three files keep their existing lowercase area and file spellings; only runtime becomes Runtime. New code directories are PascalCase, while old paths and user-package files remain accepted as written. This narrows the owner's every-path instruction and retains two conventions. The loader needs registered paths for old code and lexicon mapping for new directories, rather than A's universal round-trip rule.

Case-fold collision rejection still applies to all packages; old spelling never permits JSON.jet and json.jet beside each other. jet fmt leaves existing imports alone. Rename tooling changes runtime references and corresponding source manifests only. Core/text, Core/math, tests, Examples, and their existing generator paths avoid the full casing migration.

Diagnostics identify the registered real path rather than claiming universal capitalization. A/B's MathLibPure port-prefix cleanup is not performed: the staged unit retains top_math_lib_pure.jet and its logical name.

Core/text/fmt.jet
Core/math/Runtime/top_math_lib_pure.jet

decisions.title: List dependencies once; Jet prepares the project
decisions.situation: A dependency is a library your program needs, and an environment is the project's prepared set of libraries and tools. Today, listing Jet's command-line and data libraries still leaves a small project unable to run without separate setup. Decide whether listing libraries should be enough, require extra setup, or work automatically only for Jet's own libraries. We recommend automatic preparation with saved exact versions, offline reuse, and explicit controls for experts.
decisions.gist: Should listing dependencies be enough to run, build, and check a project?
decisions.lesson: A lockfile saves exact versions and checks their contents. Automatic setup need not mean automatic upgrades: reuse the saved choices, work offline when their files are available, and let experts choose named environments or disable preparation.
decisions.explainer: All examples use the same tiny project: two declared libraries, two ordinary imports, and a program printing ready. Shared work includes locks, verified contents, trust checks, and clear errors. Neither extra setup nor bundling removes that work.
decisions.story: Maya lists two Jet libraries, then discovers that her first program needs a separate setup declaration before it can run.
decisions.inWild:
# uv documentation: automatic lock and sync before execution
uv run app.py
# uv.lock records exact dependencies; no manual environment activation
uv run --locked --offline app.py
decisions.detail:
Owner gate, not an implementation choice: the owner directly authorized D-DEPS-ENV1 on 2026-10-05. Main filed #4614, c0wlxl44, for this gate and linked #4275. The payload is ready for posting OPEN, not a vote or ratification. The author performs no Tower writes. #4275 stays a ratified-contract implementation card; this separate card carries the new default and its implementation.

GoldenFix5's reported witness is ground truth, not rerun here: package.jet lists deps: {cli: "0.1.0", data: "0.1.0"}, but no explicit environment exists. Preparation cannot supply these first-party libraries, and compilation remains blocked. The same demo Package identity and run source remain unchanged in all three options. These are proposed outcomes, not observed successful runs.

Current citations moved since the witness. Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:4961-4974 (S52) separates dependency declarations from source/environment facts and names the single .jet/lock. Lines 4977-4993 (D-ECO-ENV1) require one checked Environment output but defer its schema and lifecycle. Lines 1918-1920 (U17) keep ordinary use. These rules do not choose whether deps synthesize a default Environment.

Docs/spec/spec.md:1695-1704 explicitly requires realized libraries and says compilation does not realize on demand; E0983 diagnoses an unrealized declared library. Therefore A is a named amendment to the command boundary, not a claim that existing law already permits build/check preparation. The compiler itself still consumes verified realized inputs and never resolves an import by network lookup.

Docs/spec/reference/jetpack-epoch5.md:12-20 requires one graph and separates inspection from realization. Lines 86-101 define exact lock facts and strict offline refusal. Lines 113-123 require checked membership and select one environment without sibling merging. crates/jetpack/src/CLI/run_enter_dev.rs:1664-1666,1839-1852 uses the declared project environment; ad-hoc -p packages are a separate explicit input, not package deps inference.

Compiler/JetCli/Source/Cli/Commands.jet:878-884 records D-RUN-PREPARE1=A and the existing --no-prepare escape for run. A extends that preparation boundary and escape to build/check. Docs/spec/reference/network-policy.md:16-28 forbids incidental networking. A narrowly authorizes declared dependency acquisition at the visible preparation boundary; it does not grant network effects to compilation, build actions, or user code.

Later law overrides S52's old reserved-file model. Docs/spec/syntax-decisions.md:6829-6833 (D-ECO-FILEROOT1) reserves only package.jet; lines 7127-7129 (D-NAME-ROLEMOD1) make ecosystem entries typed values, not module env declarations. All options preserve both. env.jet means an ordinary, explicitly included Config contribution, not another root or reserved authority. Examples/jetpack/epoch5/config/dev.jet:1-10 demonstrates Config and Environment values.

Research, consulted 2026-10-05: Cargo separates human requirements in Cargo.toml from exact selections in Cargo.lock, generated at first build and reused thereafter. Its book recommends committing the lock and explicit cargo update. This is the right separation: declaration is not installation state. Source: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/cargo-toml-vs-cargo-lock.html .

Cargo build compiles dependencies without an environment declaration; --locked rejects missing or changed locks, --offline forbids network, and --frozen combines both. Its manual warns that offline resolution without a lock can choose different versions from online resolution. A adopts automatic preparation and strict replay, not cache-dependent reselection. Source: https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/commands/cargo-build.html .

Go downloads modules as needed during ordinary commands. go.mod fixes requirements under minimal version selection; go.sum verifies downloaded contents, rather than acting as Cargo's exact selected-tree lock. Since Go 1.16, builds default to refusing needed go.mod edits. A borrows automatic acquisition and content verification, while retaining Jet's single exact lock. Source: https://go.dev/ref/mod (Automatic updates, Minimal version selection, go mod download, go.sum files).

Go's GOPATH-era versioning was a documented wrong turn: Russ Cox reports too many competing add-on solutions by mid-2016 after versioning was left unsolved. Modules integrated version awareness and allowed work outside GOPATH. Its current manual also warns that checked-in go.work can make CI test unintended dependency versions. A avoids global ambient dependency state and hidden workspace substitutions. Sources: https://go.dev/blog/versioning-proposal ; https://go.dev/ref/mod#workspaces .

JavaScript's package.json plus automatically generated package-lock.json records the exact installed tree for teammates and CI. Without that record, intervening compatible releases can change the tree. npm ci rejects a missing or mismatched lock instead of updating it. A adopts always-written locks and strict CI, without requiring beginners to learn a second setup command. Sources: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-lock-json ; https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-ci .

The no-lockfile lesson is version drift, not a promise that a lock preserves availability. npm's left-pad post-mortem reports 273 unpublished packages, hundreds of failures per minute, and 2.5 hours of disruption. Some dependents requested exact 0.0.3 and still failed. A therefore retains verified local objects for offline replay; a lock alone cannot retrieve deleted bytes. Source: https://blog.npmjs.org/post/141577284765/kik-left-pad-and-npm .

pnpm installs a workspace through one dependency model, retains still-valid locked versions, and defaults to frozen-lock behavior in CI when a lock exists. --offline fails on missing store bytes, unlike --prefer-offline, which may fetch. A makes strict offline and exact CI behavior unambiguous and never confuses a warm cache with a lock. Source: https://pnpm.io/cli/install .

Bun writes bun.lock on install and recommends committing it. Its migration preserves original npm/pnpm/Yarn locks; npm version-1 locks cannot be migrated and trigger a warning before new resolution. That is real migration friction, not a reason for multiple Jet locks. A reuses .jet/lock and its existing reader rather than inventing an implicit-environment lock format. Source: https://bun.sh/docs/pm/lockfile .

Python separates the dependency list from environment isolation. venv creates an isolated, disposable directory; its documentation warns that absolute interpreter paths make moved environments non-portable. pip's repeatable-install guide separately requires transitive pins, hashes, and locally retained wheels for stronger replay and availability. A reconstructs the environment from graph plus verified objects, never from a copied host directory. Sources: https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html ; https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/topics/repeatable-installs/ .

Poetry already creates environments automatically and installs from pyproject.toml plus poetry.lock; poetry add installs dependencies too. uv goes further: uv run automatically locks and syncs, prefers existing pins, and exposes --locked, --frozen, and --no-sync. A takes uv's integrated run workflow, but rejects stale plans instead of offering an unchecked frozen bypass. Sources: https://python-poetry.org/docs/basic-usage/ ; https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/sync/ .

Adoption data: the PSF/JetBrains 2024 survey collected over 30,000 responses in October-November 2024. Reported environment-isolation usage was venv 62%, Poetry 18%, uv 11%; dependency-tool usage was pip 74%, Poetry 20%, uv 12%. uv launched that February. These are multiple-choice survey shares, not population estimates or proof that automatic environments caused adoption. Source: https://lp.jetbrains.com/python-developers-survey-2024/ (Python Packaging, Methodology).

Deno keeps ordinary imports, a shared cache, automatic deno.lock versions and integrity checks, opt-in dependency scripts, and --cached-only network refusal. It documents strict CI refusal on missing or outdated locks. Its standard library is distributed through JSR, illustrating that first-party libraries can retain ordinary package identity rather than being tied to the runtime release. Sources: https://docs.deno.com/runtime/packages/ ; https://docs.deno.com/runtime/fundamentals/modules/ .

Nix flakes automatically generate flake.lock with exact revisions and content hashes for direct and indirect inputs. Named outputs and follows/overrides provide expert graph control. A adopts exact graph locking and expert projections without requiring a second environment recipe for a two-library application. A lock still requires cached source/output objects to work offline. Source: https://nix.dev/manual/nix/latest/command-ref/new-cli/nix3-flake (Flake inputs, Lock files, --offline).

Swift Package Manager automatically resolves on swift run/build and records selected versions in Package.resolved. Its CI guide reuses that file and requires explicit update for newer eligible versions. Its failure guide explains conflicting requirements and disappeared package versions instead of silently substituting another library. A uses the same list-to-command workflow and explains the dependency chain on failure.

Swift sources, read directly from the official documentation repository. AddingDependencies: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swiftlang/swift-package-manager/main/Sources/PackageManagerDocs/Documentation.docc/Dependencies/AddingDependencies.md . ContinuousIntegration: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swiftlang/swift-package-manager/main/Sources/PackageManagerDocs/Documentation.docc/ContinuousIntegration.md . ResolvingDependencyFailures: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swiftlang/swift-package-manager/main/Sources/PackageManagerDocs/Documentation.docc/Dependencies/ResolvingDependencyFailures.md .

Zig's build.zig.zon declares URL plus content hash, or a local path. The shipped template says builds need no internet after recursive fetching; content hash is authority and URL is only a mirror. Its fetcher checks the shared cache and validates bytes. Its 0.14 release documents naming-rule breakage and unnecessary legacy fetches during hash-format migration. A borrows content authority, not a new hash/name migration.

Zig sources. Shipped template: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ziglang/zig/0.14.0/lib/init/build.zig.zon . Fetcher: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ziglang/zig/0.14.0/src/Package/Fetch.zig . Migration notes: https://ziglang.org/download/0.14.0/release-notes.html#New-Package-Hash-Format .

Evidence limits: these sources establish shipped mechanisms, documented failure modes, and one survey's adoption shares. No controlled, comparable friction timings for these workflows were established here. No Jet speedup or adoption prediction is claimed. Best-of-all-worlds synthesis is a design judgment: automatic isolated setup, exact saved choices, verified offline reuse, strict CI, and one expert graph avoid the documented mistakes together.

options.name: Automatic setup, exact replay
options.detail: Listing dependencies implies a default environment. run, build, and check prepare it before compilation, including fetching missing declared libraries and saving their exact versions. Experts can name environments, change sources or pins, apply overrides, or disable preparation. First-party and third-party libraries follow the same rule.
options.technical:
Default projection: when no explicit environment selection applies, construct the dependency-only Environment from the selected Package graph. It contains declared dependency closure, not invented tools, services, secrets, jobs, hooks, or managed files. Use the existing checked planner, trust gates, provider acquisition, Hangar realization, and lock writer. There is no second resolver, generated source declaration, or private installation database.

Command boundary: run/build/check and explicit jet env --prep accept this projection. They prepare before the loader checks imports, then consume the verified result once. Read-only inspection, formatting, language-server background analysis, and raw compiler entry points do not fetch or write locks. A missing environment file never causes E0983 by itself. No-deps manifest-free single-file behavior remains unchanged.

Always-on .jet/lock: initial successful preparation records exact direct/transitive selectors, source authority, contents, plan and target identities, and existing receipts. Retain still-valid selections; do not refresh the index or upgrade because a newer version exists. A declaration change may extend the lock with only its required changed closure. Explicit update remains the upgrade operation; the existing explicit #auto policy remains an expert exception.

Local-first replay is offline by default when the locked closure is available. No registry probes, remote freshness refreshes, or optional cache requests occur then. On a cold miss, automatic preparation may acquire only the declared graph from authorized sources, visibly announced before acquisition. This is the narrow network-boundary amendment. It never authorizes dependency hooks or arbitrary build network effects beyond existing policy.

Strict --offline never contacts any network and never chooses a different version to fit local cache contents. Without a lock, it may create one only from exact declarations and complete verified local metadata/objects. Otherwise fail E1276 and name the missing package and digest when known. Initial cold acquisition cannot physically be offline; the ballot promises offline replay, not absent bytes.

--locked rejects a missing/stale lock before mutation, but can realize its exact missing bytes when not offline. CI=1 makes run/build/check require this same unchanged-lock contract automatically; explicit --locked works on every runner. CI never bootstraps, repairs or updates the lock. Prepare and commit .jet/lock before CI; for an air gap, supply verified local objects and use --locked --offline.

Expert escape: extend existing --no-prepare from run to build/check. It disables acquisition, realization and dependency-lock writes, but still requires matching verified inputs. E0983 names an unrealized library, its declaration, and the remedy: run jet env --prep, or remove --no-prepare. It is not --offline, which still permits local realization, nor permission to bypass locks or trust.

Named environments: explicit --env wins; otherwise reuse the ratified checked environment default/sole-candidate selection when environments exist. Multiple candidates without a default fail with sorted names; never pick a sibling arbitrarily. Explicit environments use the Package's dependency edges plus their checked facts through ordinary graph composition. They cannot remove or silently replace a declared dependency. Conflicts fail before realization.

Sources, pins and overrides remain typed Config facts in package.jet or its explicitly included ordinary contributions. env.jet is a conventional optional filename, not an authority. Pins already allowed in deps do not require a separate file. No module env syntax returns. Default projection and named environment projections share source identity, trust, lock and receipts.

Workspaces: retain the declared member index and root-owned single .jet/lock. A selected member prepares only its required dependency closure, including addressed local members, while retaining unrelated lock entries unchanged. Do not fetch sibling outputs or start workspace services. Resolve remote monorepos index-first, preserving sparse subtree acquisition and existing identity, containment and ambiguity checks.

Errors show the declaring member, dependency/version, chosen source, and action to fix the cause. Offline missing bytes remain E1276; content mismatch remains E1204 and never rewrites the expected hash. Locked missing/stale state refuses before writes, with a declaration-to-lock difference and explicit preparation/update hint. Source ambiguity, version conflict and denied trust remain their existing located diagnostics, not a generic missing-env error.

Scope amendments: D-RUN-PREPARE1's frontend delegation extends to build/check and deps-only projects. Amend spec.md's compilation boundary text to distinguish preparation from compiler import lookup. Narrow network-policy.md's local-command rule only for manifest-requested dependency preparation. Preserve U17 ordinary imports, U7 standalone use, D-ECO-FILEROOT1, D-NAME-ROLEMOD1, strict offline, one graph, and existing trust/effect policy.

options.name: Always declare setup
options.detail: Every Package with dependencies must explicitly declare an environment. jet new and jet add create and include the conventional setup file. Dependencies still appear only once; the environment refers to that checked graph. Hand-written manifests must add the declaration too.
options.technical:
Require an explicit typed Environment for every deps-bearing Package before preparation or compilation. jet new/add scaffold an included ordinary env.jet Config, not a reserved root or module env declaration. The proposed minimal environment has no extra tools and refers to the Package dependency graph without repeating cli/data versions.

Preserve run's existing explicit-environment delegation. build/check remain explicit prepared-environment consumers rather than preparing automatically. jet env --prep performs preparation; docs teach that command before build/check. Missing declaration fails early, naming deps and showing the typed Config/include fix or jet add scaffold route. Missing realized bytes still report E0983 with the preparation command.

Use the same single lock, exact-version retention, strict --offline/E1276, integrity/E1204, trust and workspace identity rules as A. CI requires a matching committed lock and explicit environment preparation; preparation and compile are separate visible steps. No cache-driven reselection, automatic upgrades, or environment activation is inferred from import names.

Experts control all setup explicitly. --no-prepare keeps run's existing escape and does not bypass verified inputs. Named environments, sources, pins and overrides use ordinary Config composition and one selected environment. Every deps-bearing member requires an environment declaration or an explicit shared graph reference; there are no automatically created per-member defaults.

Tradeoff: the setup boundary is visibly declared for every project, but copied deps-only examples fail until users know the additional declaration. Scaffolding helps generated projects, not hand-written or independently copied manifests. This is a real preference for explicit state ownership, not a claim that it improves lock reproducibility over A.

options.name: Ship Jet libraries together
options.detail: Jet ships its first-party libraries, so this tiny project needs no prepared environment. Other libraries require an explicit environment, scaffolded by jet new/add. Projects retain dependency declarations and ordinary imports; shipping does not make undeclared libraries ambient.
options.technical:
The Jet distribution includes verified cli/data packages and the first-party dependency closure. A matching declared version resolves from that distribution without Environment realization. Record bundled package digests and toolchain identity in the same .jet/lock before compilation. Bundling is a fulfillment source, not a second compiler namespace or a second lock.

Define first-party membership through the signed distribution inventory, not package-name spelling. Never substitute the installed version when the manifest requests another. A missing bundled first-party version fails with the requested and installed versions and the matching signed distribution remedy. Matching signed cached distributions can supply an older bundle; strict offline never downloads one.

Third-party dependencies follow B: explicit typed Environment, ordinary Config inclusion, preparation before build/check, exact lock, strict offline, trust gates and CI replay. A mixed Package requires the explicit declaration for its third-party closure while bundled libraries remain distribution inputs. Source overrides that leave the signed inventory follow that external dependency path too.

Workspaces share one root lock and retain selected-member boundaries. Each third-party-bearing member needs explicit environment ownership; first-party-only members need none. Named environments and expert --no-prepare still govern external preparation, not access to a verified bundled declared library. First-party libraries do not inject names outside ordinary use.

Tradeoff: first-party teaching examples and fresh offline installations are convenient, but library availability follows distribution inventory. Independent library upgrades need matching distribution content, and adding one external dependency changes the setup model. Bundling must cover supported versions and target artifacts honestly; it cannot mean ignoring version pins or pretending all versions ship.

comparisons.note: One manifest plus automatic exact lock; build handles dependencies without a separate environment declaration.

# Cargo book: first cargo build creates Cargo.lock

recommendation.why: A combines one-step setup with exact saved choices, offline reuse, and full expert control. It avoids forgotten setup and changing dependencies.
gains: One rule for all libraries.
Saved choices; verified offline reuse.
Strict CI and explicit expert control.

whyNot.reason: B makes setup visible, but requires another declaration without stronger reproducibility.
C starts offline, but splits library rules and couples library availability to Jet releases.

recommendation.tradeoff: No lost control: automatic defaults, explicit environments, and a no-preparation escape use one checked graph. Initial downloads remain visible and policy-bound.

decisions.checkInstructions:
Validate this payload with node $JET_STATE_ROOT/ballots/READY/validate.mjs $JET_STATE_ROOT/ballots/READY/D-DEPS-ENV1.json; require exit 0. Validation uses an in-memory snapshot and writes no Tower state. Main posts OPEN on #4614 for the owner's vote; do not implement before ratification.

After the vote, Main verifies the chosen contract end-to-end on the same deps-only demo through run/build/check and jet env --prep. For A, require first acquisition and lock creation, unchanged warm replay with zero network attempts, and no environment source file. Test another ordinary third-party dependency through the same path.

Test strict offline with complete and incomplete verified local closures, with and without lock; never substitute a cached version. Test locked missing/stale refusal without writes, CI=1 immutable locks, exact cold locked acquisition, denied trust/hooks/network effects, corruption/E1204, and source/version conflicts. Required missing-object output is E1276 with the dependency identity.

Test --no-prepare across run/build/check with valid and missing realizations; missing library remains E0983 with the correct remedy. Test explicit named selection, sole/default selection, ambiguous environments, source pins and overrides, and no sibling merging or automatic services. Read-only inspection and background editor checking must not mutate or acquire.

Test one workspace root lock, selected members, local member edges, remote index-first sparse acquisition, subdirectory invocation, and no unrelated member fetching. Test manifest-free no-deps single files unchanged. Update command help, diagnostic registry source and generated projections, spec boundary text, environment docs, lock/offline/network docs, onboarding, examples and golden fixtures for the selected law in one cutover. Frozen Rust references remain evidence, not implementation authority.

options.name: Automatic setup, exact replay
options.gist: List libraries once. Jet prepares, saves exact choices, and reuses them offline.
gains: One rule; no forgotten setup; experts keep control.

options.name: Always declare setup
options.gist: Every dependency project declares its environment; project creation and adding libraries provide it.
gains: Every setup is explicitly declared.
losses: Hand-written projects need another declaration.

options.gist: Jet's libraries work immediately; other libraries still require explicit setup.
gains: Bundled libraries work on a fresh offline installation.
losses: Two setup rules; bundled availability follows Jet releases.

recommendation.why: A combines easy setup, unchanged versions, offline reuse, and expert control without a second declaration or two library rules.
gains: Strict CI: automated builds cannot change the saved choices.

whyNot.reason: B adds setup without stronger reproducibility.
C splits the rules and ties availability to Jet releases.

recommendation.tradeoff: First downloads need available sources; afterward, verified local files suffice. Experts can name environments or use --no-prepare to disable setup.

designAway.loss: Automatic preparation could silently upgrade dependencies.
attempts: Retain exact lock selections and skip remote freshness checks on replay.
Require explicit update; CI rejects missing or changed locks.
designAway.result: Removed: ordinary replay never upgrades; explicit #auto remains an expert policy.

attempts: Project the existing checked dependency graph rather than infer from imports.

designAway.result: Removed: inspectable defaults and explicit facts share the same authority.

designAway.loss: Automatic setup could remove expert control over effects and writes.
attempts: Reuse --no-prepare across the three commands.
Keep strict --offline, immutable --locked, existing trust gates and read-only inspection.
designAway.result: Removed: the user can prohibit preparation, networking and lock mutation independently.

designAway.loss: A lockfile could be mistaken for an offline copy of a dependency.

Keep existing local Hangar retention and object provisioning mechanisms.

decisions.title: [Superseded by D-ROUTE-FILES2; vote there] Capitalized route files, friendly web addresses
decisions.situation: Jet can turn a page file's name into its web address, but capitalizing the file currently capitalizes that address too. The new naming rule would change familiar lowercase addresses and still leave multiword addresses without hyphens. This vote decides how page names and web addresses fit together. We recommend automatic lowercase, hyphenated addresses with a tag on the page function whenever you want a different address.
decisions.gist: How should capitalized page files become web addresses?
decisions.lesson: PascalCase capitalizes each word: OrderItems. A route connects a web address to its handler, the function that answers it. A marker is a tag before that function. A dynamic segment, such as :id, captures one address part.
decisions.explainer: Every option serves the same tiny shop: home at /, items at /order-items, one order at /orders/:id, and purchases at /purchases. GET means reading a page. The examples are file-to-address maps plus a tag excerpt, not complete source files. Each mapped file contains its page function. Shared work: preserve published addresses during the rename, update scaffolds and links, and check the final route list for collisions.
decisions.story: Maya renames her shop's page files to match the new style, but wants customers' bookmarks to keep working.
decisions.detail:
DECISION BOUNDARY AND OBSERVED JET FACTS

Card #4613 is c0itvqcw. Read-only card show confirms D-PATH-CASE1 was ratified A on 2026-10-05. All Jet source directories and stems become PascalCase with capital acronyms. Logical imports remain lowercase through a shared lexicon mapping. This settles physical names, not URLs.

D-HTTP-ROUTE-EXPOSE1=A supplies #server.Get("/path") on mounted struct methods. It requires explicit mux.mount, without package-wide exposure. Neither law chooses App's PascalCase-to-URL mapping. A supplies it; B retires file routing; C expressly amends source naming for route subtrees. This is an OPEN owner choice for #4613, not a ratification or Tower write.

Observed Rust code, 2026-10-05: crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/App.rs:96-108 expands only roots supplied by .routes(from:). At :1794-1880 it enumerates files, requires fn page except leading-underscore opt-outs, derives a path and records an AppRoute. At :1902-1922 it omits only terminal lowercase index/page, changes [name] into :name and otherwise copies each component literally.

Thus Orders.jet becomes /Orders, OrderItems.jet becomes /OrderItems and Index.jet becomes /Index rather than /. At :1930-1940 page detection scans line prefixes, not parsed declarations. Source/CmdBackendScaffold.rs:1936-1939 emits a // route: comment; that scanner ignores it. Capitalization changes public addresses and misses scaffold intent. The selected contract must cover both compiler halves and shared tools.

RESEARCH: PROVEN RIGHT WAYS, WITH PRIMARY SOURCES

1. Next.js Pages Router: https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/pages-and-layouts documents pages/about.js -> /about and index.js -> its directory root. blog/first-post.js yields /blog/first-post; posts/[id].js captures an id. Hyphens are literal, not an automatic PascalCase conversion.

Next.js App Router uses folders as segments and lowercase page files to expose them: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/layouts-and-pages. app/page.tsx is /; app/blog/page.tsx is /blog; app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx supplies dynamic blog pages. The page filename itself is not the segment.

Overrides use external rewrites: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/rewrites. These map source to destination while masking the destination in the address bar. beforeFiles/afterFiles/fallback supply ordered layers. Right way: predictable segments, root omission and deliberate exposure. Avoid copying literal capitals plus separate rewrites solely to get lowercase addresses.

2. SvelteKit: https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/routing documents src/routes/about -> /about and blog/[slug] dynamic directories. +page.svelte exposes a page; +server supplies endpoints; root +page is /. Hyphenated directories remain literal segments.

https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/advanced-routing documents [...rest], [[optional]], matchers and sorting. Filesystem-forbidden characters, especially Windows \\ / : * ? " < > |, require [x+nn] or [u+nnnn] escapes. Its .well-known discussion cites TypeScript's leading-dot directory difficulty.

https://svelte.dev/docs/kit/hooks#reroute supplies a universal client/server hook for alternate or localized addresses. Browser address and event.url stay unchanged. Right way: consistent client/server routing facts. Pain: portable filenames require a URL escape language. Jet can put exceptional URLs in markers instead.

3. Remix v2: https://v2.remix.run/docs/file-conventions/routes/ documents _index.tsx -> / and concerts.salt-lake-city.tsx -> /concerts/salt-lake-city. concerts.$city.tsx captures a city. Dots supply nesting, underscores change layout relationships, parentheses mark optional segments and splats capture rest paths.

Its disclaimer calls filesystem conventions subjective. routes/ignoredRouteFiles and manual configuration are first-class opt-outs. The maintainers acknowledge chaos in apps with hundreds or thousands of routes regardless of convention. This is documented experience, not measured productivity data.

React Router makes decoupling direct: https://reactrouter.com/start/framework/routing has route("some/path", "./some/file.tsx"), index(file), dynamic :name, optional segments and splats. Optional @react-router/fs-routes can join that same configuration. Right way: useful file defaults and deliberate control. Jet can keep control beside a handler without mandatory configuration for every beginner page.

4. Nuxt: https://nuxt.com/docs/3.x/getting-started/routing shows pages/about.vue -> /about, index.vue -> / and posts/[id].vue -> /posts/:id. Its kebab-case normalization claim concerns middleware names, not PascalCase page filenames.

https://nuxt.com/docs/3.x/api/utils/define-page-meta exposes page-local path and alias. Its custom /:postId(\\d+)-:postSlug example resolves overlapping filename patterns. Vue Router documents case-insensitive matching and optional trailing slashes, with sensitive/strict controls: https://router.vuejs.org/guide/essentials/route-matching-syntax.html#sensitive-and-strict-route-options. Right way: local override. Forgiving matching does not guarantee canonical lowercase addresses.

5. Astro: https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/routing/ documents src/pages/index.astro -> /. Both about.astro and about/index.astro map to /about. [author] captures a value; [lang]-[version] mixes parameters and punctuation; [...path] captures rest segments. Static output enumerates getStaticPaths; server rendering matches on request. Paths follow filenames; redirects are separate. Right way: align generated and runtime URLs and detect competing files. This is not evidence of PascalCase slugification.

6. Rails: https://guides.rubyonrails.org/routing.html maps get "/users/:id", to: "users#show" to UsersController.show. It generates named path helpers. Root is an explicit route, not an index-file rule. Resources reduce boilerplate; module scopes can differ from URL prefixes. Written patterns choose casing and hyphens independently of filenames.

The guide warns that a dynamic show route can consume /photos/poll when declared first. Right way: deliberate URLs and common route facts for links. Pain: overlaps resolved by implicit declaration order.

7. Phoenix: https://hexdocs.pm/phoenix/routing.html shows get "/", PageController, :home and resources "/users", UserController. These supply literal and :id routes independently of module capitalization. Macros compile matching and metadata; mix phx.routes exposes the effective table. VerifiedRoutes warns when ~p references an unknown route. Right way: one visible compiled mapping, not competing scanners and rewrite facts.

8. Django: https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/5.2/topics/http/urls/ defines URLconf mappings independently of module filenames. An empty pattern supplies root; index is an action name, not a reserved filename. <int:year>, <slug:slug> and converters handle typed values and hyphenated slugs.

The guide says /articles/2003 does not match /articles/2003/. Patterns are tried in order. Reverse lookup decouples links from implementations. Right way: explicit public patterns with typed binding; punctuation is a contract, not host filesystem behavior.

9. Razor Pages is the closest proven A. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/razor-pages/?view=aspnetcore-10.0 documents Pages/Index.cshtml -> / or /Index and Pages/Store/Index.cshtml -> /Store or /Store/Index. Pages/Contact.cshtml maps to /Contact. Custom routes use @page "/Some/Other/Path" for a full override and @page "{id}" for parameter extension.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/razor-pages/razor-pages-conventions?view=aspnetcore-10.0 documents PageRouteTransformerConvention. SubscriptionManagement/ViewAll.cshtml becomes /subscription-management/view-all. Only generated folder/file segments transform; explicit @page segments and AddPageRoute entries stay untouched. This proves capitalized source, lowercase-hyphen defaults and explicit control can coexist.

Jet should make that default fixed, without application-specific configuration. Do not blindly copy Razor's sample lower-to-upper regex: it does not define Jet acronym boundaries. Jet has a canonical naming lexicon.

10. TanStack Router: https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/routing/file-based-routing recommends filesystem routing with directory/flat/mixed routes, index roots, $postId parameters and route-a hyphens. Virtual File Routes provide control when defaults do not fit. Simplicity and organization benefits are documentation claims, not benchmarks. This corroborates defaults plus an escape hatch, not an absolute ban on either filenames or explicit routes.

PROVEN WRONG WAYS AND ACTUAL FRICTION

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/21498 reports inconsistent URL casing in Next.js 10.0.5 on Windows. Opened in 2021 and now closed, it demonstrates /about matching while /ABOUT 404s. Redirects and rewrites matched both /TEAM and /team.

A workplace comment reports an infinite /About -> /about redirect because the redirect matcher also matches /about. Localization comments report pt-br/pt-BR breakage and a 100-locale workaround limit. These are historical reports, not claims about every current release. The opener's assertion that Google indexes case-insensitively is wrong; Google's primary source below contradicts it.

Lesson: do not globally lowercase incoming URLs, give route origins different case policies, or layer implicit case redirects over sensitive values.

Filesystem mismatch is distinct. https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/module-not-found says incorrect import casing causes Linux CI failures and Fast Refresh problems. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/wsl/case-sensitivity documents Windows' normally case-insensitive behavior, per-directory exceptions and applications opening only one of two case-only files. Linux/WSL filesystems differ.

https://support.apple.com/guide/disk-utility/file-system-formats-dsku19ed921c/mac distinguishes ordinary APFS from case-sensitive APFS, using Homework/HOMEWORK as the example. Never infer URL matching from filesystem behavior. Reject nonportable physical collisions during discovery, keeping one route table on every host.

https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/url-structure recommends descriptive words and hyphens instead of underscores. /APPLE and /apple are distinct Google URLs. It recommends consistent case when servers treat cases alike. Lowercase is our convention, not a claimed mandatory ranking factor. Audience-language URLs are encouraged, so explicit localized and non-ASCII addresses remain possible.

Django's URL guide points to W3C's Cool URIs don't change to motivate implementation-independent addresses. Source renames must not casually discard published paths.

Evidence limits: no controlled cross-framework productivity measurements or SEO ranking deltas were retrieved. This recommendation rests on documented framework mechanisms, a historical failure report, official filesystem behavior and Google's guidance. No invented adoption percentages or performance gains.

SYNTHESIS

A combines Razor's transformation and local override, Next/Svelte/Astro beginner convenience, React Router/Remix control and Phoenix's single route truth. It avoids literal capitals, filename escape alphabets, casing loops and silent collisions. It promises neither automatic redirects nor whole-program scans.

B strongly separates addresses and implementation, but requires every simple page to be declared. C follows familiar literal-file frameworks, but expressly creates an exception to ratified source naming. Shared work: coordinated compiler/scaffold/docs/link migration, collision checks, platform-independent discovery and published-address preservation. These are not extra losses charged to A.

options.name: Friendly defaults, exact overrides
options.detail: Keep PascalCase everywhere. A discovered page gets a lowercase, hyphen-separated address automatically; Index and Page name the enclosing address. A By-prefixed segment captures one value, so Orders/ByID names an order by id. Put an existing GET marker on the page function to replace the entire inferred address, including its folders. Beginners add files; experts choose exact public addresses without breaking the file naming rule.
options.technical:
Scope: only App .routes(from: "Routes") roots contribute convention pages. Existing builder routes and mounted HTTP structs stay explicit; no unmounted-method exposure or package scan. Read the parsed fn page declaration and resolved marker identity, not source line prefixes.

Explicitly extend core.http.server.Get's permitted sites to a free fn page inside an opted-in root. This adds no bare #Get language marker and changes no mounted-method behavior. Outside that scope a marked free function exposes nothing; diagnose the unregistered handler and name explicit registration as the fix. Other verbs keep their ratified registrations. File discovery still supplies GET pages, not an implicit API server.

Fixed mapping: remove .jet and decode each PascalCase component using D-PATH-CASE1's shared lexicon/inverse mapping. Lowercase canonical ASCII word tokens and join with '-'. Digits remain attached to their token. An adjacent-acronym underscore becomes a hyphen separator. No locale folding or project-specific slugifier. Examples: Orders -> orders, OrderItems -> order-items, HTTPClient -> http-client, UTF8Codec -> utf8-codec, Base64 -> base64, HTTP_JSON -> http-json.

Naming-invalid or non-round-tripping stems get the shared naming diagnostic. Exceptional public spellings use a marker on a validly named file. The opted-in root itself contributes no URL segment. Nested folders use the same transformation: Admin/OrderItems.jet -> /admin/order-items.

Omit only terminal file stems exactly Index or Page. Either maps to its parent: Index.jet -> /; Orders/Page.jet -> /orders. Index and Page folders remain ordinary /index and /page segments. Create no index/page aliases. Competing omitted roots are collisions, not two exposures.

Dynamic spelling: reserve leading canonical word By plus a nonempty parameter name for one captured segment, whether folder or terminal stem. Convert its suffix through the existing lowercase underscore identifier mapping: ByID -> :id, ByOrderID -> :order_id, ByURLKey -> :url_key. Orders/ByID.jet -> /orders/:id; Orders/ByID/OrderItems.jet -> /orders/:id/order-items. Use existing typed parameter checks.

ByLaw therefore captures :law; #server.Get("/by-law") is the literal escape. Bare By remains /by. Physical names need no brackets, colons, dollars or optional/rest punctuation. Complex routes use the existing explicit grammar; this ballot invents no optional/rest feature. Migrate [id] components to ByID and rewrite bindings. Preserve unsupported legacy patterns with existing explicit registrations instead of guessing.

Override: #server.Get("/purchases") on Orders.jet's fn page replaces /orders completely, including folders. It is not a suffix or alias. Use the literal after common path validation/canonicalization, never PascalCase splitting or lowercasing. Markers can choose uppercase, hyphens, dots, localized text and existing :name patterns. Multiple GET overrides are errors. A marker on another declaration changes nothing. Validate bindings exactly as explicit routes; do not also register the inferred path.

One final App route table carries provenance, parameters and chosen paths. All sources share collision and precedence checks, without filename priority or override-wins suppression. Equivalent /orders/:id and /orders/:order_id patterns collide despite different capture names. Existing literal-first precedence keeps /orders/new ahead of /orders/:id.

Server, client navigation, emitted builds and dev server use the same validated spelling. Never lowercase captured values, queries or incoming paths. Links and manifests read the final table rather than re-slugifying names. Filesystem behavior never chooses URL matching. Introduce no case-insensitive aliases or automatic redirects.

Migration: compare old/new tables before renaming and preserve changed published addresses with real markers or existing registrations. Convert scaffold // route: intent into a marker and delete the obsolete comment. Comments never become metadata. Scaffolds emit Routes, Index.jet and PascalCase stems, deriving friendly defaults or marking exact requested URLs.

Old underscore helper opt-outs do not authorize non-PascalCase stems. Move helpers outside the opted-in root during cutover instead of inventing a naming exception. Every discovered page file must supply its declared handler. Update all legacy index/page/bracket fixtures, generators and both compiler implementations together. Reuse portability collision checks; never rely on case-only moves. Comments, generated addresses and the final table must agree.

options.name: Write every address explicitly
options.detail: Keep PascalCase files, but filenames never choose addresses. Register each shop page explicitly or mark a mounted handler with its exact address. Moving or renaming files cannot change public addresses. This is the strongest separation of source organization and URL design, at the cost of a declaration even for a simple page.
options.technical:
Retire .routes(from:) and convention expansion, including index/page and bracket special cases. Migrate every caller to existing App page/route builder registrations. Marked HTTP methods still require mux.mount under D-HTTP-ROUTE-EXPOSE1=A. Markers alone expose neither functions nor files. Never keep .routes(from:) as a deprecated no-op or reinterpret it as a package scan.

Page references use lowercase logical modules resolving PascalCase files under D-PATH-CASE1. Map / to routes.index.page, /order-items to routes.order_items.page, /orders/:id to routes.orders.by_id.page and /purchases to routes.orders.page. The short example displays registration facts, not new arrow syntax.

Scaffolds write source plus a real builder registration or mounted HTTP marker, never a // route: hint. Refuse ambiguous target builders instead of failing silently. Replace scanner-only tests with explicit registration tests. One final route table, shared duplicate/parameter checks and host-independent matching remain required.

Explicitly amend the opt-in file-routing portion of D-WEBAUTHOR1/D-DX-ROUTER1, without abolishing App builders or HTTP markers. No new marker sites. B fits apps whose URLs and code organization diverge throughout.

options.name: Exempt route files from capitals
options.detail: Keep the familiar lowercase and hyphenated route subtree. Its names copy public address segments; index and page name their directory root, and brackets mark dynamic values. Exact marker overrides still work for exceptional addresses. This follows common web frameworks closely, but route source files and folders now follow a different naming rule from the rest of Jet.
options.technical:
Explicitly amend D-PATH-CASE1=A only beneath .routes(from:) roots. Route directories/stems may be lowercase/hyphenated, retaining [id] and terminal lowercase index/page. Elsewhere PascalCase remains mandatory, including Routes itself. Bind these files through an explicit discovered module map, without a second import spelling that violates lowercase underscore identifier syntax. Reject case-only physical collisions on every host.

The shop uses Routes/index.jet, Routes/order-items.jet, Routes/orders/[id].jet and Routes/orders.jet. The last has #server.Get("/purchases") as a complete override. Use A's parsed-page marker extension and replacement semantics, not ignored-comment pseudo-overrides. Otherwise preserve literal routing and parameter spellings. Do not silently rename files to Orders.jet or OrderItems.jet.

Collision checks, typed bindings, final-table generation and shared case behavior are as in A. Scaffolds intentionally emit exempt names; formatter/package tooling recognizes the opted-in subtree. Roots become naming boundaries as well as discovery boundaries. The owner must expressly approve narrowing the every-path law.

Helpers outside the root retain PascalCase. Existing underscore opt-outs remain only inside this exempt subtree. Do not spread exemptions to ordinary components or general source directories.

comparisons.note: A documented route transformer converts capitalized folder/file segments to lowercase-hyphen addresses; an explicit page route stays untouched. See the primary sources in detail.
App uses folder segments and a page file; Pages uses filenames and index omission. Both need an explicit rewrite mechanism for an alternate address.
Directories supply literal address segments; +page exposes a page and [id] captures a value. Special filesystem characters require escape conventions.
Remix keeps a file convention with a manual opt-out. React Router supports explicit path-to-module configuration and optional file routes in one table.
Both use index roots and bracket parameters. Nuxt offers a page-local path override; neither cited page proves automatic PascalCase slugification.
All choose public patterns independently of filenames. Resources or typed converters reduce boilerplate without tying URL casing to source names.
comparisons.code:
# Rails: get '/orders/:id', to: 'orders#show'
# Phoenix: get '/orders/:id', OrderController, :show
# Django: path('orders/<int:id>/', views.order)

recommendation.why: A keeps adding a page effortless while giving experts the exact address they want. It combines proven friendly defaults and local overrides without filename exceptions or a second rewrite layer.
gains: Uniform source names and readable lowercase-hyphen addresses.
Add a file for a normal page; add a tag only for an exception.
One checked route list, with no hidden aliases or competing overrides.

losses.loss: Renaming an untagged page can change its address.
losses.mitigation: The rename tool shows the address change and offers a marker preserving the old address before moving the file.

losses.loss: The By prefix reserves a filename spelling for captured values.
losses.mitigation: A marker chooses a literal address for names such as ByLaw; ordinary code filenames stay unchanged.

whyNot.reason: B makes addresses independent of filenames, but requires explicit wiring for every ordinary page.
C keeps familiar literal filenames, but breaks the single naming rule just approved for all Jet source.

recommendation.tradeoff: Learn one small default rule; retain exact control whenever the public address should differ. Shared migration work preserves existing published addresses.

decisions.checkInstructions:
Run node $JET_STATE_ROOT/ballots/READY/validate.mjs $JET_STATE_ROOT/ballots/READY/D-ROUTE-FILES1.json; require exit 0 and boardWritten:false. Main attaches/posts OPEN on #4613 for the owner. This worker neither writes Tower nor ratifies the decision.

After ratification Main verifies once across both compiler halves, scaffold generation, development server, client/server builds and route manifests. Serve the same four-page shop and compare its effective routes and responses. Cover Index/Page omission, nested folders, OrderItems, HTTPClient, UTF8Codec and acronym seams. Cover ByID and multiword parameters, exact hyphen/dot/mixed-case/localized overrides, typed binding and multiple overrides. Check wrong-declaration markers, handlers outside opted-in roots and unchanged mounting semantics.

Check literal /orders/new precedence over /orders/:id. Duplicate roots, explicit paths, marker-versus-builder collisions and equivalent dynamic patterns must error with both sources. Overrides remove inferred routes, not create aliases. Scaffold-requested addresses must work without // route: comments. Links/manifests use chosen addresses; rename tools offer preserving markers.

Exercise physical case-collision fixtures on Linux and case-insensitive macOS/Windows without host-dependent behavior. Preserve captured-value casing and add no implicit case redirects. For B remove .routes(from:) and obsolete convention callers/tests; each page needs real registration. For C verify root boundaries, exempt lowercase/hyphen/bracket names and PascalCase elsewhere. Update source naming, routing and scaffold docs together. Remove deprecated aliases and ignored-comment compatibility paths.

surface.lesson: PascalCase capitalizes words: OrderItems. A route connects an address to its answering function. A marker is a tag before that function; :id captures one address part.

current.note: Today, capitals reach the address; the comment cannot override it.

decisions.title: One casing law for every name in Jet source
decisions.situation: Casing is how a name uses capital letters, as in UserProfile, user_profile or MAX_RETRIES. Jet's casing rules exist, but they are spread over many separate decisions, and a few kinds of names have no rule yet. You asked for one consistent rule that favors capitalized words with fully capitalized acronyms such as HTTP. This vote picks the one rule for names written in Jet code; companion votes cover files, web addresses and data formats. We recommend letting case show what a name is: capitals for kinds of things, lowercase with underscores for values, and full capitals for fixed module values.
decisions.gist: Which capitalization rule should every name in Jet code follow?
decisions.lesson: PascalCase capitalizes each word: UserProfile. snake_case uses lowercase words joined by underscores: user_profile. SCREAMING_SNAKE uses capitals: MAX_RETRIES. An acronym is a word made of initials, such as HTTP or ID. A type is a kind of thing; a value is something you hold or call, such as a function or a field.
decisions.explainer: Every option shows the same small program: one record type, one choice type, one constant, and two functions. The examples show how each option spells them. Shared work for any option: one written casing section in the spec, compiler checks with automatic fixes, and the same rules in both compiler halves.
decisions.story: Kai writes a small web service. He wants to guess the spelling of a type, a function and a constant without looking anything up, and to know which ones are types at a glance.
decisions.inWild:
# Python PEP 8: capitalized words for classes, lowercase for functions
class HTTPServerError(Exception): ...
def parse_http_url(raw): ...
MAX_RETRIES = 3
decisions.detail:
DECISION BOUNDARY

Owner request, 2026-10-05, card #4613 (c0itvqcw): one research-backed casing proposal covering everything in Jet. The owner prefers PascalCase with all-caps acronyms and wants one consistent, understandable rule. The full proposal, with evidence and a census, is Docs/proposals/casing-2026-10-05.md on branch proposal/casing.

This ballot covers names written in Jet source. D-PATH-CASE2 covers file names, D-ROUTE-FILES2 covers web addresses from files, and D-WIRE-CASE1 and D-WIRE-ACRONYM1 cover names in data formats, environment variables, command lines and SQL.

RATIFIED LAW THIS RESTATES

D-SHAPE-CASE1=C (syntax-decisions.md:73-82): type-like names PascalCase, value-like names snake_case, enforced by E0357. Owner rulings of 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-30 (syntax-decisions.md:84-99): module-level immutable bindings are ALL_CAPS, and casing never implies compile time.

D-ACRO-CASE1=A and D-ACRO-LEX1=A (S66, syntax-decisions.md:101-112): a closed acronym list in Syntax::ACRONYMS, all caps inside PascalCase, underscore only between touching capital runs, E0358 with a fix. D-CASING1 and D-MARKER-CASE1=A: every marker part after # is PascalCase. D-ONCE-CASE1=A: one lexicon for every surface.

CENSUS, 7,409 tracked .jet files on master 3e5349196

Type declarations: 5,396, averaging 2.44 words; 45% have three or more words; none has two touching acronyms. Functions and methods: 32,749, averaging 2.95 words; 53% have three or more; 43 have two touching acronyms. Module constants: 2,180, averaging 3.22 words; 10 have touching acronyms.

Example: recipe_update_parse_http_url, Jetpack/Recipe/Source/Toolchain/UpdateTransport.jet:114. Under option B it becomes RecipeUpdateParseHTTP_URL.

RESEARCH

Binkley et al., ICPC 2009, 135 subjects: camelCase answers were more accurate but 13.5% slower. Sharif and Maletic, ICPC 2010, eye tracking: no accuracy difference; underscores 20% faster overall. The gap was nil at two words and 36% at three. Binkley et al., Empirical Software Engineering 2013, 150 subjects: experts are less affected by style.

No study shows a large, stable winner. The evidence favors separators in long names and one consistent style per role.

Rust, Python, Swift, Kotlin, Java, Zig, Nim and Haskell all separate kinds from values by case. C# capitalizes methods and properties but uses camelCase parameters. Delphi and Ada are case-insensitive. Go makes an initial capital mean exported.

Acronyms: Go, Swift, Python PEP 8 and the Ada style guide keep them fully capitalized. Rust, .NET, Kotlin, Google Java and Zig word-case them, as in Uuid or XmlHttpRequest. The capitalized camp needs a project-wide list, as Ada's guide says. Jet already has one.

Case as visibility in Go forces capitalized fields, so JSON keys need a tag on almost every field. That is the strongest evidence against capitalized fields.

NEW RULES COMPLETED BY OPTION A

Compile-time number parameters are SCREAMING, as in <prep N: Int> or ROWS. Generic type parameters are PascalCase. A trailing lowercase s after an acronym is a plural: URLs, IDs; snake urls, ids. Today no Jet identifier uses a plural acronym.

A word made only of digits, as in x_0, is rejected with the fix x0, because such names cannot round-trip through camelCase. Protobuf's JSON guide documents that loss. Version pairs keep one underscore between numbers, as in windows10_1709.

Brand words with inner capitals stay single words unless the compound table lists them, as it lists MacOS, IPv4 and IPv6. New compounds join by ballot. All case changes use locale-independent simple case folding, as the Ada reference manual requires.

options.name: Case shows what a name is
options.detail: PascalCase names kinds of things: types, traits, enum cases, markers, effects and type parameters. snake_case names values and namespaces: functions, methods, fields, parameters, locals, modules and import names. SCREAMING_SNAKE names fixed module-level values. Acronyms are fully capitalized in PascalCase and SCREAMING, and lowercase in snake_case. Compiler errors offer the exact fix.
options.technical:
One spec section replaces the casing paragraphs of S54, S66, D-CASING1 and the owner constant rulings, without changing their meaning. The table is: PascalCase for types, traits, enum variants, markers including their library part, effects and capabilities, unit families and generic type parameters. snake_case for functions, methods, fields, parameters, locals, module paths, import aliases, unit members, lint names and labels. SCREAMING_SNAKE for module-level immutable bindings and compile-time number parameters.

Words are the identity: underscores, hyphens, case changes and acronym ends split words. Acronyms come only from Syntax::ACRONYMS, mirrored in Casing.jet. Touching acronyms keep one underscore in PascalCase, as in HTTP_API.

New checks: SCREAMING number parameters, plural acronyms, digit-only words, and new brand compounds by ballot. E0357 and E0358 report them with machine-applicable fixes; jet fix applies them. decisions.title: One import-to-file rule; capitals in Jet's repository, reserved files lowercase
decisions.situation: Jet is module-based: files in one package see each other with no import, so a file name matters only when a module name such as use app.httpClient must find its file. You decided Jet's own files use capitals without forcing them on users, and asked for best practice in this module-first design. Proven module systems such as Rust, Rails, Python and TypeScript tie each module to one file by a fixed rule and never let the disk's letter case decide. We recommend matching that file by its words in any capitalization, so web kebab-case, Python snake_case and Jet's PascalCase files all work, and refusing two files that spell one module.
decisions.gist: How should an import find its file when people capitalize file names differently?
decisions.lesson: An import names code with words joined by dots, like app.httpClient. A file may spell those words as http_client, http-client or HTTPClient. PascalCase capitalizes each word and keeps acronyms such as HTTP fully capitalized. Jet's own repository uses PascalCase; your projects need not. Whichever option wins, errors must show the real file path.
decisions.explainer: Every option uses the same project: one import, use app.httpClient, and one file holding that code. Imports are spelled in camelCase, the value style recommended by the companion casing-law vote; the matching rule is the same under either value style. The examples show which file spellings the import finds. Shared work: keep one matching function in both compiler halves, keep the reserved files package.jet and run.jet lowercase, and update documentation and fixtures together.
